abandon-embeds-rationale-in-retract-reas.text: The `abandon` branch interpolates the triage rationale into the `retract_node` `reason` string in addition to `set_metadata`.

abandon-repair-embeds-triage-rationale-i.text: The `abandon` repair branch interpolates the triage rationale into the `retract_node` reason string in addition to setting metadata.

absence-and-outlist-form-complete-negati.text: The system has complete semantics for all forms of negation: structural absence produces emergent premise behavior and asymmetric fail modes, while explicit outlist entries provide conjunctive defeat with defined absent-node handling and persistence — together covering every mechanism by which beliefs can be negated or defeated.

justifications.label: Structural absence semantics and explicit outlist semantics together cover the full negation space (depth-3)

absence-and-outlist-form-complete-negati.text: The system defines consistent semantics for specific absence patterns and a conjunctive defeat mechanism: structural absence (no justifications) yields premise behavior via vacuous truth over empty lists, referential absence (missing nodes) follows conservative/permissive asymmetry, and the outlist primitive specifies conjunctive OUT-ness with a permissive absent-node default and persistence via JSON serialization with rebuilt dependent indexes — together constituting the specified mechanisms by which beliefs can be negated or defeated in the system.

absence-has-consistent-dual-semantics.text: Absence has deliberate, defined semantics throughout the system at two levels: structural absence (no justifications) creates premise behavior via vacuous truth over empty lists, while referential absence (missing nodes) follows conservative/permissive asymmetry — both forms of absence produce predictable behavior rather than errors or undefined state.

justifications.label: Structural absence (depth-1) and referential absence (depth-1) are independently well-defined, and together show the system treats all forms of absence as meaningful semantic choices

absent-outlist-node-is-treated-as-out.text: A justification may reference an outlist node that does not exist in the network; this is treated as "OUT" and therefore satisfies the outlist condition (`tests/test_outlist.py:test_outlist_node_not_in_network`).

absolute-claims-are-primary-contradictio.text: Most contradictions detected by the `contradictions` command involve a belief making an absolute claim ("all", "never", "sole", "every") when another belief documents a specific exception — imprecise premises (fixable via `reasons update`) are a secondary category.

accept-beliefs-does-not-recount-existing.text: Re-running `accept-beliefs` over the same proposals accepts 0 new beliefs while `total_beliefs` remains unchanged, so already-stored beliefs are not re-counted as newly accepted.

accept-beliefs-is-gated-from-propose-bel.text: The `accept-beliefs` step can accept 0 beliefs from a large `total_beliefs` pool (0 accepted from 201), showing acceptance is a distinct decision separate from proposal.

accept-beliefs-is-idempotent.text: Re-running `accept-beliefs` against the same 260 proposals accepts 0 new beliefs (versus 78 on first run) while `total_beliefs` remains 201, so acceptance is state-dependent and does not re-count already-stored beliefs.

accept-beliefs-produces-zero-accepted.text: The `accept-beliefs` step accepted 0 of 260 proposals, leaving `total_beliefs` at 201 while the run still reports `"completed"`.

accept-beliefs-reports-total-belief-coun.text: The `accept-beliefs` step records both newly accepted beliefs and the resulting total belief count, as shown by `accepted: 78` and `total_beliefs: 201`.

accept-beliefs-tracks-accepted-and-total.text: The `accept-beliefs` step records both the number of beliefs accepted in the run and the total belief count after processing.

accept-bellefs-gate-accepted-zero.text: In this run, the `accept-beliefs` step accepted 0 of the 182 proposed beliefs while the belief store remained at `total_beliefs: 123`.

accept-definition-not-found-in-observati.text: The `find_accept_definition` search returned zero matches for `def accept|accept_|Accept`.

accept-flow-requires-existing-plan-file.text: `reasons contradictions --accept <missing>` exits with code 1; an existing but empty plan exits 0 with a `"No APPLY entries"` message.

accept-proposal-actions-closed-four.text: `accept_proposal` supports exactly four actions — `add`, `retract`, `supersede`, `nogood` — and raises `ValueError` on any other action.

accept-proposal-detects-drift-before-app.text: `accept_proposal()` compares the target node's current truth value against the proposal's expectation before mutating; if the node was retracted out-of-band, it returns `{"applied": false, "status": "stale"}` without modifying the network.

accept-proposal-drift-detection.text: `accept_proposal` re-validates the stored `snapshot_json` against the live network state; if `truth_value` or `text_hash` has drifted since the proposal was created, the proposal is marked `stale` and the change is not applied.

accept-proposal-drift-yields-stale-not-e.text: When the target state changed between proposal and acceptance, `accept_proposal` returns `{"applied": False, "status": "stale"}` and does not mutate the store, rather than raising.

accept-proposal-is-not-a-single-transact.text: The read, the network mutation, and the proposals-row update happen in three separate SQLite connections; the docstring's "single write transaction" claim is aspirational.

accept-proposal-is-optimistic-no-lock.text: Proposal creation does not lock the target; conflicts between propose and accept are resolved by accept-time drift re-validation.

accept-proposal-mutation-and-status-upda.text: `accept_proposal` performs re-validation read, network mutation, and proposals-row update across separate connections/transactions; the final `UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending'` serializes only proposal status, not the prior network mutation.

accept-proposal-partial-failure-leaves-p.text: If the network mutation raises after drift checks, the proposals-row update is skipped and the proposal can remain `pending` even if a change was partially applied.

accept-proposal-pg-dispatch-bypasses-sql.text: When `pg_conninfo` is set, `accept_proposal` delegates entirely to `PgApi`, and the SQLite-specific drift re-validation does not run in this process.

accept-proposal-pg-dispatch-skips-sqlite.text: When `pg_conninfo` is set, none of the SQLite-side drift checks run in this process; the Postgres backend must replicate them.

accept-proposal-race-detection-is-post-h.text: A losing acceptor only learns it lost after the network mutation may have already been applied; the `UPDATE … WHERE status='pending'` returning `rowcount=0` is the only signal.

accept-proposal-requires-pending-status.text: `accept_proposal` only applies proposals whose status is `pending`; missing IDs raise `KeyError` and non-pending IDs raise `ValueError`.

accept-proposal-requires-proposal-status.text: The initial `SELECT … WHERE status='pending'` is the sole precondition checked; already-accepted/rejected/withdrawn proposals raise `ValueError`.

accept-proposal-requires-snapshot-match.text: `accept_proposal` marks a proposal `stale` and returns `{"applied": False}` whenever the live node's `truth_value` or `text_hash` no longer matches the proposal's `snapshot_json`.

accept-proposal-returns-stale-not-raises.text: Drift is reported as `{"applied": False, "status": "stale"}` rather than as an exception; callers must branch on `applied`.

accept-proposal-revalidates-against-live.text: Every action re-reads the network and compares against the stored `snapshot_json` before mutating; drift short-circuits to `status='stale'`.

accept-proposal-stale-is-normal-outcome.text: Drift and lost accept races return `{"applied": False, "status": "stale", ...}` rather than raising, so callers must branch on `applied`/`status`.

accept-revalidates-drift-before-apply.text: `reasons/api.py:5631-5633` re-validates against the live network and marks a proposal stale without applying it when drift is detected.

access-control-enforced-at-read-not-writ.text: Access control (`_is_visible`) is enforced at read/query boundaries (`show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`) via `PermissionError`, but write operations (`add_node`, `retract_node`, `assert_node`) do not check visibility.

access-control-is-transitive-subset-gate.text: Access control enforces transitive subset-based authorization: visibility requires the caller's tags to be a superset of the node's tags, derived nodes inherit the sorted union of all ancestor tags transitively, and enforcement occurs at read boundaries only — write operations are unrestricted.

justifications.label: Three access control properties (subset gate, transitive inheritance, read-boundary enforcement) form a complete authorization model

access-denied-prefix-used-for-standalone.text: `cmd_show`, `cmd_explain`, `cmd_trace_access_tags`, and `cmd_trace` print `Access denied: {e}` to stderr on `PermissionError`.

access-predicate-separated-from-content-.text: Access control uses `_is_visible` over `access_tags`, while `_filter_by_tags` implements user-supplied topic/status/tag query filters.

access-tag-inheritance-uses-antecedents-.text: `Network._inherit_access_tags` unions `access_tags` only from antecedent nodes, not from outlist nodes.

access-tag-matching-is-exact-and-case-se.text: Visibility uses set membership with no normalization, prefix matching, wildcards, or hierarchy.

access-tag-membership-is-exact-and-case-.text: Access-tag visibility uses exact set membership with no normalization, prefix matching, wildcards, or hierarchy.

access-tags-are-monotonically-inherited.text: A derived node's `access_tags` are the union of its own tags and all antecedent tags; tags are never removed by inheritance, only accumulated, so access restrictions can only grow along derivation chains.

access-tags-are-prefixed.text: Access tags are inserted into `node_tags` as `access:<tag>`, while plain `metadata["tags"]` are inserted verbatim.

access-tags-are-stored-in-metadata-not-n.text: Access control checks `access_tags` from `node.metadata`, so calling `add_tags` with a tag like `access_tags:secret` does not gate visibility.

access-tags-gate-all-query-commands.text: No CLI command (show, explain, trace, status, trace-access-tags) leaks access-restricted content to unauthorized viewers; a node tagged `finance` is invisible to `--visible-to hr` queries across all inspection commands.

access-tags-inherit-by-union.text: A derived node's effective access tags are the union of all its antecedents' tags, meaning visibility scope only tightens (grows) as you ascend the justification chain.

access-tags-inherit-through-antecedents.text: Derived nodes receive the union of antecedent `access_tags` plus explicit tags, and new justifications propagate tags to dependents.

access-tags-migrate-to-tag-namespace.text: Passing `access_tags=["internal"]` to `api.add_node` results in a stored tag `access:internal`, not a raw `access_tags` field.

access-tags-not-fabricated-for-untagged-.text: When all parent nodes are untagged, a derived node receives no inherited access tags; the system does not fabricate tags.

access-tags-rbac-is-introduced-in-0-18-0.text: The `access_tags` field, `--visible-to`, tag inheritance, forward propagation, and `PermissionError` on single-node reads are all first documented under `[0.18.0]`.

access-tags-require-subset-for-visibilit.text: A node is visible only when all of its access tags are present in the caller's `visible_to` set (subset semantics); nodes with empty access tags are always visible. `show_node`/`explain_node` raise `PermissionError` on violation while list operations silently filter.

access-tags-subset-gate.text: A tagged node is visible only when its `access_tags` are a subset of the caller's `visible_to` set; partial overlap (intersection without containment) is insufficient for access.

access-tags-survive-sqlite-roundtrip.text: `access_tags` survive write-to-SQLite and read-back through `api.add_node` and `api.show_node`.

access-tags-union-inheritance.text: A derived node's `access_tags` is the sorted, deduplicated union of all antecedent tags across all justifications, merged with any explicit tags on the node itself.

action-is-uppercased-for-display-and-bra.text: `proposal["action"].upper()` is compared against `"UPDATE"`/`"RETRACT"`, so actions are case-insensitive in the input.

action-values-not-validated.text: `parse_repair_response` uses `item.get("action", "retract")` without restricting to `{"rewrite","retract"}`, so an arbitrary model-supplied action can reach callers.

active-inactive-relay-pair.text: Each imported agent gets exactly two infrastructure nodes: `agent:active` (premise, starts IN) and `agent:inactive` (derived via SL with `outlist=[active_id]`, starts OUT); every imported belief includes `inactive_id` in its outlist

active-nogood-selects-least-entrenched-c.text: When `find_culprits` returns candidates, `add_nogood` retracts `culprits[0]["premise"]`, which is sorted by least entrenchment, not by fewest dependents.

active-not-in-antecedents.text: The `active` premise is deliberately excluded from imported beliefs' antecedents; if it were an antecedent, it would provide a second always-valid justification path that defeats per-belief retraction semantics

active-precondition-is-not-an-antecedent.text: For every imported belief, `{agent}:active` is excluded from `justifications[0].antecedents`; this is the explicit fix for the issue-#16 resurrection bug.

active-premise-is-excluded-from-antecede.text: `<agent>:active` is never placed in antecedents of imported justifications; only `<agent>:inactive` appears in outlists.

active-premise-is-retraction-entry-point.text: `{agent}:active` is a plain premise node whose retraction is the sole trigger for revoking an agent.

add-justification-achieves-consistent-pr.text: Adding a justification to an existing node produces a fully consistent network state through guaranteed-terminating multi-dimensional propagation: truth values cascade via BFS through dependents, the reverse index is updated, and access tags recompute transitively — all within a single operation whose termination is guaranteed by BFS traversal and stop-on-unchanged semantics.

justifications.label: Multi-dimensional propagation composed with termination guarantees yields a consistent single-operation update

add-justification-any-mode-expands-only-.text: `add_justification` applies `any_mode` expansion only for `jtype == "SL"` with multiple antecedents.

add-justification-any-mode-is-sl-only-an.text: `any_mode` only expands SL justifications with more than one antecedent; it is ignored for CP/outlist-only justifications, and a PostgreSQL call with `any_mode=True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

add-justification-any-mode-returns-last-.text: In `any_mode`, `add_justification` creates one SL justification per antecedent but returns only the last iteration's result and sets `premise_count=1`, discarding intermediate `changed` sets.

add-justification-api-defined-at-api-py-.text: `add_justification` is defined at `reasons/api.py:406` and also at `reasons/mcp_server.py:204`.

add-justification-appends-not-replaces.text: `Network.add_justification()` appends a new justification to the node's existing justification list rather than replacing existing justifications.

add-justification-appends-without-replac.text: Adding a justification to a node appends the new justification to the existing list rather than replacing prior justifications, and new justifications are appended in call order.

add-justification-bypasses-retraction-fl.text: `add_justification` does not check `node.metadata["_retracted"]`; adding a valid justification to a retracted node can recompute it back to `"IN"`.

add-justification-defaults-to-sl.text: `add_justification` defaults `jtype` to `SL`, and `any_mode` expansion applies only to SL justifications with more than one antecedent.

add-justification-does-not-deduplicate.text: The function never checks whether an equivalent justification is already attached; duplicates are appended and can become `supporting_justification`.

add-justification-does-not-deduplicate-j.text: `add_justification` appends the supplied `Justification` without deduplication; adding the same instance twice grows `node.justifications` and can make the duplicate the supporting justification.

add-justification-ignores-retracted-flag.text: Unlike `recompute_all`, this function does not check `node.metadata["_retracted"]` before recomputing truth, so adding a valid justification can silently flip a retracted node back to `IN`.

add-justification-is-fully-propagating.text: Adding a justification triggers complete multi-dimensional propagation: truth values cascade through dependents via BFS, the dependents reverse index is updated on both antecedent and outlist nodes, and access tags flow downstream transitively through all dependent chains.

justifications.label: A single add_justification call triggers three independent propagation dimensions (truth, structure, authorization) ensuring complete downstream consistency

add-justification-lazily-imports-merkle.text: `.merkle` imports are performed inside the function to avoid a circular import at module load time.

add-justification-may-change-supporting-.text: `_compute_truth` reassigns `node.supporting_justification` on every call, even when `old_truth_value == new_truth_value`, and the return dict does not expose this.

add-justification-missing-node-raises-ke.text: `Network.add_justification` raises `KeyError` with a message matching `"not found"` when the target node does not exist.

add-justification-namespace-skips-colon-.text: When `namespace` is provided, `add_justification` prefixes the node and antecedent/outlist IDs only if they lack a `:` and does not inject an `{namespace}:active` premise as `add_node` does.

add-justification-nonexistent-node-raise.text: `Network.add_justification()` raises `KeyError` when the target node ID does not exist.

add-justification-propagates-tags-downst.text: Calling `add_justification` on an existing node recomputes `access_tags` for the target and all its transitive dependents, enabling retroactive tag propagation.

add-justification-registers-antecedent-a.text: Adding a justification registers the target node in the dependents of each antecedent and outlist node.

add-justification-registers-dependents.text: `add_justification` updates the `dependents` set on both antecedent and outlist nodes so that future retraction/restoration propagation reaches the target node.

add-justification-requires-existing-node.text: `add_justification` raises `KeyError` when `node_id` is not present in `self.nodes`.

add-justification-requires-one-support-f.text: `add_justification` raises `ValueError("Must provide --sl, --cp, or --unless")` when `sl`, `cp`, and `unless` are all empty.

add-justification-requires-type.text: add_justification raises ValueError when no justification type is specified.

add-justification-return-omits-tag-chang.text: The returned `changed` list contains only truth-value changes; `_propagate_access_tags` effects are not surfaced to the caller.

add-justification-returns-change-dict.text: `Network.add_justification` returns a dict with keys `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `changed` (list of all nodes whose truth value changed).

add-justification-returns-diff-dict.text: `add_justification` returns a dict with exactly `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `changed`; `changed` is empty when the node's truth value does not change.

add-justification-returns-truth-transiti.text: `Network.add_justification(...)` returns a dict containing `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `changed`, where `changed` includes the target and any cascaded dependents whose truth value changed.

add-justification-silently-skips-unknown.text: Antecedent/outlist IDs absent from `self.nodes` are ignored for the `dependents` index but remain in the justification, where `_justification_valid` treats them as `OUT`.

add-justification-sl-silently-precedes-c.text: When both `sl` and `cp` are non-empty, `add_justification` uses `sl` and silently ignores `cp` because of its elif chain.

add-justification-tolerates-missing-refe.text: `add_justification` silently skips antecedent/outlist IDs absent from `self.nodes` when updating the reverse index, while the stored justification still references those missing IDs.

add-justification-triggers-propagation.text: Adding a justification that changes a node's truth value triggers BFS propagation that cascades to all transitive dependents, including restoring OUT nodes whose justifications become valid.

add-node-always-writes.text: `api.add_node` in `reasons/api.py` opens `_with_network(db_path, write=True)`, has no `dry_run` parameter, and cannot be previewed.

add-node-any-mode-namespace-only-first-j.text: With `any_mode` and `namespace`, only `justifications[0]` gets `{namespace}:active` as an antecedent; the other OR justifications do not depend on the namespace premise.

add-node-any-mode-produces-or-justificat.text: When `any_mode=True` and `sl` contains more than one antecedent, one single-antecedent SL justification is created per antecedent.

add-node-body-confirms-empty-sl-short-ci.text: The entry does not actually show the body of `api.add_node`, so the exact short-circuit behavior for empty `sl` remains inferred rather than confirmed.

add-node-enforces-referential-integrity.text: `PgApi.add_node` raises `KeyError` naming the missing id when any `sl` or `unless` id is absent, so phantom antecedents cannot enter the network.

add-node-evaluates-justification-at-inse.text: When `add_node` is called with justifications, the node's initial truth value is computed immediately from the current state of its antecedents — a derived node added when its antecedent is OUT starts OUT

add-node-has-no-preview-mode.text: `api.add_node` always opens the network with `write=True` and has no `dry_run` parameter, so it cannot be used for a non-mutating preview.

add-node-justification-priority-sl-over-.text: `add_node` builds at most one justification source with priority SL > CP > unless-only.

add-node-namespace-auto-creates-active-p.text: Setting `namespace` auto-creates `{namespace}:active` as a premise with metadata `{"agent": namespace, "role": "agent_premise"}`, and scoped nodes depend on it.

add-node-namespace-auto-wiring-creates-a.text: When a namespace is supplied, `add_node` creates the `ns:active` premise and prepends it to the new node's antecedents.

add-node-namespace-prefix-skipped-if-col.text: The namespace prefix is not applied when `node_id` already contains `:`, allowing cross-namespace references.

add-node-normalizes-access-tags.text: `add_node` stores provided access tags as a sorted, deduplicated list in node metadata.

add-node-outlist-only-creates-empty-ante.text: An `unless`-only `add_node` call creates an SL justification with empty antecedents, i.e. a premise gated by the outlist.

add-node-pg-drops-source-type-and-accept.text: The PostgreSQL dispatch path omits `source_type` and `accepted_pr`, so those metadata fields are never persisted on PG.

add-node-pg-path-drops-source-type-and-a.text: The PG dispatch path for `add_node` does not forward `source_type` or `accepted_pr`, so metadata parity with the SQLite path is not guaranteed.

add-node-premise-count-is-max-antecedent.text: `add_node`'s return `premise_count` is `max(len(j.antecedents))` over justifications, not the number of justifications.

add-node-rejects-invalid-source-type.text: Invalid `source_type` values raise `ValueError` with a message containing `"Invalid source_type"`.

add-node-requires-comma-separated-ids.text: `sl`, `cp`, and `unless` are parsed as comma-separated strings with no escaping; IDs containing commas cannot be expressed.

add-node-returns-premise-count.text: `api.add_node` returns a dict whose `"premise_count"` key holds the antecedent count for the created SL, and `0` for premise nodes.

add-node-sl-defaults-to-empty-string.text: `add_node` declares `sl=""`, so omitting the `sl` argument is equivalent to passing an empty support list.

add-node-stores-example-in-metadata.text: `reasons/api.py:add_node` sets `metadata["example"]` when `example` is not `None` at lines 379–380.

add-node-stores-source-type-in-node-meta.text: A non-empty valid `source_type` is written to `node.metadata["source_type"]`; empty values are omitted.

add-node-validates-source-type.text: `source_type` must be a member of `{"code", "document", "self-description", "derived"}` or `ValueError` is raised.

add-node-writes-through-with-network.text: Every write goes through `_with_network(write=True)`, which skips `save()` when an exception propagates and publishes pubsub change events on success.

add-nogood-always-records.text: `add_nogood` appends a `Nogood` record unconditionally before checking whether the contradiction is active, so nogoods are preserved even when not all member nodes are currently IN

add-nogood-api-returns-nogood-id-key.text: `api.add_nogood(...)` returns a dictionary containing a `"nogood_id"` key.

add-nogood-can-return-empty-for-active-n.text: If the selected culprit premise is already `OUT`, `add_nogood` can return `[]` even though the listed contradiction was active, because `retract` reports no truth-value change.

add-nogood-composes-with-retract.text: `add_nogood` selects a culprit via `find_culprits` and then calls `retract`; it does not implement a separate truth-recompute path.

add-nogood-docstring-mismatches-lowest-e.text: `add_nogood`'s docstring says it retracts the premise with the fewest dependents, but the implementation retracts the lowest-entrenchment premise.

add-nogood-does-not-persist.text: `add_nogood` mutates only in-memory state; persistence to `reasons.db` or `network.json` is the caller's responsibility.

add-nogood-does-not-retrigger-inactive-n.text: If a nogood is inactive when recorded, later changes that make all listed nodes `IN` do not automatically re-trigger resolution; the caller must call `add_nogood` again or resolve manually.

add-nogood-duplicates-silently-accepted.text: `add_nogood` silently accepts duplicate nogood records without raising an error.

add-nogood-empty-input-raises-indexerror.text: `add_nogood([])` reaches the fallback victim-selection path with an empty candidate list and raises `IndexError`.

add-nogood-empty-list-crashes.text: Bug report about an edge case (empty `node_ids` causes `IndexError`) — this is a bug to fix, not an architectural invariant to track as a belief

add-nogood-fallback-uses-dependent-count.text: When `find_culprits` returns no candidates (all nogood nodes are premises with no justification chains), the fallback retracts the nogood member with the fewest direct dependents

add-nogood-has-no-remove-api.text: There is no `remove_nogood`; once a nogood is recorded, it remains in `self.nogoods` permanently.

add-nogood-inactive-contradiction-return.text: If any node in the nogood set is already OUT, `add_nogood` returns an empty list immediately after recording the nogood.

add-nogood-inactive-when-either-node-out.text: `add_nogood` is a no-op returning `[]` (no log entry, no retraction) if either member of the nogood is already OUT.

add-nogood-logs-backtrack-with-culprit.text: A real `Network.add_nogood` backtrack writes a log entry with `action == "backtrack"` and a `"culprit"` field.

add-nogood-mutates-and-backtracks.text: `api.add_nogood` records a nogood via `net.add_nogood(node_ids)` and returns `changed` and `backtracked_to`.

add-nogood-records-before-active-check.text: It appends a `Nogood` and logs it before determining whether all listed nodes are `IN`.

add-nogood-retraction-prefers-least-entr.text: The primary retraction path traces back through justification chains to premises and chooses the one with the lowest entrenchment score (speculative assumptions before evidence-backed observations)

add-nogood-retracts-premises-not-derived.text: `Network.add_nogood` retracts a selected premise and cascades dependent derived nodes `OUT` rather than retracting a derived nogood member directly.

add-nogood-single-node-list-accepted.text: `add_nogood` accepts a single-element `node_ids` list without a validation error.

add-nogood-uses-first-culprit.text: `add_nogood` retracts `culprits[0]["premise"]` when the list is non-empty, else falls back to the nogood node with the fewest dependents.

add-nogood-validates-node-ids-before-rec.text: `add_nogood` iterates `node_ids` and raises `KeyError` before appending a `Nogood` record if any ID is missing.

add-source-bypasses-network-cache.text: Because it opens sqlite directly rather than using `_with_network`, `add_source` does not update `_network_cache` or emit pubsub events; the next read reloads the network from disk due to the mtime change.

add-source-deduplicates-against-node-sou.text: `api.add_source(node_id, source_ref, ...)` deduplicates sources against those already supplied through `add_node(..., source=...)`.

add-source-does-not-update-node-record.text: `add_source` writes only to `node_sources`; it does not update `node.source`, `node.source_url`, or `node.updated_at`.

add-source-is-not-idempotent.text: Calling `add_source` twice with identical arguments inserts two rows in `node_sources`; there is no uniqueness constraint or deduplication.

add-source-rejects-postgres.text: Any truthy `pg_conninfo` raises `NotImplementedError` before touching the database; PostgreSQL support is explicitly deferred.

add-source-requires-existing-node.text: An unknown `node_id` raises `KeyError` before any insert; the existence check is a `SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE id = ?`.

add-tags-does-not-validate-tag-strings.text: `add_tags` stores tag strings verbatim, including empty, whitespace-containing, or colon-containing values, without format validation.

add-tags-relies-on-insert-or-ignore-for-.text: `add_tags` uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` per tag, so duplicate tags are silently ignored only if `node_tags` has a uniqueness constraint on `(node_id, tag)`.

add-tags-requires-existing-node.text: `add_tags` raises `KeyError` when `node_id` is absent from `nodes`; it does not auto-create nodes.

add_tags-raises-keyerror-for-missing-nod.text: A nonexistent `node_id` raises `KeyError`; the function never returns an error-shaped dict.

add_tags-rejects-postgres.text: Setting `pg_conninfo` triggers `NotImplementedError`; there is no PostgreSQL dispatch path for tag writes.

add_tags-requires-unique-constraint.text: Idempotent behaviour of `INSERT OR IGNORE` depends on a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY constraint on `(node_id, tag)` that this function does not create or verify.

add_tags-returns-full-tag-list.text: The return value contains all tags currently stored for the node (sorted), not only the tags passed in.

any-mode-copies-outlist-to-each-expanded.text: When `unless="enemy"` is supplied alongside `any_mode=True`, every expanded justification contains `"enemy"` in its `outlist`.

any-mode-creates-one-justification-per-a.text: Applying a proposal with `mode == "any"` produces N justifications of length 1 (one per antecedent), and retracting any single antecedent leaves the node IN.

any-mode-creates-per-premise-justificati.text: When `any_mode=True` and multiple antecedents are given, each antecedent gets its own SL justification (OR semantics: node is IN if *any* antecedent is IN), rather than the default single multi-antecedent justification (AND semantics).

any-mode-does-not-create-persisted-any-t.text: OR expansion is represented as multiple single-antecedent SL justifications; there is no stored `ANY` justification type.

any-mode-expands-conjunction-into-separa.text: `add_node(..., any_mode=True)` with an N-premise comma-separated `sl` produces N justifications, each containing exactly one antecedent.

any-mode-expands-multi-premise-sl-into-u.text: With `any_mode=True`, `sl="a,b,c"` creates three justifications, each with one antecedent.

any-mode-expands-sl-to-or.text: `any_mode` converts a multi-antecedent SL into one justification per antecedent, making the antecedents alternatives.

any-mode-expansion-implemented-in-api-la.text: `any_mode` expansion is implemented in `reasons_lib.api.add_node` and `reasons_lib.api.add_justification`, not in the `Network` propagation engine.

any-mode-expansion-is-evaluation-invisib.text: Any-mode expansion from conjunctive to disjunctive justifications is invisible to truth evaluation: the expanded justifications propagate completely through the same BFS mechanisms, and truth evaluation produces identical results regardless of whether justifications arrived via original specification or any-mode expansion — a consequence of transformation invariance.

justifications.label: OR-expansion is indistinguishable from manual justification under transformation-invariant evaluation

any-mode-expansion-propagates-completely.text: When any_mode expands a conjunctive justification into per-premise disjunctive justifications, each resulting justification inherits the complete outlist specification (conjunction semantics, absence tolerance, persistence across save/load), and all resulting truth-value changes propagate completely to every affected dependent — but only when outlist nodes are tracked in the dependents index, ensuring outlist-mediated effects are not silently dropped.

justifications.label: Outlist inheritance (depth-1) guarantees semantic completeness of expanded justifications; full outlist specification (depth-1) guarantees well-defined evaluation — but propagation completeness requires outlist nodes to be in the dependents index for cascade reach.

any-mode-expansion-requires-more-than-on.text: The expansion branch only runs when `len(antecedents) > 1`, so `sl="a"` remains a single justification.

any-mode-implements-or-semantics.text: `any_mode=True` expands a multi-antecedent SL into one justification per antecedent (`reasons/api.py:324`, `:457`), so the conclusion survives retraction of any single premise.

any-mode-is-rejected-by-postgresql-backe.text: Both `api.add_node` and `api.add_justification` raise `NotImplementedError` when `any_mode` is used with PostgreSQL.

any-mode-is-sl-only-and-single-anteceden.text: `any_mode` only expands when `jtype == "SL"` and `len(antecedents) > 1`; it is otherwise silently ignored (including for CP).

any-mode-is-structural-expansion.text: Duplicates existing belief `any-mode-creates-per-premise-justifications` which already captures that any_mode expands N premises into N single-premise SL justifications.

any-mode-nodes-never-produce-restoration.text: `retract_node` does not emit restoration hints for any_mode nodes because each expanded justification is independent and a single retraction never cascades the node to OUT.

any-mode-only-expands-sl.text: `reasons/api.py:457` only expands multi-antecedent SL justifications when `any_mode` is true; CP justifications are not expanded.

any-mode-only-expands-sl-justifications.text: `any_mode` expansion is applied only to SL justifications; CP justifications are not expanded into per-antecedent justifications.

any-mode-outlist-preserved.text: When `any_mode` expands `sl="a,b" unless="enemy"`, each resulting single-premise justification inherits `"enemy"` in its outlist.

any-mode-premise-count-is-one.text: With `any_mode=True`, `add_node`'s returned `"premise_count"` is `1` (per unary justification), not the total number of expansions.

any-mode-preserves-full-outlist-semantic.text: When any_mode expands a single multi-antecedent justification into per-premise justifications (OR semantics), each resulting justification preserves the original outlist entries — ensuring non-monotonic defeat works correctly under disjunctive expansion with no semantic loss.

justifications.label: Structural expansion (any_mode) and semantic preservation (outlist inheritance) are co-guaranteed — disjunction never silently drops defeat conditions

any-mode-produces-multiple-single-antece.text: With `any_mode=True`, the API creates one SL justification per premise, each containing one antecedent.

any-mode-reports-premise-count-of-one.text: In the `any_mode` branch the returned `premise_count` is hardcoded to `1` regardless of how many single-antecedent justifications were created.

any-mode-requires-no-schema-column.text: `any_mode=True` in `api.add_node`/`api.add_justification` is realized by inserting N single-antecedent `justifications`/`rms_justifications` rows, so no ANY/ALL column is required.

any-mode-requires-sqlite.text: `reasons/api.py:313–314` and `:432–433` raise `NotImplementedError` when `any_mode` is combined with the PostgreSQL backend.

any-mode-single-premise-no-expansion.text: When `any_mode=True` is used with a single premise, no expansion occurs.

any-mode-skips-expansion-for-single-prem.text: `any_mode` expansion only occurs when there is more than one antecedent, so `sl="a"` stays a single justification.

any-mode-survives-single-retraction.text: With `any_mode=True`, a derived node remains IN after any single premise is retracted and flips OUT only when all expanded premises are retracted.

api-add-justification-namespace-prefixes.text: `api.add_justification()` applies the configured namespace prefix to the node ID in its result, for example returning `ns:b` rather than `b`.

api-add-justification-requires-a-justifi.text: `api.add_justification` raises `ValueError` matching `"Must provide"` when none of `sl`, `cp`, or `unless` is supplied.

api-add-justification-requires-justifica.text: `api.add_justification` raises `ValueError` if none of `sl`, `cp`, or `unless` is provided — at least one justification specification is mandatory.

`api.add_justification` requires at least one justification-type keyword argument (`sl=`, `cp=`, or `unless=`); calling it with none raises `ValueError` with a "Must provide" message rather than silently creating a no-op.

api-add-justification-supports-cp-and-un.text: `api.add_justification()` supports CP justifications and outlist-only `unless` justifications in addition to SL justifications.

api-add-node-auto-wires-namespace-active.text: When `namespace` is provided to `add_node`, it creates an `ns:active` premise and injects it as an antecedent of the node's justification.

api-add-node-lacks-source-hash-and-date-.text: `api.add_node` does not accept `source_hash` or `date`; tests set those attributes directly on a `Network` node and re-save.

api-add-node-rejects-source-hash-and-dat.text: `api.add_node` does not accept `source_hash` or `date`; those must be set directly on the `Network` node and re-saved via `Storage.save`.

api-add-nogood-returns-mutation-and-back.text: `api.add_nogood` records a nogood via `net.add_nogood(node_ids)` and returns `nogood_id`, `nodes`, `changed`, and `backtracked_to`.

api-and-vertex-paths-skip-cost-recording.text: The `api:` and `vertex:` LangChain path returns only response content and never calls `_record_cost`, so those models do not appear in per-model cost summaries.

api-and-vertex-paths-skip-cost-tracking.text: `_record_cost` is never invoked for `api:` / `vertex:` / `ollama:` models, so those models will not appear in `by_model` unless manually inserted.

api-and-vertex-skip-cost-recording.text: `_invoke_api` returns only `response.content` and never calls `_record_cost`, so `api:` and `vertex:` models never appear in `get_cost_summary()["by_model"]`.

api-assert-already-in-returns-empty-chan.text: Calling `api.assert_node()` on an already-IN node returns `changed: []` without raising an error.

api-backends-discard-tool-calls.text: `_invoke_api` calls `llm.invoke(prompt, config=...)` and returns only `response.content`, so any LangChain `AIMessage.tool_calls` are dropped.

api-backfill-hashes-delegates-to-merkle-.text: `reasons/api.py:backfill_hashes` delegates to `reasons.merkle.backfill_hashes` and returns its result.

api-cascade-symmetry-tested.text: Test coverage claim; the underlying behavioral invariant (symmetric retract/restore cascades) is already covered by existing beliefs including `reasoning-engine-is-deterministic-and-reversible`.

api-default-db-is-reasons-db.text: DEFAULT_DB in reasons_lib/api.py is "reasons.db" and is used as the default db_path by API functions.

api-defers-pg-import-to-pgapi.text: `reasons/api.py` never imports `psycopg` directly; `_pg_dispatch` imports `PgApi` lazily and relies on `_require_psycopg()` in `pg.py` to surface the missing-dependency error.

api-detect-contradictions-result-has-che.text: `api.detect_contradictions` returns a result dict containing `checked`, `found`, and `applied` counts.

api-emits-events-only-after-successful-s.text: API operations publish events after updated truth values are visible through `api.show_node`, and failed mutations emit no events.

api-enforces-typed-preconditions.text: API functions enforce preconditions at the system boundary with typed exceptions: duplicate node IDs raise ValueError, missing justification arguments raise ValueError, and unauthorized single-node access raises PermissionError — establishing a consistent error contract at every entry point.

justifications.label: Three independent boundary validations share a systematic pattern of typed-exception precondition enforcement

api-error-contract-exceptions.text: Duplicate of existing `api-enforces-typed-preconditions` which covers typed exceptions (ValueError, KeyError, PermissionError) at API boundaries.

api-fts-search-bounds-query-calls.text: `_fts_search` makes at most 51 internal `_fts_query` calls regardless of input query length, preventing combinatorial explosion from progressive relaxation on long queries.

api-functions-accept-db-path-string.text: Public functions in `reasons_lib.api` accept a `db_path` string keyword and open and close their own SQLite connection internally.

api-functions-open-save-close-db.text: Every write-type public function in `api.py` uses `_with_network(db_path, write=True)`, which loads the DB, mutates the in-memory `Network`, saves on successful exit, and closes `Storage`.

api-functions-return-dicts.text: Every public API function returns a `dict` (or `str` for markdown/compact), never a `Network` or `Node` object, ensuring JSON-serializability at the boundary for CLI, HTTP, and tool-call consumers.

api-get-belief-set-excludes-out-nodes.text: `api.get_belief_set()` returns only IN node IDs and excludes OUT nodes.

api-get-belief-set-returns-only-in-node-.text: `api.get_belief_set()` returns only the IDs of nodes whose truth value is IN.

api-get-log-supports-last-n-truncation.text: `api.get_log(last=N)` returns at most the last N audit-log entries.

api-hidden-node-raises-permissionerror.text: When `visible_to` is set and a target node's access tags are not a subset, `show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`, and `trace_access_tags` raise `PermissionError`.

api-idempotent-operations-return-empty-c.text: Retracting an already-OUT node or asserting an already-IN node returns `changed == []`.

api-idempotent-retract-assert.text: Already exists as an accepted belief with the same ID and content.

api-imports-check-stale-pinning-helpers.text: `reasons/api.py` imports `pin_sources`, `pin_update`, and `pin_lines` from `.check_stale`, making them part of the internal check-stale contract.

api-init-db-refuses-overwrite.text: Covered by existing `api-enforces-typed-preconditions` which captures typed exception enforcement at the API boundary.

api-init-requires-force-to-overwrite.text: `api.init_db()` refuses to overwrite an existing database unless `force=True` is passed.

api-layer-ensures-atomic-isolated-mutati.text: The API layer enforces mutation safety through four mechanisms: context-managed load/save, per-function transaction scope, write-flag gating to prevent unintended persistence, and dict-only returns that prevent callers from holding live network references.

justifications.label: Each API safety mechanism prevents a different class of state corruption: stale reads, cross-function leaks, accidental writes, and reference escapes

api-list-gated-excludes-superseded.text: Covered by existing `supersession-is-reversible-and-view-consistent` which explicitly states superseded nodes are excluded from gated belief lists.

api-list-negative-filters-hallucinated-i.text: `list_negative()` discards any node IDs returned by the LLM that don't exist in the database, preventing hallucinated IDs from appearing in results.

api-list-negative-graceful-on-malformed-.text: When the LLM returns unparseable output, `list_negative()` returns `count == 0` rather than raising an exception — graceful degradation over failure.

api-llm-mocking-patches-consumer-namespa.text: LLM-dependent API tests must patch the imported name in the consumer module's namespace (e.g., `reasons.ask.invoke_model`) rather than the source module (`reasons.llm.invoke_model`) for the mock to take effect.

api-missing-node-raises-keyerror.text: `show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`, and `what_if_*` raise `KeyError` when a node ID is not found.

api-models-skip-per-model-elapsed.text: `api:` and `vertex:` calls never create a `by_model` entry, so their per-model `elapsed_seconds` is never accumulated (only the global counter).

api-mutating-ops-use-before-after-diffin.text: Mutating operations (`retract_node`, `assert_node`, `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`) snapshot all truth values before the operation and diff afterward to classify changes into `went_out`/`went_in` lists.

api-noop-or-failed-mutations-emit-no-eve.text: API mutations that do not change truth values, such as `set_metadata`, and mutations that raise before saving emit no pubsub events.

api-prefix-does-not-record-cost.text: `_invoke_api` returns content without calling `_record_cost`, so `api:` and `vertex:` calls are invisible to `get_cost_summary()`.

api-propagate-repairs-external-storage-c.text: `api.propagate()` recomputes truth values and repairs the store even when a node's stored `truth_value` was corrupted by direct `Storage` writes outside the API.

api-proposals-stage-in-separate-table-wi.text: Hive proposals are stored in a separate `proposals` table and `propose_*` functions do not mutate node truth values; truth changes occur only when an accepted proposal is applied.

api-propose-update-is-shared-by-cli-and-.text: Both the CLI and MCP front ends call `api.propose_update`, so a basis gate placed only in `cmd_propose_update` would not cover MCP clients.

api-py-is-1500-lines.text: The api.py module is approximately 1500 lines long.

api-py-is-public-programmatic-facade.text: `api.py` is the public programmatic facade; `cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, and `mind_service.py` are thin adapters over it.

api-repair-premises-is-the-dry-run-gate.text: Per `tests/test_repair_premises.py::test_dry_run_no_changes` and `::test_dry_run_no_repair_action`, `api.repair_premises(..., dry_run=True, ...)` must leave node text and `repair_action` metadata untouched, implying the `dry_run` gate lives in `reasons/api.py:repair_premises` (line 4347).

api-repair-premises-requires-review-file.text: Calling `api.repair_premises()` with neither argument raises `ValueError` with a message matching `"Either review_file or belief_ids"`.

api-report-gated-aggregates-four-signal-.text: `reasons/api.py:report_gated` gathers IN/OUT counts, retracted OUT premises, active gates from `list_gated`, and blocker dependent counts before delegating rendering to `reasons.report_gated.report_gated`.

api-report-gated-returns-fixed-shape.text: `api.report_gated` always returns a dict with exactly four keys: `report` (str), `blocker_count` (int), `gated_count` (int), `retracted_count` (int), even for an empty database.

api-requires-facade-justification.text: `reasons/api.py` does `from . import Justification`, so removing that symbol from `reasons/__init__.py` breaks `reasons.api` at import time.

api-research-is-api-repair-alias.text: `reasons.api.research` is the same function object as `reasons.api.repair`.

api-resolve-namespace-prefixes-only-unqu.text: `_resolve_namespace` only prefixes an ID when the namespace is truthy and the ID does not already contain `":"`, treating pre-namespaced IDs as cross-namespace references.

api-retract-already-out-returns-empty-ch.text: Calling `api.retract_node()` on an already-OUT node returns `changed: []` without raising an error.

api-retract-cascade-is-transitive.text: `api.retract_node()` propagates OUT to all transitively dependent SL-derived nodes, not just direct children — retracting a root premise retracts the entire downstream chain.

api-retract-cascade-symmetry.text: Retracting a root node and re-asserting it must produce identical `changed` sets, verified end-to-end by `TestEndToEnd.test_retract_and_restore_chain`.

api-retract-cascade-tested.text: Describes test coverage rather than an architectural invariant; the cascade behavior itself is already captured by retraction beliefs.

api-retrieval-functions-return-formatted.text: The retrieval functions `api.search`, `api.lookup`, and `api.compact` return human-readable markdown-formatted strings (not dicts), so callers and tests assert on substring presence/absence rather than structured field access.

api-review-beliefs-persists-review-metad.text: Successful API review calls write `reviewed_at` and `metadata.review_result` unless `dry_run=True`.

api-search-expands-by-one-hop.text: `search` expands results by one hop in the dependency graph (neighbors).

api-search-regex-bad-pattern-raises-valu.text: `api.search(..., regex=True)` compiles the query with Python `re` and raises `ValueError` for invalid regular expressions.

api-search-supports-three-output-formats.text: `search` supports three output formats: markdown, JSON, and minimal.

api-summarize-returns-over-key.text: `api.summarize` returns a dict containing `summary_id`, `truth_value`, and `over` keys.

api-summary-counts-classifications.text: The API summary reports `reviewed` as result count and maps `ANY`, `ALL`, and `MIXED` classifications to `convert_any`, `keep_all`, and `convert_mixed`.

api-superseded-nodes-excluded-from-gated.text: `list_gated()` omits nodes that have been superseded via `api.supersede()`, even if they still have active blockers — stale conclusions don't pollute the blocker view.

api-tests-black-box.text: Test methodology claim, not a behavioral invariant about the codebase. Developers learn this from reading the tests, not from a belief registry.

api-tests-cover-subset.text: Test coverage inventory, not a behavioral claim about the codebase. Coverage gaps are better tracked as project-level issues.

api-tests-one-class-per-function.text: Test organization pattern, not a code invariant — violating it wouldn't break functionality.

api-tests-use-fresh-sqlite-db-per-test.text: The API test suite uses a `db_path` pytest fixture that creates a fresh SQLite database in `tmp_path` for each test.

api-tests-use-isolated-temp-sqlite.text: `tests/test_api.py` gives each test a fresh SQLite database created via `api.init_db()` in pytest `tmp_path`.

api-tests-use-real-sqlite.text: All API tests run against a real SQLite database with FTS5; storage is never mocked, ensuring the API contract includes correct SQL and full-text search behavior.

api-topics-returns-sorted-topics-and-tot.text: `reasons.api.topics` returns a dictionary with `topics` sorted by frequency descending and a `total_nodes` count; an empty DB yields empty topics and zero nodes.

api-trace-access-tags-returns-structured.text: `api.trace_access_tags(node_id, db_path=...)` returns a dict with `node_id` and `access_tags` after enforcing `visible_to` visibility.

api-trace-assumptions-returns-premises-d.text: `reasons.api.trace_assumptions` returns a dict with `"node_id"` and a de-duplicated `"premises"` list.

api-unless-defaults-to-sl-type.text: `api.add_node(..., unless="y")` creates an `SL`-type node whose justification has `y` in its outlist, even when `sl` is omitted.

api-unless-param-maps-to-outlist.text: The `api.add_node(..., unless="y", sl="a")` keyword parameters map to `Justification(type="SL", antecedents=["a"], outlist=["y"])`; `unless` is syntactic sugar for the outlist and `sl` for the inlist/antecedents.

api-uses-lazy-imports.text: Heavy modules (`derive`, `compact`, `export_markdown`, `check_stale`, `import_beliefs`, `import_agent`) are imported inside function bodies in `api.py`, not at module level, to keep the module fast to import for callers that only need a subset of operations.

api-uses-with-network-context-manager.text: `api.py` uses a `_with_network` context manager to ensure load-operate-save atomicity for all network mutations.

api-verdict-applier-acts-only-on-confirm.text: The observed API verdict-application block branches only on `CONFIRMED` and `STALE`; `PARTIAL` and unknown strings are not action-triggering there.

api-verdict-applier-defaults-missing-to-.text: The API verdict applier defaults a missing `verdict` key to `INCONCLUSIVE`.

api-verify-consumer-handles-only-confirm.text: `reasons/api.py:3876-3878` branches only on `CONFIRMED` and `STALE`; no `PARTIAL` or unknown branch appears in the observed snippet.

api-with-network-is-class-context-manage.text: `_with_network` is implemented as a class with `__enter__` and `__exit__` rather than using `@contextmanager`, and it saves the network on clean exit only when `write=True`.

api-with-network-write-false-discards-ch.text: `_with_network(db_path, write=False)` loads the network but does not save on exit, so in-memory mutations are discarded.

apply-contradiction-plan-is-non-atomic.text: Each plan entry is applied by a separate `add_nogood` write transaction; a failure on entry *N* does not roll back entries *0…N‑1*.

apply-contradiction-plan-is-sqlite-only.text: Unlike most other `api.py` functions, this function has no `pg_conninfo` / `domain_id` parameters and therefore only works against SQLite.

apply-contradiction-plan-maps-to-add-nog.text: The function is a thin loop over `add_nogood`; it adds no validation, no filtering, and no idempotency checks beyond what the caller supplies.

apply-contradiction-plan-produces-backtr.text: Each successful result includes the premise actually retracted by `add_nogood`, or `None` when the claim set was not fully IN at apply time.

apply-contradiction-plan-requires-id-key.text: The exception handler formats errors with `entry['id']`, so a missing `"id"` raises an uncaught `KeyError` rather than being reported in `errors`.

apply-dedup-plan-collects-errors-not-rai.text: `apply_dedup_plan` collects errors into `result["errors"]` rather than raising, allowing partial application — one missing node does not block processing of the remaining dedup plan

apply-dedup-plan-reports-missing-nodes-a.text: api.apply_dedup_plan returns missing nodes as error strings in its result dict rather than raising exceptions.

apply-gate-proposals-adds-unless-outlist.text: When `apply_proposals` applies a `gate` proposal, its `unless` entries become the applied node’s outlist.

apply-marker-drives-contradiction-plan-i.text: Only headers matching `[APPLY]` case-sensitively contribute entries; `[SKIP]` and other casing are ignored.

apply-marker-drives-inclusion.text: Only headers ending in `[APPLY]` (case-sensitive) contribute entries; `[SKIP]` and any other casing are ignored, and a `SKIP` block's claims lines are also ignored.

apply-mode-writes-defeat-reason-type-met.text: With `dry_run=False`, the classifier result is persisted at `node["metadata"]["defeat_reason_type"]`.

apply-proposals-catches-per-proposal-exc.text: Any `Exception` raised while joining proposal fields or calling `api.add_node` is caught and converted to a string result for that proposal.

apply-proposals-comma-joins-antecedents-.text: `apply_proposals` serializes proposal antecedents and `unless` lists as comma-joined strings, so node IDs containing commas would corrupt justification serialization.

apply-proposals-converts-api-errors-to-r.text: `apply_proposals` catches exceptions from `api.add_node` per proposal and returns them as strings instead of raising.

apply-proposals-has-no-batch-rollback.text: It catches failures inside the loop and does not roll back earlier successful `api.add_node` calls if a later proposal fails.

apply-proposals-maps-mode-any-only-lower.text: `any_mode` is passed as true only when `p.get("mode")` equals the exact lowercase string `"any"`.

apply-proposals-requires-prior-validatio.text: `apply_proposals` trusts its input unconditionally; callers must run `validate_proposals` first to avoid database errors from missing antecedents or duplicate IDs.

apply-proposals-requires-unless-key.text: The function directly indexes `p["unless"]`, so a missing `unless` key causes a per-proposal `KeyError` result instead of defaulting to an empty list.

architecture-enforces-structural-and-ope.text: Architectural safety is enforced along two independent dimensions: structurally, the central network dependency is contained within clean three-layer boundaries preventing cross-layer corruption; operationally, every mutation path is atomic and isolated preventing within-layer partial state — neither dimension alone is sufficient, but together they eliminate both classes of corruption.

justifications.label: Structural containment (layer boundaries) and operational containment (atomic mutations) are orthogonal safety dimensions that together prevent all corruption vectors

architecture-has-no-hidden-fragility.text: The system's architectural safety is robust end-to-end: structural containment via clean layer boundaries and operational atomicity via context-managed mutations leave no hidden consistency hazards across the persistence boundary.

justifications.label: Architectural safety is robust only when no cross-layer denormalization hazard exists; the dependents index fragility would undermine the containment claim if it were active

architecture-is-self-contained-and-safel.text: The project is both externally self-contained (zero runtime dependencies at packaging and implementation levels) and internally well-structured (central network dependency safely contained within clean three-layer boundaries) — the architecture neither imports external risk nor allows internal complexity to leak across layers.

justifications.label: Connects external isolation (zero deps) with internal safety (contained central dependency) into a unified architectural self-containment claim; both unused as antecedents

architecture-sustains-consistent-lifecyc.text: Architectural safety (clean layer boundaries with atomic isolated mutations) sustains consistent lifecycle management across supported operations (conservative staleness detection for IN nodes with both source fields plus propagation lifecycle awareness); supported beliefs are managed consistently for those operations, backed by structural guarantees that lifecycle operations execute atomically and without cross-layer leakage, without claiming exhaustive coverage.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

architecture-sustains-gapless-lifecycle.text: Architectural safety (clean layer boundaries with atomic isolated mutations) sustains gapless lifecycle management (staleness detection plus propagation lifecycle awareness) — beliefs are correctly managed at every point in their lifecycle, backed by structural guarantees that lifecycle operations execute atomically and without cross-layer leakage.

justifications.label: architectural enforcement ensures lifecycle operations execute correctly and without gaps

ask-agentic-loop-is-bounded.text: The tool-call loop in `ask()` has a maximum iteration count; an LLM that perpetually requests more searches is terminated and the raw response is returned.

ask-always-returns-string.text: `ask()` returns a string on every code path — LLM response, raw search results, or fallback; it never raises an exception to the caller.

ask-catches-tool-exceptions-into-history.text: `tests/test_ask_mcp.py` asserts "MCP tool errors are captured in tool history, not raised," implying `ask()` wraps `bridge.call_tool` in a catch block (exact code not in observations)

ask-consumes-text-not-native-tool-calls.text: `reasons/ask.py:514` passes the raw model string to `extract_tool_call`, not a provider-native tool-call structure.

ask-degrades-across-all-external-depende.text: The ask module degrades gracefully across all three external dependencies: LLM binary (catches TimeoutExpired/RuntimeError, falls back to raw search), FTS5 index (self-healing derived index with substring fallback), and source chunks database (catches OperationalError/DatabaseError and returns empty results) — no single external system failure prevents useful query responses.

justifications.label: Extends existing LLM fault tolerance to cover all external dependency failure modes including source chunk database

ask-dual-empty-detection-coupled-to-sent.text: Dual mode detects TMS emptiness via `NO_BELIEFS_MSG` or the substring `"don't have enough beliefs"` and FTS emptiness via `answer_fts.startswith("No relevant documents")`, so changing those prompt/sentinel strings silently breaks dual short-circuiting.

ask-dual-mode-makes-three-llm-calls.text: Dual mode makes up to 3 LLM calls (1 TMS synthesis + 1 FTS RAG + 1 merge), short-circuiting to 2 if either retrieval path returns empty.

ask-dual-mode-requires-sources-db.text: In ask.py, dual mode requires a sources_db value and raises ValueError when dual=True is used without one.

ask-dual-mode-uses-three-llm-calls.text: In `dual=True` mode, `ask()` performs three LLM calls: one for the TMS leg, one for the FTS leg, and one merge call.

ask-dual-performs-three-sequential-llm-c.text: `ask(..., dual=True)` performs three sequential LLM calls: one for TMS beliefs, one for source documents, and one to merge the two answers.

ask-dual-requires-sources-db.text: Calling `ask(..., dual=True)` without providing a `sources_db` path raises `ValueError`.

ask-dual-short-circuits-if-either-path-e.text: `ask()` in dual mode short-circuits the merge step if either the TMS answer or the FTS RAG answer is empty.

ask-dual-timeout-is-per-call.text: `ask(..., dual=True, timeout=T)` forwards `T` unchanged to each of the TMS, FTS RAG, and merge `invoke_model` calls, so total wall-clock can reach N×T.

ask-empty-network-returns-no-beliefs-mes.text: When the belief network is empty or no beliefs match the query, `ask()` returns `NO_BELIEFS_MSG` rather than raising an exception.

ask-falls-back-to-raw-context-on-llm-err.text: Both `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and generic exceptions from `invoke_model` return `_beliefs_or_no_match(ctx)` instead of raising.

ask-falls-back-to-raw-search.text: When LLM synthesis fails for any reason (timeout, missing CLI, non-zero exit), `ask()` returns the raw FTS5 search results as fallback.

ask-final-round-omits-tool-schema.text: The final ask round uses `FINAL_ASK_PROMPT` with no tool definitions; if the model still emits a tool call, `ask` returns the fallback context instead of looping again.

ask-has-no-aggregate-deadline.text: Neither `ask()` nor any of its helpers constructs a shared deadline object; each stage starts with a fresh `timeout`, so per-stage multiplication is unavoidable without caller-side enforcement.

ask-has-tiered-query-modes.text: The ask module supports tiered query modes with graceful degradation: full LLM synthesis with a bounded 3-iteration tool loop, no-synth mode that bypasses the LLM entirely, and automatic fallback from LLM failure to raw FTS5 search results.

justifications.label: Three orphan premises describing independent query modes that together define ask's complete tiered execution model

ask-is-fault-tolerant-and-bounded.text: The ask module is fault-tolerant (always returns a string, catches LLM failures, falls back to raw FTS5 search) and execution-bounded (tool loop capped at 3 iterations), ensuring reliable bounded knowledge retrieval regardless of LLM availability.

justifications.label: Three independent safety properties (guaranteed return type, exception handling, iteration bound) form a complete reliability contract for the ask module

ask-last-iteration-structurally-forces-a.text: On the final iteration of the ask tool loop, the prompt switches to `FINAL_ASK_PROMPT` which omits the tool definitions section entirely, making it structurally impossible for the LLM to issue another tool call via the defined protocol.

ask-mcp-achieves-accurate-bounded-tool-u.text: MCP tool integration in ask() achieves both bounded safety (iteration caps, error tolerance, transport timeouts at two layers) and accurate tool discovery (catalog reflects current server capabilities rather than a stale snapshot).

justifications.label: Accurate tool catalog requires live refresh rather than connect-time snapshot

ask-mcp-dispatch-routes-by-tool-name.text: When the LLM returns an MCP tool call, `ask()` dispatches it to the matching bridge's `call_tool` method and feeds the returned result back into the tool history.

ask-mcp-dispatch-strips-tool-key.text: When dispatching an MCP tool call, `ask()` passes `bridge.call_tool(name, args)` with the parsed tool-call dict minus the `"tool"` key.

ask-mcp-errors-non-fatal.text: When an MCP bridge's `call_tool` raises an exception during the ask loop, `ask()` catches the error, feeds it back to the LLM as context, and continues the tool loop rather than propagating to the caller.

ask-mcp-integration-is-safely-bounded.text: MCP tool calls in `ask()` are both error-tolerant (exceptions caught and fed back as context for alternative tool selection) and iteration-bounded (5 tool-call rounds max), preventing both crashes from MCP server failures and runaway tool loops.

justifications.label: MCP errors caught + iteration cap independently bound MCP integration risk

ask-mcp-is-defense-in-depth-bounded.text: MCP-backed ask queries are bounded at two independent layers: application-level iteration caps with error-tolerant fallback at the ask layer, plus per-call and connection timeouts at the MCP bridge transport layer — no single timeout failure can cause unbounded execution.

justifications.label: Layered timeout enforcement across ask application and MCP bridge transport

ask-mcp-iteration-limit-is-five.text: When `mcp_servers` is non-empty, `ask()` allows up to 5 tool-call iterations before forcing a final LLM response (6 total invocations), compared to the lower limit without MCP servers.

ask-mcp-tool-use-has-current-catalog.text: Ask's MCP tool integration achieves full reliability — errors caught, iterations bounded — with the tool catalog always reflecting the MCP server's current capabilities rather than a stale connection-time snapshot.

justifications.label: Full MCP reliability requires fresh tool catalogs, not just error handling and iteration bounds

ask-natural-flag-strips-belief-metadata.text: When natural=True, ask.py uses the natural citation rule without belief IDs and calls _strip_belief_metadata to remove status, justification, and dependency lines from belief context.

ask-natural-mode-strips-belief-citations.text: With `natural=True`, both `_CITE_RULE_NATURAL` and `_strip_belief_metadata` remove belief IDs and structured metadata from the final answer, producing prose-only output.

ask-natural-mode-strips-metadata-and-cit.text: When `natural=True`, all belief metadata (`**Status:**`, `### ` headers, `**Source:**`) is stripped from the prompt context and the "Cite belief IDs" instruction is replaced with "plain natural language".

ask-never-raises-on-llm-failure.text: `ask()` catches `TimeoutExpired` and `RuntimeError` from `_invoke_claude()` and returns raw FTS5 search results instead of propagating the exception — the function guarantees a string return.

ask-no-synth-bypasses-llm.text: When `no_synth=True`, `ask()` returns raw `api.search()` results without invoking the Claude CLI.

ask-no-synth-returns-no-results-when-no-.text: In `no_synth=True` mode, `ask()` returns the string 'No results' when FTS5 finds no matches.

ask-pipeline-is-end-to-end-fault-toleran.text: Every failure mode in the ask pipeline—LLM timeout/crash, MCP bridge exception, synthesis failure—has an independent non-fatal fallback path that returns a useful result, guaranteeing the function never propagates an unhandled exception to the caller.

justifications.label: Each antecedent independently demonstrates a distinct fault-tolerance mechanism; any single one suffices to show the pipeline degrades gracefully for its class of failures (convergent evidence).
