card-type-is-eem.text: The frontmatter `type` field is always the literal string `"eem"`.

cascade-depth-does-not-validate-target-n.text: A missing `target_id` does not necessarily raise; it returns zero if unreachable or a positive depth if the ID appears in a dependents set without a node entry.

cascade-depth-ignores-justification-and-.text: `_cascade_depth` traverses only `net.nodes[current_id].dependents` and does not inspect justification types, truth values, or labels.

cascade-depth-is-computed-per-target.text: `_cascade_depth` (`reasons/api.py:737`) measures how far a target node sits from the retracted node, used to annotate cascade effects.

cascade-depth-is-operational.text: `_cascade_depth` is a BFS hop count from the just-changed node to each affected dependent, and is the sort key for every cascade report (`reasons/api.py:568–569`, `635–636`, `724–725`).

cascade-depth-is-operational-bfs-depth.text: `_cascade_depth` computes a BFS hop count over the dependents graph from the changed node to each affected node, and this operational depth is used to sort cascade reports.

cascade-depth-requires-root-node-exists.text: If `retracted_id` is absent from `net.nodes`, `_cascade_depth` raises `KeyError` on the first queue pop.

cascade-depth-returns-shortest-dependent.text: For reachable targets other than the root, `_cascade_depth` returns the number of `dependents` edges in the shortest BFS path.

cascade-depth-uses-bfs-shortest-path.text: The `_cascade_depth` function performs BFS through dependents edges to find the shortest path from a retracted node to a target.

cascade-depth-zero-is-ambiguous.text: `_cascade_depth` returns zero both when the target equals the start node and when no dependent path exists, so callers cannot distinguish root from unreachable by return value alone.

cascade-does-not-set-retracted-at.text: `retracted_at` is populated only on nodes the user directly retracted; cascade-affected dependents end up `OUT` with an empty `retracted_at`.

cascade-impact-not-computed-by-propose.text: `propose_updates()` never computes cascade impact; proposal Markdown shows “not computed” unless an external caller supplies cascade data.

cascade-is-computed-pre-accept.text: Cascade impact is produced at proposal-generation time via `what_if_retract` and rendered into the proposals markdown; acceptance itself is manual via suggested CLI commands.

cascade-item-text-truncated-to-80-chars.text: Every cascade listing entry slices `item["text"]` to `[:80]`, so long belief texts are silently clipped without an ellipsis marker.

cascade-none-renders-not-computed.text: When `cascade` is `None` (or `{}`), the output always contains `**Cascade impact:** not computed` rather than omitting the line.

cascade-rendering-is-action-dependent.text: RETRACT proposals with cascade data render "will go OUT" language (dependents are destroyed), while UPDATE proposals render "need re-review" language (dependents are invalidated, not retracted) — reflecting the semantic difference between the two actions.

cascade-reports-sort-by-cascade-depth.text: Cascade result lists are sorted by `(cascade_depth, id)`, so retracted/restored nodes are reported nearest-first from the triggering change.

cascades-produce-both-out-and-in-sets.text: `reasons/api.py:517-627` and `reasons/cli.py:114-115` split cascade results into `went_out` and `went_in`.

central-dependency-is-safely-contained.text: Despite `network.py` being imported by virtually every module in the codebase, the three-layer architecture with clean boundaries ensures this central coupling does not create cross-cutting mutation paths — layer separation contains the dependency's blast radius so that the hub topology does not compromise architectural integrity.

justifications.label: clean layer boundaries contain the impact of the central network dependency (depth-2 from depth-0 + depth-1, integrates orphaned base belief)

challenge-adds-to-target-metadata.text: The challenge method appends the new challenge ID to the target's metadata['challenges'] list.

challenge-converts-bare-premise-to-justi.text: Challenging a bare premise with no justifications converts it into a justified node with `SL(antecedents=[], outlist=[challenge_id])`.

challenge-converts-premises-to-justified.text: When a premise (node with no justifications) is challenged, it is converted to a justified node with an SL justification containing empty antecedents and the challenge in the outlist.

challenge-creates-counter-node.text: `Network.challenge(target, reason)` creates a `challenge-<target>` node with `truth_value == IN` and retracts the target, cascading to dependents.

challenge-defense-is-crash-safe.text: The dialectical challenge/defend system reaches correct truth states through recursive outlist injection evaluated by deterministic terminating propagation.

justifications.label: Challenge/defend creates new nodes and dependent relationships dynamically; if propagation crashes on a dangling dependent reference, dialectical operations could leave the network inconsistent

challenge-destroys-premise-identity.text: When a premise is challenged, it loses its defining characteristic: premise identity emerges from absence of justifications, but challenge adds a justification (converting the premise to a justified node), meaning the target's truth value becomes conditional on the challenge node being OUT rather than unconditionally held — challenge reclassifies the target in the node type system.

justifications.label: Challenge adds justifications (base) + premise identity is absence of justifications (depth-1) together reveal that challenge is a type-level transformation, not just a truth-value change

challenge-id-auto-generation.text: Auto-generated challenge IDs follow the pattern `challenge-{target}`, then `challenge-{target}-2`, `-3`, etc.; explicit IDs that collide raise `ValueError` rather than auto-deduplicating.

challenge-id-collisions-get-numeric-suff.text: A second call to `challenge(target)` with the same target produces `challenge-<target>-2`, not an error and not an overwrite.

challenge-implements-outlist-defeat.text: Dialectical challenges are modeled by appending the challenge's node ID to the target's justification `outlist`, so retracting the challenge automatically restores the target (`reasons/api.py:1331-1394`, `tests/test_dialectical.py:test_dismiss_challenge_restores_target`).

challenge-is-outlist-injection.text: The challenge mechanism creates a new premise node and adds it to the target's outlist; all truth-value changes flow through normal BFS propagation, not direct mutation

challenge-modifies-all-justifications.text: When the target has multiple justifications, the challenge node is added to the outlist of every justification, ensuring no single justification can independently keep the target IN.

challenge-node-creation-is-duplicate.text: This is already covered by existing `challenge-is-outlist-injection` and first-class-node beliefs.

challenge-node-is-premise.text: The challenge node itself is always created as a premise (no justifications, IN by default) and can only be driven OUT by explicit retraction or by being challenged/defended.

challenge-premise-starts-in-and-defeats-.text: A challenge creates a new premise node that starts IN, and adding it to the target's outlist makes the target go OUT until defended.

challenge-propagation-is-automatic.text: After creating the challenge, truth value recomputation and BFS propagation through dependents happen within the same call; callers never need to trigger propagation manually.

challenge-records-target-and-back-refere.text: Challenge creation records `challenge_target` on the challenge node and back-references the challenge in the target node's metadata under `challenges`.

challenge-registers-dependency.text: After a challenge, the challenge node's dependents set includes the target_id so the target gets recomputed when the challenge changes.

challenge-returns-dict-with-challenge-id.text: `Network.challenge` is contractually required to return `{"challenge_id": ..., "changed": [...]}`, and `"changed"` includes every node whose truth value was affected, including cascaded dependents.

challenge-uses-outlist-mechanism.text: `challenge` works by creating an IN premise node and adding it to the target's outlist in every justification, reusing the same non-monotonic mechanism as `supersede`.

change-event-has-db-path-only.text: `ChangeEvent.db_path: str` (reasons/pubsub.py:22) is the sole location field; there is no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` field, so subscribers are partitioned by filesystem path.

change-event-has-no-cause-metadata.text: `ChangeEvent` carries only `type`, `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, `db_path`; cause and cascade-root information is explicitly absent by design.

change-event-is-frozen-dataclass.text: `ChangeEvent` is an immutable frozen dataclass with fields `type`, `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `db_path`.

change-event-keyed-by-db-path.text: `ChangeEvent` has a required `db_path` field and no `pg_conninfo` or `domain_id` field; subscriber registration is likewise keyed by `db_path`, tying pub/sub to the file-backed storage model.

change-event-uses-none-for-absent-state.text: `ChangeEvent` encodes absent state as `None`: new nodes have `old_truth_value=None`, and deleted nodes have `new_truth_value=None`.

change-events-are-snapshot-diffs.text: `compute_changes` in `reasons/pubsub.py:96` derives events by diffing truth-value snapshots rather than observing the propagator.

change-events-carry-no-causality.text: `ChangeEvent`s carry old/new truth values and `db_path` but not cause or cascade-root information.

changeevent-uses-none-for-absent-state.text: New nodes have `old_truth_value=None`; deleted nodes have `new_truth_value=None`.

changelog-documents-reasons-lib-api-as-p.text: `CHANGELOG.md:136` records `reasons_lib.api` as a Python API layer returning dicts for CLI and tool-call consumers.

changelog-follows-keep-a-changelog-1-1-0.text: CHANGELOG.md follows the Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 convention with version headers and Added/Fixed/Changed sections.

changelog-has-missing-and-folded-version.text: `CHANGELOG.md` has no `0.11.0` heading, and `0.8.0`/`0.9.0` appear only as inline version tags inside `0.10.0` bullets.

changelog-has-no-code-consumers.text: `CHANGELOG.md` is Markdown with no imports and nothing in `reasons/`, `reasons_lib/`, or `tests/` reads it.

changelog-has-no-reasons-lib-removal-tim.text: The only `reasons_lib` mention in `CHANGELOG.md` is line 136 (0.1.0 origin note); there is no "Deprecated" or "Removed" entry with a timeline.

changelog-has-no-unreleased-section.text: The changelog keeps no `[Unreleased]` block; in-progress work is tracked in `.forge/` instead.

changelog-header-format-is-parsed-by-too.text: Changelog version headers use exact `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` format because wiki/Forge tooling parses them.

changelog-is-reverse-chronological.text: Entries run from `[0.18.0] - 2026-04-25` at the top down to `[0.1.0] - 2026-03-23` at the bottom.

changelog-is-stale-after-0-18.text: `pyproject.toml` version is `0.58.0` while `CHANGELOG.md` ends at `0.18.0`, leaving 40 minor releases undocumented.

changelog-lacks-reasons-lib-shim-depreca.text: `CHANGELOG.md:136` mentions `reasons_lib.api` only as an added API layer; no changelog entry documents the shim or a deprecation policy.

changelog-lags-package-version.text: `CHANGELOG.md` is significantly behind the version declared in `pyproject.toml`, leaving recent releases undocumented.

changelog-mentions-reasons-lib-only-hist.text: `CHANGELOG.md:136` mentions `reasons_lib.api` only in the `0.1.0` entry; later changelog entries do not mention `reasons_lib`.

changelog-omits-reasons-lib-rename.text: `CHANGELOG.md` references `reasons_lib.api` only at v0.1.0 and records `rms`→`reasons` at v0.3.0, but never documents the `reasons_lib` → `reasons` module rename.

changelog-records-reasons-lib-api-as-pyt.text: `CHANGELOG.md` records `reasons_lib.api` historically as a Python API layer returning dicts for CLI and tool-call consumers.

changelog-records-rms-to-reasons-rename.text: `CHANGELOG.md` records a historical rename from `rms` to `reasons` for the CLI, library, and package name.

changelog-rename-explains-reasons-lib-an.text: The `0.3.0` changelog entry records a rename from `rms` to `reasons`, explaining the `reasons_lib` library path and `ftl-reasons` PyPI package name.

changelog-top-version-must-match-pyproje.text: The top `## [x.y.z]` changelog header is expected to equal `pyproject.toml`'s `[project].version`.

changelog-tracks-reasons-lib-shim-migrat.text: CHANGELOG.md lacks a deprecation or migration entry for the `reasons_lib` shim.

changelog-uses-issue-and-pr-references.text: Fixed/feature bullets carry `(#N)` or `(#N, PR #M)` markers (e.g., `(#16, PR #17)`, `(#11, PR #14)`) linking entries to GitHub work items.

changelog-uses-only-three-change-categor.text: `CHANGELOG.md` uses only `Added`, `Changed`, and `Fixed` categories; `Deprecated`, `Removed`, and `Security` never appear.

check-integrity-filters-finding-types.text: Only findings whose `type` is `"text_mutation"` or `"chain_mutation"` are returned; any other finding type from `verify_all` is silently dropped.

check-integrity-findings-have-only-text-.text: `api.check_integrity` partitions Merkle results only into `text_mutations` and `chain_mutations`; there is no structural `cycle` finding category.

check-integrity-is-read-only.text: The function opens the network with `_with_network(db_path, write=False)`, so it never calls `Storage.save()` and never publishes pubsub events.

check-integrity-is-sqlite-only.text: `check_integrity` takes no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` parameters and supports only the SQLite backend.

check-integrity-maps-findings-to-two-key.text: `api.check_integrity` exposes only `text_mutations` and `chain_mutations`, so a new structural cycle finding would require API/CLI changes (`reasons/api.py:2736-2740`).

check-integrity-requires-merkle-module.text: `check_integrity` imports `reasons.merkle.verify_all` lazily inside its body, so a missing `merkle` module surfaces as `ImportError` only when the function is called.

check-integrity-returns-result-dict-not-.text: For the corruption and cycle cases covered here, `api.check_integrity()` returns a dict and tests assert on `text_mutations`, `chain_mutations`, and `missing_hashes` rather than expecting exceptions.

check-integrity-reuses-network-cache.text: A matching `(db_path, mtime)` in `_network_cache` causes the function to verify the cached `Network` without re-reading the SQLite file.

check-integrity-routes-through-canonical.text: The integrity-check API imports `verify_all` and `backfill_hashes` from the canonical `.merkle` module.

check-integrity-unsupported-for-postgres.text: Unlike most sibling API functions, `check_integrity` takes no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` and only supports the SQLite backend.

check-stale-and-hash-sources-mutate-in-p.text: Both `check_stale` (with `upgrade_hashes=True`) and `hash_sources` modify `node.source_hash` directly on the Network object; neither persists — the caller must save.

check-stale-api-delegates-to-check-stale.text: `api.check_stale` delegates the staleness algorithm to `reasons.check_stale.check_stale` and only orchestrates network lifecycle and result reshaping.

check-stale-auto-bumps-pinned-sha-on-con.text: In git-aware mode, `check_stale` auto-bumps `pinned_sha` to the new HEAD when the file content hash is unchanged despite intervening commits, preserving `pinned_lines`.

check-stale-checked-count-is-eligibility.text: `checked` counts IN nodes that have both `source` and `source_hash`, not the number of files actually opened.

check-stale-classifies-content-changed-a.text: check_stale categorizes results as content_changed when the hash differs and source_deleted when the resolved path is missing.

check-stale-content-changed-populates-so.text: A `content_changed` result from `check_stale` includes the resolved filesystem path in its `source_path` field.

check-stale-content-unchanged-commit-mov.text: If file content is unchanged but `get_file_commit_sha` differs from `pinned_sha`, `check_stale` updates `pinned_sha` and `verified_at` and increments `sha_bumped`.

check-stale-delegates-to-check-stale-mod.text: The staleness algorithm lives in `reasons/check_stale.py`; `api.check_stale` only orchestrates lifecycle and reshaping.

check-stale-detects-source-staleness-onl.text: `check-stale` detects source staleness (source file changed on disk) via hash comparison but cannot detect world staleness (the belief is outdated even though the source file hasn't changed) — beliefs can silently decay without any artifact triggering re-examination.

check-stale-empty-file-with-matching-has.text: An existing empty source file whose hash matches the node's `source_hash` is treated as fresh and produces no staleness result.

check-stale-existing-empty-file-is-not-d.text: An existing zero-byte source file is not reported as `source_deleted`; it is fresh if its hash matches and `content_changed` if the hash differs.

check-stale-exits-nonzero.text: `cmd_check_stale` calls `sys.exit(1)` when any stale nodes are found, making it usable as a CI or pre-commit gate.

check-stale-exits-nonzero-on-stale.text: `cmd_check_stale` calls `sys.exit(1)` when stale nodes are found (even on success), making the command usable as a CI or pre-commit gate.

check-stale-exits-nonzero-on-stale-nodes.text: Unlike the general error-to-exit-1 convention, `cmd_check_stale` deliberately exits 1 when any source is stale or deleted, enabling CI freshness gates.

check-stale-falls-back-to-net-repos.text: When `repos` is `None`, the function uses `net.repos` (the persisted repo map); passing an explicit dict overrides it.

check-stale-get-file-commit-sha-timeout-.text: Unlike the `*_changed_since` helpers, `get_file_commit_sha` has no `TimeoutExpired` handling, so a hung git call can propagate out of `check_stale`.

check-stale-is-read-only.text: `check_stale` never mutates the network; it returns a list of stale-node dicts and leaves all nodes unchanged — staleness detection is separated from staleness resolution.

check-stale-keeps-source-and-agent-separ.text: `check_stale` accepts `source: str` and `agent: str | None` as separate parameters.

check-stale-mutates-in-place-caller-pers.text: `check_stale`, `hash_sources`, and all `pin_*` functions mutate `Node.source_hash` and/or `Node.metadata` in place; callers are responsible for saving the network.

check-stale-mutates-network-in-place.text: `check_stale`, `hash_sources`, and all `pin_*` functions write to `node.source_hash` / `node.metadata` directly; the caller must persist the network.

check-stale-never-raises-on-missing-file.text: `check_stale()` returns a structured `source_deleted` dict for nodes whose source files don't exist on disk; it never raises `FileNotFoundError` or any exception.

check-stale-no-dedup-by-source-path.text: Multiple nodes referencing the same missing source file each produce independent `source_deleted` results — no deduplication by file path.

check-stale-operates-per-node-not-per-fi.text: Multiple nodes pointing to the same source file each receive their own independent result entry in the returned list; the function iterates nodes, not files.

check-stale-output-is-deterministic-and-.text: Staleness checking produces deterministic (sorted by node ID), uniformly structured (consistent 6-key schema across all result types), and exception-free (returns structured dicts for missing files rather than raising) output suitable for programmatic consumption and diffing.

justifications.label: Three output-shape guarantees unify into a programmatic consumption contract

check-stale-pg-dispatch-bypasses-sqlite-.text: If `pg_conninfo` is truthy, the function returns via `_pg_dispatch` and never touches `_with_network` or the local `check_stale` module.

check-stale-pinned-lines-unchanged-skips.text: When pinned lines are unchanged, `check_stale` continues without emitting a stale result, even if it updates the pinned SHA.

check-stale-processes-only-in-nodes.text: `check_stale` and `pin_sources` skip any node whose `truth_value` is not `"IN"`.

check-stale-propagates-errors-without-ca.text: `api.check_stale` has no `try/except`, so path, database, and delegate exceptions propagate to the caller rather than being converted into result dicts.

check-stale-propagates-file-read-errors.text: File read errors from hash_file, such as OSError or PermissionError, are not caught by check_stale and propagate to the caller.

metadata.retract_reason: Stale duplicate of check-stale-is-read-only; also contradicted by check-stale-and-hash-sources-mutate-in-place (issue #101)

check-stale-reports-content-changed-and-.text: check_stale returns problem records with one of two reason values: content_changed when the file hash differs, or source_deleted when the resolved file path no longer exists.

check-stale-reports-content-changed-with.text: When a source file changes, `check_stale()` reports a result with `reason='content_changed'` and includes the old and new hashes.

check-stale-reports-missing-sources-as-s.text: `check_stale()` returns `reason="source_deleted"` for IN nodes whose source path resolves to `None`.

check-stale-repos-none-still-detects-sou.text: When `check_stale` is called with `repos=None`, a missing source file still produces a `source_deleted` result.

check-stale-requires-both-source-fields.text: A node must have both `source` (non-empty) and `source_hash` (non-empty) to be eligible for staleness checking; nodes missing either field are silently skipped.

check-stale-requires-in-source-and-hash.text: `check_stale` only examines nodes that are IN, have a non-empty `source`, and have a non-empty `source_hash`.

check-stale-result-schema-is-exact.text: Every result dict must contain exactly `node_id`, `old_hash`, `new_hash`, `source`, `source_path`, and `reason`.

check-stale-result-schema-uniform.text: All `check_stale` result dicts share the same 6-key schema (`node_id`, `old_hash`, `new_hash`, `source`, `source_path`, `reason`) regardless of reason type, so consumers can iterate results without type-checking.

check-stale-results-sorted-by-node-id.text: The list returned by `check_stale` is sorted ascending by `node_id`, providing deterministic output for consumers.

check-stale-returns-result-list-and-upgr.text: `check_stale(net, ...)` returns a tuple whose first element is the list of stale-result dicts and whose second element is the upgraded-hash count.

check-stale-returns-upgraded-and-sha-bum.text: `check_stale` returns a 3-tuple `(results, upgraded_count, sha_bumped_count)`, where the counts track in-place hash upgrades and pinned-SHA updates.

check-stale-skip-rules-precede-file-exis.text: Retraction, missing `source`, missing `source_hash`, and empty-string `source` all suppress results even when the referenced file is also missing on disk; the eligibility check precedes the filesystem existence check.

check-stale-skips-nodes-without-source-a.text: check_stale silently skips nodes that do not have both source and source_hash set, emitting no error or report entry.

check-stale-skips-non-in-nodes.text: Only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` are considered; all other nodes are silently excluded from both `results` and the counts.

check-stale-skips-out-nodes.text: Only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` are checked for staleness; retracted (OUT) nodes are ignored even if their source file has changed.

check-stale-source-deleted-returns-none-.text: When a source file is missing, `check_stale` returns a result dict with `reason="source_deleted"`, `new_hash=None`, and `source_path=None` (fix for issue #25 — previously this case was silently skipped).

check-stale-upgrade-hashes-excludes-upgr.text: When upgrade_hashes=True, check_stale silently upgrades matching truncated hashes in place on the node and excludes them from stale results.

chunks-fts-requires-refresh-via-rebuild-.text: The observed tests refresh `chunks_fts` either with `INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts) VALUES('rebuild')` or by direct `chunks_fts(rowid, text)` inserts, and no triggers are observed.

classify-defeat-reason-is-not-used-insid.text: `classify_defeat_reason` is not called within `reasons/review.py`; it is exported for external callers that build structured defeaters.

classify-defeat-reason-non-string-return.text: The `.strip().lower()` normalization in `classify_defeat_reason` is outside the `try`, so a non-string `invoke_model` return raises `AttributeError` to the caller.

classify-defeat-reason-returns-empty-str.text: `classify_defeat_reason` never raises; every failure path (binary not found, subprocess exception, unparseable LLM output) returns the empty string `""`, allowing callers to distinguish "no classification" from an exception.

classify-defeat-reason-substring-fallbac.text: When the LLM output contains multiple canonical defeat types, `classify_defeat_reason` returns the first type in `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` declaration order, not necessarily the model’s intended answer.

classify-defeat-reason-types-dangling-de.text: If a defeater's `defeats_node` points to a missing node, `classify_defeat_reason_types` passes an empty defeated text to the LLM and records no error for the dangling reference.

classify-defeat-reason-types-dry-run-wri.text: With `dry_run=True`, classifications appear in the result but the defeater's `metadata["defeat_reason_type"]` remains absent (`test_dry_run_classifies_without_writing`)

classify-defeaters-defaults-to-dry-run-w.text: `cmd_classify_defeaters` sets `dry_run = not args.apply`, so omitting `--apply` runs in dry-run mode.

classify-defeaters-rejects-pg-backend-be.text: `cmd_classify_defeaters` prints an error to stderr and exits with status 1 before calling the API if `--pg` or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` is truthy.

claude-child-env-strips-claudecode.text: Before invoking the `claude` CLI, `invoke_model` removes `CLAUDECODE` from the child environment while preserving other environment variables such as `HOME`.

claude-md-is-auto-loaded-agent-context.text: `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root is an informational Claude Code memory file auto-loaded into agent context; it is not imported or executed by the Python package.

claude-md-lists-a-curated-subset-of-modu.text: The Project Structure and Commands sections document roughly half of the ~34 modules in `reasons/`, so both lists must be verified against the tree rather than trusted as complete.

cleanup-order-respects-foreign-keys.text: The teardown `DELETE` loop orders tables leaves-first (`rms_propagation_log`, `rms_justifications`, `rms_nogoods`, `rms_network_meta`, `rms_nodes`) to satisfy foreign-key constraints.

clear-network-cache-does-not-touch-stora.text: The function performs no database or filesystem I/O and does not save or close any `Network`.

clearing-retracted-flag-restores-propaga.text: Removing `_retracted` via the import/API paths makes the node eligible for normal recomputation and cascade again.

cli-api-key-documents-env-default.text: The CLI documents `MIND_API_KEY` as the default environment source for `--api-key`.

cli-auto-retract-sets-invalid-derived-no.text: `review-beliefs --auto-retract` changes invalid reviewed beliefs to `truth_value="OUT"`, while `--dry-run` prevents the mutation.

cli-backends-lack-native-tool-flags.text: `resolve_model_cmd` constructs `claude`, `gemini`, and `ollama` invocations without any native tool/MCP flags.

cli-backends-lack-native-tool-surface.text: `resolve_model_cmd` and the CLI branch of `invoke_model` pass only a prompt on stdin and parse stdout, with no CLI flag in the codebase that selects native tools.

cli-catches-permission-error-for-named-r.text: CLI commands catch `PermissionError` from named retrieval operations and convert it into a user-facing error.

cli-db-flag-defaults-to-api-default-db.text: Every CLI subcommand accepts a --db flag defaulting to api.DEFAULT_DB.

cli-deprecations-unrelated-to-reasons-li.text: The observed `deprecated` strings in CLI/API code concern `--domain-id` and `research`/`repair` aliases, not the `reasons_lib` package shim.

cli-dispatch-is-flat-dict-lookup.text: CLI dispatch uses a flat `commands` dict mapping subcommand strings to `cmd_*` handler functions — no plugin system or subclass hierarchy.

cli-entrypoints-use-reasons-package.text: `pyproject.toml` maps `reasons` and `reasons-mcp` to `reasons.cli:main` and `reasons.mcp_server:main`, not to `reasons_lib`.

cli-exit-1-on-error.text: All CLI error paths catch specific exceptions from the API (`KeyError`, `ValueError`, `PermissionError`, `FileNotFoundError`), print to stderr, and call `sys.exit(1)`.

cli-exit-code-contract-is-binary.text: Every CLI subcommand returns exit code 0 for success and 1 for any user-facing error; no other exit codes are used or tested.

cli-exit-code-contract-zero-or-one.text: Every CLI command returns exit code 0 on success and 1 on error; no other exit codes are used across the entire test suite (~90 tests).

cli-exit-code-zero-success-one-error.text: All CLI subcommands use exit code 0 for success and exit code 1 for every error condition (missing nodes, access denied, duplicate IDs, file not found); no other exit codes appear in the test suite.

cli-explain-shows-failed-antecedents-and.text: The CLI `explain` command displays failed antecedents and violated outlists.

cli-flags-override-env-vars.text: `_backend_kwargs` gives precedence to CLI `--pg`/`--project-id` flags over `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`/`REASONS_PROJECT_ID` environment variables when both are present

cli-flags-take-precedence-over-env-vars.text: `_backend_kwargs` resolves the storage backend with CLI flags (`--pg`, `--domain-id`) overriding environment variables (`REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`, `REASONS_PROJECT_ID`); when neither is set, SQLite is the default.

cli-global-db-option-precedes-subcommand.text: The CLI accepts `--db` as a global option before the subcommand, e.g. `reasons --db <path> topics ...`.

cli-global-options-must-precede-subcomma.text: Because global flags are declared on the root parser, they must appear before the subcommand; `reasons --db foo status` works but `reasons status --db foo` generally does not.

cli-handlers-are-api-facade-except-deriv.text: CLI subcommand handlers act as thin facades over `reasons.api`, with `cmd_derive` as the only handler containing real orchestration.

cli-handlers-are-thin-api-wrappers.text: Every `cmd_*` function other than `_derive_one_round` (and its helpers) performs exactly one `reasons.api` call followed by dict-formatted `stdout` output.

cli-has-35-subcommands.text: The CLI entry point (reasons command) exposes 35+ subcommands.

cli-has-no-direct-callback-handling.text: `reasons/cli.py` has zero matches for callback or token/chunk streaming terms in the supplied observations.

cli-help-advertises-cache-path.text: The `--token` help text at `reasons/cli.py:3457,3464,3469` explicitly documents `~/.cache/huggingface/token` as the fallback.

cli-help-documents-token-cache-path.text: The CLI `--token` help text explicitly documents `~/.cache/huggingface/token` as the fallback token location.

cli-idempotent-operations-report-already.text: The CLI reports `already OUT` when retracting an already-OUT node and `already IN` when asserting an already-IN node.

cli-idempotent-retract-assert-return-zer.text: `retract` on an already-OUT node and `assert` on an already-IN node both return exit code 0 with informational messages rather than an error.

cli-idempotent-transitions-are-success.text: Retracting an already-OUT node or asserting an already-IN node exits `0` and prints `"already OUT"` or `"already IN"` respectively.

cli-init-requires-force-to-overwrite.text: A second `init` without `--force` exits `1` and writes stderr containing `"--force"`.

cli-init-requires-force-to-overwrite-db.text: The CLI `init` command refuses to overwrite an existing database unless `--force` is supplied.

cli-is-deterministic-and-stream-correct.text: The CLI achieves full scriptability through three deterministic properties: flat dict dispatch with no dynamic plugin resolution, binary exit codes (0 success, 1 error) with no ambiguous intermediate codes, and clean stream separation (diagnostics to stderr, results to stdout)

justifications.label: Three independent CLI interface properties — dispatch determinism, exit code simplicity, and stream correctness — combine into full scriptability: shell scripts can dispatch, check status, and parse output without heuristics

cli-is-entry-point.text: `cli.py` is the only declared entry point for the project.

cli-is-pure-delegation-layer.text: The CLI is a pure delegation layer: every handler dispatches through a flat dict lookup to API functions with no business logic, producing binary exit codes and correct stream separation — a complete separation of formatting from computation.

justifications.label: Pure delegation holds for all handlers except cmd_propagate, which bypasses the API and goes directly to Storage/Network

cli-is-pure-formatter.text: Every cmd_* function delegates to api.* and only formats the returned dict for terminal output; no business logic lives in the CLI layer.

cli-is-thin-over-tms-engine.text: `reasons/cli.py` maps each TMS command to network/storage API calls; command logic delegates to the engine rather than implementing truth propagation itself.

cli-is-verified-end-to-end.text: The CLI is verified through hermetic end-to-end integration tests (isolated databases per test, full argv-parsing pipeline, deterministic stream-correct output) — unless cmd_propagate bypasses the API layer, leaving one code path's safety guarantees unverifiable through the standard integration testing harness.

justifications.label: Deterministic CLI behavior (depth-1) combined with hermetic test isolation (depth-0) provides end-to-end verification — except for the one handler that skips the API layer entirely

cli-is-verified-pure-delegation.text: The CLI is both structurally pure (every handler delegates to API functions with no business logic) and end-to-end verified (hermetic integration tests confirm delegation produces correct output through the full argv-parsing pipeline).

justifications.label: Structural purity guarantees the CLI adds no behavior; verification confirms this guarantee holds in practice — together they establish the CLI as a trustworthy transparent interface layer.

cli-json-parse-fails-open.text: `_parse_cli_json` returns raw output on any JSON parse failure, ensuring callers always receive a string response.

cli-main-does-not-catch-handler-exceptio.text: `main` does not wrap the `cmd_*` dispatch in try/except, so uncaught handler exceptions propagate as tracebacks and exit code 1.

cli-multi-premise-warning-is-suppressed-.text: `_warn_multi_premise` prints only when `premise_count >= 3` and `any_mode` is false.

cli-no-op-cases-exit-zero.text: No-op cases such as already OUT, already IN, no nodes, and no matching nodes print informative messages and return exit code 0 rather than raising errors.

cli-no-subcommand-prints-help-and-exits-.text: When `reasons` is invoked without a subcommand, `main` prints help to stdout and calls `sys.exit(1)`.

cli-output-is-plain-text-not-json.text: CLI command handlers format returned result dicts as plain text for terminal output rather than JSON.

cli-parse-visible-to-returns-none-when-a.text: _parse_visible_to returns None rather than an empty list when --visible-to is absent, and the API layer interprets None as no access control.

cli-parser-and-dispatch-table-are-parall.text: The argparse subcommand registrations and the `commands` dispatch dict are maintained manually in parallel; an out-of-sync command causes `KeyError` at dispatch or dead parser code.

cli-path-requires-shutil-which.text: `reasons.llm.invoke_model` calls `shutil.which(binary)` (line 297) before `subprocess.run` (line 302) only for CLI models; `api:`, `vertex:`, and `openai:` prefixes bypass both.

cli-permission-errors-are-formatted-inli.text: `reasons/cli.py` handles `PermissionError` inline in each command handler with direct `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` calls; there is no shared permission-error formatting helper.

cli-plan-review-apply-pattern.text: Several commands (`derive`, `deduplicate`, `contradictions`) follow a three-phase workflow: (1) generate proposals to a file, (2) human reviews/edits the file, (3) `--accept FILE` parses and applies the reviewed plan — with `--auto` collapsing all three phases

cli-prints-access-denied-to-stderr.text: CLI handlers catch `PermissionError` and print an `Access denied: {e}` message to stderr.

cli-project-id-is-documented-deprecated-.text: `--project-id` is an argparse option whose help text calls it a deprecated alias for `--domain-id` at `reasons/cli.py:3064`.

cli-propose-update-routes-through-api-pr.text: The `propose-update` CLI handler does not call the library `propose_updates` directly; it calls `api.propose_update`.

cli-read-commands-enforce-visible-to.text: The `status`, `show`, `explain`, `trace`, and `trace-access-tags` CLI commands enforce `--visible-to`; denied reads exit `1` with `"Access denied"`.

cli-remove-justification-tested-via-subp.text: the CLI test invokes `uv run reasons ... remove-justification <node> <index>` and asserts stdout contains `"Removed justification 0"`.

cli-report-gated-splits-report-and-summa.text: The default CLI writes the Markdown report to stdout and a `blocker(s)` summary to stderr.

cli-report-timestamps-strip-colons.text: Report files written by the CLI use ISO timestamps with colons stripped (for example `T105808`) for filesystem safety.

cli-research-is-documented-deprecated-al.text: `research` is a subparser labeled “Alias for 'repair' (deprecated)” at `reasons/cli.py:3854`, with arguments duplicated from `repair`.

cli-resets-cost-tracker-at-command-entry.text: Observed CLI command entry points import `reset_cost_tracker` and call it immediately so previous invocations’ costs do not accumulate.

cli-resolver-rejects-api-vertex-prefixes.text: `resolve_model_cmd` handles only CLI backends and raises `ValueError` for `api:`/`vertex:` model strings, naming both API prefixes in the error.

cli-runner-catches-systemexit.text: `run_cli` catches `SystemExit` from `reasons.cli.main` and returns its exit code with captured stdout/stderr.

cli-search-sources-supports-text-and-jso.text: `cmd_search_sources` emits either text or JSON depending on `args.format`.

cli-search-sources-text-reports-no-match.text: In text mode, zero results print a message containing `"No matching chunks"`.

cli-show-omits-source-type-line-when-abs.text: `cmd_show` omits the `Source type:` line when the node has no `source_type` metadata.

cli-sqlite-only-commands-exist.text: Commands `derive`, `ask`, `review-beliefs`, `deduplicate`, and `contradictions` are guarded by `_require_sqlite()` and exit with an error if `--pg` is set — they do not support PostgreSQL

cli-sqlite-only-commands-guard-before-ap.text: CLI commands marked SQLite-only call `_require_sqlite` and exit with status 1 before any API call when PostgreSQL is configured.

cli-stream-discipline-separates-payload-.text: CLI user payload is written to `stdout`, while diagnostics, warnings, progress, and cost summaries go to `stderr` so commands remain pipeable.

cli-subparser-handler-parity-lacks-struc.text: `tests/test_cli.py` exercises CLI commands through `main()` but does not structurally compare `sub.add_parser` names with keys of the `commands` dispatch dict.

cli-summary-includes-total-nodes.text: The summary line at `reasons/cli.py:2317` appends `{result['total_nodes']} nodes`, producing output like `N topics from M nodes`.

cli-tests-are-black-box-integration.text: All CLI tests invoke `main()` through the full argv-parsing pipeline via the `run_cli` harness rather than calling internal APIs, with one exception (`TestPropagateWithChanges` directly mutates storage to create inconsistent state).

cli-tests-cover-commands-readme-omits.text: `tests/test_cli.py` exercises `what-if`, `supersede`, `check-integrity`, `backfill-hashes`, `convert-to-premise`, `add-repo`/`repos`, `import-json`, `summarize`, `import-agent`/`sync-agent`/`namespaces`, `deduplicate`, `derive`, `accept`, `lookup`, `trace-access-tags`, the full `propose-*`/`accept-proposal`/`reject-proposal`/`withdraw-proposal`/`propose-nogood`/`propose-update` family, and `--format names-only`, none of which appear in `README.md`.

cli-tests-exercise-commands-through-main.text: `tests/test_cli.py` invokes `main()` by patching `sys.argv`, not by checking parser-to-handler registration.

cli-tests-patch-sys-argv-not-subprocess.text: CLI integration tests simulate invocations by patching `sys.argv`, `sys.stdout`, and `sys.stderr` in-process (capturing `SystemExit`), testing only the Python entry point and not the installed script's shebang or shell integration.

cli-tests-set-up-networks-via-chained-cl.text: CLI tests build belief networks by sequentially calling `run_cli("init", ...)`, `run_cli("add", ...)`, and similar commands rather than constructing synthetic database states.

cli-tests-treat-human-readable-output-as.text: CLI tests assert on human-readable output substrings such as `Added a [IN]`, `Went OUT`, and `already IN`, treating CLI output copy as part of the tested API.

cli-tests-use-real-temporary-sqlite-db.text: Every DB-backed test uses a real SQLite file under pytest’s `tmp_path`, created either by `run_cli("init")` or by `TestProposalLifecycle`’s fixture.

cli-threads-db-path-through-api.text: Every CLI command handler threads args.db through to the API, with args.db defaulting to api.DEFAULT_DB.

cli-to-propose-updates-requires-api-laye.text: The `propose-update` CLI command does not call `propose_updates` directly; it goes through `api.propose_update` (imported as `_propose` at `reasons/api.py:4475`).

cli-topics-json-output-is-parseable-json.text: Running `reasons topics --json` must emit stdout that `json.loads` can parse and that contains `topics` and `total_nodes`.

cli-translates-permission-error-to-acces.text: CLI handlers print `Access denied: {e}` to stderr when a permission failure escapes from the API or database layer.

cli-update-errors-without-text-or-source.text: The CLI `update` command returns an error when neither a text nor a source flag is provided.

cli-uses-lazy-imports-for-heavy-modules.text: `asyncio`, `derive`, `ask`, and `Storage` are imported inside function bodies rather than at module level, keeping `reasons --help` fast.

cli-uses-reasons-console-script.text: All documented CLI invocations use the `uv run reasons ...` form, which requires a `reasons` console script defined in `pyproject.toml`.

cli-uses-relative-api-import.text: `reasons/cli.py` imports its API via `from . import api`, which is why the same module works unchanged behind the `reasons_lib` shim.

cli-verdict-display-maps-all-four-values.text: `reasons/cli.py:2236-2237` maps all four verdicts to display symbols, and `:2245` defaults missing verdicts to `INCONCLUSIVE`.

cli-version-flag-eagerly-resolves-metada.text: `reasons/cli.py:3057` calls `_pkg_version('ftl-reasons')` when the argument parser is constructed, not when `--version` is invoked.

cli-version-flag-has-no-metadata-fallbac.text: `reasons/cli.py:3057` calls `_pkg_version('ftl-reasons')` unguarded inside `argparse.add_argument(..., action="version")`, so a missing distribution aborts parser construction rather than only failing `--version`.

cli-version-flag-resolves-at-parser-cons.text: `reasons/cli.py` resolves `_pkg_version('ftl-reasons')` eagerly when constructing the argument parser, not only when `--version` is invoked.

cli-version-requires-installed-ftl-reaso.text: `main` evaluates `importlib.metadata.version("ftl-reasons")` eagerly while building the parser, so a missing package distribution raises `PackageNotFoundError` before help or version handling.

cli-warns-on-three-premise-sl-without-an.text: The CLI warns at add time when an SL justification has 3 or more premises and --any was not used.

cli-what-if-does-not-persist-changes.text: CLI `what-if` tests verify that cascade simulation runs without persisting changes and that output contains `NOT modified`.

cli-what-if-never-modifies-database.text: cmd_what_if is read-only and never modifies the database; its output explicitly states (database NOT modified).

cli-what-if-outputs-not-modified.text: The CLI `what-if` command prints `NOT modified` and does not change network state.

client-does-not-catch-mcperror.text: `McpBridge.call_tool` calls `future.result(timeout=60)` without a `try/except`, so protocol-level `McpError` exceptions propagate uncaught to the caller.

client-uses-call-tool-result-content-cha.text: `_call_tool_async` in `reasons/mcp_client.py` joins text from every item in `result.content` and returns the joined string; it never reads `result.isError` or `result.structuredContent`.

close-only-closes-owned-connections.text: `PgApi.close()` closes the connection only when `_owns_conn` is true, which happens only for string `conninfo`.

closed-guided-recovery-operates-over-top.text: The guided-recovery closure achieved by recoverable bidirectional revision and defeat reversal operates over truth effects that are topology-complete, robust, and traceable across all transitive dependents.

justifications.label: The first antecedent establishes closed guided recovery; the second establishes the topology-complete robust traceable effect space it must cover. Both are load-bearing.

closed-loop-is-origin-agnostic.text: The minimality-sustained closed maintenance loop operates identically across all belief origins — external beliefs achieve full integration parity within the same forward-computation and backward-revision cycle as internally-derived beliefs, making the maintenance loop source-agnostic.

justifications.label: integration parity means external beliefs participate identically in the closed loop

closed-loop-preserves-all-invariants.text: The closed revision-and-lifecycle maintenance loop not only sustains belief consistency but preserves all system invariants through architecturally grounded enforcement — the loop is both self-maintaining and invariant-preserving.

justifications.label: the closed loop inherits invariant preservation from its architectural grounding

cloud-run-mcp-server-exposes-search-show.text: The Cloud Run FastAPI MCP server exposes search, show, explain, list_topics, and get_topic tools.

cloud-run-mcp-server-is-read-side-sharin.text: The Cloud Run MCP server handles the read side and shares network.json with the GCE builder via GCS.

cloud-run-mcp-server-loads-network-json-.text: The Cloud Run MCP server loads network.json from GCS on cold start and caches it in memory.

cloud-run-mcp-server-uses-streamable-htt.text: The Cloud Run MCP server uses Streamable HTTP transport rather than SSE.

cloud-run-scales-to-zero-with-no-idle-co.text: Cloud Run scales to zero and incurs no cost when idle.

cluster-and-sample-are-mutually-exclusiv.text: The `--cluster` and `--sample` flags in `cmd_derive` are mutually exclusive, enforced with an explicit check and `sys.exit(1)` — they represent competing strategies for belief subset selection.

cluster-auto-k-caps-by-budget-thirds.text: `cluster_beliefs` and `cluster_beliefs_intra` use `max_k=min(budget // 3, 20)` for auto-k, while `list_clusters` uses the default `max_k=20`.

cluster-auto-k-floors-at-two.text: `_auto_k` always returns at least 2 clusters (when auto-computed), ensuring cross-domain sampling is meaningful even for small belief sets

cluster-auto-k-heuristic.text: Auto cluster count is computed as `len(beliefs) // 5`, clamped between 2 and `min(budget // 3, 20)`, targeting approximately 5 beliefs per cluster with at least 3 beliefs per cluster given the budget.

cluster-auto-k-is-n-beliefs-div-five-cla.text: `_auto_k` computes the cluster count as `n_beliefs // 5`, clamped to `[2, max_k]`, and `cluster_beliefs` further constrains `max_k` to `budget // 3`.

cluster-beliefs-allocates-remainder-to-l.text: `cluster_beliefs` iterates clusters in descending size order when assigning remainder quota, biasing extra selections toward larger clusters.

cluster-beliefs-can-undershoot-budget-wh.text: Per-cluster quotas are capped by cluster size and unused quota is not redistributed, so `cluster_beliefs` can select fewer than `budget` beliefs even when enough beliefs exist.

cluster-beliefs-cluster-sizes-ordered-by.text: `cluster_stats["cluster_sizes"]` is ordered by ascending KMeans label, not by cluster size.

cluster-beliefs-cluster-sizes-use-label-.text: `cluster_stats["cluster_sizes"]` is ordered by ascending KMeans label, while sampling iterates clusters in descending size order.

cluster-beliefs-deterministic-with-seed.text: Given the same beliefs dict, budget, and seed, `cluster_beliefs` produces identical output across calls.

cluster-beliefs-honors-explicit-n-cluste.text: When `n_clusters` is passed to `cluster_beliefs`, the returned `stats['n_clusters']` matches the requested value exactly.

cluster-beliefs-intra-produces-at-most-b.text: The selected ID list length is always at most `budget`, but may be shorter when the focus cluster is smaller.

cluster-beliefs-intra-requires-cluster-d.text: The function raises `ImportError` before the early-return path if clustering dependencies are missing.

cluster-beliefs-may-return-fewer-than-bu.text: Per-cluster quotas are capped by cluster size and unused quota is not redistributed, so `len(selected_ids)` can be less than `budget`.

cluster-beliefs-mutates-provided-cache.text: When a `ClusterCache` is passed, `cache.embed` adds new `(node_id, text_hash)` embeddings to its internal cache.

cluster-beliefs-requires-cluster-deps-ev.text: Calls `_require_cluster_deps()` before checking `len(beliefs) <= budget`, so missing optional dependencies raise `ImportError` even when no embedding is needed.

cluster-beliefs-respects-budget.text: `cluster_beliefs` never returns more IDs than the `budget` parameter; each cluster's allocation is individually capped by `min(alloc, len(members))`.

cluster-beliefs-returns-all-keys-in-inse.text: The shortcut returns `list(beliefs.keys())` with stats using `n_clusters=1`, `cluster_sizes=[len(beliefs)]`, and the `model_name` argument.

cluster-beliefs-returns-exact-budget.text: `cluster_beliefs` returns exactly `budget` belief IDs when the input set is larger than the budget, and all items when the input set is smaller.

cluster-beliefs-returns-exactly-budget.text: When `0 < budget < len(beliefs)`, `cluster_beliefs` returns exactly `budget` ids, not at most `budget`.

cluster-beliefs-returns-selected-ids-and.text: `cluster_beliefs` returns `(selected_ids, cluster_stats)`, where `cluster_stats` includes cluster count, sizes, and model name.

cluster-beliefs-uses-local-random-instan.text: `cluster_beliefs` samples with a local `random.Random(seed)` instance and does not mutate Python's global RNG state.

cluster-budget-cap-can-underselect.text: `cluster_beliefs` caps each cluster’s allocation at cluster size and does not redistribute unused slots, so it can return fewer than `budget` IDs.

cluster-budget-is-hard-ceiling.text: `cluster_beliefs` never returns more than `budget` belief IDs; when the belief set is smaller than budget, it returns all beliefs without clustering

cluster-cache-embed-returns-ids-and-embe.text: `ClusterCache.embed(beliefs)` returns a tuple of belief IDs and their embeddings.

cluster-cache-enables-embedding-reuse.text: Reusing a `ClusterCache` persists newly computed embeddings in its internal cache across calls.

cluster-cache-is-not-thread-safe.text: `ClusterCache._cache` is a plain Python dict with no locking; concurrent `embed()` calls on the same cache instance may double-encode or observe inconsistent intermediate state, relying on the derive pipeline being single-threaded.

cluster-cache-key-includes-text-hash.text: `ClusterCache` keys embeddings by `(node_id, sha256(text)[:16])`, so modified belief text invalidates the cached embedding without requiring explicit cache eviction

cluster-cache-keys-include-content-hash.text: `ClusterCache` keys embeddings by `(node_id, sha256_prefix)`, so editing a belief's text with the same ID forces re-embedding rather than serving stale vectors.

cluster-cache-keys-on-node-id-and-text-h.text: `ClusterCache.embed` invalidates cached embeddings when belief text changes by keying entries on `(node_id, sha256(text)[:16])`.

cluster-cache-no-recompute.text: `ClusterCache.embed()` does not recompute embeddings for previously cached belief texts; cache size stays constant on repeated calls with the same input and grows by exactly the count of new texts on superset calls.

cluster-default-model-is-all-minilm-l6-v.text: The default sentence-transformer model used by `cluster.py` is `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

cluster-deps-are-optional.text: `sentence-transformers` and `scikit-learn` are optional dependencies behind a `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS` gate; the module degrades to a clear `ImportError` with install instructions when they are absent.

cluster-deps-flag-conflates-any-import-e.text: In `tests/test_cluster.py`, the top-level grouped import sets `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS = False` for any `ImportError`, not only for a missing cluster dependency.

cluster-deps-flag-is-set-false-by-any-in.text: In `tests/test_cluster.py`, the top-level `except ImportError` assigns `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS = False` for any `ImportError` during the grouped import, not only for a missing cluster dependency.

cluster-deps-optional-with-graceful-skip.text: The clustering module (`reasons_lib.cluster`) is behind an optional `[cluster]` install extra; when `sentence-transformers` or `scikit-learn` are missing, `_require_cluster_deps` raises `ImportError` and all dependent tests skip cleanly.

cluster-derive-is-semantically-informed-.text: When using cluster-based belief selection, the derive pipeline achieves semantically-informed budget allocation (embedding-based grouping ensures topical diversity across the prompt) with end-to-end determinism (sorted embedding order, fixed-seed clustering, and exact budget counts feed into reproducible prompt construction with accurate token allocation).

justifications.label: Cluster-embedding determinism chains through to prompt-construction determinism

cluster-early-return-skips-ml-when-under.text: All three public cluster functions (`cluster_beliefs`, `cluster_beliefs_intra`, `list_clusters`) check `len(beliefs) <= budget` (or `<= 3` for listing) and return immediately with a single-group result, avoiding loading the SentenceTransformer model and running KMeans entirely.

cluster-embed-order-is-deterministic.text: Beliefs are sorted by ID before embedding (`ids = sorted(beliefs.keys())`), making cluster assignments reproducible given the same random seed.

cluster-embed-sorts-belief-ids.text: `ClusterCache.embed()` uses `ids = sorted(beliefs.keys())` so the ID list and embedding array have consistent ordering regardless of dict insertion order.

cluster-extra-requires-sentence-transfor.text: The cluster optional dependency extra requires sentence-transformers >=2.2 and scikit-learn >=1.2.

cluster-flags-gate-clustercache-import.text: `ClusterCache` is imported only when `args.cluster` or `args.intra_cluster` is truthy; the import is otherwise skipped to avoid the `sentence-transformers`/`torch` cost.

cluster-helper-importable-without-option.text: `_require_cluster_deps` remains importable from `reasons.cluster` even when optional cluster dependencies are absent.

cluster-import-error-message-requires-ex.text: The expected `ImportError` string must contain the literal text `ftl-reasons[cluster]`.

cluster-inter-sampling-is-not-budget-gua.text: `cluster_beliefs` can return fewer than `budget` IDs because per-cluster allocations are capped by cluster size and not redistributed.

cluster-intra-focus-is-size-sorted-index.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` reports `focus_cluster` as an index into the descending-size-sorted cluster list, not as the original KMeans label.

cluster-intra-rotates-size-sorted-cluste.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` selects the focus cluster by `round_num % k` after sorting clusters by descending size.

cluster-k-clamped-to-valid-range.text: The final cluster count `k` is clamped to `[1, len(beliefs)]` so KMeans never receives an invalid cluster count.

cluster-kmeans-uses-n-init-10.text: `cluster_beliefs` runs KMeans with `n_init=10` and the user's seed for reproducibility.

cluster-list-clusters-short-circuits-at-.text: `list_clusters` short-circuits without clustering when the belief set contains 3 or fewer items.

cluster-missing-dep-test-skips-when-deps.text: `test_require_cluster_deps_message` skips when `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS` is true and only exercises `_require_cluster_deps()` when cluster deps are absent.

cluster-missing-deps-error-includes-inst.text: `_require_cluster_deps()` raises `ImportError` whose message includes the exact `pip install 'ftl-reasons[cluster]'` remediation command.

cluster-missing-deps-error-mentions-extr.text: `_require_cluster_deps` raises an `ImportError` whose message mentions `ftl-reasons[cluster]` when clustering dependencies are missing.

cluster-missing-deps-path-requires-impor.text: `_require_cluster_deps` must remain importable from `reasons.cluster` even when optional cluster dependencies are absent.

cluster-ml-errors-propagate.text: Beyond the optional-dependency `ImportError`, embedding and clustering errors in `cluster.py` are not caught and propagate to the caller.

cluster-mode-ignores-sample-flag.text: When `cluster` or `intra_cluster` is truthy, the `sample` parameter is not consulted; sampling is handled inside `reasons.cluster`.

cluster-module-import-is-soft.text: Importing `reasons.cluster` succeeds even when `sentence-transformers`/`scikit-learn` are absent; `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS` reports whether the optional imports succeeded.

cluster-numeric-tests-run-without-extras.text: The three `_auto_k` tests and `test_require_cluster_deps_message` are the only tests without `@skip_no_cluster`; they exercise pure arithmetic or the missing-dep path.

cluster-public-functions-require-cluster.text: Every public clustering function calls `_require_cluster_deps()` before its fast path, so missing sentence-transformers/scikit-learn raises `ImportError` even when clustering would be skipped.

cluster-public-functions-require-deps-be.text: All public clustering functions call `_require_cluster_deps()` before their small-input fast paths, so missing optional dependencies raise `ImportError` even when clustering would be skipped.

cluster-remainder-favors-largest.text: When the budget doesn't divide evenly across clusters, extra slots are distributed one-per-cluster to the largest clusters first via descending size sort.

cluster-remainder-favors-largest-cluster.text: When the sampling budget does not divide evenly across clusters, `cluster_beliefs` allocates remainder slots to the largest clusters first, sorted by descending size.

cluster-require-deps-raises-import-error.text: When cluster deps are absent, `_require_cluster_deps()` must raise `ImportError` whose message contains `ftl-reasons[cluster]`.

cluster-selection-is-deterministic-and-b.text: Cluster-based belief selection produces identical results given the same seed, returns exactly the requested budget count, and processes beliefs in sorted order — ensuring fully reproducible, precisely-sized belief subsets for derive prompt construction.

justifications.label: Three independent determinism properties combine to guarantee reproducible budget-exact clustering

cluster-selection-preserves-cross-domain.text: With a mixed auth/database corpus and `budget=20`, `cluster_beliefs` selects at least one belief from each domain.

cluster-shim-inherits-api-from-reasons-c.text: The set of names importable from `reasons_lib.cluster` is exactly `reasons.cluster`'s public (`__all__` or non-underscore) namespace; the shim performs no curation.

cluster-shim-preserves-name-identity.text: Symbols accessed via `reasons_lib.cluster.X` are the same objects as `reasons.cluster.X`, not copies.

cluster-shim-requires-reasons-package.text: Importing `reasons_lib.cluster` hard-fails with `ImportError` if `reasons.cluster` is not importable; there is no try/except fallback.

cluster-shim-reverse-import-list-is-mirr.text: The reported reverse-importer list for `reasons_lib.cluster` includes `reasons/cluster.py`, but a literal reverse import would be circular; treat that list as API-surface mirroring, not a real dependency edge.

cluster-shim-suppresses-only-f401-and-f4.text: The `# noqa: F401,F403` annotation silences only the "unused import" and "wildcard import" flake8 rules, leaving other linting of this file active.

cluster-sizes-do-not-map-to-focus-cluste.text: `cluster_sizes` is in ascending cluster-label order, while `focus_cluster` indexes size-sorted clusters.

cluster-skips-ml-when-under-budget.text: When the number of beliefs is less than or equal to the budget, all ML work (embedding, clustering, sampling) is skipped and every belief is returned directly.

cluster-stats-account-for-all-beliefs.text: `sum(cluster_beliefs(...)[1]["cluster_sizes"])` equals the number of input beliefs, and stats include `n_clusters`, `cluster_sizes`, and `embedding_model`.

cluster-stats-cluster-sizes-sum-to-input.text: The `stats` dict returned by `cluster_beliefs` always contains `cluster_sizes` as a list of integers whose sum equals `len(beliefs)`, ensuring no beliefs are silently lost during the clustering reduction.

cluster-stats-has-fixed-keys-and-sum.text: `cluster_beliefs` returns a `stats` dictionary containing `n_clusters`, `cluster_sizes`, and `embedding_model`, and the cluster sizes sum to the total number of beliefs.

cluster-stats-include-embedding-model.text: The `cluster_beliefs` stats dict includes an `embedding_model` field naming the sentence-transformer model used.

cluster-stats-presence-signals-cluster-m.text: The second return value is a dict iff clustering ran (early-return path); otherwise it is `None`, even when the section is non-empty.

cluster-stats-sizes-sum-to-input.text: The `cluster_sizes` list in the stats dict returned by `cluster_beliefs` always sums to the total number of input beliefs, enforcing that every belief is assigned to exactly one cluster.

cluster-tests-skip-only-dep-requiring-ca.text: Clustering behavior tests are skipped when `HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS` is false, while pure `_auto_k` tests run without the cluster extra installed.

cluster-tests-skip-when-deps-missing.text: Every behavior test in `tests/test_cluster.py` is decorated with `@skip_no_cluster = pytest.mark.skipif(not HAS_CLUSTER_DEPS, ...)`; only the pure `_auto_k` tests run unconditionally.

cluster-tests-verify-cross-domain-divers.text: `test_cluster_beliefs_cross_domain` creates auth and database belief groups and asserts both are represented in the selected output.

clustercache-importerror-conflates-missi.text: The `ImportError` handler treats any import-time failure inside `.cluster` or `ClusterCache.__init__` as a missing optional dependency, so an internal import bug can be reported as a missing package.

clustercache-importerror-exits-1-after-s.text: Any `ImportError` from importing `.cluster` or constructing `ClusterCache` is caught, printed as `Error: <message>` to `stderr`, and followed by `sys.exit(1)`.

clustercache-importerror-produces-exit-c.text: Any `ImportError` raised by the `.cluster` import or by `ClusterCache.__init__` is caught and converted into a `stderr` message plus `sys.exit(1)`.

clustercache-non-importerror-exceptions-.text: `RuntimeError`, `OSError`, `ValueError`, and other non-`ImportError` exceptions from `ClusterCache(...)` are not caught by this handler and will crash `derive` with a traceback.

clustercache-non-importerror-propagates.text: `RuntimeError`, `OSError`, `ValueError`, and other non-`ImportError` exceptions from `ClusterCache(...)` are not caught by this handler and propagate as tracebacks.

cmd-add-warns-for-three-premises-without.text: cmd_add and cmd_add_justification call _warn_multi_premise to hint about --any mode when 3+ premises form an AND conjunction without --any.

cmd-check-stale-exits-nonzero-on-stale.text: cmd_check_stale calls sys.exit(1) when any stale node is found.

cmd-derive-shells-out-to-claude-or-gemin.text: cmd_derive shells out to an external CLI (claude or gemini) via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec to generate belief proposals.

cmd-get-metadata-maps-permissionerror-to.text: `cmd_get_metadata` catches `(KeyError, PermissionError)` together and prints `Error: {e}`, not `Access denied: {e}`.

cmd-init-catches-fileexistserror-suggest.text: cmd_init catches FileExistsError and suggests using --force.

cmd-propagate-bypasses-api.text: `cmd_propagate` is the only CLI handler that bypasses `api.py`, going directly to `Storage` → `Network.recompute_all()` → `Storage.save()` — a design inconsistency in the otherwise pure-presentation CLI layer.

cmd-propagate-bypasses-api-layer.text: The cmd_propagate CLI handler goes directly from Storage to Network instead of through the API layer.

cmd-propagate-delegates-to-api-propagate.text: cmd_propagate delegates to api.propagate() using the _with_network pattern, removing the only CLI handler that bypassed the API layer.

cmd-propose-update-is-the-cli-handler.text: `cmd_propose_update` at `reasons/cli.py:2775` is the sole CLI handler for the `propose-update` subcommand, registered in the dispatch dict at `reasons/cli.py:4007`.

cmd-propose-update-is-the-registered-cli.text: `cmd_propose_update` is the CLI handler registered in the dispatch table for the `propose-update` subcommand.

cmd-search-sources-does-not-catch-retrie.text: `cmd_search_sources` has no `try`/`except` around `search_source_chunks`, so SQLite schema or connection errors propagate as tracebacks rather than being converted to a CLI error.

cmd-search-sources-empty-result-skips-js.text: On zero matches, `cmd_search_sources` prints `"No matching chunks found."` regardless of `--format`, so JSON consumers do not receive `[]` on empty results.

cmd-search-sources-lazy-imports-ask.text: `search_source_chunks` is imported inside the function body to avoid loading `reasons.ask` for unrelated CLI commands.

cmd-show-assumes-metadata-is-a-dict.text: `cmd_show` assumes `node["metadata"]` is a dict (not `None`); calling `.get` on a `None` value would raise `AttributeError`.

cmd-show-only-catches-lookup-errors.text: `cmd_show` catches `KeyError`/`PermissionError` only around the `api.show_node` call; formatting-time `KeyError`s propagate as uncaught tracebacks.

cmd-show-requires-non-optional-top-level.text: `cmd_show` accesses `node['source']`, `node['source_hash']`, `node['metadata']`, `node['justifications']`, and `node['dependents']` without `.get`, so `api.show_node` must always return them.

cmd-show-truncates-pinned-sha.text: When `metadata["pinned_sha"]` is truthy, `cmd_show` displays only its first 12 characters.

cmd-show-uses-fixed-timestamp-order.text: Timestamp display order is hard-coded to `created_at, updated_at, reviewed_at, verified_at, retracted_at` and entries with falsy values are silently skipped.

cmd-update-prevalidates-one-field.text: `cmd_update` validates that at least one of `--text`, `--source`, or `--source-url` is provided before calling the API.

cmd-what-if-output-notes-database-not-mo.text: cmd_what_if explicitly notes 'database NOT modified' in its output.

code-expert-update-produced-242-new-beli.text: A code-expert update run produced 242 new beliefs, bringing the total to 542, with 217 derived beliefs.

colon-means-already-namespaced.text: `_resolve_namespace` treats a colon in a node ID as "already namespaced" and never double-prefixes; this is the convention for cross-namespace references.

command-dispatch-uses-parallel-dict.text: Dispatch is implemented via a hand-maintained `commands` dictionary, not `subparsers.set_defaults(func=...)`; parser registration and dispatch entries are two parallel lists with no automatic synchronization check.

command-escapes-only-double-quotes.text: The `reasons update` line escapes only `"` in `proposed_text`; `reasons retract` escapes nothing in `failure_mode` or `comment`.

command-per-file-maps-to-cli-subcommand.text: The overview uses “nearly” and “effectively,” making the mapping too vague to accept as a codebase invariant without checking `cli.py` dispatch.

commands-dict-is-defined-at-reasons-cli-.text: `reasons/cli.py` contains the only `commands = {` assignment at line 3923.

commands-dict-must-mirror-subparsers.text: Adding a CLI subcommand requires entries in both the argparse subparser definitions and the `commands` dispatch dict in `main()`; omitting either silently breaks the command.

compact-and-export-markdown-lack-visible.text: `reasons/compact.py:compact` and `reasons/export_markdown.py:export_markdown` iterate `network.nodes.values()` without any visibility parameter, so gating must be applied in `reasons/api.py` before delegation.

compact-and-export-markdown-return-plain.text: `compact` and `export_markdown` MCP tools return plain strings rather than JSON-encoded objects.

compact-api-and-cli-default-budget-is-50.text: The public `compact()` API and the CLI `compact --budget` option both default to 500.

compact-appends-omitted-sentinel-when-bu.text: When compact() stops adding items because the budget would overflow, it appends a ... (N more omitted) sentinel and ends that section.

compact-budget-applies-to-all-output-sec.text: The compact output budget applies to nogoods, OUT, and IN sections using a running character counter.

compact-budget-check-ignores-newline-cos.text: In `reasons/compact.py`, candidate line budget checks use `estimate_tokens(line)` without the newline character, while `_add_line` tracks `1 + len(line)`, so newline costs are omitted from the check.

compact-budget-controls-output-size.text: The compact module's token budget reliably constrains total output size

compact-budget-exhaustion-appends-omissi.text: When the global token budget is exhausted mid-section, `compact` appends a `"<N> more <section> omitted"` notice to the output rather than raising an exception or silently truncating, preserving the contract that `compact` never raises.

compact-budget-guarantee.text: `compact()` output estimated token count never exceeds the `budget` parameter; every line is gated by `_over_budget` before appending.

compact-budget-includes-structural-lines.text: Section headers, blank separators, omission messages, and the footer are added through `_add_line` and therefore consume budget.

compact-budget-is-approximate.text: A 200-token budget test allows output below 250 estimated tokens and expects omission markers for overflowed sections.

compact-budget-is-soft-cap.text: The compact token budget is approximate; structural overhead (section headers, truncation messages) can cause up to ~25% overshoot beyond the specified budget.

compact-budget-omits-entries-with-more-o.text: Each compact output section independently respects the token budget and emits a `more … omitted` message when entries are dropped.

compact-budget-only-limits-in-nodes.text: The token budget only constrains the IN nodes section; nogoods and OUT nodes are always emitted regardless of budget, so compact output can exceed the specified budget value.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #39

compact-budget-soft-ceiling.text: The `compact` function treats the token budget as approximate; structural overhead (headers, truncation messages) can cause output to exceed the budget by up to ~25%.

compact-budget-tracking-is-efficient-and.text: The compact module tracks token budgets efficiently through an approximate but computationally fast strategy: O(1) per-line budget checks via a running character count, with token estimation based on chars/4 — a lightweight approximation avoiding external tokenizer dependencies while maintaining accuracy sufficient for budget enforcement.

justifications.label: Grouping the two implementation choices that define compact's budget tracking strategy — deliberate trade of precision for efficiency

compact-char-tracking-o1.text: Budget tracking uses a running `_char_count` integer, making per-line budget checks O(1) instead of O(n).

compact-default-budget-is-500-words.text: compact() defaults to budget=500 and truncate=True.

compact-empty-network-reports-zero-nodes.text: For an empty network, `compact` outputs the text `0 nodes tracked`.

compact-estimate-tokens-char-div-4-floor.text: estimate_tokens approximates token count as len(text) // 4 and returns at least 1.

compact-estimate-tokens-chars-div-4.text: `estimate_tokens` uses `len(text) // 4` with a floor of 1, not word count or any external tokenizer.

compact-estimate-tokens-is-length-div-fo.text: compact.estimate_tokens approximates token count as max(1, len(text) // 4).

compact-export-form-bounded-faithful-out.text: Compact and export together form a bounded, faithful output pipeline: compact is pure and infallible with priority-ordered truncation and explicit omission notices, while export preserves behavioral equivalence through roundtrip — any output representation is both correct-within-budget and semantically faithful to the source network.

justifications.label: Each antecedent independently supports "bounded faithfulness" (purity ensures no side effects, infallibility ensures no crash, omission notice ensures transparency of truncation, roundtrip ensures semantic preservation).

compact-footer-pre-reserved.text: The footer line's token cost is pre-computed and reserved before any section starts filling, guaranteeing it always fits within the budget.

compact-footer-reservation-uses-placehol.text: `compact()` reserves footer budget from a placeholder string using the nominal budget, so the reservation can differ from the final footer’s token estimate.

compact-header-and-footer-are-unconditio.text: `compact` always emits the header and token-count footer regardless of budget; only the nogoods, OUT, and IN content sections are budget-gated.

compact-header-includes-date-and-counts.text: compact emits a header containing the date, total node counts, and nogood count.

compact-hides-covered-nodes-iff-summary-.text: `compact` suppresses covered node lines only while the covering summary's truth value is `IN`; an `OUT` summary leaves covered nodes visible.

compact-hides-covered-nodes-only-when-su.text: `compact()` suppresses covered nodes from its output only when the covering summary's truth value is "IN"; if the summary is "OUT" (due to a retracted covered node), all covered nodes reappear in the output unhidden.

compact-hides-covered-only-when-summary-.text: Covered nodes are hidden from `compact()` output only while the covering summary's `truth_value == "IN"`; an OUT summary leaves them visible.

compact-in-line-includes-first-non-summa.text: Each emitted IN node line includes the antecedents of its first non-summary justification.

compact-in-nodes-ordered-by-dependent-co.text: Within the IN section of `compact()` output, nodes are sorted by `len(node.dependents)` descending so the most structurally important (most-referenced) beliefs appear first and are least likely to be cut by the budget.

compact-in-nodes-ordered-by-dependents.text: IN nodes are sorted by descending dependent count so structurally important nodes (those depended on by many others) are emitted first and survive budget truncation.

compact-in-nodes-sorted-by-dependent-cou.text: compact() sorts IN nodes by len(node.dependents) descending, so more-depended-on beliefs appear first and survive budget truncation.

compact-in-section-orders-by-dependent-c.text: Within the IN (active) section, `compact` orders nodes by dependent count descending (most-connected first), so that budget-driven truncation preferentially drops the least-connected nodes while preserving structurally important ones.

compact-is-deterministic-pure-and-bounde.text: The compact module produces output that is simultaneously deterministic (pure function with fixed priority ordering), bounded (guaranteed to never exceed the token budget), and self-describing (includes its own token count for auditability).

justifications.label: Three independent compact properties unify into a single reliability guarantee for downstream consumers

compact-is-efficient-deterministic-and-b.text: The compact module simultaneously achieves computational efficiency (O(1) per-line budget tracking via running character count with chars/4 token estimation), mathematical determinism (pure function with no side effects), and guaranteed output bounds (never exceeds the budget parameter) — all three desirable output properties without trade-offs.

justifications.label: Efficient approximate tracking is the mechanism that enables deterministic bounded output without expensive per-line recomputation

compact-is-infallible.text: `compact()` handles empty networks, zero-budget, and missing metadata without raising exceptions — designed to always produce a valid string.

compact-is-predictable-bounded-distillat.text: The compact module is a fully predictable information distillation: a pure function with deterministic priority ordering that reliably constrains output within token budgets, self-reports resource usage, and structurally important nodes are prioritized through dependent-count sorting

justifications.label: Purity and determinism combined with reliable budget enforcement yields predictable distillation

compact-is-pure-function.text: `compact()` performs no I/O, no database access, no mutations, and no side effects; it is a pure transformation from `Network` to `str`.

compact-never-exceeds-budget.text: `compact()` guarantees the returned string's estimated token count (chars/4) does not exceed the `budget` parameter, enforced by pre-checking every line addition against remaining space.

compact-nogoods-render-under-heading-wit.text: `compact()` includes nogood contradiction sets under a `## Nogoods` section with auto-generated IDs.

compact-omitted-markers-include-count.text: When the budget is exhausted, compact emits '... (N more omitted)' markers for omitted nodes.

compact-orders-by-dependent-count.text: In the tested scenario, a node with one dependent must appear before a node with zero dependents.

compact-orders-nodes-by-dependent-count.text: In compact output, nodes with more dependents appear before nodes with fewer dependents, e.g. a node with one dependent appears before a node with zero dependents.

compact-out-reason-priority.text: For OUT nodes, `compact` surfaces the reason using priority order `retract_reason`, then `stale_reason`, then `superseded_by`.

compact-out-reason-priority-is-retract-s.text: compact annotates OUT nodes by checking metadata retract_reason and stale_reason first, then falling back to superseded_by.

compact-out-section-header-is-include-ou.text: `api.compact` emits the literal `OUT (retracted)` section header if and only if `include_out=True`.

compact-output-is-faithful-bounded-proje.text: The compact output is a faithful bounded projection of the belief network: it never exceeds the token budget, emits sections in a fixed priority order (nogoods → OUT → IN) that no later section can displace, and always appends an explicit omission notice when content is truncated—never silently dropping beliefs.
