defeat-justification-error-contract.text: `defeat_justification` raises `KeyError` (message contains "not found") for missing nodes, `ValueError` (message contains "no justifications") for nodes with zero justifications, and `IndexError` (message contains "out of range") for out-of-range justification indices — it never returns an error dict for these conditions.

defeat-justification-extends-outlist.text: `defeat_justification` suppresses an existing argument by appending a defeater node ID to that justification’s `outlist`.

defeat-justification-is-idempotent-on-ou.text: Appending `defeater_id` to `outlist` is guarded, but creating the defeater node is not — a repeat call with a colliding `defeater_id` relies on `Network.add_node`'s duplicate semantics.

defeat-justification-manually-updates-de.text: Because premises have no justifications, the reverse edge `defeater.dependents.add(node_id)` is added explicitly rather than derived by `add_node`.

defeat-justification-mutates-outlist.text: `api.defeat_justification` appends the defeater to `Justification.outlist` (`reasons/api.py:1392-1393`, `1526-1527`) rather than removing antecedents, so defeat reuses the native outlist propagation.

defeat-justification-outlist-idempotent-.text: `defeat_justification` only appends `defeater_id` to `outlist` when absent, but does not check for a duplicate defeater node ID before calling `net.add_node`.

defeat-justification-produces-premise-de.text: The defeater is added via `net.add_node` with no justifications, so it evaluates `IN` by default and blocks the target's outlist.

defeat-justification-requires-a-writable.text: `reasons.api.defeat_justification` raises `ValueError` when the target has no justifications (line 1361) and appends the defeater ID onto `justification.outlist` (line 1392-1393)

defeat-justification-requires-in-range-i.text: The function raises `IndexError` when `justification_index` is negative or `>= len(node.justifications)`; no clamping occurs.

defeat-justification-returns-only-flippe.text: `changed` is computed by diffing against a pre-add snapshot, not from `recompute_all()`'s return, so it can be empty when the justification was already blocked.

defeat-metadata-keys-are-generic-node-me.text: `scope_of`, `for_defeater`, and `defeats_node` are stored as ordinary `Node.metadata` keys rather than dedicated top-level export-schema fields.

defeat-metadata-lives-in-node-metadata.text: `scope_of`, `for_defeater`, and `defeats_node` are stored inside each node’s `metadata` dictionary rather than as dedicated top-level JSON fields.

defeat-reason-embedded-in-defeater-text.text: In `defeat_justification`, the `reason` string is embedded in the defeater node's text and therefore participates in its `text_hash` and Merkle chain hashing.

defeat-reason-taxonomy-has-four-categori.text: `classify_defeat_reason` in `reasons/review.py` assigns one of four defeater types: `unsupported-conjunct`, `over-generalizes`, `scope-mismatch`, or `migrated-retraction`

defeat-reason-type-absent-when-unset.text: When `defeat_reason_type` is empty or unset in `defeat_with_scope`, the key is deliberately absent from the defeater's metadata dict rather than present with an empty-string value.

defeat-reason-type-is-conditional-metada.text: `defeat_justification` writes `defeat_reason_type` to metadata only when the argument is truthy; omitted values leave the key absent rather than storing an empty string.

defeat-reason-type-is-omitted-when-empty.text: `defeat_reason_type` is only written to metadata when the caller supplies a non-empty string (api.py:1383–1384, 1510–1511).

defeat-reason-type-key-omitted-when-empt.text: `defeat_reason_type` is only written into defeater metadata when the caller supplies a non-empty string.

defeat-reason-type-metadata-is-condition.text: `defeat_reason_type` is written to metadata only when non-empty (`reasons/api.py:1383-1384`), verified by `test_defeat_reason_type_omitted` vs `test_defeat_reason_type_stored`

defeat-reason-type-omitted-is-empty-and-.text: When `defeat_reason_type` is omitted, `defeat_with_scope` returns `""` and does not store the key in defeater metadata; when supplied, the value is stored in defeater metadata.

defeat-reason-type-populated-by-post-hoc.text: `defeat_reason_type` is populated post-hoc by `classify_defeat_reason_types` via `set_metadata`, not at defeater creation time.

defeat-reason-type-requires-llm-classifi.text: `defeat_reason_type` is populated post-hoc by `classify_defeat_reason_types` via `set_metadata` (api.py:1715), not at defeat-creation time.

defeat-reason-type-written-conditionally.text: `defeat_justification` only adds `defeat_reason_type` to metadata when the argument is truthy (`api.py:1383–1384, 1510–1511`), unlike `defeater_type`/`defeats_node` which are always written.

defeat-reason-types-are-closed-seven-val.text: `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` in `review.py` is a fixed list of exactly 7 strings that serves as both the LLM's allowed output vocabulary and the validation set in `classify_defeat_reason`; any downstream code matching on `defeat_reason_type` can exhaustively branch over these 7 values plus `""` for unclassified.

defeat-reason-types-are-kebab-case.text: Every entry in `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` contains a hyphen.

defeat-reason-types-is-closed-seven-elem.text: `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` contains exactly 7 kebab-case strings; the parser performs a membership check against this set, so any new classification type must be added to this constant before the LLM prompt can reference it.

defeat-relationship-is-dual-encoded.text: Defeat relationships are represented both by metadata pointers (`scope_of`, `for_defeater`, `defeats_node`, `defeats_justification`) and by the defeater’s SL justification antecedents, so export/import must preserve both to retain full behavior.

defeat-reversal-is-automatic-with-guided.text: All outlist-based defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) not only reverse automatically through BFS propagation cascades — recovering all transitively dependent nodes — but also provide surgical recovery guidance through restoration hints that target cascade victims with surviving premises, enabling both automatic and manual recovery paths.

justifications.label: Automatic reversal handles the common case (retract the defeater, everything recovers), while guided recovery handles the complex case (multi-premise justifications where only some premises survive) — together they provide complete recovery coverage.

defeat-reversal-is-topology-complete-wit.text: Automatic defeat reversal with surgical recovery guidance propagates through topology-complete inconsistency-safe cascades — recovery reaches all transitively affected nodes including outlist-connected ones, handles dangling references gracefully, and provides restoration hints targeting only cascade victims with surviving premises.

justifications.label: Defeat reversal (automatic with guided recovery from depth-4) composes with topology completeness (inconsistency-safe from depth-4) into robust complete recovery that strengthens the existing depth-3 belief defeat-reversal-propagates-automatically by adding topology completeness and dangling-reference resilience

defeat-reversal-propagates-automatically.text: All outlist-based defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) not only reverse in principle but propagate recovery automatically through safe terminating BFS — when a defeating node is retracted, the outlist entry becomes satisfied, and propagation cascades truth-value restoration to all affected nodes without manual re-assertion

justifications.label: Defeat reversibility (outlist semantics flip truth without destroying structure) plus safe propagation (BFS with guaranteed termination) should yield automatic recovery — but only if outlist nodes are tracked in the dependents index so that retracting a defeating node triggers propagation to the defeated nodes

defeat-reversal-with-guided-recovery.text: All defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) are reversible through outlist semantics, and the system provides surgical restoration hints for cascade victims with viable recovery paths — enabling guided recovery from retraction cascades where multi-premise justifications have surviving premises.

justifications.label: Reversible defeat (depth-1) plus surgical hints (depth-0) provide both mechanism and guidance for recovery — unless missing outlist tracking leaves some cascade effects undetected and therefore unguided

defeat-reversals-are-guided-recovery-com.text: Backend-agnostic lifecycle-governed defeat reversals are guided-recovery-complete because they are paired with topology-complete guided recovery.

justifications.label: Links backend-agnostic outlist defeat reversal governance to the guided-recovery completeness result.

defeat-reversals-are-lifecycle-governed.text: All outlist-based defeat reversals (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) operate within metadata-enabled lifecycle governance — every reversal produces not just a truth-value change but a fully governed lifecycle transition with metadata-tracked state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags), ensuring reversals are first-class lifecycle events rather than bare truth flips.

justifications.label: reversible defeats + metadata governance = reversals are governed lifecycle transitions

defeat-reversals-are-lifecycle-governed-.text: All outlist-based defeat reversals (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) operate within metadata-enabled lifecycle governance and maintain safety across all architectural layers and storage backends — the same lifecycle state transitions and safety guarantees hold regardless of whether backed by SQLite or PostgreSQL

justifications.label: Lifecycle governance of defeat reversals is backend-independent — SQLite and PostgreSQL provide equivalent mechanisms

defeat-reversals-have-lifecycle-governed.text: Outlist defeat reversals remain lifecycle-governed across all backends while producing topology-complete and traceable truth effects.

justifications.label: Combines backend-wide lifecycle governance of defeat reversals with topology-complete traceable truth propagation.

defeat-uses-outlist.text: The defeat API appends the defeater ID to a justification’s `outlist` rather than deleting or rewriting the justification.

defeat-with-scope-cascades-to-dependents.text: Defeating a node through scope beliefs propagates `OUT` to nodes whose justifications depend on the defeated node.

defeat-with-scope-creates-derived-defeat.text: The defeater node created by `defeat_with_scope` has an SL justification over scope beliefs; it is not a premise, which is what makes the defeat reversible.
`defeat_with_scope` creates scope-belief premise nodes and a derived defeater whose SL justification cites all scope beliefs, making the defeat reversible by retracting any scope belief.

defeat-with-scope-creates-scope-beliefs-.text: Each scope finding produces one `IN` premise node with no justifications and metadata linking it to the antecedent and defeater.

defeat-with-scope-does-not-link-antecede.text: Scope belief nodes are created as premises with no justification dependency on the `antecedent` node referenced in their ID and text.

defeat-with-scope-emits-pubsub-events-on.text: When pubsub subscribers exist, the write path computes truth-value changes from the `_before` snapshot and publishes them after a successful save.

defeat-with-scope-error-contract.text: `defeat_with_scope` raises `KeyError` for an unknown `node_id`, `ValueError` for no justifications, `IndexError` for an out-of-range `justification_index`, and `ValueError` for empty `scope_findings`.

defeat-with-scope-is-atomic-on-exception.text: Any exception raised inside the write context prevents `Storage.save` and cache updates, because `_with_network.__exit__` only persists when `exc_type is None`.

defeat-with-scope-requires-non-empty-fin.text: `defeat_with_scope` raises `ValueError` (message matches "scope_findings must not be empty") when the `scope_findings` parameter is an empty list, in addition to the standard KeyError/ValueError/IndexError for missing node, no justifications, and out-of-range index.

defeat-with-scope-requires-nonempty-scop.text: Passing an empty `scope_findings` list raises `ValueError` before any mutation.

defeat-with-scope-returns-scope-belief-i.text: `defeat_with_scope` returns `scope_belief_ids` in the same order as the input `scope_findings` list.

defeat-with-scope-validates-inputs-with-.text: Missing targets raise `KeyError`, no-justification targets and empty findings raise `ValueError`, and invalid indices raise `IndexError`.

defeater-classification-requires-defeats.text: An outlist node becomes `Defeated by` only when its `defeats_node` metadata matches the current node ID; otherwise it is exported under `Unless`.

defeater-classifications-are-not-persist.text: ANY/ALL/MIXED classification results are produced as ephemeral output and are not written back to any schema column.

defeater-default-id-is-deterministic.text: When `defeater_id` is not provided, the system generates a default ID following the exact pattern `{defeater_type}-{target_node_id}-j{justification_index}` (e.g., `over-generalizes-belief-j0`).

defeater-default-id-pattern.text: When `defeater_id` is omitted, `defeat_justification` generates the defeater ID as `"{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{index}"`.

defeater-export-tests-call-recompute-all.text: All three defeater/outlist tests call `Network.recompute_all()` before invoking `export_markdown`.

defeater-id-composed-from-type-node-and-.text: Defeater IDs are deterministically composed from `defeater_type`, node ID, and justification index.

defeater-id-default-format.text: A defeater's default ID is `{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{justification_index}`, overridable via `defeater_id`.

defeater-is-first-class-graph-node.text: A defeater created by `defeat_justification` is a full first-class node in the belief graph with its own `truth_value` ("IN"), metadata, deterministic ID, and is exportable via `export_network` and retractable via `retract_node` like any other node — not a side-table, annotation, or flag.

defeater-justifications-reference-scope-.text: The defeater node’s SL justification `antecedents` list contains the generated scope belief IDs.

defeater-metadata-keys-identify-target.text: Every defeater node created by `defeat_justification` carries metadata keys `defeater_type`, `defeats_node`, and `defeats_justification`.

defeater-metadata-records-defeats-node-a.text: A defeater node stores `defeater_type`, `defeats_node`, and `defeats_justification` in its metadata.

defeater-type-affects-defeater-id.text: `defeater_type` is embedded in the defeater node ID (`f"{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{justification_index}"` at `reasons/api.py:1372, 1470`), so it is part of node identity, not just metadata.

defeater-type-defaults-to-invalid-infere.text: The default `defeater_type` is `"invalid-inference"` in both defeat API functions (api.py:1326, 1419) and their CLI wrappers (cli.py:208, 260, 2493, 2500).

defeater-type-enables-classification-fil.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` accepts `defeater_type_filter` and skips candidates whose `defeater_type` does not match (`api.py:1688–1689`), as covered by `tests/test_classify_defeaters.py:test_filters_by_defeater_type`.

defeater-type-filter-matches-existing-me.text: `defeater_type_filter` matches against the defeater node's existing `defeater_type`, not the new `defeat_reason_type`.

defeater-type-filters-classification-can.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` accepts a `defeater_type_filter` and records candidates with non-matching `defeater_type` as skipped rather than classifying them.

defeater-type-filters-classification-sco.text: `defeater_type_filter` in `classify_defeat_reason_types` restricts which defeaters are sent to the LLM (api.py:1688–1689), exposed to users via `cli.py:3163` `--type`.

defeater-type-participates-in-id-constru.text: `defeater_type` is embedded in the defeater node ID as `f"{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{justification_index}"`, so changing it renames the defeater node.

defeater-types-are-enumerated.text: Exactly four defeater types are recognized and stored in `metadata["defeater_type"]`: `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`.

defeater-types-are-four.text: The known `defeater_type` values exercised are `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`.

defeater-types-roundtrip-through-metadat.text: The defeat API accepts defeater types `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`, and stores the supplied value verbatim in `metadata.defeater_type`.

defeater-vs-regular-outlist-rendering.text: An outlist entry renders as `- Defeated by: <id> (<type>)` if and only if the referenced node carries `defeater_type` metadata; otherwise it renders as `- Unless: <id>`, and the two formats never appear for the same entry.

defeater-vs-unless-disambiguated-by-defe.text: An outlist id is treated as `Defeated by` only when the corresponding node's `metadata["defeats_node"]` equals the current node's id; otherwise it becomes `Unless`.

defeats-node-enables-defeater-classifica.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` requires `metadata["defeats_node"]` to identify defeater nodes and to fetch the defeated text for the LLM (`api.py:1683, 1699`).

defeats-node-is-required-for-classificat.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` skips any node without a `defeats_node` metadata entry (api.py:1683).

defeats-node-metadata-is-consumed-by-api.text: API code scans `metadata["defeats_node"]`, and both `build_wiki` and `export_markdown` also read that metadata key to resolve defeat relationships.

defeats-node-required-for-defeater-class.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` uses `metadata["defeats_node"]` to identify defeater nodes and to fetch the defeated node's text for LLM classification; nodes without it are skipped.

defend-delegates-to-challenge.text: `Network.defend(target_id, challenge_id, ...)` is implemented by calling `challenge(challenge_id, ...)`, treating a defense as a challenge against the challenge node.

defend-invalidates-challenge-by-node-mec.text: After `defend`, the challenge node is `OUT` and the target is `IN`, demonstrating defense is an ordinary TMS invalidation rather than a special-cased mutation (`test_defend_restores_target`).

defend-invalidation-is-duplicate.text: This is already covered by the existing `defend-is-recursive-challenge` belief.

defend-is-challenge-applied-to-challenge.text: The `defend` operation is implemented as `challenge()` applied to the challenge node itself, not as an independent mechanism; this makes dialectical defense a uniform instance of the same outlist-injection primitive.

defend-is-challenge-of-challenge.text: `defend` works by calling `challenge` on the challenge node itself, creating a recursive dialectical structure where truth values resolve automatically through the same outlist mechanism.

defend-is-recursive-challenge.text: Defense is implemented by calling `challenge()` on the challenge node itself, enabling arbitrarily deep dialectical chains using the same outlist mechanism recursively with no special-case code

defend-retracts-challenge-not-target.text: `PgApi.defend(target, challenge_id, ...)` brings `target` back IN by retracting `challenge_id`, so with multiple outstanding challenges the target remains OUT until every challenge is defended (`TestDefend.test_defend_multiple_challenges`).

defend-retracts-challenge-to-restore-tar.text: `Network.defend(target, challenge_id, reason)` creates a `defense-<challenge_id>` node with `truth_value == IN` and flips `challenge_id` OUT, which re-satisfies the target's outlist and restores it to IN.

defense-id-is-derived-from-challenge-id.text: The default defense node ID is `defense-<challenge_id>`, making the defense's identity a deterministic function of the challenge it neutralizes.

defense-in-depth-is-resource-efficient.text: The system's defense-in-depth across LLM and system boundaries — layered defenses including bounded execution, fail-soft error handling, process isolation, and referential integrity validation — achieves comprehensive protection within the same resource-efficient pipeline that spans packaging, startup, and runtime with zero external dependencies and lazy loading.

justifications.label: Defense-in-depth (depth-5) and resource efficiency (depth-4) arise from independent architectural chains; their combination shows comprehensive security does not require unbounded resource consumption

defense-in-depth-spans-llm-and-system-bo.text: Defense-in-depth is enforced at every external interface through two independently-established layers: LLM integration applies layered defenses across application and process isolation boundaries (bounded execution, fail-soft handling, subprocess isolation), while all system boundaries simultaneously enforce strict validation, evolution tolerance, and resource constraints.

justifications.label: LLM-specific defense-in-depth and general boundary enforcement are independently comprehensive — together they show no external interface lacks layered protection.

defense-is-challenge-to-challenge.text: `Network.defend()` is implemented as `challenge(challenge_id, ...)`, making a defense a challenge to the original challenge node.

deferred-imports-for-llm-modules.text: Same architectural pattern already captured by `api-uses-lazy-imports`; the cli.py instance follows the same rationale.

deferred-retraction-ordering.text: During agent import, nodes are added and truth values propagated before explicit retractions are applied, ensuring the dependency graph is fully wired before OUT transitions are forced.

dependency-completeness-enables-accurate.text: Complete dependency tracking for all reference types — both antecedent and outlist entries maintained eagerly by every network mutation — ensures deduplication accurately reflects the complete network topology: survivor selection considers all incoming dependencies including outlist references, and reference rewiring targets both antecedent and outlist positions across all justifications, preventing dedup from creating dangling references or miscounting dependents.

justifications.label: Dedup accuracy is a downstream consequence of dependency tracking completeness — incomplete tracking would cause dedup to misjudge survivors or miss rewiring targets

dependency-completeness-enables-dedup-fo.text: Complete dependency tracking for all reference types — both antecedent and outlist references in the dependents index — enables deduplication to reflect the dependency mechanism it actually uses: auto-dedup keeps the node with the most dependents (ties broken lexicographically), and retraction rewrites both antecedent and outlist references to the survivor, preventing dangling references and miscounting dependents without claiming global structural optimality.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

dependency-tracking-is-complete-for-all-.text: The dependents index fully tracks all relationship types — both antecedent references and outlist references — enabling complete incremental propagation for every truth value change without requiring periodic full recompute as a fallback

justifications.label: Mutations maintain dependents and outlist semantics are fully specified, so if outlist nodes were tracked in the dependents index, incremental propagation would reach all affected nodes — the gap is the sole obstacle to complete incremental consistency

dependent-count-is-len-dependents-in-net.text: `reasons/network.py:372` computes dependent count as `len(self.nodes[premise_id].dependents)` in the same retraction path that calls `_entrenchment`.

dependents-bidirectional-index.text: Each node maintains a `dependents` set (reverse of antecedent/outlist edges), eagerly maintained by `add_node`, `add_justification`, `supersede`, `challenge`, and `convert_to_premise`.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-index-covers-outlist.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `dependency-tracking-is-complete-for-all-reference-types`, `every-network-mutation-maintains-dependents-invariant`, and `rewrite-dependents-updates-both-antecedents-and-outlists` which already establish that both antecedent and outlist edges populate the dependents index.

dependents-index-derived-on-load.text: The `node.dependents` set is never persisted to SQLite; it is rebuilt by walking all justification antecedents and outlists during `load()`.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-index-is-a-reverse-index.text: Each `Node.dependents` set contains the nodes that list it as an antecedent **or** an outlist member, so outlist-only GATE nodes are indexed too (`test_outlist_dependency`, `test_both_antecedent_and_outlist`).

dependents-index-is-derived-from-justifi.text: The `dependents` reverse index is reconstructible via `_rebuild_dependents()` and validated by `verify_dependents()`; no independent source of truth exists.

dependents-index-is-fragile-denormalizat.text: The dependents set is a manually-maintained denormalized reverse index that is never persisted and must be rebuilt on every load, creating a consistency obligation on all mutation paths

justifications.label: Three beliefs triangulate the same fragility: any mutation path that forgets to update dependents silently corrupts propagation

dependents-index-is-reference-counted.text: a node remains in an antecedent's `dependents` set as long as *any* surviving justification references it.

dependents-index-maps-both-antecedent-an.text: `Y.dependents` contains X whenever X cites Y as an antecedent **or** as an outlist element (`reasons/api.py:2579-2582`, `tests/test_dependents_integrity.py:test_both_antecedent_and_outlist`).

dependents-index-remains-structural.text: `_retracted` does not remove the node from the reverse `dependents` set; the skip is a runtime propagation filter.

dependents-integrity-errors-distinguish-.text: `verify_dependents()` error strings distinguish bogus reverse entries containing `"extra"` from absent reverse entries containing `"missing"`.

dependents-is-a-denormalized-reverse-ind.text: `Node.dependents` is a `set[str]` that must mirror the inverse of all `antecedents` and `outlist` edges; this module never populates or checks it.

dependents-is-manual-reverse-index.text: `Node.dependents` is a denormalized reverse pointer set that must be kept in sync by external code (primarily `network.py`); nothing in the data model enforces consistency.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-not-self-enforced.text: The `Node.dependents` reverse index is not maintained by the data model itself; `network.py` is responsible for keeping it consistent with justification references (antecedents and outlists).

dependents-set-deduplicates-multiple-jus.text: Because `dependents` is a set, multiple justifications referencing the same antecedent produce a single reverse-index entry rather than duplicate entries.

dependents-survive-storage-roundtrip.text: After `Storage.save()` followed by `Storage.load()`, the loaded network's dependents index passes `verify_dependents()` with no errors.

dependents-tracks-outlist-entries.text: `outlist` entries are added to and removed from `dependents` the same way as `antecedents`.

depends-on-flattens-justifications.text: The `Depends on:` line concatenates antecedents across every justification without dedup or type/label markers, conflating alternate (OR) support with a single dependency list.

deprecated-aliases-are-undocumented-cli-.text: The only two real deprecation markers in the codebase are `--domain-id` (reasons/cli.py:3064) and the `research` subcommand alias for `repair` (reasons/cli.py:3854), and both have zero mentions in README.md or SKILL.md

deprecated-cli-aliases-are-undocumented.text: The only real code deprecations are the `--domain-id` argument alias and the `research` subcommand alias for `repair`, and neither is documented in `README.md` or `SKILL.md`.

deprecated-cli-aliases-remain-functional.text: Both deprecated CLI aliases remain functional: `--project-id` parses as a normal option and `research` is a fully defined subparser.

deprecated-string-matches-are-unrelated-.text: Occurrences of `deprecated` in canonical code refer to CLI/domain aliases and a heuristic word list, not to `reasons_lib` import deprecation.

deprecation-is-not-runtime-signaled.text: The observed `deprecat` matches are limited to two CLI help strings and an unrelated `reasons/api.py:3919` word list; no runtime deprecation warning is observed.

deprecation-marker-search-finds-no-reaso.text: The observed `deprecat` matches are unrelated CLI/API strings at `reasons/api.py:3919`, `reasons/cli.py:3064`, and `reasons/cli.py:3854`.

deprecation-runtime-warning-claim-is-dup.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that importing `reasons_lib` emits no deprecation warning.

depth-code-duplicated-across-files.text: The same memoized depth pattern appears in `api.py`, `derive.py`, `export_card.py`, and `repair.py`.

depth-functions-overwrite-placeholder-af.text: After visiting antecedents, the helpers overwrite the placeholder with `max_d + 1`.

depth-helpers-overwrite-zero-placeholder.text: After visiting antecedents, the depth helpers overwrite the placeholder with `max_d + 1`.

depth-helpers-write-zero-before-recursin.text: The memoized depth helpers in `api`, `derive`, `export_card`, and `repair` set `memo[nid] = 0` before recursing to mark an in-progress node.

depth-memo-is-keyed-only-by-node-id.text: The memo cache does not distinguish “visiting” from “finished” and is not parameterized by root or traversal order.

depth-memo-keyed-only-by-node-id.text: The depth memo cache is keyed only by node id and does not distinguish in-progress from finished nodes or traversal roots.

depth-memo-order-dependent-under-cycles.text: Memoized max-depth can become order-dependent on cyclic graphs because the zero in-progress marker is observable through back-edges.

depth-memo-pattern-duplicated-across-fou.text: The same memoized depth pattern appears in `reasons/api.py`, `reasons/derive.py`, `reasons/export_card.py`, and `reasons/repair.py`.

depth-order-dependence-requires-cycles.text: In an acyclic graph, memoized max-depth should be order-independent; order-dependence appears when the zero placeholder is read through a cycle.

derive-achieves-flexibility-with-reprodu.text: The derive pipeline resolves the tension between strategic flexibility and deterministic reproducibility: three budget strategies (alphabetical truncation, random sampling, semantic clustering) provide diverse exploration approaches, while fixed-seed deterministic sampling and accurate proportional allocation ensure each strategy produces identical results across runs.

justifications.label: multiple strategies with deterministic seeds = flexibility without sacrificing reproducibility

derive-agent-budget-proportional.text: When agents are present, `_build_beliefs_section` allocates prompt token budget proportionally to each agent's belief count, with a floor of 5 beliefs per agent

derive-agent-budget-proportional-formula.text: The agent belief budget in `_build_beliefs_section` is computed as `max(5, int(max_beliefs * len(agent_beliefs) / total_all))`.

derive-agent-count-bug.text: `_build_beliefs_section` has a bug: `count += len(belief_ids)` is inside the per-belief loop instead of outside it, inflating the count and shrinking the non-agent budget below intended size

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #33

derive-agent-count-increment-moved-outsi.text: `_build_beliefs_section` was fixed by moving the belief-count increment outside the per-belief loop, preventing count inflation and non-agent budget shrinkage.

derive-apply-auto-stamps-source-type-der.text: `apply_proposals` unconditionally sets `metadata["source_type"] = "derived"` on every newly created derived node, regardless of what the proposing LLM or caller specifies in the proposal dict.

derive-apply-fail-soft.text: Duplicates the existing belief `derive-apply-isolates-per-proposal-errors` which already captures that `apply_proposals` catches exceptions per-proposal.

derive-apply-is-isolated-and-caller-vali.text: The derive apply stage achieves defense-in-depth: callers must run validation before apply (trust boundary), and even if invalid proposals reach apply, each proposal is wrapped in independent error handling so one failure cannot corrupt the batch.

justifications.label: Validation-before-apply establishes the trust contract; per-proposal isolation provides the safety net when the contract is violated

derive-apply-isolates-per-proposal-error.text: `apply_proposals` wraps each `api.add_node()` call in try/except and accumulates `(proposal, error_string)` tuples, so one malformed proposal does not abort the batch.

derive-apply-tags-source-type-as-derived.text: `apply_proposals` in `reasons/derive.py` calls `api.add_node()` with `source_type="derived"` for every accepted proposal, marking the provenance of the belief so downstream tooling can distinguish LLM-derived beliefs from observations or imports.

derive-auto-assigns-derived-source-type.text: `apply_proposals` stamps generated derivation nodes with `source_type="derived"` without caller input.

derive-auto-writes-json-round-report.text: derive --auto writes a JSON report with round-by-round stats, and --no-report suppresses the report.

derive-budget-agent-match-uses-startswit.text: `_build_beliefs_section` identifies agent beliefs by checking whether node IDs start with the agent name followed by a colon.

derive-budget-allocation-is-accurate.text: The derive pipeline's proportional belief-budget allocation produces correct per-agent token counts

justifications.label: Budget allocation is correct only when the belief count is correct; the per-belief loop count bug inflates counts and distorts proportional allocation

derive-budget-allocation-is-proportional.text: When agent namespaces are detected, _build_beliefs_section allocates the belief budget proportionally by agent size.

derive-budget-ceiling-enforced.text: In `_build_beliefs_section`, the sum of agent-shown and local-shown beliefs never exceeds `max_beliefs`.

derive-budget-ceiling-invariant.text: `_build_beliefs_section` enforces that the combined count of agent-shown and local-shown beliefs never exceeds the configured `max_beliefs` budget.

derive-budget-count-accumulates-across-a.text: Agent belief count in `_build_beliefs_section` accumulates across all agents rather than resetting per agent.

derive-budget-count-is-linear.text: Agent belief counting in `_build_beliefs_section` accumulates as N (number of beliefs shown per agent), not N² — the corrected behavior after the issue #23 fix where `count += len(belief_ids)` was moved outside the per-belief loop

derive-budget-floor-five.text: Each agent group and the non-agent group are guaranteed at least 5 belief slots in the prompt regardless of proportional budget allocation.

derive-budget-is-efficient-and-floor-bou.text: The derive pipeline's per-agent budget allocation is both computationally efficient (O(N) linear accumulation, not quadratic) and representation-safe (each agent and local group guaranteed at least 5 belief slots), ensuring proportional allocation never starves minority agents.

justifications.label: Linear counting ensures scalability while floor guarantees ensure minimum representation — together they make budget allocation both performant and fair

derive-budget-is-flexible-and-efficient.text: The derive pipeline's budget allocation is both strategically flexible (three selection strategies: alphabetical truncation, random sampling, semantic clustering) and computationally efficient (linear accumulation with guaranteed floor of 5 per agent group), enabling callers to trade off reproducibility, diversity, and semantic coherence without performance penalty.

justifications.label: Strategy flexibility (what to select) and computational efficiency (how fast selection runs) are independently established — combining them shows the system avoids the usual flexibility-performance tradeoff

derive-budget-local-floor-is-five.text: `_build_beliefs_section` guarantees at least 5 local beliefs are shown regardless of agent budget pressure, via `max(5, max_beliefs - count)`

derive-budget-local-remainder-formula.text: When enough local beliefs exist, `_build_beliefs_section` sets `local_shown` to `max(5, max_beliefs - agent_total)`.

derive-budget-proportional-allocation-mi.text: When multiple agents contribute beliefs, `build_prompt` divides prompt budget proportionally to each agent's belief count with a minimum floor of 5.

derive-budget-sampling-is-seed-determini.text: In sample mode, `_build_beliefs_section` produces identical output across calls when given the same random seed.

derive-budget-section-handles-empty-inpu.text: `_build_beliefs_section` returns a valid formatted string for empty nodes, empty agents, or agents pointing to missing nodes.

derive-budget-tests-parse-header-format.text: Test infrastructure coupling detail (regex parsing of `_build_beliefs_section` headers), not a production code invariant.

derive-budget-tests-parse-output-headers.text: Test implementation detail (regex parsing of `"showing N"` headers), not a production code invariant

derive-budget-three-strategies.text: `_build_beliefs_section` supports three budget strategies — alphabetical truncation (default), random sampling (`sample=True`), and semantic clustering (`cluster=True`) — all controlled by a single `max_beliefs` parameter.

derive-build-beliefs-groups-by-id-prefix.text: Without agents, `_build_beliefs_section` groups beliefs by the first ID segment before `-`.

derive-build-prompt-default-budget-is-30.text: build_prompt has a default budget of 300 beliefs.

derive-build-prompt-returns-prompt-and-s.text: `build_prompt` returns a tuple of prompt text and a stats dict.

derive-build-prompt-wraps-template-forma.text: `build_prompt` catches `KeyError` and `ValueError` from `str.format()` and suppresses the original traceback with `from None`.

derive-cluster-and-sample-are-mutually-e.text: `cmd_derive` exits with code 1 if both `--cluster`/`--intra-cluster` and `--sample` are supplied, before making any API call.

derive-cluster-import-is-lazy.text: `cluster` is imported lazily inside `_build_beliefs_section` only when `cluster=True`.

derive-cross-agent-task-injected-when-mu.text: `CROSS_AGENT_TASK` is injected into the derive prompt only when multi-agent beliefs are detected.

derive-default-budget-groups-by-kebab-pr.text: In default budget mode, `_build_beliefs_section` groups beliefs by kebab-case ID prefix and outputs groups largest first, truncating at budget.

derive-delegates-llm-invocation-to-calle.text: `reasons/derive.py` owns prompt construction, response parsing, validation, and persistence but does NOT perform the LLM call itself — the `invoke_model` call is made by `api.py` or `cli.py`, which import and orchestrate the derive pipeline stages.

derive-depth-counts-only-antecedents.text: `_get_depth` counts only justification antecedents when computing derivation depth and deliberately ignores outlist edges.

derive-depth-cycle-guard.text: `_get_depth` sets `memo[node_id] = 0` before recursing to prevent infinite recursion on cyclic justification chains; cycles resolve to depth 0

derive-depth-cycle-guard-returns-zero.text: _get_depth sets memo[node_id] = 0 before recursing into antecedents, so circular justification chains terminate with depth 0 rather than infinite recursion.

derive-depth-cycle-guard-sets-memo-befor.text: `_get_depth` in `reasons/derive.py` sets `memo[node_id] = 0` *before* recursing into antecedents, so a cyclic justification graph resolves the back-edge to depth 0 rather than causing infinite recursion.

derive-depth-is-max-antecedent-depth-plu.text: Premises have depth 0 and derived nodes have depth equal to the maximum antecedent depth plus 1.

derive-depth-memoizes-and-guards-cycles.text: _get_depth memoizes computed depths and sets memo[node_id] to 0 before recursion as a cycle guard.

derive-depth-premises-zero-derived-one-p.text: `_get_depth` assigns premises depth 0 and derived nodes depth 1 plus the maximum antecedent depth, using memoization.

derive-derived-section-sorts-deepest-fir.text: `_build_derived_section` renders existing derived conclusions sorted by depth deepest first, showing status, antecedents, and outlist.

derive-detect-agents-skips-active.text: `_detect_agents` identifies multi-agent networks by colon-namespaced IDs and skips `:active` premise nodes when scanning.

derive-detect-agents-skips-active-sentin.text: `_detect_agents` identifies agent namespaces from colon-separated node IDs and skips `:active` sentinel nodes.

derive-enforces-budget.text: Forward derivation is bounded by a configurable budget (`test_derive_budget.py`), so any new derivation rule must be budget-aware.

derive-exhaust-iterates-until-no-new-pro.text: The derive --exhaust option iterates until the LLM produces no new proposals.

derive-exhaust-run-added-119-derived-bel.text: A derive --exhaust run of 10 rounds added 119 new derived beliefs to the network.

derive-fail-soft-validation.text: `validate_proposals` filters invalid proposals into a skipped list rather than raising; `apply_proposals` catches per-item exceptions so one bad proposal never blocks others

derive-gate-proposals-normalize-to-unles.text: `derive.py` parses both `### DERIVE` and `### GATE` proposal headers and maps a GATE proposal’s `Unless:` list into the proposal’s `unless` field, which becomes outlist support.

derive-has-dependents-includes-outlist-r.text: `build_prompt` treats a node as having dependents if it appears in any justification’s outlist, not only in antecedents.

derive-imports-unused-subprocess-sys-pat.text: `derive.py` imports `subprocess`, `sys`, and `Path` but does not use them.

derive-local-budget-has-floor-of-five.text: The derive prompt builder gives the local-belief section at least 5 slots even when agent sections consume the nominal budget.

derive-maps-llm-mode-any-to-any-mode.text: `derive.py` maps an LLM proposal `Mode: ANY` to `any_mode=True`.

derive-min-antecedents-is-prompt-only.text: The minimum-2-antecedents rule for derived beliefs is enforced only by the LLM prompt instructions, not validated in code by `validate_proposals`.

derive-min-antecedents-is-soft-constrain.text: The requirement that derived beliefs use ≥ 2 antecedents is enforced only through the prompt instruction to the LLM; `validate_proposals` does not check antecedent count, so a single-antecedent proposal will pass code-level validation.

derive-module-observation-lacks-trace-sl.text: The observed portion of `reasons/derive.py` contains no `trace` logic and no exact `sl` matches; SL appears only in prompt text.

derive-no-llm-call.text: `derive.py` builds prompts and parses responses but never calls an LLM itself; the caller (CLI or API) is responsible for the model invocation.

derive-one-round-return-protocol.text: The key invariant (negative = error) is captured by existing `derive-round-returns-negative-on-error`; positive = count added and 0 = saturated are the obvious complement.

derive-parse-distinguishes-derive-and-ga.text: `parse_proposals` distinguishes DERIVE proposals from GATE proposals, where GATE proposals supply outlist entries.

derive-parse-proposals-backward-compat.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new `### DERIVE id` format first and falls back to the legacy `### DERIVE: \`id\`` format with bold markdown labels, so it can consume outputs from any version.

derive-parse-proposals-is-regex-not-json.text: `derive.py:parse_proposals` extracts proposals via `re.finditer` on a markdown format and does not invoke `json`.

derive-parse-returns-empty-list-on-no-ma.text: parse_proposals silently returns an empty list when the LLM response matches neither the new nor old proposal format.

derive-parse-strips-backticks.text: `parse_proposals` strips backticks from proposal IDs and antecedent IDs.

derive-parse-supports-two-format-version.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new `### DERIVE id` format first, falling back to the older `### DERIVE: \`id\`` format only when the new parser returns zero matches.

derive-parse-supports-two-formats.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new format first (v0.10+: `### DERIVE id`), falls back to old format (v0.9: `### DERIVE: \`id\``) only when no new-format matches are found

derive-parser-falls-back-to-legacy-forma.text: parse_proposals tries the current ### DERIVE format first and only falls back to the legacy bold-field format if zero matches are found.

derive-parser-supports-legacy-and-backti.text: `parse_proposals` accepts both current `### DERIVE`/`### GATE` markdown blocks and legacy `### DERIVE:`/`**Antecedents**:` format, stripping backticks from IDs and lists.

derive-parser-supports-legacy-format-fal.text: `parse_proposals` in `reasons/derive.py` tries the v0.10+ regex pattern (`### DERIVE <id>`) first, then falls back to the v0.9 regex (`### DERIVE: \`belief-id\``), ensuring backward compatibility with previously-generated or user-edited files.

derive-parser-supports-two-formats.text: `parse_proposals` supports a new v0.10+ format and an old v0.9 format, falling back to the old format only when the new format yields no matches.

derive-pipeline-achieves-end-to-end-faul.text: The derive pipeline achieves end-to-end fault tolerance through three independent layers: proactive defense (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), reactive resilience (partial results persisted via JSON reports after each round, error states signaled through return codes), and prompt reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds enables consistent re-runs after failures).

justifications.label: proactive defense + reactive resilience + reproducible re-runs = end-to-end fault tolerance

derive-pipeline-constraints-are-structur.text: The derive pipeline enforces its structural constraints at the code level — fail-soft validation filters invalid proposals, and application explicitly tags source-type as "derived" — BUT the min-antecedents constraint is only enforced at the prompt level, leaving a gap where structurally-valid but semantically-weak proposals can pass.

justifications.label: The code-level enforcement (validation filtering + explicit tagging) establishes structural constraints; the gate acknowledges that the min-antecedents semantic constraint is not code-enforced, limiting the claim's scope.

derive-pipeline-has-complete-coverage.text: The derive pipeline achieves complete coverage along three axes: safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination), and production-readiness (accurate proportional budgets, roundtrippable prompt format).

justifications.label: Two independently-established depth-2 properties (safety+completeness and production-readiness) unify into full pipeline coverage — connecting the previously-orphaned derive-pipeline-is-safe-and-complete

derive-pipeline-has-end-to-end-quality-e.text: The derive pipeline achieves end-to-end quality enforcement: defensive validation prevents invalid proposals, Jaccard retraction guards prevent re-derivation of known-bad conclusions, budget allocation is accurate, AND the minimum-antecedents rule for derived beliefs is enforced in code — not just as an LLM prompt instruction that can be ignored.

justifications.label: Defensive validation (depth-1) and production readiness (depth-2) establish pipeline quality, but true end-to-end enforcement requires the min-antecedents rule to be validated in code rather than relying solely on LLM prompt compliance

derive-pipeline-is-defensive.text: The derive pipeline applies multiple defensive measures: fail-soft validation, Jaccard-based retraction guard, and environment variable stripping to prevent recursive spawning

justifications.label: Each defense addresses a distinct failure mode (bad proposals, re-derivation of retracted beliefs, infinite recursion)

derive-pipeline-is-error-accumulating.text: Covered by existing `derive-fail-soft-validation` (validation returns skipped entries with reasons) and `derive-pipeline-is-defensive` (broader defensive characterization)

derive-pipeline-is-exhaustive-and-termin.text: The derive pipeline supports exhaustive exploration mode while guaranteeing termination: `--exhaust` enables automatic application of all discovered proposals, and depth-based cycle detection with pre-recursion memoization prevents infinite loops even when justification chains are cyclic.

justifications.label: Depth-1 — completeness mode (exhaust) and termination guarantee (cycle guard) together yield the strongest usable exploration strategy: explore everything, stop safely

derive-pipeline-is-production-ready.text: The derive pipeline correctly allocates budgets, validates proposals defensively, and produces well-formed beliefs through a round-trippable prompt contract.

justifications.label: The pipeline's defensive validation and prompt contract provide production-grade reliability, but the count-accumulation bug in `_build_beliefs_section` undermines budget accuracy

derive-pipeline-is-reproducible-and-defe.text: The derive pipeline achieves both reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation) and defense-in-depth at the application stage (validation-before-apply trust boundary with per-proposal error isolation), ensuring pipeline runs are repeatable and any surviving bad proposal cannot corrupt sibling proposals.

justifications.label: Reproducibility guarantees identical inputs across runs; application isolation guarantees safe outputs regardless of individual proposal quality — two orthogonal quality axes covering the full pipeline.

derive-pipeline-is-reproducible-and-full.text: The derive pipeline achieves quadruple assurance: reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation), safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination), and efficiency (O(N) budget accumulation with guaranteed floor) — four independently established properties reinforcing pipeline trustworthiness.

justifications.label: Reproducibility and defense-in-depth combine with safety, completeness, and efficiency for full pipeline assurance

derive-pipeline-is-safe-and-complete.text: The derive pipeline simultaneously provides safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation) and completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed cycle-free termination), ensuring LLM-driven belief generation discovers all derivable conclusions without corruption risk.

justifications.label: Defensive validation prevents harmful output while exhaustive mode with cycle guard ensures the derivation space is fully explored (depth-2)

derive-pipeline-is-safe-complete-and-eff.text: The derive pipeline simultaneously achieves safety (fail-soft validation with Jaccard retraction guards and environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination via cycle guards), and efficiency (linear O(N) budget accumulation with a floor of 5 beliefs per agent preventing representation starvation).

justifications.label: Safety+completeness and efficiency are independently established — together they show the derive pipeline is production-ready across all quality dimensions.

derive-pipeline-provides-three-level-ope.text: The derive pipeline exposes its operational state at three independent granularities: per-item error accumulation in the skipped list (fine-grained), partial JSON reports written after each round (medium-grained, crash-surviving), and a return code of -1/0/positive-N (coarse-grained completion signal).

justifications.label: Convergent observability — each mechanism independently provides a distinct level of operational visibility; even if one is unavailable (e.g., reports disk full), the other two still communicate pipeline state to callers and operators.

derive-produces-new-beliefs.text: `derive.py` writes newly inferred beliefs into `storage` rather than returning transient results, so derivations are auditable.

derive-prompt-detects-multi-agent-networ.text: build_prompt detects multi-agent networks and adjusts the prompt accordingly.

derive-prompt-is-deterministic-and-repro.text: The derive pipeline's prompt construction is fully reproducible: deterministic sampling with fixed seeds selects consistent belief subsets, and accurate proportional budget allocation ensures each agent receives the same token share across runs.

justifications.label: Deterministic sampling plus accurate budgets yield reproducible derive prompts

derive-prompt-round-trippable.text: `write_proposals_file` output can be parsed back by `parse_proposals` with no data loss, enabling a write-review-accept cycle where humans edit proposals in the same format the parser reads

derive-prompt-roundtrips-through-parser.text: The `### DERIVE` / `### GATE` format is a shared contract between `DERIVE_PROMPT` LLM output, `parse_proposals()` input, and `write_proposals_file()` output, forming a closed serialization loop

derive-proposal-parser-extracts-antecede.text: `parse_proposals` maps `Antecedents:` and `Label:` lines into proposal fields and strips backticks.

derive-proposal-persistence-via-add-node.text: The entry infers but does not show the code that persists parsed proposals via `api.add_node`, so that persistence path is not a confirmed claim.

derive-proposals-file-roundtrips-through.text: write_proposals_file output parses identically through parse_proposals.
`write_proposals_file` serializes valid proposals to the same `### DERIVE` and `### GATE` markdown format that `parse_proposals` can re-read for human review.

derive-quality-is-comprehensively-code-e.text: All derive pipeline quality constraints — structural validation, retraction guards, environment isolation, format contracts, AND minimum-antecedent requirements — are enforced through code-level validation, ensuring no invalid proposals can reach the database regardless of LLM prompt compliance.

justifications.label: Defensive code validation and the prompt/parser round-trip contract provide comprehensive code-level enforcement — but only once the minimum-antecedents rule is moved from prompt instructions to code validation

derive-report-json-has-rounds.text: The `derive` CLI with `--report-dir` writes a JSON file named `derive-<ts>.json` containing keys `status`, `model`, `exhaust`, `rounds`, and `total_added`; `--exhaust` appends a saturation round whose `added == 0`.

derive-report-json-has-rounds-array.text: The `reasons derive --auto --report-dir` command writes a JSON report containing a `rounds` array where each entry has `proposals_found` and `added` counts.

derive-reports-survive-partial-runs.text: `cmd_derive` and `cmd_review_beliefs` write partial JSON reports after each round/batch via `_write_derive_report`, so crash recovery is possible from the last completed step.

derive-resilience-preserves-progress-on-.text: The derive pipeline is resilient to partial failures: partial results are persisted via JSON reports after each round, and error states are signaled through return codes (-1 for error, 0 for saturation, positive for progress) rather than exceptions, enabling callers to recover and resume.

justifications.label: Two independently-established resilience properties (durable partial output + structured error signaling) combine to ensure no derivation work is lost on failure

derive-retraction-guard.text: Proposals whose ID has at least 50% Jaccard token overlap with any OUT node ID are rejected.

derive-retraction-guard-uses-jaccard.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposed belief ID with Jaccard similarity >= 0.5 to an existing OUT node, preventing re-derivation of retracted beliefs

derive-returns-negative-one-on-error.text: `_derive_one_round` returns -1 on error, 0 on saturation, and a positive int for the number of beliefs added, which `cmd_derive` uses to control the exhaust loop.

derive-review-contradict-is-convergent-c.text: The full belief maintenance cycle is `derive --exhaust → review-beliefs → retract invalid → contradictions → retract/fix/file → derive --exhaust`, where each tool catches a different error class (derive generates, review validates individual steps, contradictions finds cross-belief inconsistencies) and the cycle converges toward a stable belief set.

derive-round-return-codes-are-zero-satur.text: _derive_one_round returns 0 when derivation is saturated and -1 on error.

derive-round-returns-negative-on-error.text: `_derive_one_round` returns -1 on error, 0 on saturation, and a positive count on success — using return values instead of exceptions for flow control in the exhaust loop.

derive-sample-uses-reservoir-sampling.text: `_sample_beliefs` uses reservoir-style random sampling to stay within the token budget.

derive-sampling-uses-reservoir.text: `_sample_beliefs` uses reservoir-style random sampling to stay within token budgets and returns identity when the list is already under budget.

derive-shim-has-no-all.text: Already covered by existing `reasons-lib-is-uniform-star-reexport-shim` and related star-import beliefs.

derive-shim-import-executes-target-side-.text: Importing `reasons_lib.derive` causes `reasons.derive` module-level initialization/side effects to run once, not duplicated per import path.

derive-shim-name-rebinding-does-not-affe.text: Reassigning a name on `reasons_lib.derive` only changes the shim namespace; functions inside `reasons.derive` that reference their own module global continue to see the original binding.

derive-strips-claudecode-env.text: `_derive_one_round` explicitly removes the `CLAUDECODE` environment variable before spawning the model subprocess, preventing recursive Claude Code invocation.

derive-topic-filter-ors-keywords.text: `_filter_by_topic` treats space-separated keywords as OR conditions so any keyword match passes.

derive-topic-filter-uses-or-keyword-matc.text: `_filter_by_topic` keeps nodes whose ID or text matches any whitespace-separated topic keyword, using OR semantics.

derive-topic-filter-uses-or-semantics.text: `_filter_by_topic` matches space-separated terms case-insensitively against node ID and text, including a node if any keyword matches.

derive-unused-imports.text: Dead code observation (`subprocess`, `sys`, `Path` imported but unused) — unstable detail that will change when cleaned up.

derive-uses-subprocess-not-sdk.text: The derive command invokes LLMs by shelling out to `claude` or `gemini` CLI binaries via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, not through any Python SDK.

derive-validate-before-apply.text: `apply_proposals` trusts its input unconditionally; callers must run `validate_proposals` first or risk database errors from missing antecedents or duplicate IDs.

derive-validate-blocks-retracted-redisco.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose ID has >= 50% Jaccard token overlap (tokenized on hyphens/colons) with an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of previously retracted conclusions

derive-validate-rejects-duplicate-ids.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose belief ID already exists in the network, preventing overwrites of existing beliefs through the derive pipeline.

derive-validate-rejects-jaccard-similar-.text: validate_proposals skips any proposal whose ID has at least 50% Jaccard token similarity to an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of retracted conclusions.

derive-validate-rejects-missing-antecede.text: validate_proposals rejects proposals whose antecedent or outlist references do not exist in the current network.

derive-validate-rejects-similar-retracte.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposed belief whose tokenized ID has ≥50% Jaccard overlap with an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of retracted conclusions.

derive-validate-rejects-similar-to-out.text: Covered by existing `derive-retraction-guard-uses-jaccard` which captures the same invariant

derive-validate-requires-existing-antece.text: `validate_proposals` rejects a proposal if any antecedent or unless node does not exist in the network.

derive-validation-is-layered-with-semant.text: The derive pipeline's validation is stratified: structural validity (parse success, fail-soft filtering) and semantic similarity (Jaccard rejection of OUT-near-duplicates) are code-enforced, but the cardinality constraint (≥2 antecedents) is delegated to LLM prompt instructions, making the most semantically meaningful constraint the least code-enforced.

justifications.label: Three validation layers form a coherent stratification only when all three are present together; removing any one collapses the "layered" characterization into a flat claim.

derive-validation-requires-antecedent-ex.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose antecedents or unless-list reference nodes that are not present in the network.

derive-validation-requires-at-least-two-.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal with fewer than two antecedents as skipped.

derive-write-proposals-file-roundtrips-t.text: write_proposals_file serializes proposals to a markdown file in the same format parse_proposals() can read back, enabling human review before reasons accept.

derived-access-tags-union-antecedent-tag.text: Derived nodes' `metadata["access_tags"]` is the union of their explicit tags and all tags reachable through antecedent justifications, including transitive chains and diamond graphs.

derived-belief-pipeline-achieves-code-en.text: The derived belief pipeline — creation via defensive derivation with structural validation, Jaccard retraction guards, and environment isolation, followed by independent review with scope restricted to derived beliefs and mutation gated behind dry-run — achieves completely code-enforced quality assurance including logical soundness validation, only when inference soundness checking is implemented in code rather than relying solely on LLM prompt instructions.

justifications.label: Creation-phase structural safety + evaluation-phase scoped review achieve full code enforcement only when logical soundness moves from prompt-only to programmatic validation

derived-belief-soundness-is-llm-only.text: Structural validation ensures justification references exist and are IN, but the logical soundness of the inference from antecedents to derived conclusion is validated only by the proposing LLM — no code-level check verifies that the reasoning step is logically valid.

derived-claims-get-sl-justifications.text: Every `DERIVED` claim is imported with exactly one justification of `type == "SL"` whose `antecedents` equal the `Depends on:` list.

derived-node-evaluates-on-creation.text: Adding a derived node evaluates its justification immediately, and the new node starts OUT if its antecedents are OUT.

derived-node-merges-explicit-and-inherit.text: A derived node's effective `access_tags` merge any explicit tags declared on the node with the inherited tags from its antecedents.

derived-node-tracing-requires-sl-paramet.text: `test_trace_derived` and `test_derived_without_trace` both create their derived node via `api.add_node(..., sl=...)`, confirming `sl` is the field that encodes a node's antecedent edges.

derived-nodes-auto-set-source-type.text: Derivation code sets `source_type="derived"` in `reasons/derive.py`, so `derived` is system-generated as well as user-selectable.

derived-nodes-inherit-antecedent-tags.text: Derived nodes carry the union of their antecedents' `access_tags`, so `explain_node`'s `PermissionError` prevents leaking restricted antecedents via the explanation text.

derived-nodes-union-access-tags.text: A derived node’s `access_tags` is the union of its explicit tags and all antecedent tags across its justifications, and adding a justification can propagate new tags to dependents.

derived-section-includes-out-nodes.text: The derived section includes all filtered nodes with non-empty justifications, including OUT nodes, and labels their status.

design-doc-policy-evidence-missing.text: The docs search for `detected[-_]contradiction|auto[-_]accept|scrutiniz|cheap` returned zero matches, and `.claude/skills/reasons/SKILL.md` was not read.

detect-agents-excludes-active-sentinel.text: _detect_agents identifies colon-namespaced agent prefixes and excludes :active sentinel nodes from belief counts.

detect-contradictions-auto-apply-errors-.text: When `auto_apply=True`, per-contradiction application failures in `detect_contradictions` are caught, warned to stderr, and omitted from `applied_details`; the return dict has no error field.

detect-contradictions-auto-apply-mutates.text: With `auto_apply=True`, the call records nogoods via `add_nogood`, which can retract premises and cascade `IN → OUT` dependent beliefs.

detect-contradictions-auto-apply-swallow.text: Failures during `add_nogood` are printed to `stderr` and are not raised, and are not represented in the return dict (only detectable via `applied < found`).

detect-contradictions-delegates-to-contr.text: All detection, LLM batching, semantic clustering, and output-file writing live in `reasons/contradictions.py`; the wrapper only filters, samples, dispatches, and optionally applies.

detect-contradictions-empty-belief-ids-m.text: In `detect_contradictions`, an empty `belief_ids=[]` is falsy and means "no filter", so it checks all IN beliefs rather than none.

detect-contradictions-has-no-postgres-ba.text: Unlike most functions in `reasons/api.py`, this one omits `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` and therefore supports only the SQLite backend.

detect-contradictions-only-checks-in-bel.text: Only nodes whose `truth_value` is `"IN"` are ever candidates, regardless of what `belief_ids` contains.

detect-contradictions-only-considers-in-.text: Both `detect_contradictions` and its semantic variant skip any node whose `truth_value` is not `"IN"`.

detect-contradictions-sample-nondetermin.text: When `sample` is used, `detect_contradictions` uses `random.sample` without a seed, so the sampled candidate set is non-deterministic across calls.

detect-contradictions-silently-ignores-u.text: IDs in `belief_ids` that are missing or `OUT` are dropped without any error or count in the return dict.

detect-contradictions-swallows-batch-err.text: A `subprocess.run` exception during batching is caught and yields `[]` rather than propagating to the caller.

detect-contradictions-total-in-before-fi.text: `detect_contradictions` computes `total_in` before applying `belief_ids` or `sample` filtering, so `checked` may be less than or equal to `total_in`.

detected-contradiction-basis-has-no-auto.text: No observed code maps `basis="detected-contradiction"` to an auto-accept path; proposals are rendered for manual review.

determinism-enables-safe-dialectical-ext.text: Dialectical transformation is operationally safe precisely because it composes with the minimal deterministic engine — the irreversible premise-to-justified conversion inherits deterministic propagation and uniform evaluation, so dialectics need no dedicated safety machinery beyond what the core already provides.

justifications.label: Cross-cuts the minimality/determinism narrative with the dialectical safety narrative; reveals that dialectical safety is not independently engineered but inherited from core determinism

determinism-spans-revision-semantics-thr.text: Determinism is maintained end-to-end from belief revision semantics through source integrity verification: revision operations produce deterministic traceable state transitions (structured before/after diffs with controlled irreversibility), AND the source verification that triggers revision actions is itself deterministic and architecturally grounded (fail-safe path resolution, exact SHA-256 comparison, clean layer boundaries) — no step in the revision-triggered-by-source-change pathway introduces non-determinism.

justifications.label: End-to-end determinism from the source change that triggers revision through the revision that responds to it

deterministic-and-supported-lifecycle-co.text: The reasoning-and-revision architecture is deterministic in its state trajectories and lifecycle-managed consistently across supported operations — supported beliefs are predictably computed and tracked for those operations, without claiming exhaustive monitoring coverage or that no belief can escape every lifecycle gap.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

deterministic-history-extends-to-all-ori.text: Every state change for every belief — including externally-originated beliefs at full integration parity — follows a deterministic path with complete traceable history, meaning origin can never be used as an excuse for opacity.

justifications.label: Depth-8 — integration parity means external beliefs get the same deterministic traceable history as internal ones, eliminating provenance as a source of audit gaps

deterministic-reasoning-is-boundary-safe.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine operates within evolution-tolerant boundaries AND produces reproducible LLM-driven derivations through deterministic prompt construction with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation — determinism extends from core truth evaluation through system boundaries to external model interaction.

justifications.label: Core determinism (uniform evaluation, guaranteed termination) extends through validated boundaries to reproducible derive prompts with defense-in-depth

deterministic-reasoning-operates-on-soun.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine operates on architecture with no hidden fragility — architectural stability ensures that determinism holds in deployed operation, not just in theoretical isolation.

justifications.label: Engine determinism is practically guaranteed because the substrate has no hidden fragility that could violate it

deterministic-reasoning-with-consistent-.text: The system's belief-state trajectory is deterministic for premise sets and lifecycle-managed consistently across supported operations: deterministic reversible reasoning yields exactly one truth-value assignment, while lifecycle consistency for supported operations ensures monitoring and verifiability for those operations, without claiming exhaustive coverage of every lifecycle gap.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

deterministic-reasoning-with-gapless-lif.text: The system's belief-state trajectory is both fully determined and fully monitored: deterministic reversible reasoning ensures any given set of premises produces exactly one truth-value assignment, while gapless lifecycle management ensures no belief escapes monitoring across any lifecycle phase — the state at any point is predictable from its inputs and verifiable through its monitoring infrastructure.

justifications.label: Deterministic reasoning (from TMS core branch) plus gapless lifecycle monitoring (from staleness/propagation branch) bridges predictability with verifiability

deterministic-reasoning-within-evolution.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine — producing predictable terminating results through uniform evaluation — operates within system boundaries that gracefully handle format and schema evolution, ensuring deterministic correctness remains stable as external data formats change over time.

justifications.label: Deterministic reasoning provides correctness within a format version; evolution-tolerant boundaries extend that correctness across format versions without breaking deterministic properties

deterministic-self-correction-spans-all-.text: Self-correction operates deterministically across both temporal dimensions — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection — on architecturally sound foundations, meaning the system's corrective behavior is predictable at every timescale.

justifications.label: Depth-5 — determinism on sound architecture combined with full temporal coverage yields predictable self-correction: no timescale produces surprising corrective behavior

deterministic-self-correction-spans-crea.text: Self-correction operates deterministically along creation and supported maintenance axes — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection for existing IN beliefs with both source fields — on architecturally sound foundations, meaning corrective behavior is predictable for supported operations and tracked evidential evolution without claiming exhaustive lifetime coverage.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

dialectical-api-wraps-load-operate-save.text: The `reasons.api` dialectical functions (`challenge`, `defend`) wrap each call in a load → operate → save cycle against the SQLite file at `db_path`, ensuring the public API is a faithful pass-through to `Network` methods.

dialectical-assurance-achieves-governanc.text: Dialectical operations achieve complete bidirectional assurance (forward reliability and backward recovery with dual semantic grounding) within a governance framework that is complete across topology, source, and traceability — every dialectical challenge, defend, and reversal produces outcomes that meet the full governance quality bar across all three output dimensions.

justifications.label: bidirectional dialectical assurance + three-dimensional governance = dialectics produce governance-complete outcomes

dialectical-assurance-with-supported-gov.text: Dialectical operations achieve complete bidirectional assurance (forward reliability and backward recovery with dual semantic grounding) within a governance framework that supports topology-complete reach and metadata-enriched traceability with robust source-verified integrity; dialectical challenges, defends, and reversals produce verifiable, traceable, and source-grounded outcomes under these mechanisms, without claiming exhaustive source completeness.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

dialectical-chains-are-recursively-node-.text: Challenges and defenses are nodes, so they can themselves be challenged; the test suite exercises a four-layer alternating dialectical chain.

dialectical-default-ids-use-prefix-and-c.text: Challenge nodes default to `challenge-<target>` with `-2`, `-3`, … on collision, and defense nodes default to `defense-<challenge_id>`.

dialectical-defeat-is-reversible-but-ide.text: The dialectical system exhibits a fundamental asymmetry between defeat and identity: the truth-value defeat caused by a challenge is fully reversible (defending or retracting the challenge node restores IN status via outlist semantics), but the premise-to-justified identity transformation is permanent — a challenged premise can never return to unjustified status because the added justification cannot be removed, only defeated.

justifications.label: Outlist reversibility at the truth level coexists with irreversibility at the structural level, a designed asymmetry

dialectical-depth-is-unbounded.text: Because challenges/defenses are nodes, they can be recursively challenged; `test_three_level_chain` verifies four alternating layers propagate correctly.

dialectical-edges-are-metadata-encoded.text: Challenge/defense relationships are encoded in node metadata via keys such as `challenge_target`, `challenges`, `defense_target`, and `defends`, not a dedicated edge table.

dialectical-errors-use-keyerror-not-cust.text: `Network.challenge()` and `Network.defend()` raise the built-in `KeyError` (not a domain-specific exception) when the target or challenge node ID does not exist in the network.

dialectical-metadata-links-are-bidirecti.text: A challenge node always records `metadata["challenge_target"]` pointing to the target, and the target always records the challenge ID in its `metadata["challenges"]` list; defenses follow the same pattern with `defense_target` and `defends`.

dialectical-naming-convention-is-determi.text: Challenge nodes are named `challenge-{node_id}` (with sequential `-2`, `-3`… suffixes for duplicates on the same target); defense nodes are named `defense-{challenge_id}`; the first challenge always gets the bare suffix.

dialectical-nodes-are-metadata-linked-no.text: Challenges and defenses attach to the graph via `metadata["challenge_target"]` / `metadata["challenges"]` / `metadata["defense_target"]` / `metadata["defends"]`, not via a separate edge collection.

dialectical-operations-raise-keyerror-fo.text: `Network.challenge` and `Network.defend` raise `KeyError` when the target or challenge node does not exist, rather than silently creating stubs.

dialectical-pipeline-is-three-stage.text: The challenge-and-defense pipeline flows in order: `contradictions.py` discovers NOGOODs → `network.py` executes formal retraction via outlist propagation → `repair.py` attempts defense (link/soften/abandon) before final commitment

dialectical-revision-governs-rich-tracea.text: Dialectical revision — deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete with controlled irreversibility — governs metadata-enriched state beyond binary truth values, producing traceable deterministic changes to retraction flags, stale reasons, and access tags through every challenge/defend operation, not just binary IN/OUT transitions.

justifications.label: Dialectical revision's three trustworthiness properties (determinism, reliability, completeness) apply to the full richly-governed state space, not merely binary truth

dialectical-revision-is-deterministic-re.text: The dialectical revision system achieves three independent trustworthiness properties simultaneously: determinism (through semantic transparency inheriting uniform evaluation rules), reliability (through safe crash-free premise-to-justified transformation), and semantic completeness with controlled irreversibility (comprehensive negative semantics where all defeats reverse but identity transformation is permanent) — making dialectical operations fully production-trustworthy.

justifications.label: Deterministic reliable dialectics composed with complete controlled-irreversibility semantics yields production-trustworthy revision

dialectical-revision-is-deterministic-re.text: The dialectical revision system is deterministic and reliable, and it handles specified negative mechanisms with controlled irreversibility: outlist-based defeat mechanisms such as challenge, kill-switch, and supersession are truth-value reversible, while dialectical challenge permanently transforms premise identity by injecting a justification into a formerly unjustified node, without claiming exhaustive coverage of every possible negation mechanism.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

dialectical-revision-is-exception-safe-w.text: Dialectical revision — deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete — simultaneously governs metadata-enriched traceable state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, supersession) AND operates within an exception-safe richly-governed framework, ensuring that all dialectical operations produce rich auditable state transitions with safe failure recovery across all revision mechanisms.

justifications.label: dialectical revision unifies rich traceable state with exception-safe governance
