has-subscribers-exact-db-path-lookup.text: For a non-`None` `db_path`, `has_subscribers` checks global subscribers plus only the bucket keyed by that exact string, with no path normalization.

has-subscribers-global-bucket-short-circ.text: A non-empty global (`None`) subscriber bucket makes `has_subscribers` return `True` for any `db_path` before checking per-database buckets.

has-subscribers-has-no-locking.text: The function performs no synchronization, so concurrent subscription changes can affect the result before or after the call.

has-subscribers-is-read-only.text: The function only reads `_subscribers`; it performs no mutation, logging, I/O, or callback invocation.

has-subscribers-is-read-only-no-callback.text: `has_subscribers` only reads `_subscribers`; it performs no mutation, logging, I/O, or callback invocation.

has-subscribers-none-parameter-checks-gl.text: When `db_path` is `None`, `has_subscribers` checks only the global subscriber bucket and does not scan per-database buckets.

has-subscribers-none-parameter-checks-on.text: Passing `None` or omitting `db_path` checks only the global subscriber bucket; it does not scan per-database buckets.

has-subscribers-uses-exact-db-path-match.text: For a non-`None` `db_path`, the function checks global subscribers plus only the bucket keyed by that exact string.

has-subscribers-without-db-path-checks-o.text: `has_subscribers()` without a `db_path` checks only the global `None` bucket, so a scoped-only subscriber does not make it return true.

hash-file-full-sha256.text: `hash_file` returns a full 64-character hex SHA-256 digest (per the fix in PR #40 that removed the earlier `[:16]` truncation).

hash-file-import-unused.text: Trivial/unstable detail about an unused import; not a meaningful architectural invariant.

hash-file-returns-full-64-char-sha256.text: hash_file returns the full 64-character SHA-256 hex digest and does not catch errors for unreadable files.

hash-file-returns-lowercase-sha256-hexdi.text: `hash_file(path)` returns a lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the file bytes.

hash-file-stores-full-sha256.text: `hash_file()` stores and compares full 64-hex-character SHA-256 hashes after removing the `[:16]` truncation.

hash-file-uses-sha256.text: `hash_file()` computes a SHA-256 hash of the file's contents.

hash-sources-additive-unless-forced.text: `hash_sources` only fills nodes with an empty `source_hash`; it never overwrites an existing non-empty hash unless `force=True` is explicitly passed.

hash-sources-backfills-empty-hashes-unle.text: `hash_sources` updates nodes with empty `source_hash` by default and only rehashes existing non-empty hashes when `force=True`.

hash-sources-backfills-from-source-witho.text: `hash_sources` sets `source_hash` for any node with a resolvable source and no hash (unless `force`), whereas `check_stale` inspects only nodes that already have both `source` and `source_hash`.

hash-sources-does-not-filter-by-truth-va.text: The function iterates over all `network.nodes` and never checks `truth_value`, so it can hash nodes that are not `IN`.

hash-sources-force-rehashes-all-source-n.text: hash_sources with force=True re-hashes all source-bearing nodes regardless of whether they already have a source_hash.

hash-sources-force-rehashes-existing.text: With `force=True`, `hash_sources` rehashes nodes that already have a non-empty hash and sets `was_empty` to `False` in the result.

hash-sources-force-rehashes-existing-has.text: hash_sources with force=True re-hashes nodes that already have a source_hash and returns a was_empty flag distinguishing forced re-hashes from initial backfill.

hash-sources-idempotent-without-force.text: `hash_sources` with default `force=False` skips nodes that already have a `source_hash`, making repeated backfill calls safe; `force=True` rehashes unconditionally.

hash-sources-is-additive-by-default.text: `hash_sources` without `force=True` never overwrites an existing non-empty `source_hash`; it only backfills nodes with empty or missing hashes.

hash-sources-manifest-includes-was-empty.text: hash_sources returns a manifest record with a was_empty flag to distinguish backfills from overwrites.

hash-sources-mutates-network.text: `hash_sources` writes directly to `node.source_hash` on the in-memory network, while `check_stale` is purely read-only — an intentional asymmetry.

hash-sources-mutates-network-in-place.text: `hash_sources()` writes computed hashes directly into `net.nodes[id].source_hash` for nodes it backfills.

hash-sources-mutates-network-nodes-in-pl.text: `hash_sources` assigns each resolved node’s `source_hash` to the full SHA-256 digest before returning results.

hash-sources-no-overwrite-default.text: `hash_sources` with `force=False` (the default) only backfills missing hashes and will never modify a node that already has a `source_hash` value.

hash-sources-propagates-read-errors.text: `hash_sources` has no `try/except` around `hash_file`, so unreadable or directory paths raise and may leave earlier node mutations in place.

hash-sources-requires-caller-persistence.text: The function only mutates the in-memory `Network`; it never saves the network, so changes are lost unless the caller persists them.

hash-sources-results-include-was-empty.text: `hash_sources` returns result dicts containing at least `node_id` and `was_empty`, where `was_empty` is `True` only when the previous hash was empty.

hash-sources-skips-existing-hashes-unles.text: With `force=False`, any node whose `source_hash` is truthy is skipped; with `force=True`, all nodes with a truthy `source` and resolvable path are re-hashed.

hash-sources-skips-missing-source-or-fil.text: `hash_sources` reports only successful backfills, silently skipping nodes that lack a `source` field or whose source file is missing.

hash-sources-skips-missing-source-silent.text: `hash_sources` silently skips nodes whose source file is missing and emits no result for them.

hash-sources-string-in-require-sqlite-te.text: `hash-sources` appears in `_require_sqlite` tests only as an arbitrary command label and is not one of the remaining production `_require_sqlite` gates.

hash-sources-string-is-test-only.text: `hash-sources` appears in `_require_sqlite` tests only as a command label and is not among the remaining production `_require_sqlite` gates.

hash-sources-walks-all-truth-values.text: hash_sources walks all nodes regardless of truth value, unlike check_stale which only examines IN nodes.

hash-truncation-is-16-hex.text: Source hashes are SHA-256 truncated to the first 16 hex characters (64 bits), reducing collision resistance to ~32 bits for birthday attacks compared to the full 256-bit hash.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #40

header-flushes-previous-block.text: The parser is streaming: the previous block is flushed when the next `### NOGOOD` header is seen, and the final block is flushed after the loop.

hf-401-always-maps-to-authentication-run.text: A 401 HTTP response from any HuggingFace API call (create_repo or upload_file) is mapped to `RuntimeError` with a message matching "Authentication failed"; callers never see a raw `HTTPError`.

hf-create-repo-401-maps-to-authenticatio.text: Already covered by the existing `hf-401-always-maps-to-authentication-runtimeerror` belief.

hf-create-repo-409-is-idempotent.text: A 409 HTTP response from the HF "create repo" endpoint is swallowed and treated as success (the repo already exists), making `publish_hf` safe to invoke repeatedly against the same repo name.

hf-create-repo-idempotent-on-409.text: `create_repo` treats HTTP 409 Conflict as success and silently returns the fully-qualified repo id.

hf-create-repo-swallows-409.text: `create_repo` treats HTTP `409 Conflict` as success so it can be called unconditionally before upload.

hf-default-org-is-eem-hub.text: Already covered by the existing `hf-repo-id-normalization-with-env-override` belief.

hf-download-hardcoded-path.text: `download_network` in `reasons/hf.py` always fetches `network.json` from the `main` branch of the resolved repo (URL: `{org}/{name}/resolve/main/network.json`); there is no parameter to select a different branch or filename.

hf-download-network-maps-http-errors-to-.text: `download_network` maps HTTP 401 to a `RuntimeError` matching "Authentication required" and HTTP 404 to a `RuntimeError` matching "not found".

hf-download-network-returns-json-string.text: `download_network` returns the downloaded `network.json` as a raw JSON string, not a parsed dict, using the fixed path `resolve/main/network.json`.

hf-download-network-returns-unparsed-jso.text: `download_network` returns the response body as a decoded JSON string; parsing and schema validation are the caller’s responsibility.

hf-download-network-uses-bearer-auth-whe.text: `download_network` builds a `urllib.request.Request` and adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` only when a token is resolved.

hf-download-translates-http-errors-to-ru.text: `download_network` converts raw `urllib` `HTTPError` exceptions into higher-level `RuntimeError` with actionable messages (401 → "Authentication required", 404 → "not found"), so callers of `api.import_hf` never encounter `HTTPError` directly.

hf-endpoints-hardwired-to-main-revision.text: HuggingFace download and upload endpoints are hard-wired to the `main` revision; there is no branch/revision parameter.

hf-import-defaults-to-configured-org.text: HuggingFace imports resolve to a configurable default org when none is supplied (`test_hf_default_org.py`).

hf-import-hf-returns-resolved-repo-id.text: `import_hf` resolves bare repo names through the default org and returns the fully resolved `repo_id`, preserving an explicitly supplied `owner/repo`.

hf-module-avoids-huggingface-hub.text: `reasons/hf.py` does not import `huggingface_hub`; it reimplements the needed Hub operations with stdlib `urllib`/`json`.

hf-module-avoids-huggingface_hub.text: `reasons/hf.py` does not import `huggingface_hub`; the Hub behavior is reimplemented over `urllib.request`.

hf-publish-errors-when-token-missing.text: Already covered by the existing `hf-write-ops-require-caller-provided-token` belief.

hf-publish-uploads-exactly-three-files.text: `api.publish_hf` uploads precisely three files — `network.json`, `beliefs.md`, and `README.md` — to the target HF repo's `main` branch, and performs exactly four HTTP calls (one create + three uploads).

hf-repo-id-normalization-with-env-overri.text: `resolve_repo_id` in `reasons/hf.py` normalizes bare names by prepending `DEFAULT_HF_ORG` (`"EEM-Hub"`), which is overridable via the `REASONS_HF_ORG` environment variable; explicit `org/name` and full-URL forms pass through unchanged.

hf-resolve-repo-id-preserves-explicit-or.text: `resolve_repo_id` prepends the default org (`EEM-Hub` or `REASONS_HF_ORG` env var) only to bare names without a `/`; an explicit `org/name` string or full URL is passed through unchanged.

hf-resolve-repo-id-rejects-non-hf-urls.text: `resolve_repo_id` raises `ValueError` for URLs that do not contain `huggingface.co/` rather than silently mis-parsing them.

hf-resolve-repo-id-rejects-non-huggingfa.text: `resolve_repo_id` accepts only `https://huggingface.co/...` URLs and raises `ValueError("Not a HuggingFace URL")` for other URLs.

hf-shim-is-covered-by-hf-import-tests.text: `tests/test_hf_default_org.py` and `tests/test_import_hf.py` exercise HF behavior through the `reasons_lib.hf` shim, not only through `reasons.hf`.

hf-shim-noqa-suppresses-f401-and-f403.text: `reasons_lib/hf.py` uses `# noqa: F401,F403` to suppress both unused-import and star-import lint warnings for its deliberate wildcard re-export.

hf-token-resolution-chain.text: Token resolution in `reasons/hf.py` follows a strict priority chain: explicit argument → `HF_TOKEN` environment variable → `~/.cache/huggingface/token` file → `None`, mirroring `huggingface-cli` credential behavior so existing logged-in users work without passing `--token`.

hf-token-resolution-follows-param-env-fi.text: The HF token is resolved in order: explicit `token` parameter → `HF_TOKEN` environment variable → `~/.huggingface/token` file; if none is found, a `RuntimeError` is raised before any network call is made.

hf-token-resolution-order.text: `_resolve_token` resolves in the order: explicit arg → `HF_TOKEN` env → `~/.cache/huggingface/token`.

hf-token-resolution-precedence.text: `_resolve_token` resolves credentials in precedence order: explicit argument, then `HF_TOKEN` environment variable, then `~/.cache/huggingface/token`, then `None`, stripping whitespace from the cached file.

hf-token-resolution-priority-chain.text: `_resolve_token` follows a strict priority order: explicit argument > `HF_TOKEN` environment variable > `~/.cache/huggingface/token` file > `None`; an explicit token always shadows the environment variable regardless of whether the env var is set.

hf-upload-file-uses-put-with-bearer-auth.text: `upload_file` issues a PUT to `/api/models/{repo_id}/upload/main/{filename}` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the raw file bytes as request data.

hf-uses-stdlib-urllib-not-sdk.text: The module deliberately uses `urllib.request` and stdlib only; there is no `huggingface_hub` import.

hf-uses-stdlib-urllib-only.text: `reasons/hf.py` talks to HuggingFace via stdlib `urllib.request` and does not import `huggingface_hub` or `requests`.

hf-write-ops-require-caller-provided-tok.text: `create_repo` and `upload_file` in `reasons/hf.py` do NOT call `_resolve_token` internally — the caller must pass a non-`None` token — while `download_network` tolerates `None` (for public repos), creating an asymmetry between read and write paths.

hide-out-tests-are-presentation-filter-o.text: `tests/test_hide_out.py` tests whether OUT nodes are hidden from API search/lookup/compact output by default; it does not test sticky `_retracted` locking.

hints-exclude-directly-retracted-node.text: The node passed to `retract_node` never appears in the `restoration_hints` list — only cascade victims with surviving premises do.

huggingface-requires-lowercase-license-f.text: HuggingFace metadata validation requires the license field to be lowercase, such as mit rather than MIT.

human-edited-plan-parser-exists.text: The reviewed observations do not show a parser for a human-edited Markdown plan; absence from these snippets is not enough to establish either existence or non-existence.

iap-provides-google-oauth-gating-in-fron.text: Identity-Aware Proxy in front of Cloud Run provides Google OAuth gating for the MCP server.

idempotent-reimport-skips-all.text: Covered by existing `import-skips-existing-sync-is-remote-wins` which captures the idempotent import behavior

identity-preserved-across-paths.text: Objects imported via `reasons_lib.review_premises` are the same objects as those imported via `reasons.review_premises`.

identity-transformation-is-complete-and-.text: Premise identity is bidirectionally transformable (challenge destroys premise identity, convert-to-premise restores it) and the destructive direction achieves full reliability through crash-safe semantics-preserving propagation — making identity transformation a complete and reliable lifecycle operation in both directions.

justifications.label: Bidirectional transformability establishes completeness while crash-safe reliable dialectics establish correctness; together they ensure identity transformation is fully trustworthy

identity-transformation-is-semantically-.text: Challenge creates an irreversible structural transformation (premise → justified node), yet the resulting dialectical structure receives identical evaluation to any other belief — the permanent identity change has no lasting semantic consequence because evaluation is uniformly origin-agnostic and context-independent.

justifications.label: Architectural asymmetry (depth-4) establishes that identity loss is permanent; semantic transparency (depth-3) establishes that evaluation is indifferent to it — the "damage" is structurally real but semantically invisible.

identity-transformation-operates-within-.text: All premise identity transformations — irreversible dialectical challenge and restorative conversion — operate within reproducible, boundary-safe deterministic reasoning, ensuring that structural changes to belief identity follow predictable, evolution-tolerant paths and produce verifiable results.

justifications.label: Identity transformation reliability combined with deterministic reasoning boundary safety — even irreversible structural changes are reproducible

implements-doyle-1979-tms.text: `reasons/network.py:3` explicitly states it implements Doyle's (1979) Truth Maintenance System algorithm.

import-accepts-mismatched-schema-version.text: `tests/test_import_hf.py:17` and `tests/test_metadata.py:134-136` import fixtures declaring `schema_version: "1.0"` while `pyproject.toml` declares `0.58.0`, and the import succeeds, demonstrating no compatibility check on load.

import-achieves-ordered-convergent-recon.text: Import achieves correct final state through two reinforcing mechanisms: deliberate ordering discipline (add → propagate → retract) ensures deferred retractions don't corrupt intermediate states, while deterministic convergence (dual reconciliation modes reaching stable states, propagation terminating via fixpoint) ensures the result is unique and reproducible regardless of input ordering within each phase.

justifications.label: Ordering (depth-1) prevents phase-interaction bugs; convergence (depth-3) prevents input-order sensitivity — together they make import deterministic at both the macro (phase) and micro (within-phase) levels.

import-agent-active-is-bare-premise.text: `_ensure_agent_nodes` creates `agent:active` as a bare premise with no justifications, IN by default.

import-agent-active-premise-carries-role.text: The synthetic `<agent>:active` premise node created by `import_agent` carries `role=agent_premise` in its metadata, distinguishing it from user-authored premises and enabling programmatic identification of infrastructure nodes.

import-agent-active-premise-has-role-age.text: import_agent creates the `{agent}:active` sentinel node as an IN premise with `role=agent_premise` metadata.

import-agent-agent-name-must-not-contain.text: `import_agent` relies on `agent_name` for the `f"{agent_name}:"` prefix and reverse ID stripping, so colon-containing or empty agent names are unsafe and are not validated.

import-agent-build-justifications-synthe.text: `_build_justifications` gives even beliefs with no other justification a synthetic SL justification containing `agent:inactive` in the outlist.

import-agent-claims-retracted-counts-onl.text: `import_agent` increments `claims_retracted` only for deferred bare-OUT retractions, not for nodes marked `_retracted` via metadata.

import-agent-clears-retracted-on-remote-.text: `reasons/import_agent.py:425-426` and `485` clear `_retracted` when the remote source reports IN.

import-agent-creates-active-and-inactive.text: _ensure_agent_nodes creates agent:active as a premise node and agent:inactive with SL(antecedents=[], outlist=[agent:active]) for each agent.

import-agent-creates-active-inactive-kil.text: _ensure_agent_nodes() creates a premise node agent:active and an SL-justified node agent:inactive with outlist=[agent:active], so retracting agent:active flips agent:inactive IN and cascades all imported beliefs OUT.

import-agent-creates-namespace-active-ki.text: `import_agent` and `sync_agent` prefix imported beliefs with `namespace:` and create a `namespace:active` premise whose retraction cascades OUT every belief from that agent.

import-agent-creates-two-infra-nodes-per.text: _ensure_agent_nodes creates two infrastructure nodes per agent: agent:active as a bare premise and agent:inactive with an SL justification whose outlist contains agent:active.

import-agent-deferred-retraction.text: Nodes that should be OUT are first created as IN (so they participate in dependency registration), collected in `retract_after`, and retracted only after `recompute_all()` — ordering matters for correct graph construction.

import-agent-dual-format-normalization-s.text: _normalize_markdown and _normalize_json both produce a common claim dict with id, text, is_out, source, source_hash, date, metadata, and raw_justifications fields.

import-agent-dual-format-parity.text: `import_agent` accepts both Markdown and JSON source files and produces structurally and behaviorally equivalent network states, with the JSON path explicitly preserving the full justification array (antecedents, outlist, type, label).

import-agent-has-no-try-except.text: `import_agent.py` contains no try/except blocks and relies on parsers, `Network.add_node`, dict defaults, and set operations for fault tolerance.

import-agent-imports-companion-nogoods.text: `import_agent` imports nogoods from a companion `nogoods.md` file alongside the agent's beliefs.

import-agent-imports-nogoods.text: `import_agent` imports and counts nogood contradiction records from a co-located nogoods file.

import-agent-inactive-always-in-outlist.text: Every imported belief unconditionally has `agent:inactive` in its outlist, enforced in `_build_justifications()` with no code path that omits it — this is the mechanism behind the per-agent kill switch.

import-agent-inactive-in-every-outlist.text: _build_justifications() unconditionally injects agent:inactive into every imported belief's outlist, making bulk distrust work through TMS propagation.

import-agent-inactive-justified-by-outli.text: `agent:inactive` is justified by an SL justification with empty antecedents and `active` in its outlist, making it IN only when `active` is OUT.

import-agent-inactive-never-in-anteceden.text: Duplicates the existing belief `kill-switch-uses-outlist-not-antecedent` — the "not antecedent" half is already captured.

import-agent-infra-nodes-excluded-from-r.text: `_sync_claims()` filters out infrastructure nodes (active/inactive) via `infra_ids` before computing the removal set, so the kill-switch pair is never retracted by remote-wins sync.

import-agent-json-normalization-only-che.text: `_normalize_json` marks a node out only when `truth_value == "OUT"`, so `UNKNOWN` is not treated as out.

import-agent-json-normalization-only-tre.text: `_normalize_json` marks a node out only when `truth_value == "OUT"`, so `"UNKNOWN"` and other JSON truth values are treated as non-out.

import-agent-json-preserves-full-justifi.text: `import_agent_json()` imports JSON beliefs while preserving their full justification structure.

import-agent-lets-network-errors-propaga.text: `import_agent.py` has no explicit try/except blocks; errors from `network.add_node()`, `network.retract()`, or `network.assert_node()` propagate unhandled.

import-agent-locks-remote-out-nodes.text: This duplicates existing accepted beliefs about sticky retraction, imported OUT nodes not being resurrected, and lifecycle governance in `import_agent.py`.

import-agent-markdown-additive-skips-exi.text: `import_agent()` performs additive Markdown import and skips nodes whose IDs already exist.

import-agent-namespace-prefix.text: Every node imported from agent X gets the ID prefix `X:`, including infrastructure nodes `X:active` and `X:inactive`, ensuring zero collision with local or other-agent beliefs

import-agent-nogood-requires-two-existin.text: Nogoods are imported only if at least two of their referenced nodes exist in the network after prefixing.

import-agent-nogoods-prefixed-on-sync.text: `_import_nogoods()` adds prefixed nogood records during sync.

import-agent-nogoods-require-at-least-tw.text: _import_nogoods() filters out nogoods that reference fewer than 2 nodes existing in the network.

import-agent-normalization-diverges-on-o.text: `_normalize_markdown` drops all justifications for OUT nodes (sets to empty list), while `_normalize_json` preserves the full justification structure including outlists — meaning the shared `_import_claims`/`_sync_claims` logic receives structurally different data depending on source format.

import-agent-normalization-uses-unprefix.text: Normalized claim dicts use unprefixed belief IDs; namespace prefixing is applied later by import/sync loops and `_build_justifications()`.

import-agent-normalizers-ignore-schema-v.text: The visible `_normalize_markdown()` and `_normalize_json()` paths in `reasons/import_agent.py` do not read `schema_version`.

import-agent-normalizers-share-intermedi.text: Both `_normalize_markdown()` and `_normalize_json()` produce identical intermediate dicts (id, text, is_out, source, source_hash, date, metadata, raw_justifications) before hitting shared `_import_claims`/`_sync_claims` logic.

import-agent-normalizes-markdown-beliefs.text: `import_agent` converts Markdown via `_normalize_markdown` into `{id, text, is_out, source, source_hash, date, metadata, raw_justifications}` dicts before import.

import-agent-only-in-excludes-out-belief.text: With `only_in=True`, `import_agent` skips STALE/OUT beliefs entirely so they are absent from the database.

import-agent-only-in-excludes-stale-out-.text: With `only_in=True`, `import_agent` excludes STALE/OUT beliefs entirely so that `api.show_node` on an excluded belief raises `KeyError`.

import-agent-only-in-filters-before-pref.text: When `only_in=True`, `import_agent` drops non-`IN` claims before prefixing; those claims never enter the network and are not counted in `claims_skipped`.

import-agent-only-in-omits-out-beliefs.text: When import_agent is called with `only_in=True`, STALE or OUT beliefs from the source are skipped and do not exist in the database.

import-agent-only-in-skips-non-in-claims.text: Passing `only_in=True` to `import_agent` skips claims not marked `[IN]`, so a STALE claim is absent and `claims_retracted` is zero.

import-agent-out-beliefs-get-empty-justi.text: Beliefs that are OUT or STALE in the source are imported with empty justification lists, preventing `recompute_all` from resurrecting them to IN.

import-agent-out-beliefs-not-resurrected.text: Beliefs marked OUT or STALE in the source are imported as OUT and are never resurrected by `recompute_all`, even when their justification antecedents are all IN in the local database.

import-agent-prefixes-antecedents-and-ou.text: During agent import, antecedent IDs and remote outlist entries are prefixed with `agent_name:`; the imported belief's outlist also includes the agent's `inactive_id`.

import-agent-prefixes-ids-at-justificati.text: Imported belief IDs get the agent_name prefix during _build_justifications, while raw justifications carry unprefixed IDs.

Every node imported from agent foo has an ID starting with foo:.

import-agent-preserves-justifications-on.text: Markdown STALE/OUT claims get empty `raw_justifications` and are retracted post-propagation, while JSON OUT claims retain justifications and are pinned OUT via `_retracted` metadata.

import-agent-preserves-original-id-in-me.text: Namespaced beliefs imported by `import_agent` carry the source ID in `metadata.original_id`.

import-agent-public-api-four-wrappers.text: `import_agent`, `import_agent_json`, `sync_agent`, and `sync_agent_json` are thin wrappers that normalize input and delegate to `_import_claims` or `_sync_claims`.

import-agent-raw-justifications-filtered.text: During normalization, `raw_justifications` stores unprefixed IDs and filtering to the import set occurs before agent-name prefixing.

import-agent-rebuilds-dependents-before-.text: After adding imported nodes and nogoods, `_fixup_dependents()` calls `network._rebuild_dependents()` before `network.recompute_all()` because outlist targets may not have existed when referencing nodes were added.

import-agent-records-agent-source-path-i.text: `_import_claims` records the importing agent’s resolved parent path into `network.repos[agent_name]`.

import-agent-registers-repo.text: `import_agent` records the source file's resolved parent directory under `repos[agent]`, visible via `api.list_repos(db_path=...)["repos"]`.

import-agent-registers-source-directory-.text: `api.list_repos()` includes an imported agent with its source directory path.

import-agent-registers-source-repo.text: `import_agent` registers the imported agent's source directory in the repos list, exposed via `api.list_repos()`.

import-agent-reimport-returns-zero-impor.text: Re-importing the same agent and beliefs returns `claims_imported=0` and `claims_skipped=3`.

import-agent-remaps-dependencies.text: Importing an agent rewrites justification dependency references to use the agent's namespace prefix.

import-agent-remaps-nogood-ids-with-name.text: `import_agent` remaps imported nogood members through the same agent namespace pass as beliefs and reports `nogoods_imported`.

import-agent-removals-iterate-sorted-nod.text: Sync removal processing iterates `sorted(removed_ids)`, making removal order deterministic.

import-agent-retraction-survives-recompu.text: After retracting an imported belief, `recompute_all()` must not resurrect it — the justification structure must not provide alternative paths to IN (issue #16 regression invariant).

import-agent-retracts-out-beliefs-after-.text: _import_claims() calls recompute_all() to propagate truth values and then explicitly retracts nodes that were OUT in the source.

import-agent-returns-counts-and-control-.text: `import_agent` returns a dict containing the agent name, namespace prefix, active node ID, premise-creation flag, and counts of imported and retracted claims.

import-agent-returns-stats-dict.text: All four public import/sync functions return a stats dict with counts such as added, skipped, and retracted.

import-agent-shim-star-import-does-not-f.text: Because `from reasons.import_agent import *` binds names but not `__all__`, `reasons_lib.import_agent.__all__` is absent unless the canonical `__all__` explicitly includes `"__all__"`, so downstream wildcard imports from the shim use the non-underscore rule instead of the canonical `__all__` contract.

import-agent-silently-filters-invalid-re.text: `reasons/import_agent.py` raises no exceptions for normal operational issues: missing outlist/antecedent IDs are silently filtered during normalization, nogoods with <2 valid nodes are skipped, and topo-sort cycles are force-appended rather than raised.

import-agent-skips-existing-node-ids.text: `_import_claims` short-circuits with `skipped += 1` when `agent:id` already exists in the network.

import-agent-source-path-registers-repo-.text: If `source_path` is non-empty, `import_agent` registers `network.repos[agent_name]` as the resolved parent directory and stamps `imported_from` metadata on imported nodes.

import-agent-stores-original-id-metadata.text: Every belief imported by import_agent carries `original_id` metadata.

import-agent-supports-markdown-and-json.text: The public API `reasons.api.import_agent` accepts both the Markdown "Beliefs/Nogoods" export and the JSON network-export format, and both preserve the same namespacing/outlist invariants.

import-agent-supports-markdown-and-json-.text: The API import_agent function supports both markdown and JSON input variants before dispatching parsed data to PgApi.

import-agent-sync-asserts-resurrections-.text: Sync queues `assert_after` resurrections and processes them before `recompute_all`, while retractions are deferred until after recomputation.

import-agent-sync-marks-removed-nodes-re.text: In sync, local-only agent beliefs not present in the remote set are retracted or marked _retracted in metadata, excluding infrastructure nodes.

import-agent-sync-updates-existing-nodes.text: `_sync_claims` updates existing agent nodes by diffing `text`, source fields, date, metadata, and justifications rather than blindly replacing them.

import-agent-topo-sort-breaks-cycles.text: `_topo_sort_claims` breaks dependency cycles by appending all remaining unsorted nodes after `max_passes = len(remaining) + 1` iterations rather than raising an error, ensuring import always completes.

import-agent-uses-namespacing-and-active.text: import_agent.py implements multi-agent belief federation using namespacing and active/inactive relay nodes.

import-api-auto-initializes-sqlite.text: For SQLite backends, `import_api` initializes a missing database unconditionally; the `init` flag does not gate that branch.

import-api-delegates-to-import-json.text: All node/nogood/repo installation is performed by `import_json`; `import_api` is only responsible for fetch, optional init, temp-file staging, and cleanup.

import-api-imports-via-temp-json-file.text: Fetched export JSON is written to a temporary `.json` file and passed by path to `import_json`, with cleanup in `finally`.

import-api-init-creates-db.text: `api.import_api(..., init=True)` creates the SQLite database file when it does not yet exist.

import-api-init-flag-gates-only-postgres.text: `init=True` is only required/effective for PostgreSQL schema auto-creation; an existing SQLite file skips initialization even when `init=True`.

import-api-init-true-creates-db.text: `api.import_api(..., init=True)` creates the SQLite database file when it does not already exist.

import-api-parses-json-twice-when-initia.text: When initialization runs, `json_str` is parsed once for `meta.project_name` and then re-parsed from the temp file by `import_json`.

import-api-pg-callers-must-provide-schem.text: PostgreSQL callers must pass `init=True` or pre-provision the schema because `Path(db_path).exists()` cannot detect PG state.

import-api-propagates-errors-instead-of-.text: No try/except wraps network, init, or import operations; failures propagate as exceptions rather than being returned in the result dict.

import-api-requires-init-for-postgres.text: For PostgreSQL, `init=True` is required to auto-create the schema because the local `db_path` existence check cannot detect remote state.

import-api-requires-resolvable-config.text: `api.import_api` and `api.export_api` raise `RuntimeError("Missing required config")` when config resolution fails.

import-api-uses-temp-file-with-finally-c.text: The downloaded JSON is always written to a `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` and removed in a `finally` block, including on import failure.

import-beliefs-adds-out-nodes-before-ret.text: STALE and OUT claims are first added to the network with their full justification structure and then retracted, preserving the dependency graph for possible future restoration.

import-beliefs-claim-text-captures-first.text: `parse_beliefs` captures only the first non-empty, non-bullet line after a claim header, silently truncating multi-line claim text.

import-beliefs-copies-schema-version-wit.text: `import_into_network()` copies frontmatter `schema_version` into `network.meta` but does not compare or validate it.

import-beliefs-derived-type-maps-to-sing.text: During `import_into_network`, claims with type `DERIVED` receive exactly one SL justification whose `antecedents` list matches the source document's "Depends on" field, establishing the dependency relationship in the network graph.

import-beliefs-drops-nogoods-with-fewer-.text: Nogoods are imported only when at least 2 of their referenced nodes exist in the network; otherwise they are silently dropped.

import-beliefs-duplicate-claim-ids-last-.text: `import_into_network` builds `claim_by_id` as a last-wins dict, so duplicate claim IDs in one input collapse to the final occurrence.

import-beliefs-first-free-line-is-claim-.text: parse_beliefs treats the first non-metadata, non-empty line after a claim header as the claim's human-readable text.

import-beliefs-frontmatter-lifts-only-th.text: `import_into_network` copies only `schema_version`, `project_name`, and `created_at` from frontmatter into `network.meta`; other frontmatter keys are dropped.

import-beliefs-frontmatter-parser-is-min.text: `strip_frontmatter` is a minimal flat `key: value` parser that strips surrounding quotes and does not use a YAML library or nested structures.

import-beliefs-justifications-filter-to-.text: `import_into_network` filters `depends_on` and `unless` entries against IDs parsed from the same file, not against all existing `network.nodes`, so pre-existing external dependencies are not aggregated.

import-beliefs-maps-stale-and-out-to-ret.text: `import_into_network` retracts nodes whose parsed status is either `STALE` or `OUT`.

import-beliefs-metadata-matching-case-in.text: Claim metadata parsing is case-inconsistent: `Source URL`, `Source hash`, and `Accepted PR` are case-sensitive, while `Stale reason` and `Superseded by` are matched case-insensitively.

import-beliefs-metadata-whitelist-drops-.text: Optional import metadata is limited to a whitelist (`beliefs_type`, `source_type`, `stale_reason`, `superseded_by`, `accepted_pr`) and empty values are dropped before insertion.

import-beliefs-nogood-id-uses-high-water.text: `_next_nogood_id` is set to `max(current, parsed_id + 1)` during import, preventing future auto-generated nogood IDs from colliding with imported ones.

import-beliefs-observation-type-maps-to-.text: During `import_into_network`, claims with type `OBSERVATION` are imported as premises with an empty `justifications` list, making them un-defeatable root nodes whose truth value can only change via explicit retraction.

import-beliefs-parser-is-forward-compati.text: Unknown `- ` metadata lines in belief markdown are silently skipped via a `pass` branch, making the parser forward-compatible with new export format fields.

import-beliefs-parser-recognizes-only-in.text: `parse_beliefs` accepts only `IN`, `OUT`, and `STALE` in claim header regexes.

import-beliefs-parses-repos-until-next-h.text: parse_repos extracts the ## Repos section into a name-to-path mapping and stops parsing at the next ## header.

import-beliefs-path-import-unused.text: Vestigial import detail — too trivial and unstable to track as a belief; it could be cleaned up at any time.

import-beliefs-promotes-source-provenanc.text: `import_into_network` promotes `source`, `source_hash`, and `date` to top-level node attributes rather than storing them in `metadata`.

import-beliefs-raises-no-exceptions.text: `import_into_network` and all its helpers (`parse_beliefs`, `parse_nogoods`, `parse_repos`, topo-sort) never raise in the normal code path; the returned summary dict (`claims_skipped`, `nogoods_imported`, etc.) is the sole error-reporting channel.

import-beliefs-shim-is-covered-by-six-te.text: Six test modules (`test_import_beliefs`, `test_metadata`, `test_metadata_extended`, `test_nogood_id`, `test_roundtrip`, `test_source_type`) import through the `reasons_lib.import_beliefs` shim, making it part of their regression surface.

import-beliefs-skips-existing-node-ids.text: If a claim ID already exists in network.nodes, import_beliefs silently skips it with no upsert or merge behavior.

import-beliefs-source-is-literal-source-.text: `parse_beliefs()` stores the stripped text after `- Source: ` in `claim["source"]` without adding an `agent:` or `expert:` prefix.

import-beliefs-source-parsed-from-source.text: `parse_beliefs` stores the literal text after `- Source: ` in `claim["source"]` without prefixing it.

import-beliefs-tests-lack-out-coverage.text: The `tests/test_import_beliefs.py` fixture contains only `IN` and `STALE` claims, with no `OUT` header.

import-beliefs-topo-sort-is-cycle-tolera.text: The import_beliefs topological sort uses a multi-pass Kahn-like algorithm that detects zero progress and appends remaining claims without raising an error when circular dependencies exist.

import-functions-parse-before-dispatch.text: API import functions (`import_json`, `import_beliefs`, `import_agent`) read and parse files into structured data in the API layer before delegating to `PgApi` — PgApi never receives raw file paths

import-handles-heterogeneous-truth-state.text: The import pipeline handles mixed truth states: OUT/STALE beliefs arrive without justifications, topological sort tolerates cycles, and two-phase truth maintenance reconciles everything post-import

justifications.label: Three independent robustness mechanisms ensure import succeeds regardless of source network state

import-hf-auto-initializes-missing-db.text: With `init=False` and a nonexistent `db_path`, `import_hf` creates the DB and seeds `meta.project_name` from the downloaded network's `meta.project_name`.

import-hf-auto-initializes-missing-db-wi.text: When `api.import_hf` is called with `init=False` and a nonexistent database, it auto-initializes the DB and seeds `meta.project_name` from the downloaded network's `meta`.

import-hf-auto-initializes-sqlite-regard.text: For the SQLite backend (`pg_conninfo` falsy), `import_hf` always calls `init_db` when `db_path` is missing, even if `init=False`.
On the SQLite path (`pg_conninfo` falsy), `import_hf` auto-initializes a missing `db_path` even when `init=False`; `init` only affects PostgreSQL.

import-hf-checks-local-db-existence-even.text: `import_hf` decides whether to call `init_db` using `Path(db_path).exists()` even when `pg_conninfo` is set, so a local file named `reasons.db` can suppress PostgreSQL initialization.

import-hf-cleans-temp-file-in-finally.text: `import_hf` stages downloaded JSON in a `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` and unlinks it in `finally`, so temp cleanup is the only exception guarantee and an unlink error can replace the original exception.

import-hf-delegates-download-to-hf-downl.text: All HuggingFace I/O is performed by `reasons.hf.download_network`; `import_hf` itself makes no direct HTTP calls.

import-hf-does-not-catch-callee-errors.text: `import_hf` catches no exceptions from `download_network`, `init_db`, or `import_json`; download, initialization, import, and repo-id parsing errors propagate unchanged except for possible cleanup failure.

import-hf-normalizes-repo-id-after-impor.text: `import_hf` normalizes `result["repo_id"]` via `_parse_repo_id` after `import_json` has already succeeded, so the returned `repo_id` may differ from the input and normalization can still raise after import.

import-hf-normalizes-repo-id-in-result.text: `api.import_hf` returns `repo_id` as `"user/repo"` regardless of whether the caller supplied a bare id or a full HuggingFace URL.

import-hf-requires-init-for-postgres.text: When `pg_conninfo` is set, `import_hf` only initializes the schema if `init=True`, because the condition is `init or not pg_conninfo`.

import-hf-returns-normalized-repo-id.text: The `repo_id` in the returned dict is the output of `reasons.hf._parse_repo_id`, not the raw `repo_id` argument.

import-hf-returns-normalized-repo-id-and.text: `api.import_hf` returns a dict containing `nodes_imported`, `nogoods_imported`, and a normalized `repo_id`, even when the input was a full HuggingFace URL.

import-hf-stages-via-named-temporary-fil.text: The downloaded JSON is written to a `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` and cleaned up in a `finally` block, so `import_json` can consume it by path.

import-hf-token-path-not-established.text: The observations do not include `import_hf`'s body, so its direct token acquisition path is unconfirmed.

import-into-network-copies-selected-fron.text: `import_into_network` copies only non-empty `schema_version`, `project_name`, and `created_at` frontmatter values into `network.meta`.

import-into-network-does-not-reject-dupl.text: Duplicate claim IDs in `beliefs_text` are not rejected; `claim_by_id` keeps the last parsed occurrence for dependency membership checks.

import-into-network-is-not-transactional.text: `import_into_network` is not transactional; an exception during import can leave `network.meta`, `repos`, nodes, retractions, or nogoods partially mutated.

import-into-network-returns-summary-coun.text: `import_into_network` returns a summary dict containing `claims_imported`, `claims_skipped`, `claims_retracted`, and `nogoods_imported`.

import-into-network-skips-existing-node-.text: Re-importing the same beliefs text into a `Network` is idempotent by node existence: existing IDs increment `claims_skipped` and are not overwritten or content-compared.

import-into-network-topo-sort-ignores-un.text: The topological sort in `import_into_network` considers only `depends_on`, not `unless`, when ordering claims.

import-is-idempotent-by-node-existence.text: Re-importing claims whose IDs already exist reports `claims_imported == 0` and `claims_skipped == N`, leaving node content untouched.

import-json-copies-only-three-meta-keys.text: `import_json` copies only `schema_version`, `project_name`, and `created_at` from imported `meta`; other meta keys are silently dropped.

import-json-does-not-create-database.text: `import_json` requires the target SQLite database to already exist and be schema-initialized; it does not create the database.

import-json-is-idempotent-on-node-id.text: A second `import_json` of the same file into a populated DB returns `nodes_imported == 0` and does not raise.

import-json-missing-file-raises-filenotf.text: `api.import_json` raises `FileNotFoundError` when the specified path does not exist, rather than silently returning an empty import result — the error contract distinguishes "file not found" from "file had no nodes."

import-json-missing-justification-type-r.text: `import_json` does not defensively validate imported justification `"type"` or nogood `"id"` keys; missing keys raise `KeyError`.

import-json-only-restores-three-meta-key.text: Of the source `meta` dict, only `schema_version`, `project_name`, and `created_at` are copied to `net.meta`; all other keys are dropped, so round-trip fidelity of `meta` is partial.

import-json-parses-before-dispatch.text: `import_json` raises `FileNotFoundError` and parses JSON into `data=` before ever invoking `PgApi.import_json`, so no DB session is opened on a missing/invalid file path.

import-json-pg-dispatch-bypasses-sqlite-.text: When `pg_conninfo` is truthy, `import_json` returns immediately after `_pg_dispatch(...)`; the raw SQLite tags/sources restoration is never reached.

import-json-pg-dispatch-passes-parsed-da.text: When `pg_conninfo` is truthy, `import_json` parses the JSON file and passes the parsed `data` dict to `_pg_dispatch`, returning before the SQLite-specific `_with_network` and raw tags/sources restoration path.

import-json-propagates-file-not-found.text: import_json propagates FileNotFoundError when given a nonexistent path rather than swallowing it.

import-json-raises-on-missing-file.text: `api.import_json` on a nonexistent path raises `FileNotFoundError` rather than returning a partial summary.

import-json-requires-export-schema.text: `import_json` assumes the exact structure produced by `export_network` (dict-keyed nodes with `justifications`/`truth_value`, nogoods with `id`, meta dict); missing required keys raise `KeyError` rather than validating.

import-json-restores-generic-metadata.text: `tests/test_import_json.py::test_round_trip_metadata` verifies that at least one arbitrary metadata key survives export/import.

import-json-restores-tags-sources-via-se.text: On the SQLite path, `import_json` restores `node_tags` and `node_sources` via a separate `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` after `_with_network` has saved the network.

import-json-restores-truth-and-timestamp.text: After `add_node`, `import_json` restores exported truth values via `retract`/`assert_node` and then re-sets `reviewed_at`, `verified_at`, `retracted_at`, and `updated_at` so TMS propagation does not overwrite them.

import-json-restores-truth-values-after-.text: After `net.add_node` computes a truth value, `import_json` compares it to the exported value and forces it via `retract`/`assert_node`, then re-applies `reviewed_at`/`verified_at`/`retracted_at`/`updated_at` so the TMS doesn't overwrite them.

import-json-returns-nodes-imported-count.text: `api.import_json` returns a dict containing at minimum `nodes_imported` and `nogoods_imported`, both integer counts.

import-json-skips-existing-nodes.text: Nodes already present in the target network are counted in a local `skipped` variable but are not inserted or updated, so re-import is an approximate no-op rather than an upsert; `skipped` is not included in the return value.

import-json-skips-existing-nodes-not-ups.text: `import_json` skips node IDs already present in the target network and does not update them, so re-import is not an upsert for existing nodes.

import-json-topological-sort-enables-saf.text: Nodes are added in dependency order so that the `retract`/`assert_node` cascades during truth restoration only affect nodes that haven't been added yet, minimizing propagation from the import itself.

import-json-topologically-orders-nodes.text: `import_json` uses topological sort to add nodes in dependency order, with a fallback pass for cycles.

import-json-uses-topological-sort.text: `api.import_json()` reconstructs networks via a multi-pass topological sort loop — repeatedly adding nodes whose dependencies are already loaded — with a force-add fallback for cycles or missing deps.

import-json-writes-tags-and-sources-via-.text: Because tags and sources are not part of the `Network` save path, `import_json` opens a fresh `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` after `_with_network` exits and inserts into `node_tags` and `node_sources` using `INSERT OR IGNORE`.

import-maintenance-repo-negative-cli-now.text: Regression tests confirm that import, maintenance, repo, and negative CLI commands previously gated behind _require_sqlite now accept PG kwargs without error.

import-names-differ-from-distribution-na.text: The packages `reasons` and `reasons_lib` are importable, but the distribution is registered as `ftl-reasons`.

import-nogoods-require-two-existing-affe.text: `import_into_network` imports a nogood only if at least two of its affected nodes already exist in the network; otherwise it silently drops the nogood.

import-nogoods-require-two-valid-nodes.text: _import_nogoods only creates a nogood if at least two of its referenced nodes exist in the network.

import-ordering-ensures-correct-final-st.text: Import follows a deliberate ordering discipline — add nodes first, propagate truth values second, apply explicit retractions last — ensuring deferred retractions correctly override any truth values that propagation would compute, producing a final state that respects both structural dependencies and explicit intent.

justifications.label: The two-phase structure and deferred retraction ordering interact to guarantee correct final truth values

import-paths-bump-nogood-counter.text: Both `import_json` and `import_into_network` update `_next_nogood_id` to at least `max_imported_id + 1`, ensuring imported nogoods with explicit IDs don't create future collisions

import-pipeline-is-lenient-not-fail-fast.text: The beliefs.md import pipeline is designed to skip bad data and return counts rather than raise exceptions for malformed or missing references.

import-preserves-network-cascade-consist.text: After import, `Network.retract` on a premise correctly cascades to all transitive dependents (verified by `test_cascading_works_after_import`), which requires the importer to maintain both forward edges and the reverse `dependents` index.

import-provides-complete-reconciliation.text: The import subsystem provides complete reconciliation coverage: heterogeneous truth states are handled correctly on initial load, dual modes support additive import and remote-wins sync for different operational needs, and the colon-based namespace convention with auto-wiring prevents ID collisions across agents.

justifications.label: Import handles all truth states, sync handles ongoing updates, and namespacing prevents cross-agent collisions

import-reconciliation-converges-determin.text: Import reconciliation achieves both completeness and convergence: dual import/sync modes handle heterogeneous truth states with namespace isolation and topological cycle tolerance (completeness), while all reconciliation operations — individual propagation, agent sync, and global recompute — converge to deterministic fixed points on repeated application (convergence), ensuring that import never introduces oscillation or nondeterminism.

justifications.label: Complete reconciliation without deterministic convergence risks oscillation; convergence without completeness risks missing cases — together they guarantee stable, thorough import

import-result-shape-has-four-counters.text: `import_into_network` returns a dict with `claims_imported`, `claims_skipped`, `claims_retracted`, and `nogoods_imported` counters.

import-returns-count-summary.text: `import_into_network` returns a summary dict with counts `claims_imported`, `claims_retracted`, `claims_skipped`, and `nogoods_imported`.

import-skips-existing-sync-is-remote-win.text: Import mode (`import_agent`) is a one-time load that skips existing nodes; sync mode updates text/justifications/truth values with remote-wins semantics and retracts locally any beliefs removed from the remote

import-sync-has-dual-reconciliation-mode.text: The import/sync subsystem offers two distinct reconciliation strategies: import is additive (skips existing nodes), while sync is remote-wins (overwrites text, justifications, and truth values from the remote source).

justifications.label: The two modes represent a clear design choice between preserving local state (import) and trusting the remote source (sync)

import-sync-roundtrip-form-lossless-exte.text: The import→sync→export pipeline is lossless at every boundary: import tolerates missing metadata and topological cycles gracefully, sync preserves cascade structure with remote-wins reconciliation, and export/import roundtrips preserve behavioral equivalence including retraction and stale-reason state — external networks can be ingested, reconciled, and re-exported without semantic loss.

justifications.label: Each antecedent independently guarantees one boundary is lossless (ingestion tolerance, cycle handling, cascade preservation, roundtrip equivalence, retraction fidelity); the unified claim is end-to-end external interface losslessness.
