import-tests-separate-parse-and-import-f.text: The import test suite has separate `TestParseBeliefs` and `TestImportIntoNetwork` classes so parse bugs are distinguishable from import bugs.

import-tolerates-absent-metadata-without.text: Both JSON import (missing `"meta"` key) and Markdown import (missing YAML frontmatter) succeed with defaults rather than raising — the system must never crash on files written by older versions that lack the metadata envelope.

import-topo-sort-cycle-tolerant.text: Topological sorting of imported claims is best-effort: cycles cause remaining nodes to be appended in arbitrary order rather than raising an error, a pragmatic choice that avoids crashing on circular references.

import-topo-sort-tolerates-cycles.text: `_topo_sort_claims` attempts topological ordering but appends remaining nodes when progress stalls, gracefully handling dependency cycles instead of erroring

import-two-phase-truth-maintenance.text: Import/sync adds all nodes first, then runs `recompute_all()` to propagate truth values, then performs explicit retractions — this ordering prevents incorrect cascades from partially-constructed networks

import-wires-reverse-index.text: Covered by existing `dependents-is-manual-reverse-index` which captures that the reverse index is manually maintained

import-without-meta-is-backward-compatib.text: `api.import_json` succeeds on payloads lacking a `meta` key, imporing nodes without error.

imported-agent-nodes-carry-provenance-la.text: Imported agent nodes use the justification `label` to record provenance, e.g. `"imported from agent: agent-a"`.

imported-network-supports-retraction-cas.text: After importing SAMPLE_BELIEFS, retracting `premise-a` causes `derived-c` and `chain-e` to become OUT.

imported-nodes-namespaced-with-agent-pre.text: Every imported node ID is stored as `{agent_name}:{claim_id}`, and existing prefixed IDs cause the claim to be counted in `claims_skipped` rather than replaced.

importers-still-use-legacy-path.text: Seven internal modules under `reasons/` (`ask.py`, `cli.py`, `contradictions.py`, `derive.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `pg.py`, `repair.py`) and 50+ test files still import via `reasons_lib.api`, making the shim load-bearing until every one of those imports is migrated to `reasons.api`.

importing-shim-triggers-server-registrat.text: Any import of `reasons_lib.mcp_server` executes `reasons/mcp_server.py`'s module scope (server construction, tool registration) exactly once per process.

importlib-is-used-only-for-metadata.text: Both `importlib` imports (`reasons/cli.py:13`, `reasons/metadata.py:17`) are `importlib.metadata.version`, not dynamic module loading

importlib-used-only-for-installed-metada.text: The only `importlib` usage is `importlib.metadata.version` for installed distribution metadata, not dynamic module loading.

imports-tolerate-missing-schema-version.text: Store loading uses `meta.setdefault("schema_version", SCHEMA_VERSION)` (`storage.py:326`), and JSON/markdown imports succeed when `meta`/frontmatter is absent, so the field is not a hard requirement.

in-nodes-exclude-derived.text: `_build_beliefs_section` only includes base beliefs: nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` whose ID is **not** in `derived`.

in-requires-any-valid-justification.text: A node's `truth_value` becomes `"IN"` iff it is a premise (no justifications) or at least one of its justifications is valid (`reasons/__init__.py:30-31`).

inactive-mechanism-requires-rebuild-depe.text: outlist edges are registered only after `_rebuild_dependents()` (`import_agent.py:29–38`), since outlist nodes can be created after the beliefs that reference them.

inactive-nogood-is-no-op.text: If any node in a nogood is already `OUT`, `Network.add_nogood` returns an empty changed list and emits no backtrack log entry.

inactive-nogood-returns-empty.text: If any listed node is not `IN`, `add_nogood` returns `[]` and performs no retraction.

inactive-nogood-returns-empty-and-no-log.text: If any node in a nogood is already `OUT`, `Network.add_nogood` returns an empty changed list and writes no backtrack log entry.

inactive-nogood-short-circuits-backtrack.text: If any node in a nogood is already OUT, `add_nogood` returns an empty changed list and writes no `backtrack` entries to `propagation_log`.

inactive-not-in-antecedents.text: `inactive` is deliberately placed in outlist, never antecedents, to avoid an always-valid per-belief fallback.

inactive-relay-implements-kill-switch.text: Every imported belief's every outlist includes `<agent>:inactive`, so retracting `<agent>:active` cascades the entire agent's beliefs OUT.

inactive-relay-inverts-active.text: `{agent}:inactive` uses justification `SL(antecedents=[], outlist=[active])`, so it is IN exactly when `active` is OUT.

inactive-relay-justification-uses-empty-.text: The `agent:inactive` node uses an SL justification with empty antecedents and `outlist=[active_id]`.

inactive-relay-node-implements-kill-swit.text: `{agent}:inactive` is injected into every imported belief's outlist (or as the sole default outlist entry) so retracting `{agent}:active` cascades all imported beliefs OUT.

include-out-enables-out-visibility.text: Passing `include_out=True` causes all three retrieval APIs (`search`, `lookup`, `compact`) to include retracted nodes.

include-out-is-additive-not-exclusive.text: Passing `include_out=True` adds OUT nodes to `search`, `lookup`, and `compact` output without removing IN nodes.

incremental-propagation-is-fully-complet.text: Incremental truth propagation reaches every node whose truth value should change — including nodes that depend via outlist entries — without requiring periodic full recomputation, because safe terminating BFS traversal operates over a dependents index that tracks both antecedent and outlist relationships.

justifications.label: When the outlist-tracking gap is fixed, safe terminating propagation combined with fully-specified outlist semantics should yield complete incremental consistency — making recompute_all a verification tool rather than a correctness requirement

indefinite-self-correction-is-fully-audi.text: The system's indefinitely sustainable self-correction produces a fully auditable history without temporal degradation: every self-correction, maintenance action, and belief revision throughout the system's unbounded operational lifetime is traceable through nogoods, retraction records, and staleness metadata — auditability scales with time rather than decaying.

justifications.label: Connects the depth-7 leaf (indefinite sustainability) with depth-11 auditability — establishes that auditability is not merely a snapshot property but extends across unbounded operation, because both self-correction and its audit trail are sustained by the same minimality fixed-point

information-boundaries-are-controlled-at.text: The system controls information flow at every boundary: internally through access-tag authorization gating and token-budget constraints on output, and externally through bidirectional bounds on LLM input/output quality and defensive belief ingestion pipelines

justifications.label: Internal authorization-and-budget controls combined with external surface controls yield fully-controlled information boundaries

information-boundaries-are-controlled-at.text: The system controls information flow internally at every boundary through access-tag authorization gating and token-budget constraints on output, and externally for tracked sources through bidirectional bounds on LLM input/output quality and defensive belief ingestion pipelines.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

information-flow-is-authorization-and-bu.text: Information flow from the belief network is controlled along two independent dimensions: access tags gate which beliefs are visible to each caller (authorization control via transitive subset checks), while token budgets constrain how much of the visible network is emitted (volume control via priority-ordered truncation).

justifications.label: Authorization and budget controls independently constrain what flows out and how much

information-flow-is-controlled-in-both-d.text: Information flow is controlled at every system boundary: inbound data passes through production-hardened LLM integration (bounded execution, fail-soft handling, process isolation) and boundary-controlled information isolation (access tags, namespace partitioning), while outbound data is deterministic, authorized via transitive subset-gated access control, and budget-constrained — no uncontrolled data enters or leaves the belief network

justifications.label: Input hardening (depth-6) and output authorization (depth-4) are independently necessary but insufficient — bidirectional control means the system is a closed information boundary where every crossing is mediated, whether data flows in through LLM derivation and agent import or out through compact, search, and explain

information-governance-is-end-to-end-aut.text: Information governance is enforced end-to-end from pipeline-level resource management through output-level authorization: the pipeline is resource-governed through accurate bidirectional token budgets and access-controlled through transitive subset-gated tags, while the output layer adds deterministic authorized distillation through pure functions with fixed priority ordering — ensuring governance is not concentrated at a single chokepoint but layered across the complete information flow.

justifications.label: Pipeline-level governance and output-level authorization are complementary layers that prevent governance bypass through either channel

information-output-is-authorized-budgete.text: Information leaving the belief network is controlled along three independent dimensions: authorization gating ensures callers see only beliefs their tags permit, token budgets constrain output quantity, and the compact module's pure-function deterministic priority ordering guarantees reproducible distillation — output is simultaneously access-controlled, size-bounded, and predictable.

justifications.label: Authorization-and-budget control combined with deterministic bounded distillation provides triple-controlled information output

information-pipeline-is-resource-governe.text: The complete information pipeline is governed along two orthogonal axes: token budgets accurately constrain both input (proportional derive allocation) and output (compact distillation with budget enforcement), while access tags enforce transitive subset-based authorization at every read boundary — every piece of information is simultaneously resource-bounded and access-controlled.

justifications.label: Resource governance (depth-2) and access control (depth-1) are independent enforcement dimensions that together fully characterize information flow governance

init-db-always-reports-created-true.text: On the SQLite path, `init_db` always returns `{"created": True}` on success; it never returns `created: False`.

init-db-default-project-name-is-filename.text: `api.init_db` without an explicit `project_name` derives the default from `Path(db_path).stem`.

init-db-depends-on-storage-constructor-f.text: `init_db` performs no direct schema writes; the file and schema are created as a side effect of instantiating `Storage`.

init-db-does-not-clear-network-cache.text: `init_db` never calls `clear_network_cache`, so any cached `Network` for `db_path` is only invalidated on the next `_with_network` load via mtime comparison.

init-db-does-not-close-connection-on-fai.text: `init_db()` closes the cursor via context manager but never closes `self.conn` on exception.

init-db-does-not-create-parent-directory.text: `init_db` does not create parent directories; a missing parent for `db_path` causes `Storage` or `Path.unlink()` to raise.

init-db-does-not-rollback-on-failure.text: `init_db()` commits only on success and has no exception handler that calls `rollback()`.

init-db-force-deletes-existing-database.text: With `force=True`, `init_db` unconditionally calls `Path.unlink()` on the existing file, discarding all prior beliefs before recreating it.

init-db-force-deletes-existing-sqlite-an.text: `init_db(force=True)` irreversibly unlinks an existing SQLite database file, but `force` is not forwarded and is effectively ignored on the PostgreSQL path.

init-db-ignores-db-path-and-force-when-p.text: When `pg_conninfo` is truthy, `init_db` delegates to `_pg_dispatch` and does not forward `db_path` or `force` to the Postgres backend.

init-db-raises-fileexists-without-force.text: init_db raises FileExistsError when the target SQLite database already exists and force is not True.

init-db-raises-on-existing-file-unless-f.text: When `db_path` exists and `force=False`, `init_db` raises `FileExistsError` without mutating the existing database.

init-db-raises-on-reinit-unless-force.text: `api.init_db()` raises `FileExistsError` when called on an existing database path unless `force=True` is passed, which overwrites.

init-db-refuses-existing-db-without-forc.text: On the SQLite path, `init_db` raises `FileExistsError` when `db_path` exists and `force=False`, before any filesystem mutation.

init-db-refuses-existing-path-unless-for.text: `api.init_db(db_path)` returns `{"created": True}` for a new path, raises `FileExistsError` when the path already exists, and overwrites only when `force=True`.

init-db-refuses-existing-without-force.text: `api.init_db()` raises `FileExistsError` when the database file already exists, unless `force=True` is passed to allow overwrite.

init-db-schema-creation-delegated-to-sto.text: `init_db` creates the SQLite schema only by constructing `Storage(db_path, project_name=...)` and closing it; it performs no direct schema DDL itself.

init-db-sqlite-return-always-created-tru.text: On SQLite success, `init_db` always returns `{"db_path": str(Path(db_path)), "created": True}`; there is no already-existed success state.

init-has-zero-external-deps.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py` imports only `dataclasses` from the standard library, making it the dependency-free root of the package — imported by 29 test files and transitively by every module in `reasons_lib`.

init-is-pure-data-model.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py` contains only dataclass definitions (`Node`, `Justification`, `Nogood`) with no behavior, validation, or I/O; it imports nothing from the project and sits at the bottom of the import graph.

init-requires-force-flag-for-reinitializ.text: Running `init` on an existing database without `--force` fails with exit code 1 and mentions `--force` in stderr, preventing accidental data loss from re-initialization.

initialization-and-reconciliation-conver.text: Both initialization paths (stored-state bootstrap trusting persisted values, and deterministic reasoning computing from scratch) and reconciliation operations (dual import/sync modes with heterogeneous truth state handling) converge to equivalent correct belief states — the system reaches the same outcome regardless of how or when beliefs enter the network.

justifications.label: Path-independent initialization combined with complete reconciliation ensures convergent ingestion

initialization-is-path-independent.text: Whether beliefs enter through stored-state bootstrap (load trusts stored truth values, import builds nodes before recompute_all) or through the deterministic reasoning engine (uniform pure evaluation with guaranteed termination), the system reaches correct truth states — bootstrap trusts values that were originally computed by the same deterministic engine, and import re-derives them via recompute_all, establishing path independence of initialization.

justifications.label: bootstrap trusts values computed by deterministic engine; import re-derives via same engine

initialization-is-path-independent-and-b.text: System initialization is path-independent for correct truth states and uses backend-appropriate safety mechanisms across SQLite and PostgreSQL: initialization paths converge to equivalent correct belief states, and safety properties do not depend on a specific backend or layer; full state equivalence and initialization purity across backends are not claimed.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-1

initialization-is-pure-across-path-and-b.text: System initialization is a pure function of input data: convergence equivalence (all initialization paths yield identical state) composed with backend independence (path independence holds across SQLite and PostgreSQL) yields full initialization purity

justifications.label: Convergence equivalence eliminates path-dependence (stored-state bootstrap ≡ deterministic reasoning); backend independence eliminates substrate-dependence (SQLite ≡ PostgreSQL). The composition of two independent orthogonality axes (path × backend) yields a single purity guarantee: the resulting network state is a pure function of the input data, independent of both the implementation route taken and the storage substrate used.

initialization-is-safe-and-path-independ.text: System initialization produces identical belief states regardless of both initialization path (stored-state bootstrap vs deterministic reasoning) and storage backend (SQLite vs PostgreSQL providing equivalent safety through backend-appropriate mechanisms), eliminating all bootstrap-time variation

justifications.label: Path independence and backend agnosticism jointly eliminate all initialization-time environmental variation

initialization-is-safe-and-path-independ.text: System initialization reaches correct truth states regardless of the initialization path (stored-state bootstrap or deterministic reasoning), as bootstrap trusts values originally computed by the same deterministic engine and import re-derives them via recompute_all, supporting path independence of initialization; safety is enforced uniformly across architectural layers and storage backends (SQLite and PostgreSQL) through backend-appropriate mechanisms, with no safety property depending on a specific backend or layer.

input-validation-is-comprehensive-at-all.text: Input validation is enforced at every system boundary through complementary mechanisms: typed exceptions (ValueError for duplicates, PermissionError for access violations) enforce API-level preconditions at the call boundary, while defense-in-depth reference validation (import normalization dropping unknown refs, nogood filtering skipping invalid nodes, hallucinated ID rejection) catches invalid node references at every data-acceptance boundary.

justifications.label: API-level validation (depth-1) gates the call boundary; reference validation (depth-1) gates all data boundaries — no invalid input survives to reach the TMS engine regardless of entry point.

inspection-outputs-are-uniformly-normali.text: Both inspection mechanisms — belief review and staleness checking — produce normalized, schema-consistent, fail-safe output with deterministic structure suitable for automated consumption.

justifications.label: Review (6-key normalized schema, defaults to passing) and staleness (6-key uniform schema, sorted by node_id) both guarantee machine-parseable deterministic output

inspection-to-repair-enforces-read-mutat.text: The self-correction pipeline enforces strict phase separation: all diagnostic phases (review, check-stale) are purely read-only with zero mutation, and the sole mutation phase (repair) preserves existing outlist governance, ensuring no pipeline stage can silently corrupt network state or bypass established controls.

justifications.label: The separation claim requires both read-only diagnostics AND mutation-with-preservation; removing any one breaks the strict three-phase invariant (observe → observe → guarded-mutate).

integrity-and-scalability-are-complement.text: The system achieves comprehensive integrity (unified across all internal mutations and external belief ingestion) and sound multi-agent scalability (isolated namespaces, minimal primitives, deterministic propagation) simultaneously — these properties reinforce rather than trade off against each other because both derive from the same uniform evaluation rules.

justifications.label: Unifying the integrity story (depth-5) with the scalability story (depth-5) shows these are complementary consequences of uniform primitives, not competing design goals

integrity-detects-unhashed-text-mutation.text: `api.check_integrity` reports a direct text mutation as a `text_mutation` when stored `text_hash` no longer matches the node’s text.

integrity-enforced-across-architecture-a.text: Integrity is enforced along two orthogonal dimensions: vertically across architectural layers (clean data-model/TMS/persistence boundaries with snapshot persistence and CI gating) and horizontally across node lifecycle states (staleness checking skips OUT nodes without mutating, propagation skips retracted nodes while preserving them for restoration).

justifications.label: Architectural-layer integrity prevents cross-cutting mutations while lifecycle-state integrity prevents operating on nodes in inappropriate states — both dimensions must hold for system-wide consistency

integrity-is-an-emergent-consequence-of-.text: End-to-end integrity across all mutation paths and architectural boundaries is not an independently-achieved property requiring separate enforcement — it falls out of minimality as another emergent consequence, because uniform primitive evaluation leaves no gaps for inconsistency to enter.

justifications.label: if minimality generates all properties and the unified system has integrity, then integrity is itself a generated property rather than an imposed constraint

integrity-is-boundary-and-source-agnosti.text: System integrity is enforced agnostically along two independent dimensions — across the internal/external boundary (local mutations vs. external ingestion) and across mutation sources (human dialectics, LLM derivation, agent import) — because the same atomic-deterministic pipeline processes all combinations without branching on origin or direction.

justifications.label: Unifies the internal/external integrity boundary dimension with the mutation-source safety dimension to show integrity enforcement is fully agnostic to both boundary crossing and belief origin

interfaces-import-downward-only.text: Interface modules such as `cli.py`, `api.py`, `mcp_server.py`, and `mind_service.py` may import domain modules, but reasoning-core modules must not import interface modules.

intermediate-cascade-flaps-produce-no-ev.text: A node that flips IN→OUT→IN during a cascade produces no pub/sub event because the before/after snapshots are identical.

internal-and-external-integrity-are-unif.text: Every operation — internal mutations (atomic transactions, deterministic propagation) and external belief ingestion (defensive validation, environment isolation, agent containment) — maintains end-to-end integrity through complementary safety mechanisms.

justifications.label: depth-5 — internal operational integrity and external belief bounding are independent safety dimensions that together cover all mutation sources

internal-check-stale-consumers-use-canon.text: Observed internal consumers import `.check_stale` or `reasons.check_stale`, not `reasons_lib.check_stale`.

internal-code-no-longer-imports-reasons-.text: The claimed zero `reasons_lib` matches conflicts with other observed entries and accepted beliefs showing that internal `reasons/*` modules still import through the shim.

internal-metadata-never-appears-in-json-.text: Per 0.16.0, `_`-prefixed keys like `_retracted` are scrubbed from JSON export; this is a downstream contract.

internal-python-code-does-not-import-rea.text: The Python source grep for `reasons_lib` reports zero matches.

intra-cluster-assumes-kmeans-returns-k-c.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` assumes KMeans returns exactly `k` distinct non-empty clusters; if fewer labels are produced, `focus_idx = round_num % k` can index past the sorted cluster label list.

intra-cluster-cache-model-overrides-mode.text: When `cluster_beliefs_intra` is given a `ClusterCache`, embeddings use `cache.model_name` while the `model_name` parameter is not used for embedding and is only reported in the early-return path.

intra-cluster-explicit-n-clusters-overri.text: When `n_clusters` is provided to `cluster_beliefs_intra`, it is coerced to between `1` and `len(beliefs)` and overrides the budget-derived `max_k` cap used by `_auto_k`.

intra-cluster-focus-is-round-robin.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` concentrates the entire budget on a single cluster selected by `sorted_clusters[round_num % k]` (largest-first), meaning successive derive rounds cycle through clusters in deterministic round-robin order rather than always focusing on the largest.

intra-cluster-selection-is-budget-upper-.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` returns at most `budget` selected IDs and may return fewer when the focused cluster has fewer than `budget` members, so callers must not assume `len(selected_ids) == budget`.

intra-cluster-stats-misalign-focus-and-s.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` builds `cluster_sizes` in ascending cluster-label order but indexes `focus_cluster` into clusters sorted by descending size, so `cluster_sizes[focus_cluster]` is not guaranteed to be the focused cluster's size.

invalid-proposal-enums-default.text: Invalid `basis`, `failure_mode`, and `action` values normalize to `"prior-knowledge"`, `""`, and `"update"` respectively.

invariant-preservation-is-architecturall.text: The complete reasoning-and-revision architecture preserves invariants through minimal foundations not in a vacuum but atop concrete architectural safety — three-layer containment and atomic mutations provide the structural substrate within which minimal invariant preservation operates.

justifications.label: The logical property (invariant preservation through minimality, depth-6) and the physical substrate (three-layer boundaries + atomic mutations, depth-3) come from independent antecedent chains; their conjunction grounds the abstract in the concrete

invariant-preservation-is-comprehensive.text: System invariants are comprehensively preserved through two complementary mechanisms: the closed revision/lifecycle loop ensures temporal coverage across forward computation and backward revision, while dual structural/dynamic enforcement provides orthogonal protection through architectural grounding and minimality-enforced self-correction.

justifications.label: Temporal invariant coverage from the closed loop combines with structural/dynamic enforcement for multi-mechanism comprehensive protection

invariant-preservation-is-self-sustainin.text: Comprehensive invariant preservation — spanning revision loops, lifecycle management, and architectural grounding — is itself sustained by minimality's fixed-point property: the minimal primitives that preserve invariants are themselves invariants of the system, closing a meta-level consistency loop.

justifications.label: Minimality's fixed-point property applies reflexively to invariant preservation itself

invariant-preservation-is-total.text: Invariant preservation is both comprehensive in scope (spanning revision loops, lifecycle management, and structural/dynamic enforcement) and grounded across all independent dimensions (origin, time, and structure), achieving total invariant coverage with no gaps in either what is preserved or where preservation holds.

justifications.label: Comprehensive scope (the "what" of preservation) combined with multi-dimensional grounding (the "where/when" of preservation) yields total coverage; these address orthogonal aspects — mechanism vs. dimensions.

invariant-preservation-is-total-and-self.text: Invariant preservation is simultaneously total in scope (spanning all invariant dimensions and encompassing all belief types including externally-integrated ones) and self-sustaining in mechanism (maintained by minimality's fixed-point that dynamically corrects any departure) — comprehensiveness and sustainability are co-achieved rather than traded off.

justifications.label: Cross-connects two parallel depth-11 branches that independently established totality and self-sustainability of invariant preservation — neither is an antecedent of the other, yet they describe complementary aspects of the same system property

invariants-are-origin-time-and-structura.text: System invariants are anchored along three dimensions: they hold across all belief origins and through time (comprehensive scope), and they are grounded in the concrete architecture's clean layer boundaries and atomic operations (structural foundation) — the invariants are both broad in what they cover and deep in how they are enforced.

justifications.label: Origin-time coverage and architectural grounding converge to establish invariants with both comprehensive scope and structural foundation

invariants-are-structurally-and-dynamica.text: System invariants are preserved through two complementary layers: architectural grounding provides structural enforcement via clean layer boundaries and atomic mutations, while minimality-enforced self-correction actively detects and resolves violations through contradiction resolution and staleness detection.

justifications.label: static architectural structure and dynamic minimality-enforced correction jointly prevent invariant violations from persisting

invariants-hold-across-origin-and-time.text: System invariants hold along every independent dimension: across all belief origins (human-initiated, LLM-derived, agent-imported) via shared minimal foundations, and across both temporal phases (creation-time edge-case handling and maintenance-time staleness detection) including all semantic edge cases.

justifications.label: origin-spanning invariants plus temporal-spanning edge-case safety cover the full correctness matrix

invoke-api-creates-provider-client-per-c.text: `_invoke_api` instantiates `ChatAnthropic` or `ChatAnthropicVertex` on every call rather than caching a provider client.

invoke-api-defaults-vertex-region.text: For `vertex:` models, `_invoke_api` defaults `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` to `us-east5` when it is not set.

invoke-api-maps-timeout-heuristic.text: Any exception from `llm.invoke` whose class name or message contains `"timeout"` is re-raised as `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`; all other invoke exceptions are wrapped in `RuntimeError`.

invoke-api-requires-vertex-project.text: For `vertex:` models, `_invoke_api` raises `RuntimeError` when `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is missing or empty.

invoke-api-returns-content-unmodified.text: `_invoke_api` returns `response.content` directly without string coercion or post-processing, and a missing `.content` raises `AttributeError` outside its invoke try/except.

invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing.text: `_invoke_claude()` raises `FileNotFoundError` if the `claude` CLI is not on `PATH`, rather than returning an error string — this is the one exception that `ask()` does not catch internally.

invoke-model-always-returns-string-or-ra.text: `invoke_model()` in `reasons/llm.py` always returns a `str` on success and raises an exception on failure — it never returns `None`, a list, or a raw dict.

invoke-model-api-timeout-translated-exce.text: `_invoke_api` converts API timeout exceptions to `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, but `_invoke_openai` lets the raw OpenAI SDK timeout exception propagate.

invoke-model-cli-prompt-via-stdin.text: CLI invocations pass the prompt through stdin via `subprocess.run(input=prompt)`, not as a command-line argument.

invoke-model-forwards-timeout.text: invoke_model forwards its timeout argument to subprocess.run.

invoke-model-forwards-timeout-to-transpo.text: `invoke_model()` passes its `timeout` argument directly to `subprocess.run(timeout=...)` for CLI models and to the LangChain/OpenAI adapter's own timeout parameter for API models.

invoke-model-json-parse-failure-returns-.text: If `_parse_cli_json` cannot parse CLI stdout as JSON, `invoke_model` returns the raw stdout and records no token/cost data.

invoke-model-per-model-elapsed-only-afte.text: `invoke_model` updates `_cost_tracker["by_model"][model]["elapsed_seconds"]` only when a `by_model` entry already exists from a prior `_record_cost` call.

invoke-model-return-contract-is-str-or-r.text: `invoke_model()` in `reasons/llm.py` always returns a `str` (the model's text response) or raises an exception; it never returns `None`, a dict, or a LangChain object — a contract relied upon by 15+ caller modules.

invoke-model-returns-only-str.text: `invoke_model` in `reasons/llm.py:275` returns `str`, and callers like `reasons/ask.py:328`/`ask.py:336` chain `.strip()` on that return, so a non-`str` return would break call sites.

invoke-model-routes-api-prefixes-to-invo.text: `invoke_model` dispatches any `api:` or `vertex:` model string directly to `_invoke_api`, bypassing `resolve_model_cmd`.

invoke-model-strips-claudecode-env.text: invoke_model() in llm.py strips the CLAUDECODE environment variable before all subprocess.run() calls, preventing recursive Claude Code entry from any module that uses the shared LLM interface (ask, derive, review).

invoke-model-strips-claudecode-from-cli-.text: For CLI backends, `invoke_model` passes a copy of `os.environ` to the subprocess with the `CLAUDECODE` key removed.

invoke-model-updates-elapsed-on-failure.text: `invoke_model` increments global `_cost_tracker["elapsed_seconds"]` in a `finally` block even when the underlying call fails.

invoke_model-dispatches-by-model-prefix.text: The `model` string's prefix (`api:`, `vertex:`, `openai:`, otherwise CLI) selects the transport backend.

invoke_model-records-elapsed-in-finally.text: `_cost_tracker["elapsed_seconds"]` is incremented even when the call raises, because the increment is in a `finally` block.

invoke_model-strips-claudecode-env.text: The environment passed to CLI subprocesses omits the `CLAUDECODE` key.

is-derived-is-has-justifications.text: In both observed API response construction sites, `is_derived` is assigned from `has_justifications` (`reasons/api.py:3859`, `reasons/api.py:3904`).

is-visible-checks-only-node-own-tags.text: `_is_visible` checks only the node's own `metadata["access_tags"]`; it does not check transitive dependency visibility.

is-visible-does-not-raise-permissionerro.text: `_is_visible` returns only a bool; callers decide whether `False` means silently skip the node or raise `PermissionError`.

is-visible-is-pure-read-predicate.text: `_is_visible` only reads `node.metadata` and returns a bool; it performs no mutation, I/O, logging, or database access.

is-visible-none-visible-to-raises-for-ta.text: `_is_visible` raises `TypeError` when `visible_to=None` and the node has non-empty access tags; callers must guard `visible_to is not None` at the API boundary.

issue-121-evolution-tolerance-audit.text: Issue #121: Audit evolution tolerance at all system boundaries — not all boundaries have documented forward-compatibility mechanisms

issue-122-review-fault-tolerance-audit.text: Issue #122: Audit review module for unhandled failure modes — three specific handlers do not establish coverage of all failure modes

issue-123-resource-footprint-audit.text: Issue #123: Audit resource footprint across all lifecycle phases — only deployment and startup phases are currently evidenced

issue-126-reference-validation-audit.text: Issue #126: Audit all node ID reference boundaries for validation — three specific boundaries do not establish coverage of every boundary

jaccard-tokenizer-splits-on-hyphens-and-.text: `_tokenize_id` splits belief IDs on hyphens and colons into token sets for Jaccard similarity comparison, so `foo-bar-baz` and `foo-bar-qux` share 2/4 tokens (0.5 similarity)

json-export-includes-meta.text: `api.export_network(...)` returns a dict containing a `meta` key with `schema_version`, `node_count`, `project_name`, and `generator`.

json-import-overrides-destination-meta.text: Importing a JSON export with `meta.project_name` overrides the destination database’s default project name on re-export.

json-import-preserves-out-node-justifica.text: `_normalize_json` retains justifications on `truth_value=="OUT"` nodes, enabling resurrection; `_normalize_markdown` strips them.

json-parsers-scan-with-raw-decode.text: The LLM response parsers use `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode` while scanning each `{` so they tolerate prose around JSON.

json5-not-used-in-llm-response-parsing.text: No `json5` import, dependency, or call site is observed in the LLM-response JSON extraction paths.

justification-addition-is-robust-across-.text: Adding a justification to an existing node achieves fully consistent multi-dimensional propagation — truth values, dependents index, and access tags — even when the dependency graph contains dangling references or lifecycle-marked nodes, because propagation safely handles both graph anomalies and node lifecycle states.

justifications.label: Consistent justification propagation combined with graph-inconsistency safety ensures robust state transitions regardless of graph quality

justification-changes-count-as-updates.text: A dependency-edge change with identical text yields `beliefs_updated >= 1`, not `beliefs_unchanged`.

list-gated-excludes-superseded-out-nodes.text: Any OUT node with a truthy `metadata["superseded_by"]` is skipped before its justifications are inspected.

list-gated-filters-gated-nodes-by-visibl.text: The `_is_visible` check is applied to the OUT (gated) node, so nodes failing the tag subset are omitted entirely.

list-gated-finds-out-nodes-blocked-by-in.text: `list_gated` finds OUT nodes that are blocked by IN outlist nodes.

list-gated-finds-out-nodes-with-in-outli.text: `list_gated()` returns OUT nodes whose outlist contains IN nodes, identifying beliefs gated by an IN blocker.

list-gated-omits-blocker-visibility-chec.text: Blocker IDs and `text` are included in the result without any `visible_to` filtering on the blocker node, so caller-facing access control can be bypassed for blocker details.

list-gated-postgres-dispatch-requires-pa.text: `reasons/api.py:list_gated` delegates to `PgApi.list_gated` at `reasons/pg.py:1258` when the Postgres backend is selected.

list-gated-requires-in-blocker.text: An `outlist` entry only counts as a gate if the referenced node exists in the network and currently has `truth_value == "IN"`.

list-gated-visibility-filter-applies-onl.text: `visible_to` is checked on the gated OUT node but not on blocker nodes, so blocker IDs and text can be returned without blocker access-tag filtering.

list-negative-batches-at-40.text: `api.list_negative` splits candidates into batches of 40, so 120 keyword-matching nodes produce exactly 3 LLM calls.

list-negative-batches-at-50.text: `list_negative` splits candidate nodes into batches of approximately 50 for LLM classification, verified by the test suite asserting exactly 3 LLM calls for 120 candidates.

list-negative-filters-visibility-before-.text: `list_negative` applies `visible_to` to candidate nodes before building the LLM prompt, so restricted text is not sent to the model.

list-negative-is-bounded-and-batch-scala.text: The list-negative classification pipeline is both defensively bounded (two-stage keyword + LLM filtering with hallucination rejection and graceful malformed-output handling) and scalably partitioned (fixed batch size of ~50 candidates per LLM call), ensuring predictable resource usage and bounded LLM costs regardless of belief network size.

justifications.label: Defensive bounding prevents quality degradation; fixed batching prevents resource exhaustion — together they make classification safe at any scale.

list-negative-is-defensively-bounded.text: The negative belief listing pipeline applies defense-in-depth: keyword pre-filtering narrows candidates before LLM classification, hallucinated node IDs are discarded against the actual network, and malformed LLM output falls back gracefully to zero count rather than raising.

justifications.label: Three independent defensive measures form a complete safety pipeline for LLM-driven negative classification

list-negative-json-parser-tolerates-pros.text: The `list_negative` LLM classification response parser uses `re.finditer` to extract JSON objects from responses that include prose preamble, handling the common LLM pattern of prefacing structured output with natural language rather than requiring clean JSON.

list-negative-parser-is-fully-resilient.text: The list-negative LLM response parser handles all degradation levels: regex extraction recovers JSON objects from prose-laden responses, and completely unparseable output returns zero results gracefully rather than raising exceptions.

justifications.label: Two independent parser robustness properties combine to cover the full failure spectrum from partial corruption to total garbling

list-negative-two-stage-classification.text: `list_negative` uses keyword pre-filtering against a hardcoded `NEGATIVE_TERMS` list of about 50 words, then LLM classification via `ask._invoke_claude` to eliminate false positives.

list-negative-uses-two-stage-classificat.text: `list_negative` uses keyword pre-filtering against a hardcoded `NEGATIVE_TERMS` list (~50 words), then LLM classification via `ask._invoke_claude` to eliminate false positives.

list-nodes-aggregates-unsupported-pg-opt.text: `list_nodes` collects unsupported PostgreSQL keyword options and raises a single aggregated `NotImplementedError` at the top instead of failing one option at a time.

list-nodes-challenged-filters-to-challen.text: `api.list_nodes(challenged=True)` returns only nodes that have been challenged, excluding challenge nodes themselves and unchallenged premises.

list-nodes-clamps-limit-and-offset.text: `list_nodes` coerces non-`None` `limit` to `max(1, limit)` and coerces `offset` to `max(0, offset)`.

list-nodes-count-is-pagination-invariant.text: The returned `count` reflects the post-filter total before `limit`/`offset` are applied, so `count >= len(nodes)` whenever pagination is used.

list-nodes-count-is-pre-pagination-total.text: `list_nodes` returns `count` as the total matches after all filters including `tag` but before `limit`/`offset` pagination, so `count` can exceed `len(nodes)`.

list-nodes-defaults-source-type-to-empty.text: When a node has no `source_type` set, `api.list_nodes` returns `""` (an empty string, not None or a missing key) for the `source_type` field on that node's flat dict representation.

list-nodes-depth-filter-min-max.text: `api.list_nodes` depth filtering uses `min_depth` and `max_depth`; `min_depth=1` excludes depth-0 premise nodes and `max_depth=0` excludes derived nodes.

list-nodes-depth-is-none-unless-computed.text: `list_nodes` populates each node's `depth` field only when `min_depth`/`max_depth` are supplied or `sort == "depth"`; otherwise `depth` is `None`.

list-nodes-depth-populated-only-when-req.text: The `depth` field is `None` in the common path and is populated only when `min_depth`/`max_depth` are set or `sort == "depth"` triggers an on-demand recompute.

list-nodes-limit-clamped-minimum-one.text: A non-`None` `limit` is coerced to `max(1, limit)`; `limit=None` means unlimited, and `limit=0` yields exactly one result.

list-nodes-namespace-filter-requires-no-.text: `list_nodes` implements the `namespace` filter as `nid.startswith(f"{namespace}:")` without normalization, so passing `"ns:"` becomes `"ns::"` and matches nothing.

list-nodes-paginates-after-full-scan.text: `list_nodes` applies `limit`/`offset` only after building the complete filtered node list, so a small `limit` does not short-circuit the scan.

list-nodes-sort-is-ignored-in-pg-mode.text: In PostgreSQL mode, `list_nodes` does not forward `sort` to `PgApi.list_nodes`, so sorting is a no-op there even for `"created"`, `"updated"`, or `"depth"`.

list-nodes-supports-depth-range-filterin.text: `api.list_nodes()` supports `min_depth` and `max_depth` parameters to filter nodes by justification depth.

list-nodes-supports-review-metadata-filt.text: api.list_nodes supports `never_reviewed` and `not_reviewed_since` filters, `by_impact` sorting, and includes `last_reviewed` and `review_result` fields.

list-nodes-tag-filter-opens-fresh-sqlite.text: When `tag` is truthy, `list_nodes` resolves matches through `_filter_by_tags`, which opens a fresh raw SQLite connection to `db_path` and bypasses the in-memory `Network`.

list-operations-silently-filter-forbidde.text: `list_nodes`, `search`, `lookup`, `get_status`, `export_network`, `export_markdown`, `compact`, and `list_negative` return only visible nodes and never raise on access denial.

list-search-status-lookup-filter-results.text: `list_nodes`, `search`, `lookup`, and `get_status` filter out invisible nodes rather than raising, including search neighbor expansion.

listing-search-export-compact-filter-sil.text: `list_nodes`, `lookup`, `search`, `get_status`, `export_network`, `export_markdown`, and `compact` exclude invisible data without raising.

llm-api-path-normalizes-exceptions.text: The API invocation path maps timeout-like exceptions to `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and other exceptions to `RuntimeError`.

llm-api-path-skips-cost-recording.text: The `api:` and `vertex:` invocation path does not call `_record_cost`, so those calls do not contribute to cost/token totals.

llm-belief-operations-span-creation-and-.text: All LLM-driven belief operations — creation via derive (with safety, completeness, and resource efficiency) and classification via list-negative (with defensive bounding and batch scaling) — share consistent defensive patterns across the complete belief quality lifecycle.

justifications.label: The derive and list-negative pipelines independently achieve defensive robustness; together they cover the full LLM-driven belief lifecycle from creation through classification with no quality gap

llm-belief-pipeline-is-fully-quality-enf.text: The system's complete LLM-driven belief pipeline — both generation (derive with safety, completeness, and coverage) and classification (list_negative with defensive bounding) — achieves fully code-enforced quality constraints at every stage, provided minimum-antecedent validation moves from prompt-only to code-enforced.

justifications.label: Full LLM belief pipeline quality requires code-enforced antecedent validation

llm-callback-is-per-invocation.text: `reasons/llm.py:236` passes a Langfuse callback handler into a single `llm.invoke` call.

llm-centralizes-all-model-calls.text: Every LLM-assisted workflow (`verify`, `derive`, `review_justifications`, `contradictions`, `compact`) routes model access through `llm.py`.

llm-centralizes-model-calls.text: `llm.py` is the shared abstraction used by workflow modules (`derive.py`, `review*.py`, `ask.py`, `repair*.py`) instead of providers being called directly.

llm-checks-binary-exists-before-spawn.text: invoke_model uses shutil.which to check that the resolved model binary exists in PATH before spawning the subprocess, raising FileNotFoundError if missing.

llm-cli-json-parser-fails-open.text: `_parse_cli_json` returns raw CLI output on JSON parse failure or non-dict data instead of raising.

llm-cli-strips-claudecode-env.text: The CLI subprocess environment unconditionally removes `CLAUDECODE` to avoid the Claude CLI recursive-session guard.

llm-cost-summary-printed-to-stderr.text: Every LLM-invoking CLI handler follows a consistent three-step cost-tracking pattern: `reset_cost_tracker()` before the API call, then `format_cost_summary()` printed to `sys.stderr` (not stdout) after, keeping cost reporting separated from result output.

llm-cost-summary-returns-deepcopy.text: `get_cost_summary()` returns a deepcopy of the tracker so callers cannot mutate internal cost state.

llm-cost-tracker-mutations-are-lock-prot.text: `_cost_tracker` mutations happen under `_cost_lock`; the LLM call itself is not held under the lock.

llm-dispatch-routes-by-model-string-pref.text: `invoke_model()` uses the model string prefix as the sole dispatch mechanism: strings without `api:`/`vertex:` go through CLI subprocess (claude, gemini, ollama), while `api:*` and `vertex:*` go through langchain SDK clients.

llm-driven-mutations-are-safely-bounded.text: LLM-driven belief derivation is safely bounded by defense in depth: the derive pipeline validates proposals with fail-soft filtering, Jaccard retraction guards, and environment stripping at the LLM boundary, while the API layer enforces atomic load/save with write-flag gating and dict-only returns at the persistence boundary — malformed or adversarial LLM output cannot corrupt the network.

justifications.label: LLM-boundary defenses (depth-1) + persistence-boundary atomicity (depth-1) form defense in depth against the unique risks of machine-generated mutations

llm-exceptions-propagate-unwrapped.text: There is no `try/except` around `classify_defeat_reason`, so an LLM failure aborts the loop with already-written classifications left committed.

llm-extra-composes-api-vertex-langfuse.text: The `llm` extra installs `langchain-anthropic`, `langchain-google-vertexai`, and `langfuse`, but not `openai` or `mcp`.

llm-extra-excludes-openai.text: The `llm` meta-extra in pyproject.toml deliberately excludes `openai`; users requiring OpenAI must install `[llm,openai]` separately.

llm-extra-excludes-openai-and-mcp.text: The `llm` extra installs `langchain-anthropic`, `langchain-google-vertexai`, and `langfuse`, but does not install `openai` or `mcp`.

llm-extra-is-union-of-api-vertex-langfus.text: The `llm` extra duplicates `api` + `vertex` + `langfuse` and intentionally excludes `openai`, so its dependency lists must be manually kept in sync.

llm-failure-propagates-without-structure.text: If `model` is set and `invoke_model` raises, `report_belief` propagates the exception instead of falling back to the structured report.

llm-failures-are-swallowed-as-error-acti.text: Exceptions inside `_repair_one`'s `try` block are converted to `{"action": "error", "rationale": str(e)}` rather than re-raised.

llm-failures-return-beliefs.text: LLM timeouts and exceptions are swallowed and return `_beliefs_or_no_match(ctx)` instead of propagating.

llm-fault-tolerance-is-multi-granular.text: LLM fault tolerance operates at two independent granularities: module-level fail-soft handling ensures entire operations degrade gracefully when the LLM is unavailable, while item-level batch fault isolation ensures individual failures within derive and review batches are contained without affecting other items in the same batch.

justifications.label: Two orphaned depth-1 beliefs capturing independent fault-isolation granularities that together provide defense-in-depth within the LLM pipeline

llm-integration-fails-softly-across-modu.text: All LLM-facing modules apply consistent fail-soft error handling: the ask module always returns a string even when the LLM is unavailable, and the derive pipeline accumulates per-proposal errors rather than raising exceptions — no LLM failure path crashes the system.

justifications.label: Cross-module consistency — both LLM integration points (ask and derive) apply fail-soft patterns, establishing a system-wide invariant for LLM error handling

llm-integration-is-bounded-fail-soft-and.text: LLM integration achieves three independent safety properties across all modules: execution bounds (iteration caps and timeouts), fail-soft error handling (always returns usable results on failure), and process isolation (subprocess invocation with CLAUDECODE environment stripping to prevent recursive entry)

justifications.label: Bounded fail-soft execution combined with subprocess isolation yields defense-in-depth for all LLM interactions

llm-integration-is-defense-in-depth-acro.text: All LLM integration achieves defense-in-depth across two independent layers: application-level defensive bounding provides iteration caps, fail-soft error handling, Jaccard retraction guards, and hallucination filtering across all LLM-facing operations, while infrastructure-level process isolation executes all LLM calls through subprocess boundaries with CLAUDECODE environment scrubbing to prevent recursive invocation — ensuring safety at both the semantic and process boundaries.

justifications.label: Application-layer defense and infrastructure-layer isolation are independent safety dimensions that combine into comprehensive defense-in-depth

llm-integration-is-production-hardened.text: LLM integration achieves production-grade robustness across all dimensions: infrastructure-level safety through bounded execution, fail-soft error handling, and process isolation prevents runaway or recursive invocations, while operational-level coverage and fault tolerance ensures both derive (batch) and ask (interactive) paths complete successfully or degrade gracefully under all failure modes.

justifications.label: Infrastructure-level safety (bounded/fail-soft/isolated) combined with operational-level coverage and fault tolerance produces production-hardened LLM integration

llm-invocation-returns-strings-across-ba.text: `tests/test_llm.py` verifies `invoke_model` for Claude/Gemini/Ollama CLIs and `api:`/`vertex:` LangChain wrappers, all producing plain text responses.

llm-invoke-checks-path-before-run.text: Covered by existing `invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing` (same behavior generalized to all model binaries).

llm-invoke-default-timeout-300-seconds.text: invoke_model has a default timeout of 300 seconds for LLM subprocess calls.

llm-invoke-model-is-single-facade.text: All LLM calls in the `reasons` package route through `invoke_model()`; no other module imports the SDKs directly.

llm-is-pluggable-enhancement-not-core-in.text: LLM capabilities (summarization in `compact.py`, derivation assistance in `llm.py`) are a pluggable enhancement layered on the TMS core; the core inference engine (`network.py`, `derive.py`, `repair.py`) has no dependency on any LLM module.

llm-json-extraction-requires-strict-json.text: LLM response parsing uses `JSONDecoder.raw_decode` scanning, so it accepts only complete strict JSON and does not tolerate comments, trailing commas, single-quoted strings, or partial/streamed JSON.

llm-langfuse-callback-is-per-invocation.text: `reasons/llm.py` attaches the Langfuse callback handler to a single `llm.invoke(...)` call, making it per-invocation tracing rather than a cumulative batch callback.

llm-layer-returns-model-text-without-ref.text: `reasons/llm.py` contains no refusal-phrase matching; its parsers and dispatch paths return raw model text.

llm-layer-returns-raw-text.text: `_parse_cli_json` (line 137) falls back to `data.get("response", output)` and `_invoke_api` (line 246) returns `response.content`, so refusals reach callers as plain strings.

llm-mock-targets-subprocess-boundary.text: All LLM-dependent tests patch `reasons.llm.shutil.which` and `reasons.llm.subprocess.run` specifically, ensuring the text-parsing and type-matching logic in `classify_defeat_reason` always executes for real while only the external process invocation is replaced.

llm-model-resolution-supports-four-synta.text: resolve_model_cmd supports exact MODEL_COMMANDS names, claude:<submodel>, gemini:<submodel>, and ollama:<model> syntax forms.

llm-module-has-no-tool-schema-knowledge.text: `reasons/llm.py` contains no tool definitions or schemas; tool descriptions are built in `ask.py` prompts.

llm-module-is-shared-provider-abstractio.text: `reasons/llm.py` is the shared LLM provider abstraction used by `ask`, `review*`, `derive`, `propose_update`, and `import_agent` workflows.

llm-mutations-are-bounded-end-to-end.text: LLM-driven belief derivation is bounded at every stage of the pipeline: input validation (fail-soft filtering, Jaccard retraction guard, environment isolation), atomic persistence (context-managed load/save), and output propagation (deterministic terminating BFS with lifecycle-aware traversal).

justifications.label: depth-3 — input bounding (derive pipeline defenses) and output bounding (propagation safety) are independently established, together covering the full mutation lifecycle

llm-nonzero-exit-raises-runtimeerror-wit.text: A non-zero exit from an LLM subprocess causes invoke_model to raise RuntimeError containing the subprocess stderr output.

llm-parse-cli-json-parses-envelope-not-r.text: `llm.py:_parse_cli_json` unwraps the CLI `--output-format json` envelope (`result`/`response` + usage) and falls back to raw stdout on `JSONDecodeError`; it does not validate the model's semantic JSON.

llm-path-prepends-title-and-summary.text: In the LLM path, `report_gated()` prepends `# Gated Beliefs Report` and the generated-date summary before the LLM content.

llm-prompt-always-via-stdin.text: Prompts are passed to LLM subprocesses via `subprocess.run(input=...)`, never as command-line arguments — avoiding shell injection and argument length limits.

llm-prompts-are-passed-via-subprocess-in.text: Tests intercept LLM calls by reading `kwargs["input"]` from the mocked `subprocess.run`, establishing that the prompt travels over stdin, not argv.

llm-prompts-passed-via-stdin-not-argv.text: LLM prompts are passed to LLM subprocesses through `subprocess.run(input=...)` rather than as command-line arguments.

llm-provider-flags-are-import-guards.text: Each `_HAS_*` flag in `reasons/llm.py` is set by a successful optional import and cleared to `False` on `ImportError`; extras affect flags only by making those imports available.

llm-provider-imports-use-independent-fla.text: This duplicates the existing belief `llm-provider-flags-are-import-guards`, which already covers independent per-provider import flags in `llm.py`.

llm-requires-lock-for-cost-tracking.text: Every write to `_cost_tracker` occurs under `_cost_lock`, thread-safety is enforced at the module level.

llm-resolve-ollama-preserves-inner-colon.text: `resolve_model_cmd("ollama:model:tag")` splits on the first colon only, keeping `model:tag` intact as the Ollama model identifier.

llm-subprocess-invocation-is-security-ha.text: All LLM subprocess invocations follow a unified security pattern: CLAUDECODE env is stripped to prevent recursive invocation, and prompts are passed via stdin (never argv) to prevent shell-injection and argument parsing vulnerabilities.

justifications.label: Convergent evidence — each subprocess call site independently enforces the same two security properties (recursive-injection prevention + shell-injection prevention), establishing a project-wide invariant for LLM process spawning.

Convergent evidence — each subprocess call site independently enforces the same two security properties (recursive-injection prevention + shell-injection prevention), establishing a project-wide invariant for LLM process spawning.

llm-subprocess-isolation-prevents-recurs.text: All LLM subprocess invocations strip the CLAUDECODE environment variable to prevent recursive Claude Code entry, enforced centrally in invoke_model() and inherited by all LLM-facing modules (ask, derive, review).

justifications.label: Centralized enforcement in invoke_model covers all LLM-facing modules

llm-subprocess-mock-requires-two-patches.text: Testing infrastructure detail (which objects to patch), not a production code invariant. The underlying fact about `shutil.which` + `subprocess.run` is already captured by `all-external-execution-is-subprocess-isolated` and `invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing`.

llm-thinking-strip-ollama-only.text: Thinking-marker stripping (`Thinking...` / `...done thinking.`) is applied only to Ollama model output; Claude and Gemini output passes through unmodified even if it contains the same markers.

llm-thinking-strip-requires-both-markers.text: invoke_model strips Ollama thinking output only when both 'Thinking...' and '...done thinking.' markers are present; partial markers leave output unchanged.

llm-three-error-types.text: Too granular — the three error types (ValueError, FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError) are implementation details of the error taxonomy already captured by existing beliefs about fail-fast and fail-soft behavior.

load-bypasses-add-node.text: `load()` constructs `Node` objects directly and calls `network._rebuild_dependents()` instead of using `Network.add_node`.

loaded-network-supports-further-inferenc.text: A `Network` returned by `Storage.load()` is a fully operational inference engine (retract, restore, and propagation all work), not a frozen read-only snapshot — the storage layer must reconstruct all internal graph links including SL/justification connections.

loaded-networks-remain-operational.text: A `Network` loaded from SQLite supports `retract` and `assert_node` with propagation to dependent nodes.

loading-message-printed-before-model-loa.text: The `Loading embedding model...` message (line 1692) is emitted before `ClusterCache(...)` is constructed, so it is visible even when the constructor later fails with an `ImportError`.

local-budget-floor-is-five.text: `TestBudgetFloor` asserts the local belief budget never drops below 5 when agents exceed the budget.

lookup-searches-all-terms-substring.text: `lookup()` performs an all-terms substring search across the full belief block, including ID, text, source, and dependencies.

main-blocks-on-run.text: `mcp.run()` is a blocking stdio transport loop, so `main` normally never returns during server operation.

main-dispatches-by-command-string-dict.text: `main()` routes subcommand execution through a `commands: dict[str, Callable]` table rather than `argparse.set_defaults(func=...)`.

main-exits-1-on-missing-subcommand.text: When `args.command` is `None`, `main` prints the help to stdout and calls `sys.exit(1)` rather than relying on argparse's `required=True`.

main-finds-db-without-validating-existen.text: `_find_db()` may return `api.DEFAULT_DB` for a path that does not exist; `main` does not verify the file is present or readable.

main-prewarms-db-cache.text: `main` assigns `_db = _find_db()` before starting the MCP server, bypassing lazy initialization during normal server startup.

main-prewarms-db-cache-before-mcp-run.text: `main()` assigns `_db = _find_db()` before `mcp.run()`, so normal server startup bypasses lazy discovery in `_get_db`.

main-requires-global-flags-before-subcom.text: Global options (`--db`, `--pg`, `--version`, etc.) must precede the subcommand token because they are declared on the root parser, not passed through to subparsers.

main-requires-mcp-package.text: Importing `reasons.mcp_server` fails with `ImportError` if the `mcp` package is unavailable, before `main` can run.

main-resolves-db-before-run.text: `main` assigns `_db = _find_db()` before calling `mcp.run()`, so all tool calls use the same resolved path without re-running discovery.

main-resolves-db-eagerly.text: `main` assigns `_db` via `_find_db()` before calling `mcp.run()`, so all tool calls use the same path without re-discovery.

main-shares-db-with-get-db.text: `main` and `_get_db` intentionally share the module global `_db`, and `_get_db`'s `None`-check makes the eager assignment in `main` idempotent.

maintenance-loop-is-fully-observable.text: The minimality-sustained closed maintenance loop has complete observability: every self-correction leaves traceable history (nogoods, retraction records, staleness reports), enabling full audit of how the system maintains itself over time.

justifications.label: closed-loop maintenance combined with traceable correction history yields full observability of all maintenance activity

make-nodes-excludes-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a claim about production code behavior

make-nodes-omits-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a production code invariant

malformed-pinned-lines-falls-back-to-has.text: A `pinned_lines` value that fails `int-int` parsing triggers the full-file hash path rather than silently succeeding (check_stale.py:110-113).

mark-duplicate-and-superseded-reject-sel.text: Both `mark_duplicate(x, x)` and `mark_superseded(x, x)` raise `ValueError` with a message indicating self-reference is forbidden, leaving the node in its original `IN` truth state unchanged.

mark-duplicate-does-not-rewire-dependent.text: `mark_duplicate` records the duplicate link and retracts the source, but it does not rewrite dependents to point at `canonical_id`; `apply_dedup_plan`/`_rewrite_dependents` performs that rewiring instead.

mark-duplicate-does-not-rewrite-dependen.text: The function records `duplicate_of` and retracts, but never rewires dependent justifications to point at `canonical_id` (contrast: `apply_dedup_plan` does).

mark-duplicate-has-no-pg-dispatch.text: `mark_duplicate` has no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` parameters and never calls `_pg_dispatch`; it always opens a SQLite database at `db_path`.

mark-duplicate-is-sqlite-only.text: `mark_duplicate` has no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` parameters and never calls `_pg_dispatch`, unlike most sibling API functions.

mark-duplicate-overwrites-prior-retract-.text: Calling `mark_duplicate` or `mark_superseded` on a node that is already `OUT` (from a prior retraction) succeeds and overwrites the existing `retract_reason` metadata with the dedup/supersession-specific message (e.g., `"Duplicate of <canonical>"`) rather than failing or appending.

mark-duplicate-produces-duplicate-of-met.text: `reasons/api.py:1267` writes `metadata["duplicate_of"]`, which is verified in `tests/test_deduplication.py` and rendered by `reasons/build_wiki.py:60-63`.

mark-duplicate-produces-retraction-casca.text: Its returned `changed` list is the cascade of truth-value changes from `Network.retract(source_id)`, not just the source node.

mark-duplicate-raises-on-self-reference.text: Passing the same ID for `source_id` and `canonical_id` raises `ValueError`.

mark-duplicate-records-metadata-only-dup.text: `mark_duplicate` writes `duplicate_of` and `retract_reason` into the source node's metadata, but the `duplicate_of` relationship is metadata-only and does not participate in TMS propagation.

mark-duplicate-rejects-self-reference.text: `mark_duplicate` raises `ValueError` when `source_id == canonical_id`, before any database I/O occurs.

mark-duplicate-requires-existing-source-.text: `api.mark_duplicate` raises `KeyError("not found")` when either ID is missing.

mark-duplicate-requires-fully-resolved-n.text: `mark_duplicate` performs no namespace resolution, so callers must pass fully resolved node IDs and bare IDs that need prefixing cause `KeyError`.

mark-duplicate-stores-duplicate-of-metad.text: It writes `duplicate_of` and `retract_reason` into the source node's `metadata` dict before retracting.

mark-operations-overwrite-existing-retra.text: Marking an already-retracted node replaces its prior `retract_reason` with the duplicate/supersession reason.

mark-superseded-does-not-modify-new-id.text: `mark_superseded` only mutates `old_id`'s metadata and truth value; `new_id`'s truth value and metadata are untouched even if `new_id` is OUT.

mark-superseded-does-not-touch-new-id.text: The function only mutates `old_id`'s metadata and truth value; `new_id`'s truth value and metadata are untouched, even if `new_id` is OUT.

mark-superseded-emits-pubsub-deltas.text: Because it opens `_with_network(db_path, write=True)` with subscribers present, it captures `_before` truth values and publishes `pubsub.compute_changes` events on context exit.

mark-superseded-is-irreversible.text: `mark_superseded` uses `Network.retract()`, not an outlist justification, so the retraction cannot be undone by asserting `new_id`; only `supersede()` supports that.

mark-superseded-is-irreversible-metadata.text: `mark_superseded` uses `Network.retract()` plus metadata, not an outlist justification, so asserting `new_id` cannot restore `old_id`; only the outlist-based `supersede()` supports that.

mark-superseded-missing-node-skips-save.text: If `old_id` or `new_id` is missing, `mark_superseded` raises `KeyError` inside the write context and `__exit__` skips the save, so the attempt is not persisted.

mark-superseded-preserves-node-set.text: `mark_superseded` creates no new nodes, justifications, or nogoods; `len(net.nodes)` is unchanged by the operation.

mark-superseded-rejects-self-supersessio.text: `mark_superseded` raises `ValueError` when `old_id == new_id` before opening the write context, producing no side effects.

mark-superseded-requires-both-nodes-to-p.text: Unlike `supersede_with_text`, this function raises `KeyError` for the replacement if it has not been added to the network first.

mark-superseded-requires-existing-old-an.text: `api.mark_superseded` raises `KeyError("not found")` when either ID is missing.

mark-superseded-updates-metadata-before-.text: The `superseded_by` and `retract_reason` keys are written to `node.metadata` *before* `net.retract()` runs, so the cascade engine and later `get_status`/`list_gated` calls can read them.

mark-superseded-writes-metadata-before-c.text: `mark_superseded` writes `superseded_by` and `retract_reason` into `old_id`'s metadata before calling `net.retract()`, so the cascade engine and later readers can see those keys.

markdown-export-maps-stale-metadata-to-s.text: When `export_markdown` sees an `OUT` node with `stale_reason` or `retract_reason` metadata, it emits `[STALE]` while the stored `truth_value` remains `OUT`.

markdown-export-nogood-section-is-networ.text: `export_markdown` appends a `## Nogoods` section only when `network.nogoods` is non-empty, and each nogood lists its affected node IDs under `Affects:`.

markdown-export-omits-empty-source-url-a.text: `export_markdown` omits the `- Source URL:` and `- Accepted PR:` lines when those fields are unset.

markdown-export-quotes-schema-version.text: Markdown frontmatter emits `schema_version: "1.0"` with the version value quoted.

markdown-frontmatter-is-first-block.text: Markdown exports begin at byte 0 with a `---`-delimited frontmatter block containing schema metadata.

markdown-frontmatter-is-yaml-at-byte-zer.text: `export_markdown(net)` output starts with `---\n` and YAML frontmatter; `strip_frontmatter` returns `(text, {})` when no such header exists.

markdown-frontmatter-roundtrip-preserves.text: `net.meta` keys survive the Markdown frontmatter export/import round-trip, with string values emitted quoted.

markdown-import-accepts-separate-nogoods.text: The markdown import path reads `beliefs.md`, accepts optional nogoods text, and falls back to a sibling `nogoods.md` when present.

markdown-import-maps-unless-to-outlist.text: An exported `- Unless: <id>` line re-imports as `justifications[0].outlist == [<id>]`.

markdown-nogood-format-gap.text: Duplicate of existing belief `nogood-export-format-mismatch`; no new belief needed.

markdown-roundtrip-preserves-accepted-pr.text: The Markdown export→import pipeline preserves an `accepted_pr` value stored in `node.metadata`.

matrix-fail-fast-defaults-to-enabled.text: Since `fail-fast` is unspecified, the first failing Python version cancels the remaining matrix jobs.

max-depth-prefers-supporting-justificati.text: `_node_depth` descends only the `supporting_justification` when that index is valid, falling back to all justifications otherwise.

max-derivation-depth-counts-justificatio.text: `Max derivation depth` equals the longest chain of antecedent edges in the network (0 for premises-only, 1 for `d ← a`, 2 for `c ← b ← a`).

may-retract-already-out-premise.text: Because `find_culprits` traces all justifications and does not filter premises by truth value, `add_nogood` can select an already-`OUT` premise and return `[]` without resolving the contradiction.

mcp-accept-doc-requires-drift-revalidati.text: `reasons/mcp_server.py:485-488` documents accept as applying a change only after drift re-validation and treating drifted proposals as stale.

mcp-bridge-caches-tools-at-connect.text: `list_tools()` returns tool metadata cached during `connect()` and does not re-query the server afterward.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-joins-content-parts.text: `call_tool()` returns the MCP result as a single joined string of all content parts.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout.text: `call_tool()` blocks on the background future with a 60-second timeout and does not explicitly cancel the coroutine on timeout.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout-60s.text: `call_tool()` blocks for up to 60 seconds per invocation via `future.result(timeout=60)`; if the MCP server hangs, the calling thread unblocks with `TimeoutError`.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout-is-60-secon.text: `McpBridge.call_tool` uses `future.result(timeout=60)`, raising `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` if the tool call exceeds 60 seconds.

mcp-bridge-close-joins-thread-with-5s-ti.text: `close()` signals `_shutdown`, joins the background thread with a 5-second timeout, then closes the event loop.

mcp-bridge-command-is-shell-string.text: `McpBridge.__init__` expects a single shell command string (e.g. `"npx @mcp/server-fs /path"`) which is parsed via `shlex.split`; passing a list of arguments directly is not supported.

mcp-bridge-command-parsed-with-shlex.text: `McpBridge` parses its command string with `shlex.split()` into argv for `StdioServerParameters`.

mcp-bridge-command-uses-shlex-no-shell.text: `McpBridge` parses its command with `shlex.split`; the first token is the executable and no shell is used.

mcp-bridge-connect-blocks-up-to-30s.text: `connect()` blocks the calling thread for up to 30 seconds waiting for MCP session initialization via `_ready.wait(timeout=30)`, then raises `TimeoutError` if the server doesn't respond.

mcp-bridge-connect-startup-timeout.text: `connect()` waits up to 30 seconds for server readiness and raises `TimeoutError` if `_ready` is not set.

mcp-bridge-duck-type-interface.text: The ask module's MCP dispatch expects any bridge object to implement `list_tools() → list[dict]`, `get_instructions() → str`, and `call_tool(name, arguments) → str`; no concrete class import is required.

mcp-bridge-get-instructions-returns-serv.text: `get_instructions()` returns the server-provided instructions string captured from `session.initialize()`.

mcp-bridge-implements-context-manager.text: `McpBridge` implements `__enter__` and `__exit__`, enabling `with McpBridge(command) as bridge:` for automatic connect/close.

mcp-bridge-is-deliberately-stateless-and.text: The MCP bridge is architecturally committed to simplicity over resilience: it is a one-shot session with no retry or reconnection, its tool catalog is a frozen snapshot taken at connect time, and its interface is duck-typed (no formal protocol) — trading operational robustness for predictability and minimal coupling.

justifications.label: Convergent design philosophy — each property independently supports the "deliberately ephemeral" characterization; the conclusion holds as long as any one of these constraints is in force, since each individually precludes long-lived stateful integration.
