propose-update-shim-requires-canonical-m.text: Importing the shim requires `reasons.propose_update` to be importable, and any failure there propagates with no interception.

propose-update-store-flag-controls-persi.text: `propose_update` with `store=True` persists proposals and includes `stored_count`, while `store=False` returns `proposals`/`llm_proposals` without persisting and without `stored_count`.

propose-update-stores-proposals-with-cal.text: When storing, `propose_update` calls `api.store_llm_proposals(result, proposer=proposer, db_path=_get_db())`, so persisted proposals record the caller-supplied `proposer`.

propose-update-tests-patch-invoke-model.text: Model-calling tests replace `reasons.propose_update.invoke_model` with a mock to avoid real LLM invocation.

propose-update-uses-get-db-for-review-an.text: `propose_update` calls `_get_db()` for `api.propose_update` and, when storing, calls `_get_db()` again for `api.store_llm_proposals`, relying on `_get_db`'s cache for a consistent path.

propose-update-uses-lazy-cached-db.text: The `db_path` is resolved by `_get_db()`, which caches the first resolution in a module-level `_db` global, so `REASONS_DB` changes after the first call are ignored.

propose-updates-batch-size-not-validated.text: `batch_size` is not validated: `0` raises `ValueError` from `range`, while a negative value silently produces no batches and returns `[]`.

propose-updates-batches-and-calls-on-bat.text: `propose_updates` chunks selected belief ids according to `batch_size`, calls the model once per batch, and invokes `on_batch` with per-batch results.

propose-updates-batches-belief-ids.text: `propose_updates` calls `invoke_model` once per batch; three belief IDs with `batch_size=2` produce two calls.

propose-updates-batches-beliefs.text: `propose_updates` splits the resolved belief ID list into chunks of `batch_size` and issues exactly one `invoke_model` call per chunk.

propose-updates-catches-on-batch-callbac.text: Exceptions raised by the `on_batch` callback are caught by the per-batch `try/except` and reported as batch failures rather than propagated.

propose-updates-default-candidacy-is-in-.text: `propose_updates` selects only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` when `belief_ids` is `None`, and filters explicit `belief_ids` to IDs present in `nodes`.

propose-updates-defaults-to-in-beliefs.text: When `belief_ids` is `None`, `propose_updates` selects only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"`, iterating them in sorted order for determinism.

propose-updates-defaults-to-in-nodes.text: When `belief_ids` is `None`, `propose_updates` selects all nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` for the LLM prompt; empty or all-nonexistent ID lists short-circuit to `[]` without invoking the model.

propose-updates-does-not-emit-cascade.text: `propose_updates` returns only the LLM fields whitelisted by `parse_update_proposals`; it never calls a what-if simulator and never emits a cascade key.

propose-updates-emits-markdown-not-decis.text: `propose_updates` + `format_proposals_file` produce a markdown document of proposals with suggested commands; they do not return or apply an auto-accepted subset.

propose-updates-emits-proposals-not-acce.text: `propose_updates` returns a list of proposal dicts via `parse_update_proposals`; it never mutates or accepts beliefs itself.

propose-updates-empty-input-skips-llm.text: `propose_updates` returns `[]` without calling the LLM or printing progress when the selected belief list is empty.

propose-updates-empty-result-is-ambiguou.text: An empty return from `propose_updates` cannot distinguish “no proposals,” “no beliefs after filtering,” and “every batch failed.”

propose-updates-explicit-belief-ids-filt.text: When `belief_ids` is explicitly provided, `propose_updates` filters it to IDs present in `nodes` but does not filter by `truth_value`.

propose-updates-filters-unknown-belief-i.text: Explicitly supplied `belief_ids` not present in `nodes` are silently dropped, and no `truth_value` filtering is applied to the survivors.

propose-updates-filters-unknown-ids.text: When an explicit `belief_ids` list is passed, IDs not present in `nodes` are dropped before any LLM call.

propose-updates-is-llm-audit-of-in-belie.text: `propose_updates` audits IN beliefs via `invoke_model` and `parse_update_proposals`, classifying proposals with failure modes and bases including `detected-contradiction`.

propose-updates-is-read-only.text: `propose_updates()` returns proposal dicts and never mutates the belief graph.

propose-updates-on-batch-receives-cumula.text: The `propose_updates` `on_batch` callback receives the cumulative results list, not the current batch slice.
`on_batch` is invoked once per successful batch with the running `all_results` list, even when that batch returned zero proposals.

propose-updates-produces-proposals-witho.text: `reasons/propose_update.py:propose_updates` returns structured proposal dicts and never mutates the network; application is left to the caller, so `dry_run` is unnecessary by design.

propose-updates-requires-propose-update-.text: `propose_updates` cannot build a batch request without calling `PROPOSE_UPDATE_PROMPT.format(beliefs=...)`.

propose-updates-short-circuits-empty-or-.text: `propose_updates` returns `[]` without calling the model when `belief_ids` is empty or contains only nonexistent ids.

propose-updates-swallows-batch-errors.text: Any exception inside the per-batch `try` block (including exceptions raised by the `on_batch` callback) is logged to stderr as `WARN: batch N failed` and never propagated.

propose-updates-swallows-batch-failures.text: Exceptions from rendering, invoking the model, or parsing are caught per-batch and logged to `sys.stderr`, so one bad batch does not abort the run.

proposed-entries-contains-no-tombstones.text: The manifest can only express creation/update intent; there is no marker for deleting or orphaning an existing `entries/` file.

proposed-entries-has-no-in-repo-consumer.text: No code in the repository references the symbols `proposed-entries` or `proposed_entries`; the manifest is read by external Forge tooling, not by the `reasons` package.

proposed-entries-include-private-helpers.text: The proposal scope includes private helper symbols such as `_propagate` and `_justification_valid`, so the manifest is not limited to public API entries.

proposed-entries-is-a-flat-content-addre.text: The file is a single flat JSON object mapping wiki paths to 16-hex-char content digests, with no nested objects, arrays, or metadata envelope.

proposed-entries-is-change-detection-man.text: `.forge/proposed-entries.json` is a manifest mapping each entry path under `entries/2026/04/23/` to a 16-hex-character content hash used to detect which entries have changed.

proposed-entries-is-flat-sorted-json-wit.text: `.forge/proposed-entries.json` is a flat JSON object with lexicographically sorted path keys and no `version`, `generatedAt`, or `root` envelope fields.

proposed-entries-is-keyed-by-entry-file-.text: Every key in the manifest is a path of the form `entries/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>.md`, so keys correspond one-to-one with entry files and hashes correspond to their content versions.

proposed-entries-json-maps-entry-paths-t.text: `.forge/proposed-entries.json` is a flat map from entry path to a 16-character hash and contains no timestamp or operation field.

proposed-entries-keys-are-lexicographica.text: Keys are ordered by plain string sort, which is why `reasons_lib-network.md` (umbrella) appears after the four `reasons_lib-network-*.md` children.

proposed-entries-keys-use-date-partition.text: All 17 keys match `entries/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>.md`, and all 17 currently share the partition `entries/2026/04/23/`.

proposed-entries-keys-use-single-date-pa.text: Every key in `.forge/proposed-entries.json` is an `entries/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>.md` path, and the observed manifest uses a single date partition.

proposed-entries-makes-reasons-lib-canon.text: The manifest alone does not establish `reasons_lib/` as canonical over `reasons/`; that claim conflicts with existing beliefs that `reasons_lib` is a legacy/shim package.

proposed-entries-slug-prefix-is-schema.text: Manifest slugs use only the prefixes `reasons_lib-`, `scan-`, or `topic-`; introducing a new prefix would be a schema change.

proposed-entries-slugs-flatten-source-co.text: Entry slugs flatten `/`, `.`, and `:` from source coordinates to `-` while preserving underscores, e.g. `reasons_lib/network.py:add_nogood` becomes `reasons_lib-network-add_nogood`.

proposed-entries-values-are-16-lowercase.text: `.forge/proposed-entries.json` values are exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters and act as content-change digests, not security hashes.

provided-grep-cannot-rule-out-from-impor.text: The observed grep patterns omit `from reasons_lib.storage import ...`, so zero matches do not prove there are no consumers.

provider-dispatch-is-string-prefix-not-p.text: Provider selection in `invoke_model` is a flat `startswith` cascade (`api:`, `vertex:`, `openai:`, then CLI) with no class hierarchy, plugin registry, or factory pattern — adding a provider requires one new `if` branch and one `_invoke_*` function.

public-model-classes-live-in-reasons-ini.text: The canonical public model classes `Justification`, `Node`, and `Nogood` are defined in `reasons/__init__.py`.

publish-db-path-none-double-invokes-glob.text: If `db_path=None` is passed to `publish`, global subscribers are invoked twice because `None` is used for both the global and per-database lookup.

publish-dispatches-to-snapshot.text: `publish` iterates a copied subscriber list (`list(...)` plus `extend(...)`), so subscribe/unsubscribe mutations made during dispatch do not affect the current call.

publish-does-not-filter-events-by-db-pat.text: `publish` does not inspect `ChangeEvent.db_path`; it relies on the caller to supply events already scoped to `db_path`.

publish-empty-events-is-no-op.text: An empty `events` list causes `publish` to return before reading `_subscribers`.

publish-global-subscribers-receive-all-e.text: Subscribers registered under `None` are invoked on every `publish` call, regardless of the `db_path` argument.

publish-hf-delegates-hf-io-to-hf-module.text: All HuggingFace interaction (token resolution, repo id normalization, creation, upload) is delegated to `reasons/hf.py`; `publish_hf` itself contains no HF-specific API code.

publish-hf-does-not-rollback.text: `publish_hf` has no try/except or cleanup; a mid-sequence upload failure leaves the remote repo partially populated.

publish-hf-has-no-rollback.text: `publish_hf` has no try/except, cleanup, or retry around uploads, so a mid-sequence upload failure leaves the remote repo partially populated and propagates the exception.

publish-hf-json-export-is-deterministic.text: `publish_hf` serializes `network.json` with `json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, making the export deterministic for diffing or hashing across publishes.

publish-hf-license-is-card-text-only.text: `publish_hf`'s `license` parameter is rendered into the README card only; it does not set HuggingFace repo-level license metadata.

publish-hf-pg-exports-not-snapshot-consi.text: For SQLite, `publish_hf` exports share the module-level `_network_cache`, but in PostgreSQL mode the three export helpers perform separate round-trips and are not guaranteed to see the same snapshot.

publish-hf-private-is-create-only.text: The `private` argument is forwarded only to `create_repo` and has no effect on already-existing repos.

publish-hf-private-only-on-repo-creation.text: `publish_hf` honors `private` only when it creates a new HuggingFace repo; existing repos are reused and are not retargeted to private/public.

publish-hf-produces-three-artifacts.text: On success `publish_hf` uploads exactly `["network.json", "beliefs.md", "README.md"]` in that fixed order and reports them in `files_uploaded`.

publish-hf-produces-three-files.text: `publish_hf` uploads exactly `{"network.json", "beliefs.md", "README.md"}` and issues 4 `urlopen` calls (1 create + 3 uploads).

publish-hf-requires-token.text: `publish_hf` raises `RuntimeError("token required")` when neither `HF_TOKEN` nor `~/.huggingface/token` supplies a token.

publish-hf-uploads-fixed-three-file-set.text: On success, `publish_hf` uploads exactly `network.json`, `beliefs.md`, and `README.md` in that fixed order and reports them in `files_uploaded`.

publish-is-dispatch-only.text: `publish` at `reasons/pubsub.py:70` only fans out `ChangeEvent`s to subscribers and contains no transaction/commit logic.

publish-isolates-subscriber-errors.text: `publish` catches/logs exceptions from one subscriber and continues dispatching to later subscribers.

publish-isolates-subscriber-exceptions.text: A subscriber exception is caught and logged by `publish()`, and other subscribers still receive the event batch.

publish-noops-on-empty-event-list.text: `publish()` returns immediately when `events` is empty and does not notify subscribers.

publish-returns-immediately-on-empty-eve.text: An empty `events` list causes `publish` to return before reading `_subscribers`.

publish-routes-to-global-and-db-scoped-s.text: `publish` dispatches each event batch to global subscribers plus subscribers registered for the event’s `db_path`.

publish-routes-to-global-and-db-specific.text: `publish` sends each event batch to global subscribers plus subscribers registered for the event’s `db_path`.

publish-shares-events-list-object-with-a.text: All subscribers in one `publish` dispatch receive the same `events` list object, so mutations by one subscriber are visible to later subscribers.

pubsub-and-mind-service-are-optional-not.text: `pubsub.py` and `mind_service.py` provide optional external notification hooks outside the core inference path; they are not required for TMS correctness and do not participate in propagation or evaluation.

pubsub-callback-is-per-write.text: `reasons/pubsub.py:42` documents subscriber callbacks as receiving a list of `ChangeEvent` after each write.

pubsub-callback-receives-batched-change-.text: Subscriber callbacks receive a `list[ChangeEvent]` batch, one call per write transaction, not a single event.

pubsub-callback-receives-events-per-writ.text: `pubsub.subscribe` registers subscriber callbacks that are called with a list of `ChangeEvent` objects after each write.

pubsub-callbacks-receive-whole-event-lis.text: `publish(events, db_path)` passes the entire event list as one argument to each subscriber callback, not one event at a time.

pubsub-change-event-lacks-cause-metadata.text: `ChangeEvent` carries only `type`, `node_id`, old/new truth values, and `db_path`; it does not include cause or cascade-root metadata.

pubsub-channel-key-is-db-path-or-global.text: The only channel discriminator is `db_path`; `None` is the global channel that receives events for every database.

pubsub-clear-resets-all-subscribers.text: `clear()` removes both global and db-scoped subscribers, and `has_subscribers()` returns `False` afterward.

pubsub-dispatch-snapshots-subscribers.text: `publish` materializes the target subscriber list before iteration, so unsubscribing inside a callback does not prevent the current dispatch from calling that subscriber.

pubsub-docstring-asserts-post-save-publi.text: `reasons/pubsub.py` states that publish is called by `_with_network.__exit__` after save completes, but that call site is not shown.

pubsub-duplicate-subscription-allowed.text: `subscribe` appends callbacks without deduplicating, so the same callback registered twice is invoked twice; `unsubscribe` removes only the first match.

pubsub-empty-publish-is-no-op.text: `publish([], db_path)` must not invoke any subscribers.

pubsub-events-computed-by-snapshot-diff.text: `compute_changes(before, after, db_path)` derives pub/sub events by diffing truth-value snapshots rather than observing intermediate propagation.

pubsub-events-emitted-after-save.text: `pubsub.publish` is called after the write transaction commits, so any callback that re-queries the DB sees the persisted truth values (`api.py:158`, `test_events_after_save`).

pubsub-events-fire-post-persistence.text: Pubsub events are delivered to subscribers only after the database write has committed, so any side-effect in a subscriber callback (e.g., reading the DB) observes the already-persisted new state.

pubsub-events-lack-cause-and-cascade-roo.text: The `ChangeEvent` dataclass omits `cause` and `cascade_root` because events are computed from pre/post snapshots.

pubsub-exposes-only-post-save-state.text: Subscribers observe only the final stable post-save snapshot; intermediate cascade states during fixpoint computation are structurally invisible because `publish()` is called only after the full transaction commits

pubsub-failed-mutation-emits-no-events.text: If an API mutation raises an exception (e.g., `KeyError` on a nonexistent node), the snapshot-diff-publish pipeline is never reached and zero events are delivered to subscribers.

pubsub-fires-only-on-subscribed-writes.text: `_with_network.__exit__` computes and publishes change events only when `write=True`, the context exited without exception, and `pubsub.has_subscribers(db_path)` is truthy.

pubsub-global-and-scoped-subscribers-bot.text: A global subscriber (`db_path=None`) and a database-scoped subscriber for the same `db_path` both receive the same published batch.

pubsub-insertion-indistinguishable-from-.text: A new node (present in `after`, absent from `before`) produces a `ChangeEvent` with `old_truth_value=None` and `type="node_changed"`, making it indistinguishable from a value change by the `type` field alone

pubsub-is-nonblocking-sink.text: Modules may publish changes through `pubsub.py`, but no core operation blocks on a subscriber to complete.

pubsub-is-synchronous-in-process.text: `publish()` blocks until all subscribers return; there is no queue, thread, or IPC mechanism — safe in single-threaded use but unsafe under concurrent calls without external synchronization

pubsub-lacks-thread-synchronization.text: `reasons/pubsub.py` has no locks or synchronization, so concurrent registry mutation and dispatch are not thread-safe.

pubsub-metadata-only-changes-emit-no-eve.text: `compute_changes` diffs only truth values, so metadata-only mutations such as `set_metadata` produce no pub/sub events.

pubsub-publish-noop-on-empty-list.text: If the `events` list passed to `publish` is empty, no subscriber callback is invoked at all — the dispatch loop short-circuits before iterating subscribers.

pubsub-publish-requires-write-true.text: Events are published only when `write=True` **and** the SQLite `Storage` object exists, so read-only calls like `topics`/`get_status` never emit events on either backend.

pubsub-publish-skips-empty-batches.text: `publish` returns immediately when `events` is empty, so subscribers are never called with `[]`.

pubsub-publishes-only-final-stable-state.text: `reasons/pubsub.py` documents that subscribers receive events only after `_with_network` commits, never for intermediate cascade states.

pubsub-publishes-only-on-write-with-stor.text: `_with_network.__exit__` publishes events only when `write=True`, `exc_type is None`, and `self.store` is present; read-only calls never publish on either backend.

pubsub-registry-is-process-local.text: The subscriber registry is the module-level `_subscribers` dict in `reasons/pubsub.py`, so subscriptions are not shared across processes.

pubsub-scoped-subscriber-receives-matchi.text: Subscriber scoping is inclusive (OR semantics): a subscriber registered without a `db_path` (global) AND a subscriber registered with a specific `db_path` both fire when an event for that database is published.

pubsub-subscribe-allows-duplicates.text: Calling `subscribe(callback, db_path)` twice with the same callback registers it twice; `publish` will invoke it twice per event batch — there is no deduplication check

pubsub-subscriber-errors-do-not-propagat.text: Each subscriber is invoked inside `try/except Exception` that logs and swallows, so one failing subscriber cannot abort the save or starve others.

pubsub-subscriber-exception-isolation.text: A subscriber callback that raises an exception is caught and logged without preventing delivery of the same event to subsequent subscribers in the registry.

pubsub-subscriber-exceptions-are-isolate.text: A raising subscriber does not prevent other subscribers from receiving the same event batch, nor does it propagate to the caller of `publish()`; each subscriber is wrapped in an independent `try/except`

pure-evaluation-enables-richly-governed-.text: Evaluation purity — grounding dialectics through the minimal architecture — simultaneously enables richly-governed exception-safe revision, so dialectical structures are both minimality-grounded in their computation and richly-governed in the state they produce: challenge/defend operations inherit pure deterministic evaluation while producing metadata-enriched recoverable state changes.

justifications.label: Pure evaluation is the shared computational foundation enabling both minimal dialectics and rich governance; combining reveals dialectics benefit from both

pure-evaluation-enables-richly-governed-.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — grounds dialectical reliability through a minimal architecture, and the system's revision component supports richly-governed, metadata-enabled state management (retraction reasons, staleness markers, access tags) while maintaining exception-safety and recoverability under failure conditions.

push-belief-404-propagates-as-httperror.text: `push_belief` special-cases only HTTP 401; HTTP 404 from the push endpoint propagates as an `HTTPError` rather than becoming a `RuntimeError`.

push-belief-maps-401-to-runtime-error.text: A 401 HTTP response is converted into a `RuntimeError`; other `HTTPError` codes are re-raised.

push-belief-maps-401-to-runtimeerror.text: `push_belief` converts an HTTP 401 response into a `RuntimeError` with an authentication-failure message.

quality-lifecycle-is-complete-and-resour.text: The complete LLM-driven quality lifecycle — creation via derive with defensive validation, classification via list-negative with batch scalability, and validation via review with read-only fault tolerance — operates within resource-efficient bounds spanning zero-dependency packaging through lazy-loading startup through bounded runtime execution, ensuring quality assurance scales sustainably with belief network size.

justifications.label: Quality lifecycle completeness and resource efficiency are independently established properties that together ensure sustainable quality management

quality-lifecycle-is-fault-tolerant-and-.text: The complete LLM-driven quality lifecycle — creation via derive, classification via list-negative, review, and self-correction — is simultaneously resource-efficient (accurate budgets, linear allocation, minimal footprint) and fault-tolerant at every phase (graceful degradation on LLM failures, batch fault isolation, deterministic fallbacks).

justifications.label: Resource efficiency and fault tolerance are independent quality axes — the lifecycle achieves both simultaneously across all phases

quality-lifecycle-operates-within-self-m.text: The complete belief quality lifecycle — fault-tolerant creation, classification, review, and correction with resource-efficient operation — executes within trust boundaries that are both structurally enforced (zero external dependencies, defensive ingestion) and dynamically maintained (convergent self-correction preserving trust invariants), requiring no external trust infrastructure.

justifications.label: Quality lifecycle operates within self-maintaining trust perimeters — trust enforcement is not external to quality but embedded within it

query-degradation-is-deterministic-acros.text: All information access paths degrade gracefully while maintaining deterministic output: interactive queries cascade through tiered modes (LLM synthesis → bounded tool loop → raw FTS5 search), structured reads self-heal missing indexes via derived FTS5 reconstruction, and all fallback paths produce deterministic sorted output.

justifications.label: Tiered query degradation and deterministic read resilience are independently established — together they show every information access path is both fault-tolerant and predictable.

query-depth-filters-use-structural-node-.text: The query filter parameters `min_depth`/`max_depth` are evaluated with `_node_depth`, so they filter by derivation-graph depth independent of current truth state.

query-resilience-serves-self-correcting-.text: All query access paths — interactive LLM synthesis, batch search, and compact summarization — degrade gracefully with deterministic output while operating against a knowledge base that actively self-corrects through contradiction resolution and staleness detection, ensuring degraded queries still return data from a consistency-maintained belief network

justifications.label: Deterministic query degradation (depth-4) ensures reliable access while self-correction (depth-4) ensures the accessed data is actively maintained — users get reliable reads against a self-healing store

query-resilience-serves-self-correcting-.text: All query access paths, including interactive LLM synthesis, batch search, and compact summarization, degrade gracefully with deterministic output while operating against a knowledge base that self-corrects for supported cases through contradiction resolution and conservative staleness detection for tracked IN nodes with both source fields, so degraded queries still return data from a belief network whose consistency is maintained for supported cases without claiming exhaustive drift coverage.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

raw-decode-scanning-is-used-for-llm-json.text: The codebase calls `JSONDecoder.raw_decode` at candidate positions in at least six response-handling modules, including `reasons/propose_update.py`, `reasons/repair.py`, and `reasons/review.py`.

raw-decode-scans-stop-at-first-decoded-v.text: The observed `raw_decode` call sites discard the returned end index and stop at the first successfully decoded JSON value rather than continuing to parse trailing content.

read-and-write-paths-are-both-reliable.text: Both the read path (staleness checking detects all forms of source drift without false negatives) and the write path (truth propagation completes without runtime errors across all reachable nodes) are operationally reliable, ensuring the system functions correctly in both observational and mutational modes.

justifications.label: Independent operational reliability of the read-only inspection path and the write-path propagation engine combine to cover both system operation modes

read-and-write-paths-are-reliable-for-su.text: Both the read path (staleness checking detects source drift for nodes with both source and source_hash and provides a CI-usable nonzero exit) and the write path (truth propagation completes without runtime errors across all reachable nodes) are operationally reliable for those supported cases.

reasoning-and-knowledge-expansion-are-bo.text: The system achieves exhaustive coverage in both formal reasoning (deterministic reversible truth evaluation with guaranteed-terminating exploration of all derivable conclusions) and LLM-driven knowledge expansion (complete coverage with fault tolerance across all interactive and batch LLM operations)

justifications.label: Formal TMS reasoning and LLM-driven derivation independently achieve exhaustive coverage through complementary mechanisms

reasoning-and-revision-form-complete-arc.text: The system provides a complete reasoning-and-revision architecture: the deterministic reversible engine reliably computes truth states in the forward direction, while the comprehensive minimal revision system handles all forms of belief change (outlist defeat, contradiction resolution, dialectical challenge) in the corrective direction — together covering the full lifecycle of belief management.

justifications.label: Forward inference engine plus corrective revision system yields complete belief lifecycle coverage

reasoning-engine-is-deterministic-and-re.text: The TMS engine achieves deterministic reversible non-monotonic reasoning: truth maintenance produces predictable terminating results through uniform evaluation and conservative asym­metry, while every non-monotonic operation (challenge, kill-switch, supersession, dialectics) is inherently undoable through the single outlist primitive.

justifications.label: Determinism (from uniform evaluation + BFS termination) and reversibility (from outlist universality) are independent properties that together make the engine both predictable and undoable

reasoning-is-exhaustively-deterministic.text: The reasoning system produces deterministic, reversible truth evaluations AND can exhaustively explore all derivable conclusions with guaranteed termination, ensuring the system finds every reachable belief state with predictable outcomes.

justifications.label: Deterministic reversible TMS evaluation combined with exhaustive terminating derive exploration guarantees complete predictable inference (depth-4)

reasons_lib-is-a-backwards-compat-shim.text: `CLAUDE.md:35` and shim docstrings identify `reasons_lib/` as a compatibility layer, not a vendored legacy package.

reasons_lib-is-a-shim.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py` contains only `from reasons import *`, so any name it exposes is sourced from `reasons/__init__.py`.

reasons_lib-is-a-shim-package.text: Every observed file under `reasons_lib/` (`__init__.py`, `api.py`) is a 3-line `from reasons... import *` re-export with a "Backwards-compatibility shim" docstring.

reasons_lib-mcp-server-re-exports-reason.text: `reasons_lib/mcp_server.py` is a 3-line shim that does `from reasons.mcp_server import *`; the console script does not target it.

reasons_lib-reexports-reasons.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py:3` and `reasons_lib/api.py:3` are pure `from reasons… import *` shims; no additional logic exists in the legacy package.

reasons_lib-requires-reasons.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py:2` and submodule shims import from `reasons`, so `reasons_lib` cannot function without `reasons`.

reasons_lib-shim-has-narrow-surface.text: `reasons_lib/` covers only `reasons` top-level and `reasons.api`; any legacy `from reasons_lib.network import …` was already broken before this decision.

rebinding-shim-attributes-does-not-affec.text: `reasons_lib.export_markdown` and `reasons.export_markdown` are distinct module objects sharing references; assigning to an attribute on the shim leaves the canonical module unchanged.

rebuild-clears-before-rebuilding.text: A first pass resets every node's `dependents` to `set()` before edges are re-added, so stale entries cannot survive a rebuild.

rebuild-dependents-can-create-self-depen.text: If a node's own justification lists that node in `antecedents` or `outlist`, `_rebuild_dependents` adds the node's ID to its own `dependents` set because no cycle filter exists.

rebuild-dependents-clears-before-rebuild.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` wipes all existing dependent sets before recomputing from justifications, so stale entries are always removed rather than incrementally patched

rebuild-dependents-does-not-propagate-tr.text: Calling `_rebuild_dependents` repairs only the reverse `dependents` index and leaves all `truth_value` fields unchanged; propagation must be triggered separately.

rebuild-dependents-is-canonical.text: The docstring designates `_rebuild_dependents` as the sole canonical rebuild; other rebuild sites should delegate to it.

rebuild-dependents-is-canonical-repair.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` clears and reconstructs all dependents from justifications and is idempotent.

rebuild-dependents-is-destructive-then-r.text: `_rebuild_dependents` first clears all existing `dependents` sets on every node, then repopulates them from scratch — making it safe to call at any time as a repair mechanism and guaranteeing no stale entries survive.

rebuild-dependents-is-idempotent.text: Calling `_rebuild_dependents()` twice in succession produces identical `dependents` sets on every node.

rebuild-dependents-is-not-fts-rebuild.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` in `reasons/network.py` rebuilds the in-memory dependency index, not any FTS table.

rebuild-dependents-is-single-canonical-p.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` is the single canonical method for reconstructing the reverse dependents index (wiping all `node.dependents` sets then re-deriving from all justifications' antecedents and outlists); the codebase explicitly states all other rebuild call sites should delegate to it.

rebuild-dependents-removes-phantom-entri.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` clears and reconstructs the reverse index, removing injected phantom/extra dependents.

rebuild-dependents-repairs-corruption.text: `_rebuild_dependents()` removes injected phantom entries and reconstructs each node's `dependents` set from justification references.

rebuild-dependents-reports-no-consistenc.text: `_rebuild_dependents` returns `None`, logs nothing, and provides no changed/fixed summary, so callers cannot tell whether dangling references were dropped during rebuild.

rebuild-does-not-propagate-truth-values.text: Calling `_rebuild_dependents` leaves all `truth_value` fields unchanged; propagation must be triggered separately.

recompute-all-bounded-by-node-count-plus.text: `Network.recompute_all()` bounds its fixpoint iterations to `len(nodes) + 1` to guarantee termination.

recompute-all-bounded-iteration.text: `recompute_all` uses a bounded iteration cap rather than an unbounded fixpoint to guarantee termination on cyclic graphs; any change to propagation logic must preserve or raise this cap to avoid infinite loops.

recompute-all-does-not-propagate-access-.text: `recompute_all` updates truth values and `supporting_justification` but never calls `_propagate_access_tags`, so access-tag changes must be propagated separately.

recompute-all-exists-in-pg-backend.text: A parallel implementation documented as "Recompute truth values for all derived nodes to a fixpoint" exists at `reasons/pg.py:1593`.

recompute-all-has-pg-counterpart.text: A PostgreSQL-side `recompute_all` exists and is documented to recompute derived node truth values to a fixpoint, mirroring the in-memory network implementation.

recompute-all-ignores-dependents-index.text: Unlike `_propagate`, `recompute_all` does not consult `node.dependents`; correctness depends only on `justifications` and `_compute_truth`.

recompute-all-is-bounded-by-node-count.text: `Network.recompute_all()` iterates at most `len(nodes) + 1` times to reach a fixpoint, providing a termination guarantee that prevents infinite recomputation loops even in pathological network states.

recompute-all-is-defined-in-network-py.text: `Network.recompute_all` is declared at `reasons/network.py:904` with return type `list[str]` and is invoked by callers in `reasons/api.py:778/1397/1531/1647` and `reasons/import_agent.py:317/489`.

recompute-all-is-global-fixpoint-sweep.text: `recompute_all` re-derives truth values by iterating every node in `self.nodes` up to `len(self.nodes)+1` passes until a pass makes no changes, without consulting the `dependents` reverse index.

recompute-all-iterates-to-fixpoint.text: The docstring at `reasons/network.py:907` states the function "Iterates to a fixpoint so cascading changes propagate regardless of" traversal order, implying it is not a single topological pass.

recompute-all-max-iterations-is-a-hard-c.text: The loop stops after `len(self.nodes) + 1` passes and does not raise, warn, or log a signal when convergence is not achieved.

recompute-all-mutates-supporting-justifi.text: Every visited derived node has its `supporting_justification` field rewritten, even when `truth_value` is unchanged, because `_compute_truth` sets it as a side effect.

recompute-all-respects-retracted-metadat.text: Tests at `tests/test_network.py:147-149` and `tests/test_import_agent.py:172` require `recompute_all` to leave nodes marked `_retracted` (or pinned) as OUT rather than resurrecting them.

recompute-all-return-is-event-union-not-.text: The returned list is the union of nodes that ever flipped during the sweep; it can include nodes whose final value equals their initial value and cannot be used as a replacement for reading `node.truth_value`.

recompute-all-returns-changed-node-ids.text: Callers treat `Network.recompute_all()` as returning the IDs of nodes whose truth values changed and use its length to count propagated changes.

recompute-all-returns-union-of-changed-i.text: `recompute_all` returns a list containing the union of node IDs that changed on any pass, not the final truth state, and its order is not contractual because it comes from a set.

recompute-all-silently-incomplete-on-non.text: If `recompute_all` exhausts its `len(self.nodes)+1` pass bound without reaching a clean pass, it raises no error and returns a possibly incomplete changed-ID list.

recompute-all-skips-premises.text: Nodes with an empty `justifications` list are never visited or mutated by `recompute_all`; their truth value is preserved.

recompute-all-skips-retracted-and-preser.text: `recompute_all` only recomputes non-retracted nodes with non-empty justifications; premises and nodes whose metadata `_retracted` is true keep their current truth values.

recompute-all-skips-retracted-nodes.text: Nodes with `metadata["_retracted"]` truthy are excluded from the sweep, so retracted nodes cannot be revived by this function.

recompute-all-uses-fixpoint.text: `recompute_all` iterates until no truth values change, bounded by `len(nodes) + 1` iterations, handling cascading dependencies from arbitrary node ordering.

record-cost-assumes-numeric-inputs.text: `_record_cost` performs no validation on token/cost arguments; non-numeric or negative values are added directly and can corrupt totals.

record-cost-creates-zero-initialized-mod.text: The first `_record_cost` call for a model inserts `_cost_tracker["by_model"][model]` with zeroed `calls`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_cost_usd`, and `elapsed_seconds` before incrementing usage fields.

record-cost-is-additive-not-idempotent.text: Repeated invocations accumulate rather than replace; only `reset_cost_tracker()` clears state.

record-cost-produces-per-model-entry.text: After the first call for a given `model`, `_cost_tracker["by_model"][model]` is populated with fields `calls`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_cost_usd`, and `elapsed_seconds`.

recoverable-belief-modification-preserve.text: Recoverable belief modification preserves bidirectionally traceable structural and semantic consistency across deduplication and contradiction management.

justifications.label: Adds recoverability to the existing structural-semantic traceability result.

recoverable-belief-modification-preserve.text: Recoverable belief modification preserves not only bidirectional structural/semantic traceability but also its unification with lifecycle-governed revision traceability.

justifications.label: Lifts recoverability onto the unified revision-consistency traceability result.

recoverable-bidirectional-revision-and-d.text: Recoverable bidirectional revision and lifecycle-governed defeat reversal jointly close guided recovery across structural, semantic, and topology-complete dependents.

justifications.label: The first antecedent supplies recoverable bidirectional traceability; the second supplies lifecycle-governed topology-complete defeat reversal. Both are needed for end-to-end recovery closure.

recoverable-bidirectional-revision-prese.text: Recoverable bidirectional revision simultaneously preserves structural/semantic traceability and enables guided recovery over topology-complete truth changes across lifecycle-governed defeat reversals.

justifications.label: Combines the guided-recovery-complete truth-maintenance chain with recoverable structural/semantic traceability; both are needed for the joint guarantee.

reexported-objects-retain-canonical-modu.text: Functions and classes defined in a canonical `reasons.<module>` and re-exported by its `reasons_lib` shim keep their original `__module__` value (e.g. `reasons.repair`), not the shim module path.

reference-auditability-is-jointly-equili.text: Reference auditability covers both resource-efficient knowledge equilibria and correctness across all storage backends.

justifications.label: Joins equilibrium-level reference validation with backend-level verified correctness; the known reference-audit gap and partial API coverage gate the combined claim.

reference-integrity-is-schema-enforced.text: Referential integrity between justification antecedent/outlist references and the nodes they point to is enforced at the database schema level, preventing dangling references at the storage layer.

justifications.label: Both backends handle references at the application level (PgApi validates at insert, SQLite rebuilds on load), but the explicit absence of FK constraints in PG blocks the claim that integrity is *schema*-enforced.

reference-validated-equilibria-are-audit.text: Reference-validated resource-efficient knowledge equilibria are grounded in auditable universal guarantees.

justifications.label: Synthesizes the depth-17 equilibrium result with the depth-16 auditable-grounding result.

reference-validation-audit-finds-three-u.text: Issue #126 reference validation audit found three specific node ID reference boundaries whose coverage does not establish validation at every boundary.

reference-validation-is-defense-in-depth.text: Every system boundary that accepts node ID references validates them against the actual network: import normalization drops unknown antecedent/outlist refs, nogood recording skips invalid node IDs, and LLM-returned negative-list IDs are filtered against existing nodes.

justifications.label: Three boundaries validated; gated on full boundary audit (issue #126)

references-are-durable-across-persistenc.text: All system-generated identifiers survive both persistence boundaries (save/load cycles, cross-session durability via high-water marks) and format evolution boundaries (parser versioning, schema migration, forward-compatible metadata) — references remain valid and resolvable across time and system versions.

justifications.label: Persistence durability (depth-4) covers temporal stability; evolution tolerance (depth-2) covers version stability — together they guarantee referential integrity across all change axes.

refusal-detection-absent-in-llm-layer.text: `reasons/llm.py` (including `_parse_cli_json`, `_invoke_api`, `invoke_model`) contains no refusal-phrase matching; the parser returns raw model text.

refusal-phrase-is-test-only-fixture.text: The refusal string `"I don't have enough beliefs in the network to answer this question."` appears only in `tests/test_ask.py:182/190`, not as a shared production constant.

reject-proposal-only-updates-proposal-st.text: The only reject implementation is `reject_proposal`, which mutates `proposals.status` to `'rejected'` without changing truth.

rejection-is-proposal-scoped.text: The only "reject" implementation is `reasons/api.py:reject_proposal` (line 5801), which mutates `proposals.status` to `'rejected'`; no rejection path is triggered by version or schema mismatch.

relative-imports-are-confined-to-reasons.text: Every relative import shown (`from .metadata`, `from .network`, `from .storage`, etc.) lives in `reasons/api.py`; no relative import appears under `tests/`, which is why `tests/__init__.py` is removable while `reasons/__init__.py` is not.

reload-of-canonical-module-leaves-shim-b.text: Reloading `reasons.api` does not refresh the copied name bindings in `reasons_lib.api`, leaving the shim with stale references.

reload-reasons-lib-retains-stale-star-im.text: Reloading `reasons_lib` re-executes `from reasons import *` but does not clear names that were present before the reload and are absent from the new star-import set.

removal-effects-are-fully-reported-and-r.text: Every belief removal — whether intentional retraction or contradiction-triggered backtracking — provides three simultaneous guarantees: complete cascade coverage (transitive propagation captures every truth-value change), accurate effect reporting (structured before/after diffs reflect all affected nodes), and surgical recovery guidance (restoration hints target only cascade victims with surviving premises).

justifications.label: Complete cascade coverage ensures nothing is missed, effect reporting ensures full visibility, and recovery guidance ensures recoverability — together they make belief removal a fully transparent and reversible operation.

metadata.retract_reason: Invalid: drops conditional about outlist tracking from antecedent

remove-justification-blocks-premise-and-.text: Removing a justification from a premise (no justifications) or from a node with exactly one justification both raise `ValueError`, enforcing that premises are axiomatic and a node cannot be left with zero justifications via this operation.

remove-justification-cascades-truth-chan.text: Removing a justification re-evaluates the target node and recursively its dependents, returning all changed node IDs in `result["changed"]`.

remove-justification-cascades-truth-valu.text: If Network.remove_justification causes a node to flip from IN to OUT, the change propagates to all downstream dependents.

remove-justification-cleans-dependents-e.text: When removing a justification, an antecedent is removed from the node's `dependents` set only if it does not appear in any remaining justification — shared antecedents are preserved.

remove-justification-cleans-dependents-i.text: After Network.remove_justification, antecedent and outlist nodes' dependents sets are updated to remove the target node unless it remains referenced by another justification.

remove-justification-cleans-stale-depend.text: For each antecedent/outlist in the removed justification that no longer appears in any remaining justification, `node_id` is discarded from that node's `dependents` set; if the ref is missing from `self.nodes` the discard is silently skipped.

remove-justification-cli-argument-order-.text: The CLI command is `remove-justification <node_id> <index>` and prints `Removed justification <index>` on success.

remove-justification-compacts-justificat.text: Removing one of multiple justifications pops and re-indexes the node’s justification list, so remaining justifications shift down rather than leaving a tombstone.

remove-justification-does-not-recompute-.text: `remove_justification` does not recompute content hashes for remaining justifications; it discards the removed justification and leaves remaining hashes unchanged.

remove-justification-enforces-minimum-co.text: `Network.remove_justification` refuses to remove the last justification from a derived node — a derived node must retain at least one justification, enforced with `ValueError("only one justification")`

remove-justification-forces-fresh-load.text: The SQLite path passes `write=True` to `_with_network`, so it always calls `Storage.load()` and never reuses the cached `Network` even when the file mtime is unchanged.

remove-justification-guard-prevents-last.text: The method raises `ValueError` when a node has exactly one justification; callers must use `convert_to_premise` or `retract` instead.

remove-justification-has-no-namespace-pa.text: Unlike `add_justification` and `add_node`, `remove_justification` has no `namespace` kwarg, so callers must pass fully qualified IDs for namespaced nodes.

remove-justification-is-positional-only.text: Negative `index` values are rejected; therefore callers cannot use Python slice-style `-1` to remove the last justification.

remove-justification-leaves-justificatio.text: Unlike `add_justification`, this method does not recompute `content_hash` or `text_hash`; the returned `removed` dict aliases the popped object's original lists.

remove-justification-must-not-be-nested-.text: Callers should not invoke `remove_justification` inside an existing `_with_network` block because it opens a second `Storage` instance and the inner save can clobber changes from the outer transaction.

remove-justification-outlist-entries-are.text: Outlist entries (defeaters) listed in a justification are registered in the antecedent node's `dependents` set and are cleaned up when the justification containing them is removed, exactly like antecedent references.

remove-justification-passes-through-retu.text: The function returns the raw dict produced by `Network.remove_justification` or `PgApi.remove_justification` without adding, renaming, or filtering any keys.

remove-justification-pg-path-bypasses-lo.text: When `pg_conninfo` is truthy, `remove_justification` delegates to `PgApi` and does not use local `_network_cache` or publish local pubsub events.

remove-justification-preserves-shared-an.text: If a node appears in both justifications' antecedent lists, removing one justification does not remove it from the dependents index.

remove-justification-propagates-only-on-.text: If `_compute_truth` returns the same value as `old_value`, no BFS propagation occurs and `changed` excludes downstream nodes even if their metadata or support indices shifted.

remove-justification-propagates-only-whe.text: `remove_justification` calls `_propagate` only if the node’s recomputed truth value differs from its previous value.

remove-justification-prunes-reverse-edge.text: After removing a justification, reverse `dependents` edges are pruned only for antecedent or outlist references that no longer appear in any remaining justification.

remove-justification-publishes-only-with.text: Pubsub events are computed and published only when `pubsub.has_subscribers(db_path)` returns truthy at `__enter__` time; otherwise no before/after snapshot is even taken.

remove-justification-raises-indexerror-a.text: `Network.remove_justification` raises `IndexError` for an out-of-range justification index and `KeyError` for a missing node.

remove-justification-rejects-negative-in.text: `remove_justification` explicitly rejects negative indices with `IndexError`, disabling Python’s usual negative-index behavior.

remove-justification-rejects-premises.text: Calling Network.remove_justification on a premise node raises ValueError because premises have no justifications to remove.

remove-justification-repropagates-after-.text: `remove_justification` deletes a single justification and re-propagates truth values afterward.

remove-justification-requires-fully-qual.text: `remove_justification` has no `namespace` parameter, so callers must pass a fully qualified node ID when the node is namespaced.

remove-justification-return-dict-contrac.text: `Network.remove_justification` returns a dict with keys `removed` (the justification), `remaining` (int count), `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `changed` (collection of node IDs whose truth flipped).

remove-justification-returned-removed-li.text: The returned `removed` dict contains aliases to the popped justification’s live `antecedents` and `outlist` lists, not copies.

remove-justification-skips-save-on-error.text: `_with_network.__exit__` only calls `store.save(...)` when `exc_type is None`; therefore any exception thrown inside `Network.remove_justification` leaves the SQLite database unmodified (but the in-memory `Network` object is not rolled back).

removing-last-justification-is-rejected.text: `remove_justification` raises `ValueError` on the final justification; callers must use `convert_to_premise` or `retract` to change a derived node into a premise.

rename-from-rms-at-0.3.0.text: The project was renamed from `rms` to `reasons` in version 0.3.0, driven by a measured 5 percentage-point LLM accuracy improvement in ablation study

repair-abandon-retracts-with-abandoned-r.text: For the `abandon` pattern, `repair_beliefs` retracts the node with a reason containing `abandoned` and writes `repair_action=abandoned` metadata.

repair-action-is-write-only-in-observed-.text: No observed CLI or report module reads `repair_action` or `repair_research`; only repair code and tests reference them.

repair-action-rewritten-softened-mark-su.text: `repair_action=rewritten` and `repair_action=softened` are written on the successor node, not the original belief.

repair-aliases-are-identity-not-copies.text: `research_beliefs is repair_beliefs` and `api.research is api.repair` must hold as identity (`is`) checks, not equality — these are backward-compatibility shims that reference the same function object, not copies.

repair-api-count-invariant.text: The repair API enforces the invariant `total_invalid == linked + softened + abandoned + failed + errors`, ensuring every invalid belief is accounted for in exactly one outcome bucket.

repair-beliefs-aliased-as-research-belie.text: `repair_beliefs` is explicitly aliased as `research_beliefs` (line ~340), so both names reference the same function for backward-compatible import paths

repair-beliefs-counts-only-direct-flagge.text: `repair_beliefs` counts flagged ancestors by checking only direct justification antecedents, not transitive ancestors.

repair-beliefs-only-processes-valid-fals.text: `repair_beliefs` and `repair_smuggled_beliefs` process only review results where `valid` is explicitly false; missing `valid` defaults to valid.

repair-beliefs-orchestrator.text: Duplicate of existing repair-pipeline beliefs covering the four triage patterns and closed validation set.

repair-beliefs-reports-missing-nodes-as-.text: Missing node IDs produce `status="error"` with `"not found"` in the error message rather than raising an exception.

repair-beliefs-search-and-link-assumes-f.text: `repair_beliefs`'s search-and-link path indexes the first justification, so a node with no justifications becomes a per-belief `status="error"` result via a caught `IndexError`.

repair-beliefs-search-link-metadata-requ.text: For `search_and_link`, `repair_beliefs` writes `repair_action=search_and_link` metadata only when status is `linked` and `dry_run` is false.

repair-beliefs-shares-depth-memo-across-.text: `repair_beliefs` creates one shared `depth_memo` for a call and reuses it across all invalid beliefs.

repair-beliefs-skips-valid-results.text: `repair_beliefs` produces zero result entries for review items with `valid=True`.

repair-beliefs-statuses-differ-from-smug.text: `repair_beliefs` uses `linked` for a successful search-and-link while the older `repair_smuggled_beliefs` (as exercised in `tests/test_repair.py`) uses `repaired`.

repair-beliefs-triages-with-llm-before-m.text: `repair_beliefs` calls `triage_belief` first and only executes a repair branch when triage returns a pattern in `VALID_PATTERNS`.

repair-briefs-filters-invalid-by-valid-f.text: `repair_briefs` skips any `review_results` entry where `valid` is truthy or absent; only entries with `valid == False` (or falsy values) are processed.

repair-briefs-never-propagates-per-belie.text: Any exception raised while handling a single invalid belief is caught and stored in that belief's `result["error"]`; the loop continues.

repair-candidate-filtering-excludes-ante.text: In the smuggled-premise repair pipeline, candidate premises are filtered to exclude (a) IDs already present in the justification's antecedent list and (b) nodes that have their own non-empty `justifications` (derived beliefs), yielding `"no_candidates"` if the result is empty.

repair-captures-per-belief-errors.text: A review entry referencing a belief absent from `nodes` yields a result with `status="error"` rather than raising.

repair-depth-is-max-antecedent-depth-plu.text: `_compute_depth` returns `0` for missing nodes or nodes without justifications, otherwise `max(antecedent_depth) + 1`, using a memo table and cycle guard.

repair-dry-run-still-calls-llm-and-searc.text: `dry_run=True` suppresses database mutations in the repair orchestrators but does not suppress LLM calls or search calls.

repair-extraction-failure-short-circuits.text: If `extract_smuggled_claim` returns an empty string, the smuggled-premise repair returns status `extraction_failed` and does not call the search or match steps.

repair-lazy-imports-api-to-avoid-cycle.text: `from . import api` appears inside function bodies (not at module level) in `repair.py` to avoid circular imports, since `api.py` imports from `repair.py`

repair-lazy-imports-api-to-break-circula.text: `reasons/repair.py` imports `reasons.api` lazily inside functions rather than at module import time to avoid circular-import problems.

repair-llm-failure-produces-error-dict.text: If the LLM subprocess raises (binary missing, network error), `repair_premises` catches the exception and returns a single `{"action": "error", ...}` entry for that premise rather than propagating the exception to the caller.

repair-loop-converts-llm-failures-to-err.text: When `reasons.llm.subprocess.run` raises inside `repair_premises`, the loop returns an entry with `action == "error"` instead of propagating the exception.

repair-match-ids-silently-filtered-to-ca.text: `parse_match_response` validates LLM-returned `matched_ids` against the provided candidate set and silently drops any ID not in that set, returning a default `{"matched_ids": []}` on malformed JSON rather than raising.

repair-matched-ids-validated-against-can.text: `parse_match_response` filters LLM-returned `matched_ids` through the actual candidate node set; any ID not in the candidate list is silently dropped, preventing hallucinated references from being wired into the network

repair-metadata-audit-trail-is-pattern-s.text: Successful non-dry-run repairs write pattern-specific `repair_action` metadata: `"search_and_link"`, `"softened"`, `"abandoned"`, or `"research"`, with research additionally recording `repair_research`.

repair-metadata-is-not-read-by-cli-or-re.text: No observed CLI or report module reads `repair_action` or `repair_research`; only repair code and tests reference them.

repair-metadata-writes-respect-dry-run.text: Repair metadata writes occur inside `not dry_run` guards; dry-run tests assert `repair_action` is not set.

repair-one-does-not-validate-action-valu.text: `parse_repair_response` defaults action to `"retract"` but does not restrict model-supplied actions to `{"rewrite", "retract"}`, so arbitrary actions can reach callers.

repair-one-has-unguarded-node-lookup.text: `nodes[node_id]` is accessed outside the `try`, so a missing node id raises `KeyError` and, in parallel mode, aborts the `as_completed` loop.

repair-one-requires-node-in-nodes-before.text: `_repair_one` accesses `nodes[node_id]` with a bare subscript before its try block, so a missing node ID raises `KeyError` rather than producing an error result.

repair-one-returns-first-parsed-item-wit.text: `_repair_one` returns only `parsed[0]` and never verifies that its `id` matches `node_id`.

repair-one-source-lookup-embeds-full-doc.text: Source text is fetched via `nodes[node_id].get("source", "")` from `source_contents` with fallback `"(source not available)"`, and the full source document is embedded in each premise's prompt.

repair-parsers-never-raise-use-status-st.text: `parse_triage_response` and `parse_soften_response` never raise exceptions on malformed LLM output; they return dicts with empty-string defaults (e.g., `{"pattern": ""}`), and `repair_beliefs` maps any parse failure to a status string (`"triage_failed"`, `"soften_failed"`, `"extraction_failed"`) rather than propagating an exception.

repair-pattern-llm-call-counts.text: `search_and_link` makes two extra LLM calls beyond triage, `soften` makes one, and `abandon` / `research` make none.

repair-pattern-success-statuses.text: Successful repair statuses are `linked` for `search_and_link`, `softened` for `soften`, `abandoned` for `abandon`, and `needs_research` for `research`; failures include `extraction_failed`, `no_candidates`, `no_match`, and `soften_failed`.

repair-patterns-are-closed-and-validated.text: `VALID_PATTERNS` is the 4-element set `{search_and_link, soften, abandon, research}`; `parse_triage_response` rejects any LLM-returned pattern outside this set, and an empty pattern causes the belief to be skipped with `status: "triage_failed"`

repair-pipeline-has-four-triage-patterns.text: The repair pipeline classifies each invalid belief into exactly one of four LLM-determined patterns — `search_and_link`, `soften`, `abandon`, or `research` — each triggering a distinct mutation action (add justification, supersede with text, retract node, or set metadata only).

repair-pipeline-uses-three-defense-patte.text: `reasons/repair.py` triages challenged beliefs into exactly three LLM-selected patterns: `search-and-link` (find and wire a missing antecedent), `soften` (rewrite the belief text to weaken the claim), and `abandon` (retract the belief)

repair-premises-all-accurate-skips-llm.text: If the review file contains no inaccurate items, `api.repair_premises` returns `total_inaccurate == 0` and `results == []` without calling the LLM.

repair-premises-batches-one-premise-per-.text: `repair_premises` sends one premise per LLM call by default; the `parallel` argument parallelizes those per-premise calls.

repair-premises-callback-receives-live-a.text: The `on_result` callback in `repair_premises` receives the same mutable `all_results` list object after each completion, not a snapshot copy.

repair-premises-empty-input-short-circui.text: `repair_premises` returns `[]` immediately when `premise_ids` is empty, making no LLM calls and causing no side effects.

repair-premises-helper-is-pure.text: `reasons/repair_premises.py:repair_premises` accepts no `dry_run` parameter and performs no DB writes; it only runs LLMs and returns result dicts.

repair-premises-is-source-only.text: The `REPAIR_PREMISES_PROMPT` explicitly constrains the LLM to use only the provided source document text for rewrite decisions; external knowledge is forbidden, and a missing source is substituted with `"(source not available)"`

repair-premises-keyerror-aborts-batch.text: In `_repair_one`, `nodes[node_id].get("source", "")` is outside the `try/except`, so a missing premise ID raises `KeyError` and in parallel mode aborts the entire batch.

repair-premises-negative-parallel-runs-s.text: `repair_premises` treats `parallel <= 0` as sequential; only `parallel > 0` opens a `ThreadPoolExecutor`.

repair-premises-on-result-callback-cumul.text: `repair_premises` calls `on_result` with the cumulative results collected so far after each batch.

repair-premises-on-result-receives-cumul.text: The `on_result` callback in `repair_premises` is invoked after every result in both sequential and parallel modes and receives the full growing `all_results` list, not just the newest result.

repair-premises-parallel-exception-waits.text: If `_repair_one` raises in parallel mode, `repair_premises` lets the `ThreadPoolExecutor` context wait for pending tasks before propagating the exception, and already-completed results are discarded rather than returned.

repair-premises-parallel-ordering-uses-i.text: When `parallel > 0`, the returned result list is in thread-completion order (via `as_completed`), not input order; callers must join on the `"id"` field rather than positional index

repair-premises-parallel-uses-threadpool.text: Parallel execution in `repair_premises` uses `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` with `max_workers=parallel` (not asyncio), and `parallel=0` falls back to a sequential loop

repair-premises-requires-premise-ids-sub.text: `repair_premises` assumes every ID in `premise_ids` is a key in `nodes`; a missing key raises `KeyError` before the per-item `try` block and aborts the batch without returning partial results.

repair-premises-rewrite-creates-successo.text: A non-dry-run premise rewrite marks the original node `OUT` and creates a successor node carrying the corrected text and `metadata["repair_action"] == "rewritten"`.

repair-preserves-outlist-on-added-justif.text: When `repair_smuggled_beliefs` adds a matched premise as a new antecedent, the original justification's `outlist` is passed as the `unless` parameter to `add_justification`, preserving defeat semantics on the repaired node.

repair-research-only-writes-research-met.text: For the `research` pattern, `repair_beliefs` performs no truth-value mutation and only sets `repair_research` to the review comment plus `repair_action=research` metadata.
