report-json-is-consumed-by-report-module.text: `reasons/api.py`, `reasons_lib/report_belief.py`, and `reasons_lib/report_gated.py` read this file's schema; renaming keys is a breaking change for them.

report-json-is-single-file-overwrite-per.text: `.forge/report.json` is a single per-repository report file overwritten/updated on each `diary-update` run rather than an append-only timestamped history.

report-json-lacks-schema-version.text: `.forge/report.json` has no `schema_version` field, so readers cannot detect incompatible schema changes from the document itself.

report-json-status-completed-implies-com.text: When the top-level `status` is `"completed"`, the `completed_at` field is present and non-null.

report-json-steps-order-propose-before-a.text: The `steps` array orders `propose-beliefs` before `accept-beliefs`, reflecting sequential pipeline execution.

report-json-summary-maps-to-step-counts.text: Every `summary` field (`entries`, `proposed`, `accepted`, `total_beliefs`) equals the corresponding `counts` value in the `steps` array, making `summary` a derived denormalization.

report-json-timestamps-are-utc-iso8601.text: All timestamps use ISO 8601 with an explicit `+00:00` UTC offset.

report-json-tracks-proposed-and-accepted.text: The report distinguishes entry count, proposed belief count, accepted belief count, and total belief count in its step counts and top-level summary.

report-partial-step-records-must-be-tole.text: The entry does not provide evidence that readers must tolerate partially populated step records; this is an inference from incremental writing rather than a demonstrated contract.

report-source-evidence-uses-chunks-fts5.text: Source-evidence lookup uses a `chunks` table plus an FTS5 `chunks_fts` virtual table to map source text back to premise IDs.

report-status-completed-enables-gated-pu.text: Downstream `report_gated.py` treats the top-level `status` as a gate; only `completed` runs pass.

report-status-completed-implies-complete.text: The run and each step have `status: "completed"` and non-null `completed_at` timestamps.

report-status-enum-includes-running-and-.text: The entry says `running`/`failed` are implicit and absent from the observed document, so there is no demonstrated status enum beyond `"completed"`.

report-status-is-gate-flag.text: The entry only infers from the filename that `report_gated.py` gates on `status`; existing evidence says gating inputs are collected upstream, so this is speculative.

report-step-duration-equals-timestamp-de.text: Each step’s `duration_seconds` equals the difference between its `completed_at` and `started_at` timestamps.

report-steps-have-chained-timestamps.text: In a completed `.forge/report.json` run, `steps[i+1].started_at` equals `steps[i].completed_at`, so steps are sequential and contiguous.

report-summary-aggregates-pipeline-count.text: The `.forge/report.json` summary aggregates `entries`, `proposed`, `accepted`, and `total_beliefs` from the pipeline steps.

report-total-beliefs-corresponds-to-reas.text: The report’s `total_beliefs` field corresponds to the same `total_beliefs` metric exposed by `reasons/api.py` and `reasons/pg.py` and printed by `reasons/cli.py`.

report-total-beliefs-is-post-acceptance-.text: `accept-beliefs.counts.total_beliefs` is the post-acceptance belief-base count; subtracting `accepted` from it gives the pre-run count.

report-total-beliefs-maps-to-reasons-nam.text: The report's `total_beliefs` field corresponds to the namespace `total_beliefs` metric exposed by `reasons/api.py` and `reasons/pg.py` and printed by `reasons/cli.py`.

report-truth-value-markers-are-binary.text: In all report renderers, the TMS truth-value marker is binary: `+` if and only if `truth_value == "IN"`, and `-` for every other value (OUT, UNKNOWN, retracted) with no distinct marker per non-IN state.

report-updated-at-distinguishes-in-progr.text: `.forge/report.json` exposes `updated_at` separately from `completed_at`, letting consumers distinguish an in-progress write from a finished run.

report-updated-at-equals-completed-at-on.text: On a completed `.forge/report.json` run, the top-level `updated_at` timestamp equals `completed_at`.

reported-zero-reasons-lib-reference-coun.text: The zero counts are contradicted by `pyproject.toml` and `reasons_lib/__init__.py` themselves, so search scope is suspect.

reported-zero-reference-counts-are-unrel.text: `references_to_reasons_lib` reports `0`, but `pyproject.toml:31` and `reasons_lib/__init__.py` contain `reasons_lib`, so the search scope needs verification.

repos-none-still-reports-deleted-sources.text: `check_stale` accepts `repos=None` and still reports missing-source nodes as `source_deleted`.

repository-is-single-workflow-file.text: The provided tree contains exactly one file, `workflows/tests.yml`, and no application source code.

require-sqlite-blocks-pg-for-guarded-com.text: `_require_sqlite` enforces that certain subcommands (e.g., `hash-sources`) cannot run against a Postgres backend, checking both CLI flags and environment variables and calling `sys.exit()` if PG is detected

require-sqlite-gates-remaining-sqlite-on.text: The 19 production calls to `_require_sqlite` in `reasons/cli.py` are the commands that still reject PostgreSQL selection.

require-sqlite-hard-gates-on-pg-selectio.text: `_require_sqlite` raises `SystemExit` when either `args.pg` or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` is set, making it a hard gate for SQLite-only commands.

research-alias-captures-original-repair-.text: Because `research = repair` binds the function object at assignment time, a later rebinding of `repair` would not change `research`; it would still point to the original function.

research-alias-maps-to-cmd-repair.text: The `research` subcommand is the only alias in the CLI dispatch table, mapping to the same `cmd_repair` handler with identical argument definitions, not a separate implementation.

research-alias-preserves-repair-introspe.text: `research.__name__` remains `"repair"` and `inspect.signature(research)` matches `repair`, so introspection or CLI auto-generation sees the underlying `repair` function.

research-and-repair-aliases-are-identica.text: `reasons.repair.research_beliefs` is the same function object as `repair_beliefs`, and `api.research` is the same object as `api.repair`.

research-beliefs-is-alias-for-repair-bel.text: `research_beliefs` is a backward-compatible alias equal to `repair_beliefs`.

research-beliefs-is-repair-beliefs-alias.text: `reasons.repair.research_beliefs` is the same function object as `reasons.repair.repair_beliefs`.

research-does-not-catch-delegate-excepti.text: `research`/`repair` does not wrap `repair_beliefs` or other delegate calls in `try/except`; exceptions propagate, and the `errors` counter only counts status `"error"` results rather than caught exceptions.

research-has-no-wrapper.text: No additional validation, logging, or logic exists between the two names; `research(...)` is bit-for-bit identical to `repair(...)`.

research-inherits-repair-contract-and-si.text: `research` accepts exactly `repair`’s parameters, returns the same summary dict, and inherits `repair`’s exceptions and side effects, including LLM calls and possible database writes when `dry_run=False`.

research-is-repair.text: At import time, `reasons.api.research is reasons.api.repair` evaluates to `True`; the alias binds the same function object.

research-is-repair-alias.text: `reasons.api.research` is a bare module-level alias for `reasons.api.repair`, not a wrapper, so `reasons.api.research is reasons.api.repair` is true at import time.

research-preserves-repair-name.text: `research.__name__ == "repair"` and `research.__doc__` are the repair docstring; no renaming occurs.

research-raises-on-missing-input.text: Calling `research()` with neither `review_file` nor `belief_ids` raises `ValueError`, not a return-dict error status.

research-repair-sets-two-metadata-keys.text: The `research` repair branch writes both `repair_research=<triage rationale>` and `repair_action=research` on the original belief.

research-sets-two-metadata-keys.text: The `research` branch is the only pattern that writes both `repair_action=research` and `repair_research=<triage rationale>`.

reserved-slug-index-rewrites-to-index-to.text: A group label whose slug is `index` (the reserved slug) is rewritten to `index-topic` before file I/O.

reset-cost-tracker-enables-per-invocatio.text: CLI call sites import `reset_cost_tracker` and call it immediately to prevent previous invocation costs from accumulating.

resolve-config-assumes-truthy-url-is-str.text: `_resolve_config` assumes a truthy `url` is a string; a truthy non-string URL will raise `AttributeError` at `url.rstrip("/")` rather than producing a validation error.

resolve-config-does-not-validate-agent-i.text: `_resolve_config` performs no format, whitespace, URL-safety, or header-safety validation on `agent_id` or `api_key`; it returns them unchanged after a truthiness check.

resolve-config-does-not-validate-url-syn.text: `_resolve_config` checks only truthiness of the URL; it does not validate scheme, host, or general URL syntax.

resolve-config-missing-error-lists-field.text: The `RuntimeError` raised by `_resolve_config` lists missing fields in the deterministic order: URL, agent ID, API key.

resolve-config-normalizes-url-after-miss.text: `_resolve_config` checks for missing values before applying `url.rstrip("/")`, so normalization happens only after the truthiness validation.

resolve-config-reads-env-vars.text: `_resolve_config` reads `MIND_SERVICE_URL`, `MIND_AGENT_ID`, and `MIND_API_KEY` when explicit parameters are not supplied.

resolve-config-slash-only-url-becomes-em.text: A URL consisting only of slashes, such as `"/"` or `"///"`, passes `_resolve_config`'s missing check and is then normalized to an empty string.

resolve-config-strips-trailing-slash.text: `_resolve_config` normalizes the base URL by stripping a trailing `/` before returning it.

resolve-model-cmd-rejects-api-and-vertex.text: `resolve_model_cmd()` raises `ValueError` when given a model string with `api:` or `vertex:` prefixes, since those are exclusively routed to the langchain-based `_invoke_api()` path.

resolve-model-cmd-rejects-api-prefixes.text: `resolve_model_cmd` raises `ValueError("Unknown model")` for `api:` and `vertex:` models, and the error text lists both prefixes.

resolve-model-cmd-unknown-prefix-raises-.text: resolve_model_cmd raises ValueError for an unknown model prefix such as 'gpt-4'.

resolve-repo-id-accepts-any-string-with-.text: `resolve_repo_id("org/repo/extra")` returns `"org/repo/extra"` unchanged because `reasons/hf.py:43-44` returns any non-URL string containing `/`.

resolve-repo-id-always-returns-org-name.text: `resolve_repo_id` always returns a single-slash `org/name` string and raises `ValueError` for non-HuggingFace URLs.

resolve-repo-id-does-not-validate-repo-s.text: `resolve_repo_id` does not validate that its result is a valid or exactly two-component HuggingFace repo id.

resolve-repo-id-normalizes-input-not-env.text: `resolve_repo_id` strips whitespace and trailing slashes from `repo_id`, but does not normalize or validate `REASONS_HF_ORG`.

resolve-repo-id-reads-env-per-call.text: The default organization for bare repo names is read from `REASONS_HF_ORG` on every call, not cached at import time.

resolve-repo-id-rejects-non-hf-urls.text: `resolve_repo_id` validates that URL inputs start with `https://huggingface.co/` and raises `ValueError("Not a HuggingFace URL")` otherwise.

resolve-repo-id-requires-huggingface-url.text: HTTP(S) inputs to `resolve_repo_id` must contain the literal substring `huggingface.co/` or a `ValueError` is raised.

resolve-repo-id-url-parsing-is-substring.text: The URL branch at `reasons/hf.py:38-42` splits on the literal text `"huggingface.co/"` rather than parsing the URL host and path.

resolve-source-defaults-to-home-git.text: When no `repos` mapping is provided, `resolve_source_path` falls back to `~/git/<repo-name>/<rel-path>` by convention.

resolve-source-fallback-path.text: When no `repos` mapping is provided, `resolve_source_path` constructs paths as `~/git/<repo-name>/<relative-path>` by convention.

resolve-source-path-absolute-source-bypa.text: `resolve_source_path` assumes `source` is relative; an absolute source path overrides the repo/db_dir parent when joined with `Path`, bypassing the intended root prefix.

resolve-source-path-bare-filename-curren.text: When a source string has no slash, resolve_source_path treats it as a bare filename in the current directory.

resolve-source-path-checks-agent-repo-fi.text: When `agent` is present in `repos`, that repo is consulted before `db_dir` and the split-based lookups.

resolve-source-path-db-dir-precedence.text: `resolve_source_path` follows a strict precedence chain: `db_dir` resolution takes priority over agent repo resolution, which takes priority over repo-key-split resolution; missing files return `None`.

resolve-source-path-defaults-to-home-git.text: When `repos` is `None`, `resolve_source_path` falls back to resolving source paths under `~/git/`.

resolve-source-path-empty-source-returns.text: `resolve_source_path` returns `None` for an empty source string.

resolve-source-path-existence-is-only-re.text: `resolve_source_path` returns the first existing candidate path without validating file content or identity, so a wrong-but-existing file can be hashed as the source.

resolve-source-path-falls-back-to-git-ho.text: If the first segment isn't a key in `repos`, resolution uses `~/git/<repo_name>/<rel_path>`.

resolve-source-path-four-strategy-order.text: `resolve_source_path` attempts exactly four location strategies in fixed order: agent-specific repo → `db_dir` → named `repos` dict entry → `~/git/<name>/` home fallback, returning `None` only if no candidate exists on disk.

resolve-source-path-never-raises.text: `resolve_source_path` returns `None` for nonexistent files instead of raising exceptions; callers must check the `None` case.

resolve-source-path-prefers-agent-repo.text: `resolve_source_path` resolution order is agent repo, then `db_dir`, then `repos[first_component]`, then `~/git/...`.

resolve-source-path-priority-chain.text: resolve_source_path resolves relative source strings by checking the agent repo, then db_dir, then the repos dict, then ~/git fallback, then the bare path.

resolve-source-path-requires-file-existe.text: The function returns a `Path` only after verifying `path.exists()`; otherwise it returns `None`.

resolve-source-path-returns-none-on-miss.text: `resolve_source_path` returns `None` (not an exception) when the resolved file does not exist on disk or when the source string is empty.
Empty `source` and any unresolved/ nonexistent path yield `None`, which callers interpret as `source_deleted`.

resolve-source-path-splits-once.text: `source.split("/", 1)` preserves remaining path segments, so multi-level relative paths survive repo-name extraction.

resolve-source-path-unreadable-source-ap.text: `Path.exists()` suppresses most OS errors and returns `False` for unreadable or broken sources, so `resolve_source_path` returns `None` and callers treat the source as deleted.

resolve-token-precedence-explicit-over-e.text: `_resolve_token` prefers the explicit argument, then `HF_TOKEN`, then `~/.cache/huggingface/token`, then `None`, in that order.

resolve_repo_id-does-not-validate-repo-s.text: The returned value is not guaranteed to be a valid or exactly two-component HuggingFace repo id.

resolve_repo_id-prepends-default-org.text: Bare repo names are prefixed with `REASONS_HF_ORG` or `EEM-Hub`.

resolve_repo_id-preserves-explicit-slash.text: Non-URL inputs containing `/` are returned after trimming rather than validated or rewritten.

resolve_repo_id-reads-env-at-call-time.text: The default org is resolved from the environment on each call, not cached at import time.

resolve_repo_id-requires-hf-url-substrin.text: HTTP(S) inputs must contain the literal substring `huggingface.co/` or `ValueError` is raised.

resolved-base-url-has-no-trailing-slash.text: `_resolve_config` always strips trailing `/` from the URL before returning it.

resource-bounded-reference-validated-gov.text: Self-reinforcing governance’s resource-bounded reference-validated equilibria and universal reference auditability jointly converge on a governance closure that is both equilibrium-valid and backend-complete.

justifications.label: Both depth-19 results are needed: one supplies bounded reference-validated equilibrium, the other supplies backend closure and auditability; the known audit gaps gate the combination.

resource-bounded-reference-validated-gov.text: Resource-bounded reference-validated governance supports bidirectionally traceable, topology-complete guided recovery only while dependent-propagation assumptions and fragile denormalized indexes are OUT.

justifications.label: Both positive governance and guided-recovery claims are needed, and the gate is defeated by either propagation fragility or denormalization fragility.

resource-efficiency-spans-footprint-thro.text: The system achieves resource efficiency from the broadest to the narrowest scope: zero external dependencies and lazy module loading minimize the static footprint at packaging and startup, while efficient O(1) budget tracking with approximate token estimation constrains resource consumption during both compact distillation and derive belief allocation at runtime.

justifications.label: Connects orphaned depth-2 budget-enforcement belief with static-phase resource minimality into a unified lifecycle resource-efficiency claim

resource-efficiency-spans-full-pipeline.text: Resource efficiency is enforced across the complete operational pipeline: from packaging and startup (zero external dependencies with lazy loading) through belief derivation (linear O(N) budget allocation with floor bounds) to output generation (O(1) per-line budget tracking with bounded pure compact summaries), ensuring minimal resource consumption at every phase

justifications.label: Packaging/runtime efficiency (depth-3) and pipeline-level efficiency (depth-3) together cover the full resource lifecycle — no phase of system operation lacks efficiency constraints

resource-efficient-equilibria-are-refere.text: Resource-efficient permanent knowledge equilibria under self-reinforcing universal governance achieve reference-validated equilibrium status.

justifications.label: Governance-enabled resource-efficient equilibria are reference-validated only if the reference-validation audit is closed.

resource-efficient-equilibria-require-bo.text: Resource-efficient knowledge equilibria are jointly characterized by permanent operational bounds and reference validation.

justifications.label: Reference validation and permanent resource bounds are complementary necessary conditions; the reference-audit gap defeats the combined claim.

resource-efficient-guarantees-are-univer.text: The system's universal and permanent guarantees are achieved within resource-efficient bounds — self-sustainability, comprehensive auditability, and resource efficiency form a self-reinforcing triad that extends to all belief types without temporal degradation and without resource exhaustion.

justifications.label: Resource efficiency branch connected to universal-and-permanent guarantee apex — universality doesn't require unbounded resources

resource-efficient-self-maintenance-is-i.text: The system's fully auditable self-maintenance — where every self-correction, maintenance action, and belief revision is permanently traceable through the fully characterized maintenance loop — operates within resource-efficient bounds across the complete pipeline, demonstrating that indefinite auditability does not require unbounded resource consumption.

justifications.label: Auditable self-maintenance (depth-11) combined with resource-efficient self-correction (depth-7) from partially independent chains shows perpetual audit trails are achievable within bounded operational budgets

resource-management-supports-belief-curr.text: Active belief currency management — sustainable derivation of new beliefs and staleness detection for existing ones — operates with accurate bidirectional token budget control, ensuring derivation rounds allocate resources correctly per agent and output fits context-limited consumer constraints.

justifications.label: Token accuracy provides the resource foundation for sustainable belief derivation and maintenance

resource-sustainable-lifecycle-for-suppo.text: Lifecycle management for supported operations is resource-sustainable: accurate bidirectional token budgets support new belief derivation and staleness detection for IN nodes with both source fields, reducing lifecycle gaps from resource exhaustion without claiming exhaustive coverage.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

resource-sustainable-lifecycle-has-no-ga.text: Gapless lifecycle management is resource-sustainable: accurate bidirectional token budgets support both new belief derivation and existing belief staleness detection, ensuring no lifecycle gap arises from resource exhaustion.

justifications.label: Depth-5 — token budget accuracy prevents the specific failure mode where resource exhaustion creates lifecycle gaps, connecting the resource and lifecycle subsystems

restoration-hints-are-surgical.text: Restoration hints provide surgical recovery guidance after retraction cascades: hints exclude the directly retracted node (targeting only cascade victims) and require at least one surviving premise in a multi-premise justification — narrowing recovery scope to nodes that can actually be independently re-justified.

justifications.label: Two independent filtering rules combine to make restoration hints both precise (no noise from the trigger node) and actionable (only nodes with viable recovery paths)

restoration-hints-exclude-directly-retra.text: The node passed to `retract_node` is never included in its own `restoration_hints`, even if it has multiple premises.

restoration-hints-exclude-retracted-node.text: The hint loop explicitly `continue`s on `nid == node_id`, so the retracted node itself never appears in `restoration_hints`.

restoration-hints-require-surviving-prem.text: A retraction cascade only produces a `restoration_hint` for a node if it has a multi-premise SL justification and at least one of its premises is still IN after the cascade.

restoration-hints-skip-any-mode-nodes.text: Nodes whose justifications are all unary (as produced by `any_mode`) never appear in `restoration_hints`, because the hint gate requires a multi-premise SL.

restricted-show-explain-trace-raise-perm.text: `show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`, and `api.trace_access_tags` raise `PermissionError` when the requested node is not visible.

result-schema-uniformity.text: Both `content_changed` and `source_deleted` results from `check_stale` share exactly the same six keys: `node_id`, `old_hash`, `new_hash`, `source`, `source_path`, `reason` — consumers can handle both uniformly.

results-sorted-by-node-id.text: `check_stale()` returns results sorted lexicographically by `node_id`, enforced by iterating `sorted(network.nodes.items())`.

retained-retracted-nodes-enables-restora.text: Retracted nodes stay in the SQLite DB specifically so that restoration can recompute dependents without rederivation.

retract-and-assert-use-propagate.text: `Network.retract` and `Network.assert_node` update the target node and call `_propagate` to recompute dependents.

retract-and-rewrite-operate-on-different.text: `retract` changes whether a belief counts as IN/OUT, while `rewrite` changes what a belief says or what it depends on without flipping the belief's own truth value.

retract-assert-inverse-tested.text: Test coverage claim rather than code invariant; the behavioral property (retract/assert are inverses) is already captured by `defeat-reversal-propagates-automatically` and `supersession-is-reversible-and-view-consistent`.

retract-bypasses-compute-truth.text: Unlike `_propagate`, `retract` assigns `"OUT"` directly, overriding premises that `_compute_truth` would otherwise leave at their current value.

retract-cascades-to-dependents.text: Retracting a node sets every transitive `sl=` dependent to `OUT`, and asserting it back restores the whole subtree symmetrically.

retract-command-calls-api-retract-node.text: `cmd_retract` calls `api.retract_node(node_id, reason=..., ...)`, which loads the current network and runs the real cascade.

retract-computes-restoration-hints.text: `retract_node` computes `restoration_hints` by examining surviving premises of multi-antecedent justifications, enabling callers to identify which premises could rebuild retracted derived beliefs.

retract-does-not-modify-dependents-index.text: `Network.retract` does not update or rebuild the `dependents` reverse index; dependency structure is left unchanged.

retract-does-not-overwrite-reason-when-b.text: A falsy `reason` argument leaves any pre-existing `metadata["retract_reason"]` intact.

retract-empty-reason-preserves-existing-.text: If `reason` is empty/falsy, `Network.retract` does not store `metadata["retract_reason"]` and leaves any pre-existing value untouched.

retract-failures-are-swallowed.text: `retract_node` exceptions during stale handling are caught and reported in `retract_failed` rather than propagated.

retract-flips-truth-value-without-deleti.text: `retract_node` marks the target node OUT and cascades to dependents while leaving the node stored rather than deleting it.

retract-forces-out-bypassing-compute-tru.text: `Network.retract` sets `truth_value` to `"OUT"` directly and does not call `_compute_truth`, so manual retraction overrides normal premise truth evaluation.

retract-forces-unsupported-sl-dependents.text: `Network.retract` cascades through `dependents` and sets `truth_value = "OUT"` on nodes whose SL justifications no longer have all antecedents `IN`.

retract-is-a-truth-value-transition.text: `retract_node` (`reasons/api.py:473`) flips a node to OUT and cascades to dependents via `net.retract` (`reasons/api.py:489`); it does not delete the node.

retract-is-the-symmetric-undo-for-challe.text: Retracting a challenge restores the target to `IN`; retracting a defense reinstates the challenge and puts the target back to `OUT` — the same `Network.retract` primitive is used for both.

retract-missing-node-raises-keyerror-bef.text: `Network.retract` raises `KeyError` if `node_id` is not in `self.nodes`, before any node state or metadata mutation.

retract-node-always-returns-restoration-.text: `api.retract_node()` always returns a dict containing the `restoration_hints` key (an empty list when no hints apply), never omitting the key.

retract-node-batch-calls-reload-and-save.text: Each `retract_node` call opens a write context with a fresh full network load and save, so retracting many nodes by repeated calls pays the load/save cost per node rather than batching.

retract-node-classifies-changes-from-pre.text: `retract_node` returns `changed`, `went_out`, and `went_in`, where `went_out` and `went_in` are disjoint subsets of `changed` derived from a pre-retraction truth-value snapshot.

retract-node-delegates-to-postgres-when-.text: When `pg_conninfo` is truthy, the function bypasses the SQLite path entirely and dispatches to `PgApi.retract_node`.

retract-node-does-not-prevalidate-node-i.text: `retract_node` does not explicitly check that `node_id` exists; it relies on `net.retract()` to raise `KeyError` when the node is absent.

retract-node-does-not-validate-node-id.text: The function does not validate `node_id`; a missing node surfaces as a `KeyError` from `net.retract` only after the write context has opened (and the save is skipped on that exception).

retract-node-failure-skips-save-publish-.text: If `net.retract()` raises inside `retract_node`, `_with_network.__exit__` skips save, pub/sub, and cache update, still closes the store, and lets the exception propagate.

retract-node-opens-write-transaction.text: The SQLite path uses `_with_network(db_path, write=True)`, which always reloads from disk, re-saves on successful exit, refreshes the in-memory cache, and publishes pubsub events if subscribers are registered.

retract-node-pg-return-shape-is-backend-.text: With `pg_conninfo`, `retract_node` delegates entirely to `PgApi.retract_node`; the local SQLite docstring key set is the intended contract, but callers must test the actual PostgreSQL payload.

retract-node-restoration-hint-uses-first.text: For each `went_out` node except the retracted node, `retract_node` examines the first SL justification with at least two antecedents, breaks unconditionally after that candidate, and emits a hint only if at least one antecedent remains IN.

retract-node-result-contract-and-idempot.text: `PgApi.retract_node` returns `{changed, went_out}`, returns an empty `changed` list when the node is already `OUT`, and raises `KeyError` for a missing id.

retract-node-returns-four-keys.text: The local-backend return dict has exactly four keys: `changed`, `went_out`, `went_in`, `restoration_hints`.

retract-node-returns-restoration-hints.text: `api.retract_node` returns a dict with a `"restoration_hints"` list whose entries expose `node_id`, `all_premises`, and `surviving_premises`.

retract-out-fast-path-returns-empty-with.text: `Network.retract`’s already-OUT fast path returns `[]` and does not append a `"retract"` log entry or call `_propagate`.

retract-preserves-node.text: Duplicates existing belief `network-retracted-nodes-persist` which already states that retracted nodes remain in the network to enable restoration without rederivation.

retract-preserves-node-justifications.text: `Network.retract` leaves all node justifications intact; it changes truth/metadata/timestamps, not the justification graph.

retract-preserves-restorability.text: Retraction records `retracted_at` (schema in `reasons/__init__.py:49`) and is reversible via `assert` (`.claude/skills/reasons/SKILL.md:79`).

retract-propagates-only-on-in-to-out-tra.text: The cascade through dependents only runs when the target transitions from `IN` to `OUT`; the already-OUT branch performs no propagation.

retract-reason-is-metadata-side-channel.text: The legacy `retract_reason`/`_retracted` representation marks a node OUT via metadata while leaving its justifications satisfied.

retract-reason-not-consumed-is-unproven.text: The entry’s zero-match grep results are insufficient to conclude that `storage.py` and the derive/backtracking path do not consume retraction metadata.

retract-reason-persists-as-metadata.text: The `--reason` value is stored on the node as `metadata["retract_reason"]`, which `export_markdown.py` surfaces as `- Stale reason: …`.

retract-reason-persists-as-retract-reaso.text: `--reason` values are stored in node metadata as `retract_reason` and exported by `export_markdown` as `- Stale reason:`.

retract-reason-preserved-in-export-markd.text: `retract --reason` text must survive into `export_markdown` and `compact` output.

retract-returns-changed-node-ids.text: Both `retract` and `assert_node` return a `list` of changed node IDs and return `[]` when no state changes.

retract-returns-changed-set.text: `Network.retract()` returns a list of all node IDs whose truth value changed, including the target and all transitively affected dependents; retracting an already-OUT node returns `[]`

retract-returns-empty-when-already-out.text: If `node.truth_value == "OUT"` on entry, `retract` refreshes `retracted_at`/`updated_at` and sets `_retracted=True` but returns `[]` without logging or propagating.

retract-sets-retracted-metadata.text: The retract method forces a node OUT, marks _retracted in its metadata, and then cascades to dependents.

retract-sets-retracted-metadata-pin.text: Calling `retract` on an already-OUT node returns `[]` but sets `node.metadata["_retracted"] = True`, which prevents resurrection under `assert_node` on antecedents and `recompute_all`.

retract-sets-sticky-retracted-flag.text: Every call sets `node.metadata["_retracted"] = True`, which causes `_propagate` to skip that node forever until `assert_node` clears it.

retracted-flag-does-not-remove-reverse-i.text: Nodes marked `_retracted` remain in the `dependents` reverse index; the flag only short-circuits propagation.

retracted-flag-is-idempotent-audit-marke.text: The `_retracted` flag is set even when a node is already OUT, making it an idempotent audit marker rather than a state transition; code that checks this flag to decide "should I retract?" will miss already-OUT nodes, while code checking it for logging/audit purposes will correctly catch all retractions.

retracted-flag-lacks-direct-test-coverag.text: The claim is based on a limited grep and is too unstable/uncertain to serve as a durable codebase belief.

retracted-flag-locks-node-out.text: `_retracted` metadata is set when a node is retracted or imported as `OUT`/`STALE`, and cleared when it is asserted/restored or the remote sends `IN`.

retracted-flag-prevents-global-resurrect.text: Imported OUT/STALE beliefs marked `_retracted` cannot be restored by ordinary `recompute_all()` propagation.

retracted-flag-set-even-when-already-out.text: This duplicates the existing accepted belief `retracted-flag-is-idempotent-audit-marker`.

retracted-flag-set-on-retraction-or-out-.text: `_retracted` metadata is set when a node is retracted or imported as OUT/STALE, and cleared when the node is asserted/restored or the remote source reports IN.

retracted-metadata-blocks-recompute.text: Duplicates the existing belief `metadata-actively-governs-truth-propagation` which already captures that metadata fields (including `_retracted`) govern propagation behavior.

retracted-node-can-still-be-referenced-a.text: A node with `_retracted` can still be referenced by later justifications, but remains a propagation barrier until the flag is cleared.

retracted-nodes-are-skipped-during-propa.text: `_propagate` short-circuits any dependent with `metadata["_retracted"] == True` so explicitly retracted nodes are not silently reasserted by propagation.

retracted-nodes-can-still-be-antecedents.text: A node with `_retracted` can be referenced by later justifications, but it remains a propagation barrier until the flag is cleared.

retracted-nodes-remain-stored-for-restor.text: Retracted nodes stay in the DB specifically to enable restoration without rederivation, a design point attributed to Doyle (`CLAUDE.md:95`, `SKILL.md:36`).

retracted-nodes-skip-propagation.text: Duplicate of existing `metadata-actively-governs-truth-propagation` which states "retracted nodes are skipped during BFS traversal and trigger nodes are never recomputed."

retracted-nodes-skipped-in-propagation.text: Retracted nodes (marked with `_retracted` metadata) are skipped during BFS propagation but remain in the network for potential restoration.

retracted-nodes-stay-in-network.text: Redundant with `retracted-nodes-skipped-in-propagation` which captures the same fact plus the propagation behavior.

retracted-pin-survives-recompute.text: A node explicitly retracted via `retract()` gets a `_retracted` metadata flag that pins it OUT — surviving both `assert_node` on its antecedents and `recompute_all()`, clearable only by `assert_node` on the pinned node itself

retracted-premises-require-dependent-cou.text: `report_gated` sorts retracted premises by `dependent_count` and formats each using `id`, `text`, and `retract_reason`.

retracting-blocker-enables-restoration.text: Moving an outlist blocker from `IN` to `OUT` can restore an outlist-gated belief to `IN` during propagation.

retracting-scope-belief-restores-target.text: In the tested single-justification scenario, retracting a scope belief makes both the scope belief and defeater `OUT` and restores the target to `IN`.

retraction-cascade-enables-rederivation-.text: Retracting a node transitively marks invalidated dependents OUT, and re-asserting it restores exactly that set by re-evaluating justifications rather than replaying derivations.

retraction-cascade-is-transitive-and-ter.text: Retraction cascades are both transitive in reach (propagating OUT to all transitively dependent SL-derived nodes, not just direct children) and guaranteed to terminate safely (BFS prevents oscillation, retracted nodes are skipped, and the cascade stops when no truth values change) — ensuring thorough impact without risk of runaway propagation.

justifications.label: Transitive reach ensures thoroughness; safe termination ensures bounded execution — together the cascade is both complete and safe

retraction-effects-are-reported-with-rec.text: Every retraction provides both complete effect reporting (structured before/after diffs for all mutating operations, full changed set) and surgical recovery guidance (restoration hints targeting only cascade victims with surviving premises, excluding the directly retracted node), giving callers full situational awareness and actionable recovery paths from a single operation.

justifications.label: Effect reporting tells callers what happened; surgical hints tell them how to recover — together they provide complete operational support

retraction-hints-scan-only-first-multi-a.text: The hint loop `break`s after the first `SL` justification with `len(antecedents) >= 2`, so a node with multiple conjunctive justifications produces at most one hint.

retraction-leaves-tombstone-for-variant-.text: A retraction leaves a tombstone that blocks re-derivation of the claim under variant IDs.

retraction-records-retracted-at-and-is-r.text: Retraction records `retracted_at` on the node and the node can be restored with `assert`.

retraction-reporting-reflects-complete-c.text: The retraction reporting system provides accurate effect coverage across all cascade paths — structured before/after diffs capture every truth-value change, restoration hints target only cascade victims with surviving premises, and the cascade itself transitively reaches all dependent nodes — but only when the dependents index tracks all relationship types including outlists, ensuring no outlist-mediated cascade victims produce unreported effects.

justifications.label: Reporting completeness (depth-2) and cascade transitivity (depth-3) together guarantee full-fidelity retraction reporting — but the accuracy of "all affected nodes" depends on the dependents index being complete for all reference types.

return-value-is-not-coerced.text: The function returns `response.content` directly and assumes it is a string, with no `str()` conversion or validation.

reversible-negative-semantics-ground-det.text: Specified reversible negative semantics—structural absence producing emergent premise behavior plus conjunctive outlist defeat with automatic reversal and guided recovery—support deterministic reliable dialectics: challenge/defend operations inherit determinism from uniform evaluation rules applied to outlist primitives, and reliability from the reversibility of outlist-based defeat.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

review-achieves-verified-fault-tolerance.text: The review pipeline's scoped mutation-safe operation combined with uniform fail-safe output achieves verified fault tolerance across all failure modes — batch failures, missing antecedent references, and malformed LLM responses.

justifications.label: Verified fault tolerance pending completion of fault tolerance audit

review-and-contradictions-catch-orthogon.text: `review-beliefs` catches invalid reasoning within individual derivation steps (over-generalization, missing bridges, strength escalation) while `contradictions` catches incompatible facts across independently valid beliefs (absolute claims vs. documented exceptions) — the two commands are complementary with different cascade profiles (review: high cascade at depth, contradictions: low cascade at leaves).

review-api-is-read-only.text: `api.review_justifications` returns summary counts and the tests confirm the underlying justification/antecedent data is unchanged afterward.

review-api-summary-counts-are-reviewed-t.text: `api.review_beliefs()` returns summary counts for `reviewed`, `total_derived`, `invalid`, `insufficient`, and `unnecessary`, plus a `results` list.

review-auto-retract-retracts-invalid-bel.text: The `review-beliefs --auto-retract` flag actually changes truth values by retracting invalid beliefs.

review-batch-errors-are-swallowed.text: Per-batch exceptions in `review_beliefs` are logged to `stderr` and the batch is skipped, not propagated.

review-batch-failure-is-silent-skip.text: When an LLM call fails for a review batch, the error is logged to stderr but the batch is skipped with no indication in the returned results; callers cannot distinguish "skipped due to error" from "no problems found."

review-batch-failure-non-fatal.text: Duplicates the existing belief `review-batch-failure-is-silent-skip` which already captures that failed batches are skipped with a warning.

review-batch-size-bounds-llm-calls.text: `batch_size` in `review_beliefs` is a hard cap on LLM subprocess invocations: with N derived beliefs and `batch_size=K`, exactly `ceil(N/K)` calls to `subprocess.run` are made, verified by counting mock invocations.

review-batch-size-constant-is-20.text: `REVIEW_BATCH_SIZE` is set to 20, so `review_beliefs` sends at most 20 beliefs per LLM call by default.

review-batch-size-default-20.text: `REVIEW_BATCH_SIZE` defaults to 20 beliefs per LLM review call.

review-batch-size-not-validated.text: `batch_size` is not validated: `0` can raise `ZeroDivisionError`, and negative values can yield `[]` despite eligible beliefs.

review-batches-beliefs-by-review-batch-s.text: review_beliefs batches derived beliefs into groups of REVIEW_BATCH_SIZE before sending them to the LLM.

review-beliefs-batches-20-beliefs-with-6.text: review-beliefs evaluates batches of 20 beliefs and required a 600s timeout after two 300s batch failures.

review-beliefs-batches-llm-calls.text: The function splits work into chunks of `batch_size` (default 20) LLM invocations, one prompt per chunk.

review-beliefs-calls-invoke-model.text: `reasons/review.py:review_beliefs` invokes the LLM exclusively through the `invoke_model` symbol imported from `reasons.llm` (line 10), never directly via subprocess.

review-beliefs-classification-precedence.text: `review_beliefs` maps an LLM result to `review_result` using precedence `invalid` if invalid, then `insufficient` if not sufficient, then `unnecessary` if not necessary, otherwise `pass`.

review-beliefs-command-introduced-pr-97-.text: The review-beliefs command was introduced in PR #97 as v0.33.0.

review-beliefs-does-not-propagate.text: The writeback only mutates `reviewed_at`, `updated_at`, and `metadata["review_result"]`; no TMS recompute or pubsub events are triggered.

review-beliefs-dry-run-skips-writeback-n.text: `review_beliefs(dry_run=True)` still invokes the LLM reviewer; `dry_run` only skips the timestamp and `review_result` database writeback.

review-beliefs-explicit-ids-skip-truth-v.text: When `belief_ids` is explicitly provided to `review_beliefs`, the `truth_value == "IN"` filter is not enforced (only membership in `nodes` and non-empty justifications are checked), whereas the default auto-discovery path (belief_ids=None) requires both IN status and non-empty justifications.

review-beliefs-first-pass-cascade-amplif.text: Retracting 44 beliefs in the first review pass caused 286 additional retractions, a 6.5x cascade amplification factor.

review-beliefs-first-pass-retracted-44-i.text: The first full review-beliefs pass retracted 44 invalid derived beliefs.

review-beliefs-first-pass-targeted-448-d.text: The first full review-beliefs pass targeted all 448 derived beliefs in the ftl-reasons-expert network and reviewed approximately 420 of them.

review-beliefs-honors-batch-size-as-call.text: `review_beliefs()` honors an explicit `batch_size`; with two reviewable derived IN beliefs and `batch_size=1`, it makes two LLM calls.

review-beliefs-invokes-llm-under-dry-run.text: `dry_run=True` still executes the LLM reviewer; only the DB writeback is skipped.

review-beliefs-missing-results-are-silen.text: If the LLM reviewer returns fewer results than requested, `review_beliefs` silently skips writeback for those missing IDs without raising or warning.

review-beliefs-requires-justifications.text: `review_beliefs` only selects nodes whose `justifications` list is non-empty, whether IDs are auto-selected or caller-provided.

review-beliefs-requires-sqlite-only.text: `review_beliefs` has no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` parameters and therefore cannot run against the PostgreSQL backend.

review-beliefs-returns-normalized-result.text: Returned items are normalized by `parse_review_response` with defaults for missing review fields.

review-beliefs-reviewed-count-is-candida.text: `review_beliefs` reports `reviewed == len(review_ids)`, the number of candidates submitted to the LLM, which may exceed `len(results)` if the LLM skips IDs.

review-beliefs-sampling-is-unseeded.text: When `sample` subsampling is used, `review_beliefs` uses Python’s global `random` without a seed, so sample selection is non-deterministic between calls.

review-beliefs-selects-in-derived-nodes-.text: The review set is derived `IN` nodes with non-empty justifications; premises and `OUT` gated beliefs are excluded.

review-beliefs-selects-in-nodes-by-defau.text: When `belief_ids` is `None`, only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` and non-empty `justifications` are selected.

review-beliefs-total-derived-is-unfilter.text: `review_beliefs` sets `total_derived` to the count of all IN derived beliefs across the network before applying any caller filters.

review-beliefs-uses-unseeded-random.text: The `sample` parameter uses `random.sample` against the caller's global RNG state, making subsampling non-deterministic across runs.

review-beliefs-writeback-preserves-truth.text: `review_beliefs` writes only `reviewed_at`, `updated_at`, and `metadata["review_result"]`; it does not change truth values, trigger TMS propagation, or emit pubsub events.

review-cli-auto-retract-retracts-invalid.text: The review-beliefs CLI with --auto-retract retracts beliefs marked invalid unless --dry-run is active.

review-cli-displays-invalid-insufficient.text: The review-beliefs CLI displays INVALID, INSUFFICIENT, and UNNECESSARY(...) flags for each finding.

review-cli-no-report-suppresses-report-d.text: The `review-beliefs --no-report` flag suppresses creation of the report directory.

review-cli-output-file-writes-markdown-f.text: The review-beliefs CLI with -o writes a Markdown findings report.

review-cli-output-writes-findings-markdo.text: The `review-beliefs -o` flag writes findings to a markdown file.

review-completes-llm-quality-lifecycle.text: The LLM-driven belief quality lifecycle is complete across all phases: creation via derive (safe, complete, efficient), classification via list-negative (bounded, batch-scalable), and quality evaluation via review (scoped to derived beliefs, mutation-safe, fault-tolerant) — covering belief genesis, categorization, and ongoing quality assessment with no unmonitored phase.

justifications.label: Review adds independent quality evaluation to derive+classify, closing the LLM quality lifecycle

review-driven-quality-lifecycle-is-fully.text: The complete LLM-driven quality lifecycle — creation via derive with structural validation and retraction guards, classification via list-negative with defensive bounding, and evaluation via review with scoped mutation safety — achieves full code enforcement of all quality constraints, but only when the derive pipeline's minimum antecedent requirement is enforced in code rather than prompt-only.

justifications.label: Full code enforcement of the quality lifecycle requires the minimum-antecedent constraint to move from prompt to code

review-evaluates-direct-antecedents-only.text: `review-beliefs` presents each derived belief with only its direct antecedents to the LLM reviewer, not the transitive chain — producing occasional sufficiency false positives when support exists one level deeper, which must be triaged manually.

review-fault-tolerance-audit-finds-three.text: Issue #122 review fault tolerance audit found three specific handlers that do not establish coverage of all failure modes.

review-format-handles-missing-antecedent.text: `format_belief_for_review` renders `"(not found in network)"` for antecedent IDs that don't exist in the nodes dict rather than crashing, and returns an empty string for a nonexistent belief ID.

review-format-includes-outlist-context.text: `format_belief_for_review` renders an `Unless (must be OUT):` block per justification, and falls back to `(not found in network)` for outlist IDs missing from `nodes`.

review-format-numbers-only-multiple-just.text: format_belief_for_review numbers justification headers only when a belief has multiple justifications.

review-format-returns-empty-for-missing-.text: `format_belief_for_review` returns an empty string when the requested node does not exist.

review-format-returns-empty-string-for-m.text: `format_belief_for_review` returns an empty string when the requested node ID is not found in the `nodes` dict.

review-format-surfaces-unless-must-be-ou.text: `format_belief_for_review` renders outlist entries under the label `Unless (must be OUT)` with their node text.

review-found-about-20-unnecessary-antece.text: The first review pass found about 20 beliefs with unnecessary antecedents.

review-has-no-storage-dependency.text: The review module operates entirely on an in-memory `nodes` dict (from `export_network()`) and never reads from or writes to the database directly.

review-is-a-pure-non-mutating-diagnostic.text: The review module is a safe, non-mutating diagnostic tool: it operates entirely on in-memory data with zero storage I/O, gracefully renders missing antecedents rather than crashing, and scopes its analysis to derived beliefs only (premises are excluded) — making it safe to invoke at any time without side effects or data corruption risk.

justifications.label: Convergent safety properties — each property independently supports "review is safe to call": no I/O means no disk corruption, missing-antecedent handling means no crashes on incomplete data, derived-only scope means no interference with premise state. The conclusion holds if any one is true.

review-is-read-only-and-fault-tolerant.text: The review module operates entirely on in-memory snapshots with no storage dependency, handles missing antecedent references with placeholder text rather than exceptions, and silently skips failed LLM batches — achieving fault-tolerant read-only operation across all failure modes.
