metadata.retract_reason: Rebuilding with gated justification only

review-json-parser-scans-for-array.text: `parse_review_response` scans for a JSON array with `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode` and returns `[]` when no valid array is found.

review-justifications-belief-ids-restric.text: `api.review_justifications(belief_ids=[...])` restricts the review set to the named nodes.

review-justifications-classification-is-.text: The justification mode classification vocabulary is exactly three values — `"ALL"`, `"ANY"`, `"MIXED"` — and the parser uppercases whatever the LLM returns, tolerating lowercase input while enforcing this closed set for downstream consumption.

review-justifications-classification-str.text: `convert_any`, `convert_mixed`, and `keep_all` only count results whose `classification` is exactly `"ANY"`, `"MIXED"`, or `"ALL"`; any other value still increases `reviewed` but is omitted from all three counters.

review-justifications-delegates-with-unf.text: `review_justifications` computes its own candidate set only for `total_candidates`, then delegates to `_review` with the caller’s original `belief_ids` and relies on `_review` to reapply the IN and multi-antecedent filter.

review-justifications-does-not-guarantee.text: `total_candidates` is computed in the wrapper from a locally filtered dict, but `reviewed` is `len(results)` from `_review`, which is passed the *unfiltered* `belief_ids`; the equality holds only if `_review` re-applies the identical filter.

review-justifications-empty-belief-ids-m.text: In `review_justifications`, an empty `belief_ids` list is falsy and is treated like `None` for the wrapper’s candidate filter, so `[]` does not mean “review nothing.”

review-justifications-empty-candidates-r.text: `review_justifications` returns `results=[]` with all counters zero when there are no qualifying candidates, rather than raising an error.

review-justifications-explicit-ids-are-r.text: Even when `belief_ids` is supplied, `review_justifications` still drops IDs that are missing, not `IN`, or lack an SL justification with at least `min_antecedents` antecedents.

review-justifications-filters-out-any-ex.text: `_has_multi_antecedent_sl` with default `min_antecedents=2` excludes nodes whose ANY justifications have one antecedent each.

review-justifications-filters-to-in-trut.text: Both the default and explicit `belief_ids` branches require `node.get("truth_value") == "IN"` before including a node.

review-justifications-imports-format-fro.text: `review_justifications.py` imports `format_belief_for_review` from `reasons/review.py` as its belief serialization utility, creating a cross-module dependency within the review subsystem rather than duplicating the formatting logic.

review-justifications-is-read-only.text: The function never mutates `nodes` or the underlying database; it only returns advisory results.

review-justifications-is-read-only-diagn.text: `review_justifications` explicitly never mutates the database or belief network; it produces a report of candidates for ALL/ANY/MIXED reclassification, with the actual conversion delegated to downstream modules (e.g., `repair.py` or `propose_update.py`).

review-justifications-is-sqlite-only.text: Unlike most peers in `api.py`, `review_justifications` accepts no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` and has no `_pg_dispatch` branch, so it cannot target a PostgreSQL backend.

review-justifications-lacks-pg-dispatch.text: `review_justifications` takes no `pg_conninfo` or `domain_id` parameter and is SQLite-only, unlike API functions that dispatch to `PgApi`.

review-justifications-on-batch-exception.text: Exceptions raised by the `on_batch` callback in `review_justifications` are caught and logged as a failed batch, while prior partial results remain in `all_results`.

review-justifications-on-batch-receives-.text: `on_batch` is invoked after each batch with the full accumulated `all_results` list, not just the newest batch's results.
`review_justifications` passes the same mutable cumulative `all_results` list to each `on_batch` callback; callers must copy it if they retain it.

review-justifications-parallel-batching-.text: With `batch_size=1` and `parallel=2`, `review_justifications` invokes the model per candidate batch and combines all parsed results.

review-justifications-parallel-mode-lose.text: When `parallel > 0`, results are appended in `as_completed` order, so the returned list is not guaranteed to follow the original `belief_ids` order.

review-justifications-parallel-results-a.text: When `parallel > 0`, `review_justifications` returns results in batch-completion order, not `belief_ids` order.

review-justifications-prompt-assumes-all.text: `REVIEW_JUSTIFICATIONS_PROMPT` explicitly tells the LLM that reviewed justifications currently use ALL (conjunctive) semantics.

review-justifications-prompt-assumes-rev.text: `REVIEW_JUSTIFICATIONS_PROMPT` at `reasons/review_justifications.py:16` explicitly states that all reviewed justifications currently use ALL.

review-justifications-requires-in-and-mu.text: The candidate set counted in `total_candidates` is exactly nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` whose justifications satisfy `_has_multi_antecedent_sl(node, min_antecedents)`.

review-justifications-requires-multi-ant.text: A node is eligible only if it has at least one justification with `type == "SL"` and `len(antecedents) >= min_antecedents` (default 2).

review-justifications-scopes-to-multi-an.text: `review_justifications` only audits justifications where `type == "SL"` and `len(antecedents) >= min_antecedents` (default 2); single-antecedent SL justifications and all non-SL justification types are excluded from review as trivially unambiguous or out of scope.

review-justifications-selection-requires.text: Both the default and explicit `belief_ids` selection branches include only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"`; explicit IDs failing this filter are silently dropped.

review-justifications-shim-has-no-own-lo.text: The shim contains no classes, functions, or constants defined in-file; any behavior must live in `reasons/review_justifications.py`.

review-justifications-shim-re-exports-al.text: The shim exposes the full public API of the canonical module via `from reasons.review_justifications import *`, and defines no `__all__` of its own.

review-justifications-summary-counts-cla.text: `api.review_justifications` returns summary counts `reviewed`, `convert_any`, `keep_all`, and `convert_mixed`, directly mapping parsed `ANY`, `ALL`, and `MIXED` classifications.

review-justifications-total-candidates-c.text: `review_justifications` computes `total_candidates` with its own IN + multi-antecedent filter but passes the original `belief_ids` to `_review`, so `total_candidates` is not asserted to equal `reviewed`.

review-justifications-treats-empty-list-.text: The `if belief_ids:` guard makes `belief_ids=[]` behave identically to `belief_ids=None` for candidate selection (it does not request "review nothing").

review-justifications-unknown-belief-ids.text: `review_justifications` does not validate `belief_ids` against the network; unknown IDs are silently ignored in the candidate count and review.

review-justifications-uses-shallow-seam.text: `tests/test_review_justifications.py` patches `reasons.review_justifications.invoke_model` instead, demonstrating the more refactor-resilient boundary pattern.

review-justifications-zero-batch-size-ra.text: When `batch_size` is `0`, `review_justifications` raises `ValueError` from `range(0, n, 0)`, and this exception is not caught.

review-llm-process-failure-returns-empty.text: If `subprocess.run` raises (LLM binary crash, timeout, etc.), `review_beliefs` catches the exception and returns `[]` — the caller does not crash and no partial batch results are lost.

review-metadata-classification-priority.text: Review result classification follows a strict priority: `valid=False` → `"invalid"`, else `sufficient=False` → `"insufficient"`, else `necessary=False` → `"unnecessary"`, else `"pass"` — the first failing axis determines the stored `review_result` metadata.

review-metadata-result-classification-ha.text: Persisted `metadata["review_result"]` classification applies precedence such that `invalid` beats other defect classifications.

review-modules-gate-belief-admission.text: The `review*.py` and `report_gated.py` modules enforce a curation gate before beliefs become first-class, distinguishing `report_belief` (immediate) from `propose_update` (gated).

review-modules-vary-batch-size-by-conten.text: The three review modules use different `REVIEW_BATCH_SIZE` constants scaled to per-item content weight: `review.py` uses 20 (belief + justification chain), `review_justifications.py` uses 15 (belief + antecedent details), and `review_premises.py` uses 5 (premise + full source document text).

review-multi-justification-disjunctive.text: The review prompt instructs the LLM that a belief is valid if ANY of its justifications is sound, matching Doyle's TMS disjunctive support semantics.

review-namespace-empty-selects-local-unq.text: In review filtering, `namespace=""` means local/unqualified IDs without `:`, while namespaced IDs contain `:`.

review-on-batch-callback-fires-per-batch.text: The review flow documents `on_batch` as a callback invoked after each batch, not once after all batches.

review-on-batch-errors-swallowed-after-a.text: An exception from `on_batch` is caught by the per-batch `try/except` and logged; results already appended for that batch remain in `all_results`.

review-on-batch-is-per-batch.text: `reasons/review_justifications.py:123` documents `on_batch` as a callback invoked after each batch.

review-on-batch-receives-cumulative-resu.text: `on_batch` receives the same mutable cumulative `all_results` list after each batch, not a per-batch delta.

review-only-evaluates-derived-beliefs.text: `review_beliefs` filters out premises (nodes without justifications); only derived beliefs with at least one justification are sent for LLM review.

review-only-validates-derived-beliefs.text: The review pipeline filters out premises (nodes with empty justifications) before sending anything to the LLM; premises are never submitted for review validation.

review-output-is-uniform-and-fail-safe.text: Review response parsing defaults missing fields to passing, accepts only JSON arrays as valid input, and normalizes every result to a guaranteed six-key schema — producing uniform fail-safe structured output regardless of LLM response quality.

justifications.label: All review parsing behaviors converge on uniform fail-safe output with strict input and normalized schema

review-parse-defaults-fail-safe.text: `parse_review_response` defaults `valid`, `sufficient`, and `necessary` to `True`, so a missing or malformed field in LLM output never triggers a false alarm.

review-parse-defaults-safe.text: When the LLM response is missing fields, `parse_review_response` defaults to `valid=True`, `sufficient=True`, `necessary=True` — a parse error never generates a false-positive validity warning.

review-parse-drops-items-without-id.text: parse_review_response silently drops response entries that lack an id field.

review-parse-error-never-generates-valid.text: A review-response parse error never generates a false-positive validity warning because missing boolean fields default to `True`.

review-parse-extracts-json-array-from-pr.text: parse_review_response extracts a JSON array from LLM output even when it is surrounded by prose.

review-parse-requires-json-array.text: `parse_review_response` only accepts JSON arrays; a bare JSON object `{...}` is treated as unparseable and returns an empty list — the LLM must return a list even for single-item reviews.

review-parser-scans-for-json-array-with-.text: `parse_review_response` uses `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode` scanning from each `[` character to extract a JSON array from LLM output that may contain surrounding prose.

review-pipeline-is-scoped-and-mutation-s.text: The belief review pipeline restricts evaluation to derived beliefs only (premises excluded) and gates auto-retraction behind the dry-run flag, ensuring review operations are scope-limited and mutation-safe by default.

justifications.label: Scope restriction and mutation gating combine to make review a safe batch operation that cannot accidentally modify premises or retract beliefs without explicit opt-in

review-practice-65-of-80-beliefs-passed.text: In the first live review run, 65 of 80 reviewed derived beliefs passed the LLM review.

review-practice-8-retractions-cascaded-a.text: The first review run retracted 8 invalid beliefs, cascading approximately 100 dependent beliefs OUT and reducing the network from 812 IN to 710 IN.

review-practice-9-of-80-beliefs-invalid.text: In the first live review run, 9 of 80 reviewed derived beliefs were marked invalid.

review-practice-actionable-issue-rate-19.text: The first review run found actionable issues in 19% of reviewed beliefs (15 of 80).

review-practice-llm-call-takes-30-60-sec.text: Each review LLM call took approximately 30-60 seconds in the first live run.

review-practice-retraction-reduced-IN-by.text: After the first review run's retraction cascades, the network's IN count shrank by 12.5%, from 812 to 710.

review-practice-reviewed-80-derived-beli.text: The first live `review-beliefs` run reviewed 80 derived beliefs in 4 batches of 20, using 4 LLM calls total.

review-practice-two-beliefs-strengthened.text: The first review run fixed 2 beliefs by adding missing antecedents that already existed in the network but were not wired into the justification.

review-prebatch-errors-propagate.text: Errors before the per-batch `try` block, such as malformed node data, prompt formatting errors, or batch-size arithmetic issues, are not caught.

review-premises-accurate-error-type-mutu.text: The review output enforces mutual exclusion between `accurate` and `error_type`: if `accurate` is `true` then `error_type` must be `null`, and if `accurate` is `false` then `error_type` must be one of four specific values (`misread_source`, `overgeneralized`, `fabricated`, `unsupported`) — enforced by the prompt but not re-validated by the parser.

review-premises-caches-source-reads-by-s.text: `source_contents` is keyed by the source string so multiple premises sharing the same `source` share a single `read_text()`, but a failed read is not negatively cached.

review-premises-callback-exceptions-abor.text: Exceptions raised by `on_batch` are not caught inside `review_premises`; they abort the function and, in parallel mode, can cancel pending futures.

review-premises-empty-belief-ids-disable.text: Passing `belief_ids=[]` to `review_premises` is falsy, so no ID filtering occurs and all otherwise eligible premises are considered.

review-premises-filters-to-in-premises-w.text: Candidates are exactly IN nodes whose `justifications` field is absent or empty, before `belief_ids`/`visible_to`/`sample` narrowing.

review-premises-filters-to-leaves.text: `api.review_premises` only reviews nodes with no `sl`, so derived beliefs such as `derived-1` never appear in `results`.

review-premises-groups-by-source.text: Premises are bucketed by `node["source"]` and flattened before batching, so final result order follows first-occurrence source, not `premise_ids` order.

review-premises-groups-by-source-before-.text: Before splitting into LLM batches, `review_premises` regroups `premise_ids` by their node `source` field so premises drawn from the same document are contiguous within a batch, ensuring the LLM sees one source document rather than interleaving multiple documents per prompt.

review-premises-missing-source-uses-plac.text: When a premise's source is absent from `source_contents`, `_process_batch` renders the literal `"(source not available)"` placeholder and still sends the premise to the LLM.

review-premises-on-batch-receives-shared.text: `on_batch` is called with the same mutable `all_results` list after each batch; retaining it without copying will observe later mutations.

review-premises-requires-explicit-premis.text: Unlike `review_beliefs` and `review_justifications` which auto-discover qualifying nodes when the ID parameter is `None`, `review_premises` requires an explicit `premise_ids` list — there is no auto-discovery path, the caller must supply the IDs to audit.

review-premises-reuses-dry-run-mode-for-.text: `repair_premises` calls `review_premises(..., dry_run=True)` to obtain verdicts without writing back metadata, making dry-run the canonical "query" mode for downstream repair.

review-premises-skipped-no-source-confla.text: The `skipped_no_source` counter increments for missing source strings, unresolved/nonexistent source paths, and unreadable or undecodable source files, so it over-counts missing provenance.

review-premises-skipped-no-source-counts.text: The `skipped_no_source` counter is incremented for missing source, unresolvable path, and unreadable file, not only for "no source" premises.

review-premises-skips-nodes-without-sour.text: Premises lacking a `source` attribute are excluded before LLM invocation and counted in `skipped_no_source`.

review-premises-source-cache-keyed-by-so.text: `review_premises` caches successful source reads by source string, so multiple premises sharing a source share one file read, but failed reads are not negatively cached.

review-premises-swallows-batch-failures.text: Exceptions from `_process_batch` (and from `future.result()` in parallel mode) are caught in `review_premises` and logged as `WARN`, never re-raised.

review-premises-total-premises-is-pre-fi.text: `review_premises` captures `total_premises` as all IN nodes with empty justifications before applying `belief_ids`, access, or sample filters.

review-premises-unknown-ids-silently-dro.text: Unknown premise IDs produce empty formatted chunks and no matching LLM result, with no warning; they vanish from the returned list.

review-premises-writes-metadata-not-node.text: When `dry_run=False` and results exist, `review_premises` updates `metadata["last_premise_reviewed"]` and `metadata["premise_review_result"]` on reviewed nodes but does not update `reviewed_at` or `updated_at`.

review-premises-writes-only-metadata-not.text: Writeback updates only `metadata["last_premise_reviewed"]` and `metadata["premise_review_result"]`; unlike `review_beliefs`, it does not touch `reviewed_at` or `updated_at` node timestamps.

review-preserves-batch-order.text: `review_beliefs` preserves batch ordering so results appear in the same order as input belief IDs except for batches that fail entirely.

review-preserves-duplicate-explicit-ids.text: Explicit duplicate IDs in `belief_ids` are preserved and can be reviewed multiple times; the caller’s list is not mutated.

review-produces-structured-defeaters.text: When `valid` is `false`, results carry `scope_findings`, `missing_property`, and `defeat_reason_type` for downstream defeater construction.

review-prompt-requires-six-field-json.text: `REVIEW_PROMPT` instructs the LLM to return a JSON array with `id`, `valid`, `sufficient`, `necessary`, `unnecessary_antecedents`, and `comment` fields.

review-renders-missing-reference-as-not-.text: `format_belief_for_review` renders `(not found in network)` for antecedent or outlist entries missing from the `nodes` dict.

review-report-dir-json-contract.text: `--report-dir` writes a JSON report containing `timestamp`, `status="complete"`, `reviewed`, `total_derived`, and `results`, while `--no-report` suppresses report creation.

review-result-priority-invalid-first.text: `_classify_review_result` maps failures in a fixed precedence: `invalid` > `insufficient` > `unnecessary` > `pass`, so multi-failure results are labeled only by the first.

review-result-priority-invalid-over-insu.text: Already exists as an accepted belief with this exact ID.

review-result-schema-is-normalized.text: Every result dict returned by `parse_review_response` is guaranteed to have exactly six keys (`id`, `valid`, `sufficient`, `necessary`, `unnecessary_antecedents`, `comment`) regardless of what the LLM returned, via normalization with safe defaults.

review-result-schema-normalized.text: Duplicates the existing belief `review-result-schema-is-normalized` under a slightly different ID.

review-results-not-verified-against-requ.text: The function does not verify that LLM-returned review IDs belong to the requested batch; `parse_review_response` only requires an `"id"` key.

review-results-returned-in-batch-order.text: `review_beliefs` returns results in batch order, not necessarily matching input order within a batch.

review-shim-is-pure-reexport.text: `reasons_lib/review.py` defines no functions, classes, or constants of its own; its only executable statement is a wildcard import from `reasons.review`.

review-shim-requires-reasons-review.text: Importing `reasons_lib.review` necessarily imports the `reasons` package and the `reasons.review` module first, running their full module bodies.

review-shim-suppresses-f401-f403.text: The `# noqa: F401,F403` comment is required for linters to accept the otherwise-unused wildcard import.

review-skips-premises.text: `review_beliefs` only sends beliefs with at least one justification to the LLM; premise nodes (empty justifications list) are excluded from review entirely.

review-tests-mock-llm-subprocess.text: Lower-level review tests patch `reasons.llm.shutil.which` and `reasons.llm.subprocess.run`, so they never invoke a real Claude process.

review-tests-patch-llm-module-namespace.text: Tests in `tests/test_review.py` and `tests/test_review_premises.py` patch `reasons.llm.shutil.which` and `reasons.llm.subprocess.run` because `reasons/review.py` does not import `shutil` or `subprocess` itself.

review-tolerates-llm-failure.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `llm-integration-fails-softly-across-modules` and `all-llm-interactions-are-bounded-and-fail-soft`, which already establish that all LLM integration fails softly across the system.

review-valid-if-any-justification-sound.text: The review prompt treats a belief with multiple justifications as valid if any one justification is sound, evaluating each justification independently.

reviewed-count-is-not-results-length.text: The returned `reviewed` field equals `len(review_ids)` (submitted candidates), not `len(results)`, so it can exceed the number of LLM verdicts.

revision-achieves-complete-trustworthine.text: The revision system simultaneously achieves three independent trustworthiness properties: verifiable soundness (complete two-dimensional provenance/temporal coverage with reliable propagation), end-to-end reliability (across logical and infrastructure layers), and complete auditability (every correction leaves traceable history).

justifications.label: Verifiable soundness and reliability-with-auditability are established through different chains; soundness is gated on propagation correctness, which the combined claim inherits.

revision-and-lifecycle-form-closed-loop.text: The system forms a closed maintenance loop with no escape path for unmanaged beliefs: revision safety covers all belief origins regardless of provenance (internal creation and external ingestion), while gapless lifecycle management tracks every belief from creation through staleness — together ensuring that every belief in the network is both revisable and monitored throughout its existence.

justifications.label: Provenance-spanning revision safety and gapless lifecycle tracking are complementary coverage properties; their union closes the maintenance loop so no belief escapes both revision and monitoring

revision-and-lifecycle-form-supported-cl.text: The system forms a maintenance loop for supported operations: revision safety covers internal and external belief origins, while lifecycle management consistently tracks beliefs through staleness checking and propagation for supported operations, ensuring revisability and monitoring for those cases without claiming a gapless no-escape path for every possible belief.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

revision-completeness-follows-from-minim.text: The complete revision system — covering both proactive dialectical defeat and reactive contradiction resolution — handles all semantic edge cases uniformly because both revision mechanisms and edge-case handling derive from the same minimal outlist primitive, making completeness an emergent consequence of minimality rather than an engineering feat.

justifications.label: Connects the revision completeness narrative (dialectics + backtracking) with the edge-case uniformity narrative; both trace to outlist primitives, so their combination reveals that revision completeness wasn't designed — it followed from minimality

revision-coverage-is-verifiably-sound.text: Revision coverage spans the complete two-dimensional space (provenance axis and temporal axis) with end-to-end reliability across logical and infrastructure layers, forming a verifiably sound revision system — conditional on propagation not assuming the dependents index exists for all referenced nodes.

justifications.label: Dimensional coverage and infrastructure reliability jointly establish soundness when propagation is trustworthy

revision-coverage-is-verifiably-sound-fo.text: Revision coverage spans the complete two-dimensional space (provenance axis and temporal axis) with logical reliability across all beliefs and supported infrastructure reliability (staleness detection for nodes with source and source_hash, CI-usable nonzero exit, and runtime-error-free truth propagation across reachable supported cases), forming a verifiably sound revision system conditional on propagation correctly discovering all dependent nodes rather than assuming the dependents index exists for all referenced nodes.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

revision-coverage-requires-sound-propaga.text: Revision safety covers the complete two-dimensional space — the provenance axis (internal via comprehensive edge-case handling, external via defensive containment) and the temporal axis (creation-time contradiction resolution, maintenance-time staleness detection) — but this coverage is contingent on propagation correctly discovering all dependent nodes to complete revision cascades.

justifications.label: Provenance-axis and temporal-axis revision coverage combine into full two-dimensional coverage but depend on propagation soundness for cascade completeness

revision-governs-richer-state-than-truth.text: The belief revision system achieves complete semantics that extend beyond binary IN/OUT truth through metadata-enabled lifecycle governance — revisions track, preserve, and act on richer state (retraction reasons, staleness markers, access tags, challenges, supersession) that the binary truth model alone cannot express.

justifications.label: Complete revision semantics (depth-5) combined with metadata-based lifecycle governance beyond binary truth (depth-5) shows revision operates on a richer state space than truth values alone

revision-governs-richer-state-than-truth.text: The belief revision system achieves specified negative semantics that extend beyond binary IN/OUT truth through metadata-enabled lifecycle governance — revisions track, preserve, and act on richer state (retraction reasons, staleness markers, access tags, challenges, supersession) that the binary truth model alone cannot express, without claiming exhaustive coverage of every possible negation mechanism.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

revision-has-code-enforced-derivation-co.text: The deterministic traceable revision system with complete dialectical semantics achieves fully code-enforced derivation quality — every constraint including minimum antecedent requirements is validated programmatically, not relying solely on LLM prompt instructions for structural invariants.

justifications.label: Both revision determinism and dialectical completeness are code-enforced, but the minimum-2-antecedent rule for derived beliefs remains prompt-only — this GATE flips IN when that constraint is moved to code validation

revision-has-complete-semantics-with-con.text: The belief revision system is simultaneously comprehensive and minimal, with complete negative semantics exhibiting a controlled asymmetry: all defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) are truth-value reversible, but the identity transformation during challenge (premise-to-justified) is permanent — the system can undo the effects of any defeat but cannot restore a node's original unjustified status.

justifications.label: Connects the defeat/identity asymmetry with the comprehensive-minimal revision system to surface a deep semantic insight: reversibility has a precise boundary at identity transformation

revision-has-specified-negative-semantic.text: The belief revision system is minimal and handles specified negative mechanisms with controlled asymmetry: outlist-based defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) are truth-value reversible, while dialectical challenge permanently transforms premise identity by injecting a justification into a formerly unjustified node; this does not claim exhaustive coverage of every possible negation mechanism.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

revision-invariants-follow-from-shared-f.text: Both revision paths (reactive contradiction resolution and proactive dialectical challenge) preserve system invariants not through path-specific correctness arguments but because they operate through the same minimal primitives — shared foundations guarantee that any revision entry point inherits the same invariant-preserving behavior.

justifications.label: shared primitives make per-path invariant proofs redundant (depth-5 from two depth-4 IN)

revision-invariants-span-all-origins.text: Both revision paths (reactive contradiction resolution and proactive dialectical challenge) preserve system invariants across all belief origins — human, LLM, and agent — because invariant preservation flows from shared minimal foundations and all origins share the same deterministic revision engine.

justifications.label: Shared minimal foundations guarantee invariant preservation (depth-5) while all origins share the same engine (depth-5); together they show invariants hold regardless of belief provenance

revision-is-end-to-end-reliable.text: The revision system achieves end-to-end reliability across both logical and infrastructure layers: logically, every belief including all semantic edge cases is revisable with lifecycle-safe semantics-preserving operations — and infrastructurally, the I/O substrate supporting revision (staleness detection and truth propagation) completes without errors or false negatives.

justifications.label: Logical revision completeness from the belief-revision branch and I/O infrastructure reliability from the staleness/propagation branch converge across independent evidence chains

revision-is-end-to-end-reliable-for-supp.text: The revision system achieves reliability across logical and supported infrastructure layers: logically, every belief including semantic edge cases is revisable with lifecycle-safe semantics-preserving operations; infrastructurally, staleness detection reliably detects drift for nodes with both source and source_hash and provides a CI-usable nonzero exit, while truth propagation completes without runtime errors across reachable nodes for those supported cases.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-2

revision-is-evaluation-invariant-and-aud.text: The belief revision system achieves two independent trustworthiness properties universally: evaluation invariance (revision governs richer state than binary truth yet produces identical evaluation results regardless of mutation path) and full auditability across all origins (every correction — dialectical or automated — is reliable and auditable regardless of whether the belief was human-initiated, LLM-derived, or agent-imported).

justifications.label: Mathematical soundness (invariance) and operational accountability (auditability) are independently established then shown to hold universally across all belief origins

revision-is-exception-safe-and-recoverab.text: Every revision mechanism — whether normal (outlist defeat, dialectical challenge/defend) or exceptional (contradiction-triggered backtracking, graph inconsistency) — is simultaneously safe (handled without crashes or corruption), traceable (producing deterministic artifact trails), and recoverable (providing guided restoration hints for cascade victims) — the system never enters an unobservable or unrecoverable state regardless of failure mode.

justifications.label: Exception safety combined with traceable recoverability eliminates all unobservable or unrecoverable revision outcomes

revision-is-lifecycle-safe-and-semantics.text: Both revision entry points — reactive contradiction resolution (backtracking to least-entrenched premise, skipping retracted nodes) and proactive dialectical challenge (outlist injection preserving evaluation semantics) — respect node lifecycle and preserve semantic consistency despite operating through different mechanisms.

justifications.label: depth-4 — two independent revision mechanisms (reactive nogoods, proactive challenges) share lifecycle safety and semantic preservation, suggesting these are system-level invariants not per-feature accidents

revision-is-richly-governed-and-exceptio.text: The belief revision system simultaneously governs state richer than binary truth values — metadata-enabled lifecycle management including retraction reasons, staleness markers, and access tags — while remaining exception-safe and recoverable under all failure conditions, ensuring that metadata-carried lifecycle state is never corrupted by exceptions.

justifications.label: Rich state governance and exception safety are independently established — combining them establishes that even the richer-than-truth state (metadata, lifecycle flags) survives failures intact

revision-is-universally-safe.text: The complete revision system has no blind spots: every belief — including all semantic edge cases (vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents) — can be revised through either reactive or proactive paths while preserving semantic identity and respecting node lifecycle states.

justifications.label: Uniform case coverage plus lifecycle/semantics preservation means revision is safe for any belief in any state

revision-safety-spans-internal-and-exter.text: The revision system is universally safe across both belief provenance boundaries: internally-originated beliefs are covered by comprehensive edge-case handling and lifecycle awareness with no blind spots, while externally-originated beliefs are defensively contained through layered ingestion pipelines — the same revision guarantees apply regardless of whether a belief was created locally, derived by LLM, or imported from another agent.

justifications.label: internal universal safety + external defensive containment = provenance-agnostic revision (depth-6 from depth-5 IN + depth-3 IN)

revision-semantics-are-deterministic-and.text: The complete revision semantics — including the controlled irreversibility of premise identity transformation via challenge — produce deterministic, traceable state transitions at every level: every revision operation's outcome is predictable, every effect is auditable, and the asymmetry between reversible defeat and permanent identity change follows a traceable deterministic path.

justifications.label: Complete revision semantics with controlled irreversibility + traceable transitions → revision is fully traceable

revision-semantics-are-deterministic-and.text: The specified revision semantics — including the controlled irreversibility of premise identity transformation via challenge — produce deterministic, traceable state transitions at every level: every revision operation's outcome is predictable, every effect is auditable, and the asymmetry between reversible defeat and permanent identity change follows a traceable deterministic path, without claiming exhaustive coverage of every possible negation mechanism.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

revision-spans-lifecycle-and-all-sources.text: The revision system is safe across two orthogonal dimensions: node lifecycle (backtracking skips retracted nodes, propagation respects lifecycle states, challenge preserves semantics through irreversible transformation) and modification source (dialectical, LLM, multi-agent) — ensuring no revision path is unsafe regardless of the node's lifecycle state or the belief's origin.

justifications.label: Combines lifecycle safety (an orphan at depth-4 not yet used in any depth-5 conclusion) with operational safety across all modification sources, covering the full two-dimensional revision safety matrix

revision-system-is-reliable-and-auditabl.text: The revision system achieves two independent trustworthiness properties simultaneously: end-to-end reliability across logical and infrastructure layers with no blind spots, and complete auditability with traceable correction history spanning all belief origins.

justifications.label: Reliability (no revision blind spots) and auditability (traceable history) are orthogonal trustworthiness dimensions

revision-system-is-reliable-for-supporte.text: The revision system achieves two independent trustworthiness properties simultaneously: reliability across logical layers and supported infrastructure layers for supported cases (including staleness detection for nodes with both source and source_hash and runtime-error-free truth propagation across reachable nodes), without claiming no blind spots in unsupported infrastructure; and complete auditability with traceable correction history spanning all belief origins.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

revision-trustworthiness-inherits-resour.text: The revision system's complete trustworthiness inherits the top-level convergence of resource-bounded, reference-validated governance and universal auditability.

justifications.label: Joins revision-level inheritance of universal permanent verifiability with the governance equilibrium's converged resource-bounded reference auditability.

revision-trustworthiness-inherits-univer.text: The revision system's complete trustworthiness inherits the system's universal, permanent, and verifiable guarantee status.

justifications.label: The universal guarantee scope supplies the permanent/verifiable frame, and revision trustworthiness is the specific instance that inherits it.

rewrite-dependents-assumes-distinct-node.text: `_rewrite_dependents` does not check `old_id != new_id`; passing the same ID silently corrupts the reverse index by adding then discarding the same dependent.

rewrite-dependents-does-not-recompute-tr.text: `_rewrite_dependents` mutates antecedent/outlist references and dependents sets but does not recompute truth values, so callers must invoke `net.retract(old_id)` or `recompute_all` afterward.

rewrite-dependents-enables-surviving-dep.text: `_rewrite_dependents(net, old_id, new_id)` redirects dependents' references so they remain IN when `old_id` is retracted (`tests/test_derive.py:750-768`).

rewrite-dependents-raises-keyerror-for-m.text: `_rewrite_dependents` performs no defensive existence checks and raises `KeyError` if `old_id`, `new_id`, or a listed dependent is missing from `net.nodes`.

rewrite-dependents-requires-consistent-r.text: `_rewrite_dependents` only rewrites justifications of nodes already listed in `old_node.dependents`; any reference missed by the reverse index keeps pointing at `old_id`.

rewrite-dependents-updates-both-antecede.text: `_rewrite_dependents(net, old, new)` in `api.py` rewrites justification references and dependent sets for both antecedent and outlist occurrences of the old node ID, not just one or the other

rewrite-dependents-updates-both-edges.text: `_rewrite_dependents()` rewrites justification antecedents/outlist references and moves reverse-index entries from the old node ID to the new one.

rewrite-is-not-a-top-level-api.text: No symbol named `rewrite` has a function definition; `rewrite` exists only as a reviewer action string (`reasons/repair_premises.py:32`) and inside `_rewrite_dependents` (`reasons/api.py:4925`).

rewrite-is-not-a-top-level-tms-operation.text: There is no top-level `rewrite` TMS operation; `rewrite` appears only as a premise-repair action string and inside the private `_rewrite_dependents` helper.

rewrite-produces-superseding-node-with-r.text: A `rewrite` sets the original node `truth_value="OUT"` and creates a new node carrying `metadata["repair_action"]=="rewritten"`, whose id is exposed as `new_id` on the corresponding result.

rich-governance-assurance-is-dialectical.text: Rich governance assurance - supporting topology-complete reach, metadata-enriched traceability, and robust source-verified integrity - is dialectically assured through complete bidirectional operations (forward reliability and backward recovery with dual semantic grounding) and independently grounded through dialectical semantic (evaluation purity and edge-case uniformity) and governance (determinism, exception safety, and source integrity) chains, so no single grounding failure undermines all supported governance assurances.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

rich-governance-determinism-spans-revisi.text: Rich lifecycle governance — deterministic and lifecycle-complete — achieves end-to-end determinism from belief revision semantics through source integrity verification, ensuring that metadata-enabled state governance produces predictable outcomes at every pipeline stage from truth evaluation through hash-based staleness detection.

justifications.label: End-to-end determinism and rich governance are independently depth-7 conclusions — combining them shows the rich state (not just truth values) is deterministically maintained across the entire revision-to-source pipeline

rich-governance-emerges-from-minimal-fou.text: Rich state governance — metadata-enabled lifecycle management extending beyond binary IN/OUT truth to retraction pins, stale reasons, and access tags — is achieved through the same minimal foundations that unify truth computation and belief revision, not through additional machinery layered on top.

justifications.label: Completeness-minimality unity + rich revision → rich governance from minimal roots

rich-governance-encompasses-topology-com.text: Rich governance — deterministic from revision through source integrity, exception-safe across all failure modes, and source-grounded — encompasses topology-complete state transitions, ensuring every belief modification propagates richly-governed metadata-enriched state changes completely through the dependency graph with deterministic recoverable outcomes.

justifications.label: Unifies the system's two deepest IN governance properties (depth 9 + depth 8) into a single depth-10 characterization

rich-governance-has-verified-evolution-t.text: The system's rich governance — deterministic, exception-safe, and source-grounded — combined with gap-free lifecycle source coverage achieves verified evolution tolerance at all system boundaries when the evolution tolerance audit (issue #121) confirms that all boundaries have documented forward-compatibility, completing the governance guarantee across the format/schema evolution dimension.

justifications.label: rich governance extends to verified evolution tolerance after audit completion

rich-governance-inherits-minimality-comp.text: Rich lifecycle governance — deterministic and lifecycle-complete — achieves its determinism not as an independently-engineered property but as a consequence of the same minimality that generates completeness: the unified minimality-completeness-determinism triad ensures that rich governance's predictable state trajectories and gapless monitoring arise from the same minimal primitives that produce comprehensive truth maintenance coverage.

justifications.label: rich governance determinism arises from the same minimality that generates completeness

rich-governance-is-deterministic-and-lif.text: The deterministic lifecycle-complete architecture governs state richer than binary truth values — deterministic reasoning ensures predictable state trajectories and gapless lifecycle monitoring ensures no belief escapes management, while metadata-enabled governance extends these guarantees to retraction reasons, staleness tracking, and access control beyond IN/OUT.

justifications.label: Deterministic lifecycle-complete architecture + rich state governance → deterministic lifecycle-complete rich governance

rich-governance-is-deterministic-excepti.text: Rich lifecycle governance simultaneously achieves end-to-end determinism from revision semantics through source integrity and exception safety across TMS and source lifecycle — governance is both predictable in its state trajectories and resilient to all exceptional conditions.

justifications.label: Two independent depth-8 properties of rich governance (determinism-through-source and exception-safety) compose into fully characterized governance that is both predictable and fault-tolerant

rich-governance-is-exception-safe.text: The system's rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, extending beyond binary truth to metadata-enabled state with full monitoring — operates within an exception-safe framework spanning both TMS core and source lifecycle: contradictions are resolved through deterministic backtracking, challenges reach correct truth states through crash-safe propagation, and source failures degrade gracefully through fail-safe path resolution — ensuring that rich state transitions never produce corrupted or inconsistent lifecycle metadata.

justifications.label: Deterministic lifecycle-complete governance plus exception safety across both TMS and source domains eliminates unsafe rich-state transitions

rich-governance-spans-all-backends.text: The system's exception-safe rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, and spanning revision through source integrity — operates identically across all storage backends, achieving full behavioral parity between SQLite and PostgreSQL for metadata-enabled lifecycle management.

justifications.label: Rich governance properties are established on the SQLite path; PgApi's partial API coverage is the sole barrier to backend universality — this GATE flips IN when PgApi achieves full API parity

rich-governance-spans-all-backends-v2.text: The system's rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, and spanning TMS core through source lifecycle — operates within an exception-safe framework for metadata-enabled state management, supporting predictable state trajectories, crash-safe propagation of challenges, and graceful degradation on source failures, with the architectural design intended to prevent corrupted or inconsistent lifecycle metadata from rich state transitions.

rich-governance-supports-verified-evolut.text: The system's rich governance — deterministic, exception-safe, and source-grounded — combined with robust lifecycle source coverage, including SHA-256 source verification and exception-safe recoverable revision that mitigates silent gaps, supports verified evolution tolerance at audited system boundaries when the evolution tolerance audit (issue #121) confirms that boundaries have documented forward-compatibility, contributing to the governance guarantee across the format/schema evolution dimension.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-1

richer-revision-preserves-evaluation-inv.text: Although the revision system governs state richer than binary truth values — including metadata-enabled lifecycle governance with retraction reasons, staleness indicators, and access controls — truth evaluation remains transformation-invariant, producing identical results regardless of attachment history or structural origin; the richer governance layer operates orthogonally to evaluation, enriching management capabilities without compromising core determinism.

justifications.label: Richer-than-binary revision + transformation-invariant evaluation means governance richness and evaluation simplicity are orthogonal

rits-gateway-has-no-code-specific-handli.text: The `rits` gateway identity is carried only through the `openai:rits/...` model string; there is no rits-specific code branch or configuration reference.

rms-rename-has-no-cli-shim.text: The 0.3.0 rename dropped the `rms` console script without a compatibility entry point; `[project.scripts]` lists only `reasons` and `reasons-mcp`.

robust-topology-complete-truth-effects-e.text: Topology-complete, robust, traceable truth-change effects combined with traceable/recoverable revision mechanisms enable guided recovery across all transitive dependents under graph-state variation.

justifications.label: Combines the robust truth-effect topology chain with revision recoverability; both are necessary for guided recovery to reach all dependents.

rollback-prevents-aborted-transaction-er.text: `api.conn.rollback()` at the start of teardown resets failed-transaction state left by the test so the subsequent `DELETE`s succeed.

run-cli-harness-catches-systemexit.text: The `run_cli` test helper catches `SystemExit` raised by the CLI `main()` function and extracts its exit code.

run-cli-harness-invokes-cli-in-process.text: The run_cli test harness invokes reasons_lib.cli:main in-process by patching sys.argv, sys.stdout, and sys.stderr, returning stdout, stderr, and exit code.

run-cli-helper-catches-systemexit.text: The `run_cli` test harness intercepts `SystemExit` to extract exit codes, preventing argparse errors or explicit `sys.exit()` calls from terminating the test process.

safe-universal-revisability.text: Any mutation source — human dialectical challenge, LLM-derived proposal, or multi-agent import — can safely revise any belief in the network through complete minimal mechanisms; the system imposes no restrictions on who can revise what, while guaranteeing that every revision path preserves consistency.

justifications.label: one establishes that all sources are safe and uniform, the other that revision is complete from minimality; combining yields unrestricted-yet-safe revisability

safety-and-uniformity-are-co-derived.text: Dialectical safety (deterministic evaluation of irreversible premise transformations) and edge-case uniformity (consistent handling of vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, and empty antecedents) are independently derived from the same shared root — semantic minimality with operational determinism — revealing them as two faces of a single architectural property rather than independent design achievements.

justifications.label: Both conclusions share semantic-minimality-with-operational-determinism as their root, exposing dialectical safety and edge-case uniformity as co-derived rather than independently designed

safety-integrity-and-uniformity-converge.text: Three independently-established properties — boundary-agnostic integrity (internal/external indifference), dialectical safety (deterministic evaluation of irreversible transformations), and edge-case uniformity (consistent handling of vacuous and asymmetric cases) — converge to a single architectural invariant because all three derive from the same minimal evaluation rules applied uniformly.

justifications.label: one establishes integrity agnosticism across boundaries and sources, the other co-derives safety with uniformity from minimality; combining shows three-way convergence

safety-is-enforced-across-all-layers-and.text: Safety is enforced uniformly across both the architectural dimension (clean layer boundaries with atomic isolated mutations) and the storage dimension (equivalent guarantees through backend-appropriate mechanisms in SQLite and PostgreSQL) — no safety property depends on a specific backend or architectural layer.

justifications.label: Connects backend-agnostic storage safety with layer-enforced architectural safety into a cross-cutting safety invariant; storage-layer-is-backend-agnostic-and-safe is currently unused

scope-belief-ids-are-unique-across-defea.text: Scope-belief IDs are uniquely generated per defeat; multiple defeats on the same node with different justification indices produce disjoint sets of `scope_belief_ids`.

scope-belief-ids-are-unique-per-defeat-c.text: Two defeats on the same target create disjoint scope-belief ID sets; scope beliefs are anchored to a specific defeater rather than deduplicated globally.

scope-belief-metadata-links-antecedent-a.text: Scope-belief metadata records `scope_of` as the antecedent and `for_defeater` as the generated defeater ID.

scope-beliefs-are-atomic-in-premises.text: Scope beliefs created by `defeat_with_scope` are always `IN` with zero justifications (atomic leaf premises), and carry `metadata.scope_of` (which antecedent they scope) and `metadata.for_defeater` (which defeater consumes them).

scope-beliefs-are-premises.text: Scope beliefs created by `defeat_with_scope` have `truth_value == "IN"`, an empty `justifications` list, and metadata keys `scope_of` and `for_defeater`, per `test_scope_beliefs_are_premises`

scope-beliefs-carry-scope-of-and-for-def.text: Each scope belief stores `scope_of` pointing to the original antecedent and `for_defeater` pointing to the defeater that consumes it.

scope-defeater-justification-links-to-sc.text: The defeater node produced by `defeat_with_scope` has exactly one SL justification whose antecedents are the scope-belief IDs, making the defeater structurally derived from the scope beliefs rather than independently inserted.

scope-finding-creates-in-premise-scope-b.text: `defeat_with_scope` creates one scope-belief node per scope finding, and each scope belief is an `IN` premise with an empty `justifications` list.

scope-findings-antecedents-are-textual-n.text: `defeat_with_scope` does not validate or wire each `scope_findings[i]["antecedent"]` as a justification dependency; the antecedent ID appears only in the scope node's ID and text.

scope-id-collisions-are-suffixed.text: When a generated scope-belief ID collides with an existing node, `defeat_with_scope` appends a numeric suffix (`-1`, `-2`, ...) and creates the node under the suffixed ID.

scope-over-generalization-is-primary-der.text: The most common invalid derivation pattern is scope over-generalization — claiming "all X" or "every X" when antecedents establish only specific instances — followed by conjunction distribution fallacy, strength escalation, causal overclaim, and missing bridge assumptions.

scoped-subscribers-require-matching-db-p.text: A subscriber registered with `db_path` only receives publishes made with that exact `db_path`; global subscribers receive all.

search-and-link-appends-justification-wi.text: On `linked` and not `dry_run`, `_do_search_and_link` appends a new SL justification via `api.add_justification` and does not remove existing justifications.

search-and-link-dry-run-skips-db-mutatio.text: With `dry_run=True` the function still performs both LLM calls and search but skips `api.add_justification`, yet still returns `status == "linked"` on a successful match.

search-and-link-dry-run-skips-mutation-b.text: `dry_run=True` skips only the `add_justification` mutation; LLM and search calls still run and status can still be `linked`.

search-and-link-filters-to-leaf-in-premi.text: Candidates must have `truth_value == "IN"`, differ from `belief_id`, not appear in `existing_ants`, and have no `justifications` of their own (premise-only filter).

search-and-link-includes-results-missing.text: A search result whose ID is absent from `nodes` is still accepted as a candidate because `sr_node is None` short-circuits the premise-only check.

search-and-link-json-decode-errors-yield.text: Malformed JSON from `search_fn` is caught and converted to `[]`, producing `"no_candidates"` rather than raising.

search-and-link-metadata-written-only-on.text: `api.set_metadata(..., "repair_action", "search_and_link")` runs only when `status == "linked"` and `not dry_run`, so `extraction_failed`/`no_candidates`/`no_match` leave the belief untouched.

search-and-link-operational-exceptions-p.text: LLM, search, and `add_justification` exceptions are not caught by `_do_search_and_link`; they propagate to the caller.

search-and-link-preserves-outlist.text: `_do_search_and_link` passes the original `outlist` through as the `unless` argument to `api.add_justification` so the blocking set is unchanged.

search-and-link-restricts-candidates-to-.text: Search-and-link candidate selection excludes the belief itself, existing antecedents, non-`IN` nodes, and nodes with justifications.

search-and-link-returns-four-tuple.text: `_do_search_and_link` returns `(status, claim, matched_ids, rationale)` where status is one of `extraction_failed`, `no_candidates`, `no_match`, or `linked`.

search-and-link-returns-four-tuple-statu.text: `_do_search_and_link` returns `(status, claim, matched_ids, rationale)` with status in `extraction_failed`, `no_candidates`, `no_match`, or `linked`.

search-and-link-swallows-search-json-par.text: `JSONDecodeError` or `TypeError` while parsing search results yields an empty candidate list, typically resulting in `no_candidates`.

search-and-link-uses-first-justification.text: When `node["justifications"]` contains multiple entries, only `justifications[0]` supplies `original_ants` and `original_outlist` for the new SL justification.

search-default-excludes-out.text: `api.search` omits retracted nodes from its results when `include_out` is not specified.

search-defaults-to-format-markdown.text: `search()` routes to `_format_markdown` whenever `format` is not `json`, `minimal`, `compact`, or `names-only`, making it the effective default renderer.

search-depth-expansion-adds-antecedents.text: `api.search()` depth expansion returns only direct hits at depth 0, adds direct antecedents at depth 1, and adds transitive antecedents at depth 2.

search-empty-query-falls-back-to-match-a.text: An empty non-OR query causes `_fts_search` to return `[]`, then `_substring_search("")` matches every node because `"" in text` is always true.

search-expands-neighbors-via-justificati.text: `search` performs neighbor expansion by BFS along justification edges after the FTS5 query.

search-falls-back-to-substring.text: `api.search()` tries FTS5 full-text search first, then falls back to substring matching if FTS5 tables don't exist or error; it always produces results if substring matches exist.

search-filters-neighbor-expansion-by-vis.text: Search visibility gating applies not only to matched nodes but also to antecedent/neighbor expansion, so hidden antecedents are not expanded into results.

search-has-four-output-formats.text: The `search` function supports four output formats: markdown, json, minimal, and compact — selected by the caller to match the consumption context (human, API, LLM prompt, compact view).

search-is-resilient-across-index-states.text: Search operates correctly regardless of FTS5 index availability: the index is derived (rebuilt from scratch on every save) so stale indexes are self-healing, and search falls back to substring matching when FTS tables don't exist or error

justifications.label: A derived (rebuildable) index plus a substring fallback provides index-state-independent search

search-lookup-compact-hide-out-by-defaul.text: All three model-facing retrieval functions (`api.search`, `api.lookup`, `api.compact`) exclude OUT-status beliefs from their output by default; callers must explicitly pass `include_out=True` to include retracted beliefs.

search-names-only-skips-neighbor-expansi.text: The `names-only` format in `search` returns IDs only and skips neighbor expansion entirely.

search-namespace-and-tag-filter-matches-.text: `search` applies `namespace` and `tag` filters only to matched nodes, not to neighbor nodes added during expansion.

search-namespace-and-tag-filters-do-not-.text: The `namespace` and `tag` parameters filter only matched IDs, not expanded neighbor IDs.

search-neighbor-expansion-is-bfs-with-vi.text: `search` expands neighbors breadth-first over antecedent and dependent edges with a visited set, preventing cycles.

search-neighbor-expansion-respects-visib.text: `lookup` and `search` exclude forbidden nodes from results, including during neighbor expansion.

search-neighbor-expansion-uses-anteceden.text: Neighbor BFS traverses justification antecedents and `node.dependents`, with a visited set to avoid cycles.

search-or-mode-sorts-lexicographically.text: A query containing a literal `|` triggers OR mode in `search`, which unions FTS/substring matches and returns IDs in lexicographic order rather than relevance order.

search-paginates-before-neighbor-expansi.text: `offset` and `limit` are applied to matched IDs before BFS neighbor expansion, so skipped matches never contribute neighbors.

search-pagination-applies-before-neighbo.text: `search` applies `limit` and `offset` to matched IDs before neighbor expansion, so neighbors are not counted against the limit.

search-pagination-empty-result-varies-by.text: When pagination removes all matched IDs, `search` returns `"No results found."` for names-only/compact, `[]` for json, and an empty string for markdown/minimal.

search-pg-ignores-unsupported-query-opti.text: On the PostgreSQL branch, `search` raises `NotImplementedError` only for `depth != 1` and truthy `tag`, and silently ignores `sort`, `namespace`, `limit`, `offset`, and `regex`.

search-pipe-is-or-operator.text: In `api.search`, a `|` in the query is treated as an OR operator at the query layer.

search-postgresql-branch-ignores-sort-na.text: The PostgreSQL dispatch only forwards `query`, `visible_to`, `format`, and `include_out`; the other parameters are not passed.

search-relaxation-capped-at-50-queries.text: FTS progressive relaxation drops terms via `combinations()` (largest subsets first) until results appear, capped at 50 total relaxation queries to prevent combinatorial explosion on long search strings.

search-relaxes-queries-with-bounded-term.text: `lookup` and `_fts_search` strip stop-words and then try dropping query terms via `itertools.combinations`, capped at 50 relaxation attempts.

search-resilience-degrades-gracefully-at.text: The search pipeline guarantees non-empty results through three independent degradation mechanisms: stop-word filtering prevents degenerate queries, progressive term relaxation handles multi-term FTS5 misses, and substring fallback handles complete FTS5 infrastructure failure.

justifications.label: Convergent resilience — each mechanism independently prevents a distinct failure mode (all-stop-words, partial FTS5 match, missing FTS5 tables), and the conclusion "search always returns results" holds as long as at least one tier functions.

search-resilience-degrades-gracefully-at.text: The search pipeline supports producing results through sequential fallback mechanisms: when all query terms are stop words, the query falls back to terms longer than 1 character; when a multi-term FTS5 query returns no results, terms are progressively dropped until matches are found or all subsets are exhausted; and when FTS5 tables don't exist or error, the search falls back to substring matching, producing results when substring matches exist.

search-resilience-is-universal-and-query.text: Every retrieval path (FTS5 search, ask synthesis, compact output) is simultaneously resilient (silent error handling with graceful fallback) and query-bounded (capped relaxation at 51 calls, infallible on any input) — no retrieval operation can crash, hang, or exhaust resources.

search-source-chunks-assumes-chunks-fts-.text: The SQL assumes `chunks_fts.rowid` maps to `chunks.id` and that `chunks_fts` supports FTS5 `MATCH` and `rank`.

search-source-chunks-does-not-deduplicat.text: The FTS5 query builder in `search_source_chunks` does not deduplicate repeated terms, so a query like `"cat cat"` produces `"cat" OR "cat"`.

search-source-chunks-enables-rag-context.text: Its output is embedded under `## Source Documents` in `ask()` and as `{context}` in `_fts_rag_answer`, enabling source-grounded answers.

search-source-chunks-has-file-creation-s.text: Because `sqlite3.connect` opens the target path, a nonexistent `sources_db` leaves a 0-byte file behind even on the error path.

search-source-chunks-joins-fts-to-chunks.text: The query in `reasons/ask.py:240-243` joins `chunks_fts` to `chunks` on `c.id = chunks_fts.rowid` and filters with `chunks_fts MATCH ?`.

search-source-chunks-missing-db-propagat.text: Passing a non-existent or unreadable DB path to `search_source_chunks` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError` directly; the function does not catch, wrap, or convert the exception into a custom type or empty result.

search-source-chunks-orders-by-fts5-rank.text: `search_source_chunks` orders matches by FTS5 `rank` ascending via `ORDER BY chunks_fts.rank`.

search-source-chunks-preserves-empty-sec.text: A matched chunk with empty section metadata returns `section == ""`, not `None` or a missing key.

semantic-contradiction-55-belief-cluster.text: In the first `--semantic` contradiction run, cluster 1 with 55 beliefs exceeded the 300-second LLM timeout.

semantic-contradiction-batches-cluster-b.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` chunks each semantic cluster by `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` (50); a 51-member cluster yields a 50-member batch and a singleton batch that is still sent to the LLM.

semantic-contradiction-defaults-to-clust.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` uses `DEFAULT_MODEL` imported from `reasons.cluster` when `embedding_model` is falsy.

semantic-contradiction-detection-skips-s.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` returns `[]` without invoking `subprocess.run` when the network is empty or has only a single belief.

semantic-contradiction-first-run-used-57.text: The first `--semantic` contradiction run processed 575 IN beliefs grouped into 20 clusters.

semantic-contradiction-flushes-only-none.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` only writes to `output_path` when a batch produces at least one parsed contradiction.

semantic-contradiction-results-not-dedup.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` performs no cross-cluster or cross-batch deduplication, so the returned contradiction list can contain duplicates.

semantic-contradiction-reuses-cluster-in.text: Semantic contradiction detection delegates embedding and clustering to the existing `list_clusters()` from `reasons_lib/cluster.py` — the same infrastructure that serves deduplication also serves contradiction detection, with no duplicate embedding/clustering implementation.

semantic-contradiction-reuses-existing-p.text: After clustering, semantic contradiction detection reuses the existing contradiction prompt/parse pipeline unchanged.

semantic-contradiction-skips-singleton-c.text: Single-belief clusters are skipped during semantic contradiction detection (no contradiction possible within one belief), and clusters exceeding `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` are sub-batched within the cluster boundary.

semantic-contradictions-cluster-before-l.text: The `--semantic` flag on `detect-contradictions` embeds beliefs via sentence-transformers, clusters with KMeans via `list_clusters()`, and sends each cluster to the LLM as a batch — ensuring topically related beliefs are analyzed together instead of being scattered across random batches of 50.

semantic-contradictions-use-all-minilm-l.text: Semantic contradiction detection embeds beliefs using the sentence-transformers model `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

semantic-detection-filters-claims-by-glo.text: `parse_contradiction_response` is called with `valid_ids=set(belief_ids)`, so returned claims must be among all checked `IN` beliefs rather than only the current cluster or batch.

semantic-detection-returns-empty-without.text: If no candidate IDs remain after filtering for `truth_value == "IN"`, the function returns `[]` before calling `list_clusters` or the LLM.

semantic-detection-skips-single-belief.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` returns `[]` and never calls `subprocess.run` when fewer than 2 `IN` beliefs exist.

semantic-detection-skips-singleton-clust.text: Clusters with fewer than two belief IDs are skipped without an LLM call.

semantic-detection-swallows-llm-and-flus.text: Exceptions from `invoke_model`, `parse_contradiction_response`, or `_flush_results` are caught per batch and converted to `stderr` warnings, allowing partial results.

semantic-detection-uses-fixed-batch-size.text: Within each cluster, beliefs are chunked by the module constant `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` (`50`), and the function has no `batch_size` parameter.

semantic-minimality-with-operational-det.text: The system unifies semantic minimality (all non-monotonic features and truth semantics derive from uniform outlist/disjunction primitives) with operational determinism (all operations terminate predictably via BFS fixpoint with conservative failure semantics), yielding a small trusted kernel that powers all reasoning.

justifications.label: depth-4 — the minimal primitive set is also the deterministic primitive set; no tension between expressiveness and predictability

semantic-mode-requires-numpy-and-cluster.text: `semantic=True` imports `numpy` and `reasons.cluster.ClusterCache`, both of which can fail lazily at call time.

semantics-and-revision-share-minimal-fou.text: Both truth maintenance semantics and belief revision achieve comprehensive coverage through the same minimal primitives — the outlist primitive simultaneously enables emergent truth evaluation (disjunction over conjunction with absence semantics) and all non-monotonic revision mechanisms (defeat, backtracking, dialectics), confirming minimality as a cross-cutting architectural principle rather than a property of any single subsystem.

justifications.label: Both subsystems derive comprehensiveness from shared outlist/disjunction primitives — minimality is cross-cutting

server-does-not-import-sdk-error-types.text: `reasons/mcp_server.py` imports only `FastMCP` from `mcp.server.fastmcp` and never references `McpError`, `ErrorData`, or manual `isError` construction.

server-embeds-errors-in-tool-content.text: Every error branch in `reasons/mcp_server.py` (e.g. `show()`, `retract()`, `what_if()`) returns `json.dumps({"error": "..."})`, causing FastMCP to emit `isError=False` results whose body carries the failure.

setuptools-packages-list-is-explicit.text: The `[tool.setuptools]` packages list is an explicit `["reasons", "reasons_lib"]` rather than auto-discovery; any new top-level package directory must be manually appended or it will be omitted from the wheel.

setuptools-packaging-uses-explicit-packa.text: `[tool.setuptools] packages = ["reasons", "reasons_lib"]` hard-codes two packages rather than using `find`, so any package-directory change must be edited here too.
