structural-semantic-consistency-is-bidir.text: Structural deduplication and semantic contradiction management, combined with bidirectionally complete and traceable belief modification, yield consistency maintained across both graph and logical dimensions.

justifications.label: Consistency spans structural and semantic dimensions only when both dedup/contradiction handling and bidirectional traceable modification are present.

structured-renderer-requires-premise-id.text: `_build_structured_report` requires every `premises_data` element to contain an `id` key; missing it raises `KeyError`.

structured-report-defaults-missing-block.text: A blocker missing from `blocker_details` gets `dependent_count` `0`, while missing `text` or `gated` in blocker data raises.

structured-report-does-not-recompute-cou.text: The summary blocker/gated counts come directly from `gated_data` and are not validated against the actual `blockers` mapping.

structured-report-escapes-only-retracted.text: Markdown pipe escaping is applied only to retracted-premise text and retract reason, not to blocker text or gated-belief text.

structured-report-escapes-pipes-only-in-.text: Only retracted premise text and `retract_reason` replace `|` with `\|`; blocker and gated belief text are not escaped.

structured-report-heading-and-root-count.text: `_build_structured_report` emits a `# Belief Report: <belief-id>` heading and renders root-premise count as `Root Premises (N)`, using `No root premises found.` when empty.

structured-report-includes-root-premises.text: `_build_structured_report` includes root-premise counts and source-evidence sections when those inputs are provided.

structured-report-is-llm-free.text: `_build_structured_report` produces Markdown by string assembly only and never calls an LLM.

structured-report-renders-out-beliefs-an.text: OUT beliefs render `status: OUT` and a `[-]` marker, and outlist identifiers appear in the report with the word `"outlist"`.

structured-report-renders-source-evidenc.text: Source evidence is rendered under a `Source Evidence:` section with section paths in the form `<filename> > <section>`.

structured-report-requires-gated-data-co.text: It unconditionally reads `gated_data["blocker_count"]` and `gated_data["gated_count"]`, so missing keys raise `KeyError`.

structured-report-sorts-blockers-by-gate.text: Active blockers are ordered by descending `len(bdata["gated"])`, with ties preserving original mapping order due to stable sorting.

structured-report-truncates-retracted-an.text: The structured path truncates retracted premise text to 80 characters and gated belief text to 100 characters; the prompt path does not truncate.

subprocess-run-is-implicit-contract.text: Roughly 30+ review/classify/derive tests assert on `mock_run.call_count` or `mock_run.call_args`, making `subprocess.run` an undocumented contract of `invoke_model`.

subscriber-exceptions-are-swallowed-not-.text: Exceptions raised by subscribers are caught, logged via `logger.exception`, and never propagate to the caller.

subscriber-exceptions-do-not-propagate.text: `publish()` catches and logs exceptions from each subscriber, so one subscriber failure does not break the write path.

substring-fallback-is-order-sensitive.text: When multiple canonical types appear in the model output, the first in `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` list order wins, regardless of the model's actual intent.

sum-gf-abstraction-rationale-only-appear.text: The only repo match for `SUM|GF` is `tests/test_summarize.py:3`; the docs search returns zero matches, so the abstraction claim is documented only in that test docstring.

sum-gf-only-documented-in-test-docstring.text: The only repo match for `SUM|GF` is the module docstring of `tests/test_summarize.py`; the docs search returns zero matches.

summaries-hide-covering-in-nodes.text: An IN node whose id appears in another IN node's `metadata["summarizes"]` is omitted from the IN listing and reported via `(N nodes hidden by summaries)`.

summarize-creates-sl-node-with-anteceden.text: `Network.summarize` creates an SL node whose antecedents are the summarized nodes and whose metadata records the `summarizes` back-reference.

summarize-delegates-to-network-summarize.text: On the SQLite path, all semantic and validation logic resides in `Network.summarize`; the API function is a pure wrapper.

summarize-dispatches-to-pg-when-pg-conni.text: A truthy `pg_conninfo` routes the call through `_pg_dispatch` and never touches the SQLite path.

summarize-lacks-over-validation.text: The function does not validate `over` node IDs, `summary_id` uniqueness, or emptiness of `text`.

summarize-metadata-is-bidirectional-and-.text: Summary nodes carry `metadata["summarizes"]` and covered nodes carry `metadata["summarized_by"]`; both survive `Storage.save`/`load`.

summarize-node-is-in-when-all-summarized.text: The summarize method creates a derived node that is IN when all summarized nodes are IN.

summarize-pg-conninfo-truthiness-selects.text: Any truthy `pg_conninfo` routes `summarize` through `_pg_dispatch` to `PgApi.summarize` and ignores `db_path`; falsy values including `""` use the SQLite path.

summarize-pg-path-does-not-touch-local-c.text: The PostgreSQL branch of `summarize` performs the mutation through `PgApi` and does not update the local SQLite `_network_cache`.

summarize-publishes-pubsub-events.text: The write context compares before/after truth values and calls `pubsub.publish` when subscribers are registered, even for a node creation.

summarize-registers-summary-as-dependent.text: `summarize(..., over=[...])` registers the summary node as a dependent of every covered node.

summarize-return-shape-is-backend-define.text: `summarize` returns whatever `Network.summarize` or `PgApi.summarize` returns and does not enforce the documented three-key return schema.

summarize-sqlite-write-bypasses-network-.text: On the SQLite path, `summarize` uses `_with_network(db_path, write=True)`, which bypasses `_network_cache` and loads a fresh `Storage` for the write.

summarize-uses-write-network-context.text: Uses `_with_network(db_path, write=True)`, so a successful call persists the network and bypasses the read-only cache.

summarize-validates-existence-and-unique.text: `Network.summarize()` raises `KeyError` if any ID in the `over` list does not exist in the network, and raises `ValueError` if the given summary ID is already in use — both are hard preconditions checked before any mutation.

summarize-validates-preconditions.text: `Network.summarize` raises `KeyError` on unknown covered ids and `ValueError` on duplicate summary ids.

summary-accepted-count-is-per-run.text: `summary.accepted` reports newly accepted beliefs for that run, not the cumulative store size; the cumulative size is `summary.total_beliefs` (201), which is unchanged across runs.

summary-accepted-count-is-per-run-not-cu.text: `summary.accepted` reports newly accepted beliefs for that run, while cumulative store size is reported separately as `summary.total_beliefs`.

summary-counts-mirror-step-counts.text: Every numeric field in `summary` (entries, proposed, accepted, total_beliefs) equals the corresponding value in `steps[].counts`, so the two blocks must be updated together.

summary-coverage-uses-metadata-summarize.text: compact identifies nodes covered by a summary through the metadata key "summarizes".

summary-has-single-sl-justification-over.text: A summary node's first justification is `type == "SL"` with antecedents exactly the `over` node set.

summary-metadata-is-bidirectional.text: A summary node has `metadata["summarizes"]` listing covered IDs, and each covered node has `metadata["summarized_by"]` containing the summary ID.

summary-mirrors-step-counts.text: `summary.entries`/`summary.proposed` equal the propose step's `counts.entries`/`counts.proposed`, and `summary.accepted`/`summary.total_beliefs` equal the accept step's `counts.accepted`/`counts.total_beliefs`.

summary-node-uses-sl-justification.text: A summary node is always given exactly one `SL` justification whose antecedents are the `over` set.

summary-truth-cascades-from-covered-node.text: Retracting any covered node flips the summary to `OUT`; asserting it back restores the summary to `IN`.

summary-truth-is-conjunctive-over-covere.text: A summary node's truth value is "IN" if and only if every node in its `over` list is "IN"; retracting any single covered node immediately flips the summary to "OUT", and re-asserting restores it to "IN".

summary-truth-value-tracks-covered-nodes.text: Retracting any covered node flips its summary `OUT`; re-asserting all covered nodes restores the summary `IN`.

supersede-acceptance-retracts-old-node.text: Accepting a supersede proposal sets the *old* node's `truth_value` to `OUT` while creating the new node (`test_accept_supersede`), unlike `what_if(action="supersede")` which previews without retraction.

supersede-is-reversible-via-outlist.text: Because `supersede` uses outlist entries rather than direct truth-value mutation, retracting the `new_id` restores the `old_id` through normal propagation.

supersede-produces-correct-text-hash.text: `api.supersede_with_text` creates a successor node whose `text_hash` is the SHA-256 of the new text and leaves the network integrity-clean.

supersede-requires-exactly-one-input.text: The `supersede` command requires exactly one of `new_id` or `--text`; supplying both or neither is an error.

supersession-is-reversible.text: `supersede()` adds the new node's ID to the old node's outlist rather than deleting the old node; retracting the new belief automatically restores the old one through normal propagation

supersession-is-reversible-and-view-cons.text: Supersession is both mechanically reversible (implemented via outlist, so retracting the superseder restores the original node's truth value) and view-consistent (superseded nodes are excluded from gated belief lists even if they retain active blockers), making it a first-class lifecycle operation rather than just a truth-value toggle.

justifications.label: Reversibility (mechanism) and view exclusion (presentation) together make supersession a well-integrated feature

supersession-overwrites-prior-retract-re.text: Marking an already-`OUT` node as superseded overwrites its previous retract reason with `"Superseded by <new-id>"`.

supported-closed-loop-preserves-all-inva.text: The supported revision-and-lifecycle maintenance loop sustains belief consistency and monitors supported beliefs through staleness checking and propagation, while the complete architecture preserves all system invariants through architecturally grounded enforcement (three-layer containment and atomic mutations); the loop is supported-maintaining and the architecture is invariant-preserving, without claiming a gapless no-escape path for every possible belief.

justifications.label: re-derive-round-3

supporting-justification-contains-list-i.text: `Node.supporting_justification` is an integer index into `Node.justifications`, not an ID or object reference, so the ordering of the `justifications` list is semantically meaningful.

supporting-justification-has-zero-observ.text: The search for `supporting_justification` returned no matches in code or tests.

supporting-justification-index-bounds-ch.text: Both `_format_node` and `_format_beliefs_for_prompt` in `build_wiki.py` guard the `supporting_justification` index with a `0 <= si < len(justifications)` check before dereferencing; out-of-range values fall through to rendering all antecedents rather than raising an `IndexError`.

supporting-justification-is-list-index.text: `Node.supporting_justification` is an integer index into `node.justifications`, not a `Justification` object.

supporting-justification-is-zero-based-l.text: `Node.supporting_justification` is an integer index into `node.justifications`, not a `Justification` object or ID.

supporting-justification-narrows-travers.text: When `supporting_justification` is a valid index, only that single justification's antecedents are traversed; otherwise all justifications are.

supporting-justification-selects-active-.text: When `supporting_justification` is set, truth evaluation considers only that justification; otherwise all justifications are considered.

supporting-justification-splits-active-a.text: When `supporting_justification` is a valid index, that justification’s antecedents are active and non-overlapping antecedents from other justifications are rendered as “other”.

surviving-premises-preserve-original-sl-.text: The `surviving_premises` list in a restoration hint preserves the original SL (antecedent) order minus the OUT premises, making list order semantically significant.

sustainable-growth-is-indefinitely-self-.text: The system's knowledge growth — combining exhaustive deterministic reasoning with LLM-driven derivation — is not merely sustainable but indefinitely so: resource-sustainable self-correction within a deterministically grounded lifecycle means the expanding knowledge base never outstrips the system's ability to maintain its own consistency, regardless of accumulated network size or elapsed time.

justifications.label: Sustainable growth+correction + indefinitely sustained lifecycle means growth capacity and maintenance capacity scale together without bound

sync-agent-adds-new-remote-beliefs.text: sync_agent adds new beliefs present in the remote file to the local database with correct metadata.

sync-agent-and-json-catch-no-internal-ex.text: `sync_agent` and `sync_agent_json` in `reasons/import_agent.py` do not catch exceptions from normalization or `_sync_claims`; those exceptions propagate to callers raw.

sync-agent-atomic-write-via-with-network.text: Because delegation occurs inside `with _with_network(db_path, write=True) as net`, any raised exception skips `store.save(net)` and leaves the SQLite DB unchanged.

sync-agent-auto-discovers-sibling-nogood.text: On markdown paths, if `nogoods_file` is falsy, the function looks for `beliefs_path.parent / "nogoods.md"` and uses it if present.

sync-agent-autodetects-markdown-and-json.text: `api.sync_agent` accepts both Markdown and JSON belief files and detects the source format automatically.

sync-agent-counts-justification-only-cha.text: `sync_agent` increments the `beliefs_updated` counter for justification-only changes, not only for text or truth-value changes.

sync-agent-defers-assertions-until-after.text: Sync collects OUT-to-IN transitions in `assert_after` and asserts them after `_fixup_dependents()` so dependencies are rebuilt first.

sync-agent-does-not-open-files.text: `sync_agent` in `reasons/import_agent.py:564` takes `beliefs_text` as a parameter and never opens files; file I/O is the responsibility of `reasons/api.py:sync_agent`.

sync-agent-empty-nogoods-string-triggers.text: Passing `nogoods_file=""` is falsy, so `sync_agent` silently activates sibling `nogoods.md` auto-discovery instead of treating it as an explicit empty value.

sync-agent-first-call-equals-import.text: Calling `sync_agent` for an agent with no prior import produces identical results to `import_agent`, including all node creation and namespace wiring

sync-agent-first-call-equivalent-to-impo.text: `sync_agent` on a brand-new agent (no prior `import_agent`) behaves identically to `import_agent` and returns `created_premise=True` in the result dict

sync-agent-first-run-behaves-as-initial-.text: Calling sync_agent for a never-imported agent behaves as an initial import.

sync-agent-first-sync-equals-import.text: When no prior import exists for an agent, `sync_agent` behaves identically to `import_agent` — creating the `agent:active` premise and returning `created_premise: True` — rather than requiring a separate import step.

sync-agent-has-no-input-validation.text: `reasons/import_agent.py:sync_agent` never validates `agent_name`, `network`, or `beliefs_text` before delegating to `_normalize_markdown` / `_sync_claims`.

sync-agent-idempotent.text: Two consecutive `sync_agent` calls with identical file content produce zero additions, removals, and updates on the second call

sync-agent-idempotent-on-identical-state.text: Two consecutive calls to `sync_agent` with identical remote content produce zero mutations (all counters return 0) on the second call

sync-agent-implements-remote-wins.text: When a belief exists locally but is retracted, `sync_agent` reasserts it to IN if the remote source declares it IN; a subsequent sync is idempotent.

sync-agent-is-belief-reconciliation-not-.text: `sync_agent` / `cmd_sync_agent` synchronize beliefs between agents and do not mirror `reasons/` into `reasons_lib/`.

sync-agent-is-belief-sync-not-code-sync.text: `reasons/api.py:2016` (`sync_agent`) and `reasons/cli.py:920` (`cmd_sync_agent`) implement synchronization of *beliefs between agents*, unrelated to mirroring the two Python packages.

sync-agent-is-idempotent.text: Calling `sync_agent` twice with identical data produces the same database state; the second call returns zero adds, removes, and updates — a no-op by design.

sync-agent-is-remote-wins.text: Duplicates existing belief `import-skips-existing-sync-is-remote-wins`, which already establishes that sync mode uses remote-wins semantics including overriding local retractions.

sync-agent-json-ignores-nogoods-file-par.text: When `beliefs_file` ends in `.json`, the `nogoods_file` argument is never read; nogoods are extracted from the JSON payload only.

sync-agent-json-path-uses-exact-lowercas.text: `sync_agent` selects the JSON branch only when `Path(beliefs_file).suffix == ".json"`; suffixes such as `.JSON` or `.json5` fall through to the markdown branch.

sync-agent-json-raises-attribute-error-o.text: `sync_agent_json` (reasons/import_agent.py:585) calls `_normalize_json`, which uses `data.get(...)` and will raise `AttributeError` if `data` is not a dict.

sync-agent-json-rejects-non-dict-payload.text: `sync_agent_json` delegates to `_normalize_json`, which calls `data.get(...)`; a `None` or list payload raises `AttributeError` rather than a friendly validation error.

sync-agent-must-preserve-agent-inactive-.text: `sync_agent`'s internal `assert_node` calls must not strip `test-agent:inactive` from any justification's outlist, or the agent-revocation cascade mechanism breaks

sync-agent-namespaces-beliefs-under-agen.text: `sync_agent` stores remote beliefs under namespaced IDs of the form `agent:id` (e.g., `test-agent:alpha-fact`).

sync-agent-nogoods-file-is-ignored-on-js.text: On the JSON path, `sync_agent` never consults the `nogoods_file` parameter; JSON nogoods are derived from the JSON data itself.

sync-agent-pg-path-forwards-normalized-i.text: The PostgreSQL branch of `sync_agent` normalizes markdown or JSON into `claims` and `nogoods` before dispatching to `PgApi.sync_agent`, while the SQLite branch forwards raw text or parsed JSON to `reasons.import_agent` functions.

sync-agent-preserves-agent-revocation-ca.text: Sync must leave `agent:inactive` in each justification's `outlist`; otherwise retracting `agent:active` will not cascade beliefs to OUT.

sync-agent-preserves-cascade-structure.text: After `sync_agent` completes, the agent's outlist-based justification structure remains intact — revoking `agent:active` still cascades all agent beliefs to OUT, proving sync does not corrupt kill-switch wiring.

sync-agent-preserves-infrastructure-node.text: `_sync_claims` excludes `agent:active` and `agent:inactive` from `removed_ids`, so sync never deletes infrastructure nodes.

sync-agent-registers-repo-directory.text: `sync_agent` records the agent's file directory in the repo registry, observable through `api.list_repos`.

sync-agent-requires-beliefs-file-exists-.text: `sync_agent` raises `FileNotFoundError` if `beliefs_file` does not exist before any database or backend sync work is attempted.

sync-agent-requires-existing-beliefs-fil.text: Raises `FileNotFoundError` before any network work if `beliefs_file` does not exist on disk.

sync-agent-resurrection-clears-retracted.text: When sync sees a previously OUT node become IN remotely, it clears `_retracted` metadata and calls `network.assert_node()` to resurrect the node.

sync-agent-retracts-remote-missing-belie.text: sync_agent retracts local beliefs that are missing from the remote file by setting them OUT.

sync-agent-returns-count-dict.text: `sync_agent` returns a dict with keys `beliefs_added`, `beliefs_removed`, `beliefs_updated`, and `beliefs_unchanged` for accurate accounting of what changed

sync-agent-rewires-changed-dependencies.text: sync_agent rewires justification antecedents when the remote file changes a belief's Depends on list.

sync-agent-rewires-dependency-antecedent.text: When a remote belief's `Depends on:` line changes, `sync_agent` rewires the corresponding justification antecedents to match.

sync-agent-source-path-existence-not-che.text: `source_path` in `reasons/import_agent.py` is only resolved and recorded into `network.repos`; its existence is not checked in that layer.

sync-agent-stale-remote-maps-to-out.text: Beliefs marked `[STALE]` in the remote markdown are synced as OUT nodes; `TestSyncNoChanges` expects `beliefs_retracted == 1` for `gamma-stale`.

sync-agent-truth-value-changes-cascade-t.text: When sync_agent changes a belief's truth value, the change cascades to dependent nodes.

sync-agent-updates-changed-description-t.text: sync_agent updates the local node description when the remote file changes a belief's text.

sync-agent-uses-remote-wins.text: `sync_agent` imports another agent's beliefs with remote-wins merge semantics.

sync-agent-uses-remote-wins-semantics.text: `_sync_claims` updates existing node fields, adds remote-only beliefs, and retracts local beliefs absent from the remote.

sync-claims-is-not-atomic.text: `_sync_claims` (reasons/import_agent.py:249) mutates `network.nodes`, `network.nogoods`, and `network.repos` in place with no try/except and no rollback.

sync-claims-mutates-network-in-place-wit.text: `_sync_claims` mutates `network.nodes`, `network.nogoods`, and `network.repos` in place without its own try/except, so an exception can leave the in-memory `Network` partially mutated.

sync-counters-distinguish-removed-from-r.text: `sync_agent` reports `beliefs_removed` for IN→OUT transitions caused by the sync and `beliefs_retracted` for nodes that end OUT during the pass, so retracted is not the same bucket as removed.

sync-idempotency-requires-counting-trans.text: `beliefs_removed` counts *transitions* IN→OUT during the sync pass; re-syncing an already-removed node yields `0`, not a repeat increment.

sync-is-idempotent-on-identical-source.text: A second sync against an unchanged source performs no adds, removals, or updates; previously removed nodes are not double-counted.

sync-is-remote-wins.text: `_sync_claims` implements remote-wins reconciliation: remote text/metadata overwrites local, beliefs removed from remote are retracted locally, and beliefs remotely IN but locally OUT are re-asserted

sync-is-safe-for-automated-reconciliatio.text: `sync_agent` can be safely re-run on any schedule — idempotent execution with cascade structure preservation means repeated automated synchronization never corrupts outlist-based justification hierarchies or produces accumulating side effects.

justifications.label: Idempotency plus cascade preservation together make sync safe for unattended periodic execution

sync-must-preserve-inactive-outlist.text: `sync_agent` and its Postgres twin both re-prepend `inactive_id` on every justification rewrite; losing it silently breaks the kill switch, which is why `TestSyncAgentRevocation` exists.

sync-on-fresh-agent-creates-active-premi.text: Calling `sync_agent` for an agent with no existing state works as an initial import and reports `created_premise: True`.

sync-preserves-agent-inactive-outlist.text: Sync/assert operations must preserve the agent's `:inactive` node in each justification's outlist so later retraction of `:active` still cascades beliefs OUT.

sync-preserves-cascade-wiring.text: After `sync_agent` runs, the `agent:inactive` outlist entries on beliefs are preserved, so retracting `agent:active` still cascades all agent beliefs to OUT

sync-registers-agent-repo-directory.text: After `sync_agent`, the source file's resolved parent directory is recorded under the agent in `api.list_repos()`.

sync-registers-agent-repo-path.text: `sync_agent` records the agent's source file path in the repo registry (`list_repos`), enabling the system to track which file each agent's beliefs originated from.

sync-registers-repo-directory-mapping.text: After any `sync_agent` call, `api.list_repos` reflects the agent mapped to the parent directory of the source file

sync-removal-is-retraction-not-deletion.text: Nodes removed from the remote source end up with `truth_value == "OUT"` and remain queryable via `show_node`.

sync-removes-absent-beliefs.text: `sync_agent` retracts to OUT any existing agent belief whose node ID is absent from the synced file.

sync-requires-remote-vs-local-format-det.text: The same `sync_agent` function handles both Markdown (`### name [TRUTH] TYPE`) and JSON (`{"nodes": ...}`) sources without a format argument.

sync-returns-structured-diff-counts.text: `sync_agent` returns a dict with `beliefs_added`, `beliefs_updated`, `beliefs_unchanged`, and `beliefs_removed` counts that accurately reflect the diff between remote file and local state — no double-counting across sync cycles.

sync-rewires-justification-antecedents.text: `sync_agent` updates a node's justification antecedents when its `Depends on:` list changes.

sync-supports-markdown-and-json.text: Duplicates existing belief `import-agent-normalizers-share-intermediate-schema`, which covers that both markdown and JSON formats flow through the same normalization pipeline for import/sync operations.

sync-supports-markdown-and-json-input.text: `sync_agent` supports both beliefs.md markdown and JSON input formats.

sync-tests-lack-error-path-coverage.text: The sync agent test suite contains no tests for malformed markdown, missing files, or conflicting agent names.

sync-truth-change-cascades-to-dependents.text: When `sync_agent` changes a node's truth value, BFS propagation cascades the change to dependent nodes.

sync-updates-belief-text.text: `sync_agent` updates the stored belief text when the corresponding file text changes.

system-achieves-tripartite-operational-a.text: The system achieves a complete operational profile across three independent assurance dimensions: externally controlled (bounded interfaces with defensive ingestion), internally self-correcting (contradiction resolution and staleness detection), and query-resilient (graceful degradation across all access paths) — ensuring no operational scenario is unaddressed.

justifications.label: External control, internal self-correction, and query resilience form a complete operational triad

system-artifacts-maintain-consistent-ide.text: Both automatically-generated dialectical structures (challenge nodes with deterministic auto-ID generation) and contradiction records (nogoods with unconditional recording) maintain consistent, referenceable identification schemes — system-generated artifacts are as addressable as user-created beliefs.

system-assurance-is-universal-and-multid.text: The system's operational assurance spans all dimensions — temporal completeness of self-correction, end-to-end reliability of read and write paths, and external control through bidirectional bounds and defensive ingestion — and holds universally across all architectural layers, storage backends, and adverse graph conditions including vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, and empty antecedents.

justifications.label: Multidimensional assurance covers the independent quality axes, while universal condition-independence eliminates environmental caveats — together they establish that the system's guarantees hold without qualification across all operational scenarios.

system-assurance-spans-correction-reliab.text: The system's operational assurance spans three independent dimensions: temporal completeness of self-correction (creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection), resource sustainability (bounded token budgets preventing exhaustion), and external controllability (bidirectional interface bounds with defensive ingestion) — no assurance gap exists along any axis.

system-autonomously-converges-and-self-c.text: The system autonomously reaches and maintains consistent states through two complementary mechanisms: passive convergence ensures every modification path (import, retraction, dedup) reaches a deterministic stable state, while active self-correction (contradiction resolution and staleness detection) ensures consistency is preserved over time — combining equilibrium-seeking with consistency-maintaining.

justifications.label: Passive convergence (depth-5) and active self-correction (depth-4) are complementary — together they ensure the system both reaches and sustains correct states

system-autonomously-converges-and-self-c.text: The system autonomously reaches stable states through passive convergence on every modification path and maintains consistency for supported cases through active self-correction: deterministic contradiction resolution plus staleness detection for tracked IN nodes with both source fields, reducing undetected inconsistencies without claiming exhaustive drift coverage.

system-boundaries-are-evolution-tolerant.text: The system handles boundary interactions safely along two independent dimensions: format and schema evolution is tolerated gracefully (derive parser fallbacks, forward-compatible metadata lines, SQLite schema migration via try/except), while reference validation prevents invalid IDs from crossing any boundary (import normalization drops unknown refs, nogoods skip missing nodes, LLM hallucination filtering discards phantom IDs)

justifications.label: Evolution tolerance ensures old formats/schemas don't break new code, while reference validation ensures new data doesn't corrupt existing networks — together they make all system boundaries both forward-compatible and integrity-preserving

system-boundaries-are-validating-and-evo.text: All system boundaries simultaneously enforce strict input validation (typed exceptions, referential integrity checks, hallucination filtering) and tolerate evolution gracefully (dual format parsers, forward-compatible metadata, schema-tolerant loading) — boundaries are both strict about current invariants and adaptive to future changes.

justifications.label: Comprehensive validation (depth-2) and evolution tolerance (depth-1) are opposing concerns unified at system boundaries — strictness for correctness coexists with flexibility for evolution

system-boundary-enforcement-spans-valida.text: All system boundaries simultaneously enforce three independent properties: strict input validation through typed exceptions and referential integrity checks that reject malformed or dangling references, forward-compatible resilience that tolerates format and schema evolution without requiring coordinated upgrades, and resource governance through accurate bidirectional token budgets with transitive subset-gated access control — boundaries serve as gates for correctness, adapters for evolution, and constraints on resource consumption.

system-converges-from-addition-and-remov.text: The system reaches deterministic stable states from both directions: import reconciliation converges through fixpoint iteration and dual reconciliation modes when beliefs are added, while retraction cascades terminate through BFS with stop-on-unchanged when beliefs are removed — bidirectional convergence guarantees that no sequence of additions or removals leaves the network in an oscillating or indeterminate state.

justifications.label: Addition-side convergence (depth-3) and removal-side convergence (depth-3) together close all instability vectors — the network reaches quiescence regardless of operation direction.

system-efficiency-spans-packaging-and-ru.text: Resource efficiency is enforced at every system phase: zero external dependencies with lazy loading minimize the static footprint at packaging and startup, while O(1) per-line budget tracking with chars/4 token estimation minimize computational overhead during runtime belief distillation.

justifications.label: Packaging-level efficiency (zero deps, lazy imports) and runtime efficiency (O(1) tracking, approximate estimation) together show resource minimality is pervasive.

system-guarantees-are-universal-and-perm.text: The system's ultimate properties are both permanent (maintained indefinitely without temporal degradation) and universal (extending fully to all beliefs regardless of origin) — no belief can escape the system's guarantees along either the time or scope dimension.

justifications.label: Depth-14 apex — the two independent depth-13 conclusions close off both escape dimensions (temporal and provenance), yielding a single universal-permanence guarantee

system-guarantees-are-universal-permanen.text: The system's ultimate guarantees are simultaneously universal (extending fully to all belief types including externally-integrated ones), permanent (maintained indefinitely without temporal degradation), and independently verifiable (origin-agnostic observability enables external audit without requiring trust in the system's internal state).

justifications.label: Universality and permanence from the system-properties branch combined with independent verifiability from the origin-agnostic observability branch yield the three ultimate meta-properties (depth-15)

system-history-is-consistently-reference.text: Every event in the system's operational history follows a deterministic path with complete traceability AND produces consistently-identifiable artifacts (auto-generated challenge IDs, unconditionally-recorded nogoods), making the complete history both causally traceable and individually referenceable by stable identifiers.

justifications.label: Deterministic traceable history plus consistent artifact identification enables stable reference to any historical system event (depth-7)

system-is-externally-controlled-and-inte.text: The system achieves dual-layer assurance: external interfaces are fully controlled through bidirectional token bounds and defensive belief ingestion, while internal consistency is actively maintained through contradiction resolution at derivation time and staleness detection at maintenance time.

system-is-minimal-sound-and-scalable.text: The entire system — from single-node truth semantics through multi-agent operation — achieves semantic minimality (all features derive from uniform primitives), operational soundness (deterministic reversible truth maintenance), and safe scalability (isolated multi-agent operation) simultaneously.

system-is-resource-efficient-self-sustai.text: The system achieves a self-reinforcing triad: resource efficiency reinforces self-sustainability (preventing exhaustion of the minimality-generated maintenance loop), self-sustainability maintains indefinite auditability (the audit trail never degrades because the maintenance loop that produces it is self-maintaining), and auditability remains resource-efficient (the overhead of permanent traceability does not threaten sustainability) — forming a closed positive-feedback cycle.

system-is-self-correcting-and-exception-.text: The system is both actively self-correcting (maintaining consistency through the derive pipeline for new beliefs and staleness detection for existing ones) and passively exception-proof (handling contradictions through deterministic backtracking and challenges through reliable dialectical transformation) — providing comprehensive fault tolerance that covers both anticipated maintenance and unanticipated disruptions.

system-is-self-correcting-for-supported-.text: The system is actively self-correcting for supported cases—maintaining consistency through the derive pipeline for new beliefs and staleness detection for tracked IN nodes with both source fields—and passively exception-proof through deterministic backtracking for contradictions and reliable dialectical transformation for challenges, providing fault tolerance without claiming exhaustive drift coverage.

system-is-self-sustaining-and-invariant-.text: The fully characterized self-maintaining loop not only sustains its own operation through minimality's fixed-point property but also comprehensively preserves all system invariants through both temporal coverage (revision loops) and structural coverage (architectural grounding).

justifications.label: The depth-10 self-maintaining loop subsumes comprehensive invariant preservation as a new depth-11 apex

system-is-self-sustaining-auditable-and-.text: The system simultaneously achieves three ultimate properties: self-sustainability through minimality's fixed-point, comprehensive invariant preservation, and complete operational auditability for every maintenance action — a single closed architecture that maintains itself, preserves all guarantees, and traces every action.

system-is-unified-minimal-dialectical-an.text: The entire system — minimal primitives, sound multi-agent scaling, and complete dialectical revision — forms a unified design where every feature derives from the same core outlist/disjunction semantics with deterministic, reversible behavior.

system-output-is-complete-bounded-and-ci.text: The system's two primary output mechanisms — compact belief summaries and staleness reports — both meet production standards: structurally complete with priority ordering, predictably bounded by token budgets, and CI-pipeline ready with deterministic sorted output, nonzero exit codes, and machine-parseable schemas.

system-output-is-comprehensively-governe.text: All system output is simultaneously normalized (uniform fail-safe schemas with deterministic structure), authorized (access-tag subset gating with transitive inheritance), and resource-constrained (accurate token budgets enforced bidirectionally) — achieving comprehensive output governance across all independent quality dimensions.

system-properties-are-indefinitely-maint.text: The system's three ultimate properties — self-sustainability, comprehensive auditability, and complete invariant preservation — extend beyond external beliefs to unlimited temporal scope: resource-sustainable self-correction within a deterministic lifecycle ensures these properties hold not just now but indefinitely, provided propagation correctness is maintained.

system-properties-emerge-from-unified-de.text: All four primary system properties — integrity, scalability, extensibility, and robustness — emerge from a single unified architectural design rather than requiring independent engineering effort; integrity and scalability are complementary consequences of unified internal/external integrity with sound multi-agent scaling, while extensibility and robustness are jointly yielded by minimality, and the design that produces both pairs is the same.

system-properties-extend-fully-to-extern.text: The system's three ultimate properties — self-sustainability through minimality's fixed-point, comprehensive auditability through fully-characterized maintenance, and complete invariant preservation — extend fully to externally-sourced beliefs through self-sustaining invariant preservation that dynamically encompasses external beliefs as first-class participants.

system-reaches-equilibrium-from-all-modi.text: The system converges to deterministic stable states through every modification path: import achieves ordered convergent reconciliation (add → propagate → retract sequencing with fixpoint convergence), retraction cascades terminate through BFS with stop-on-unchanged, and both addition and removal operations reach equilibrium — no modification can leave the system in a non-convergent state.

system-reliability-spans-internal-and-ex.text: The system is reliable along both internal and external dimensions: internally, both read paths (comprehensive staleness detection) and write paths (crash-free propagation) are reliable; externally, interfaces are bidirectionally bounded with budget-constrained output and comprehensive staleness-gated input.
