verify-belief-missing-target-propagates-.text: A missing target node in `verify_belief` raises `KeyError` from `show_node`, while missing premise nodes during trace are caught and recorded as `UNKNOWN` placeholders.

verify-belief-pg-mode-skips-verified-at-.text: When `pg_conninfo` is set, `verify_belief` skips `verified_at` and `updated_at` stamping for confirmed beliefs entirely.

verify-belief-raises-keyerror-for-unknow.text: `api.verify_belief("nonexistent-id")` raises `KeyError` (not a dict return or silent skip) when the node does not exist in the database

verify-belief-requires-verify-module.text: `verify_belief` depends on `.verify`'s `read_source` and `verify_beliefs` and will raise at call time if either is missing.

verify-belief-retraction-failures-are-co.text: `verify_belief` catches exceptions from `retract_node` for stale beliefs and reports their IDs in `retract_failed` instead of raising.

verify-belief-stamping-failure-marks-all.text: If the SQLite stamping block raises while setting `verified_at`/`updated_at`, `verify_belief` sets `stamp_failed` to the entire `verified` list.

verify-belief-unknown-verdict-is-inconcl.text: `verify_belief` treats a missing or unknown verdict from `verify_beliefs` as `INCONCLUSIVE` and silently takes no action on that belief.

verify-beliefs-leaves-read-source-to-cal.text: `verify_beliefs` accepts pre-read source content; it never calls `read_source` itself, so callers control disk I/O.

verify-beliefs-never-reads-files.text: `verify_beliefs()` does not call `read_source()` or touch the filesystem; the caller (e.g., `api.py`) must resolve and read source files and pass the content as the second element of each `(belief_dict, source_content_or_None)` tuple.

verify-beliefs-returns-empty-dict-on-par.text: `verify_beliefs` (via `parse_verify_response`) returns `{}` rather than raising when the model output is empty or not valid JSON.

verify-beliefs-single-llm-call-no-batchi.text: `verify_beliefs()` sends all beliefs in exactly one `invoke_model` call regardless of count; there is no internal batching, chunking, retry, or fallback model — the only safeguard against prompt overflow is the 30,000-character per-source truncation cap.

verify-confirmed-stamps-verified-at.text: A CONFIRMED verdict from the LLM causes `api.verify_belief` to set a non-null `verified_at` timestamp on the node record in the database

verify-dependents-assumes-set-valued-dep.text: The implementation requires `Node.dependents` to support set subtraction with another set.

verify-dependents-ignores-missing-node-r.text: Justification references to IDs not present in `self.nodes` are silently skipped during expected-index construction.

verify-dependents-is-pure-observer.text: `verify_dependents` is a read-only auditor that re-derives expected dependents from justifications and diffs against stored values, returning a list of error strings without ever mutating `nodes[*].dependents`.

verify-dependents-is-read-only.text: `Network.verify_dependents()` never modifies the dependents index; it returns a list of human-readable error strings without side effects

verify-dependents-is-read-only-audit.text: `verify_dependents()` returns error strings for stale or missing dependents without mutating network state.

verify-dependents-is-readonly.text: `verify_dependents()` never modifies `node.dependents`; it only reads and reports discrepancies as a list of human-readable strings containing `"extra"` or `"missing"`.

verify-dependents-reads-only.text: `verify_dependents` does not mutate the network, nodes, dependents sets, or audit log.

verify-dependents-reports-extra-and-miss.text: `verify_dependents` returns human-readable strings naming both extra and missing dependents per node, rather than raising on inconsistency.

verify-dependents-requires-set-like-depe.text: `verify_dependents` requires each `Node.dependents` to support set subtraction with a set; otherwise it can raise `TypeError`.

verify-dependents-returns-errors-not-exc.text: Extra or missing dependents are reported in the returned list rather than raised as exceptions.

verify-dependents-skips-missing-node-ref.text: `verify_dependents` silently skips antecedent/outlist IDs absent from `self.nodes` when constructing the expected reverse index.

verify-dry-run-performs-no-llm-call-and-.text: `dry_run=True` in `api.verify_belief` short-circuits before any LLM invocation and returns an empty `results` dict with `dry_run=True`, making the call fully read-only

verify-dry-run-skips-llm.text: With `dry_run=True`, `api.verify_belief` returns `results == {}` without mocking or invoking the LLM.

verify-justification-ignores-missing-ant.text: Antecedent IDs not present in `net.nodes` are silently excluded from the recomputed justification hash.

verify-justification-mutates-only-suppli.text: `verify_justification` may populate a supplied cache but does not mutate the node, justification, or network.

verify-justification-mutates-supplied-ca.text: When `cache` is passed, recursive Merkle hashes may be inserted into it, though node and justification objects are not modified.

verify-justification-none-is-ambiguous.text: `verify_justification` returns `None` for clean verification, missing `content_hash`, or invalid `j_index`, so callers must check the stored hash or index separately to disambiguate.

verify-justification-recomputes-from-cur.text: `verify_justification` compares the stored hash against a fresh hash built from current node text and recursively fresh antecedent hashes, not stored `text_hash` values.

verify-justification-returns-chain-mutat.text: A mismatch between stored and recomputed hashes returns a dict with type `"chain_mutation"`, node ID, justification index, and both hashes.

verify-justification-returns-none-for-mi.text: A falsy `content_hash` causes `verify_justification` to return `None` before any recomputation.

verify-justification-returns-none-withou.text: A falsy `content_hash` causes an immediate `None` return before any recomputation.

verify-justification-silently-skips-miss.text: Antecedent IDs not present in `net.nodes` are silently excluded from the recomputed justification hash.

verify-justification-trusts-supplied-cac.text: If a cache is supplied, `verify_justification` trusts it without validation; stale entries can produce an incorrect verification result.

verify-justification-uses-current-text.text: The recomputed hash is based on `compute_text_hash(node.text)` and fresh recursive hashes, not stored `text_hash` values.

verify-llm-call-exceptions-propagate.text: The "no-raise" guarantee in `reasons/verify.py` applies to file-reading and response-parsing paths only; exceptions from `invoke_model` (network timeout, auth error) propagate uncaught to the caller, so `api.py` must handle LLM-call failures.

verify-missing-node-raises-keyerror.text: `api.verify_belief` raises `KeyError` when given an unknown node ID.

verify-module-implements-justification-v.text: `reasons/verify.py` contains the predicate that decides whether SL/CP/outlist justifications are satisfiable.

verify-parse-drops-malformed-entries.text: `parse_verify_response()` silently discards individual JSON entries that lack a string `"verdict"` key (or where `verdict` is not a string) rather than failing the entire batch; only structurally valid entries appear in the returned dict, and verdicts are normalized to uppercase.

verify-parser-greedy-brace-regex.text: `parse_verify_response` extracts JSON using a greedy `r"\{.*\}"` `DOTALL` regex, so extra braces after the JSON object can make parsing fail and return `{}`.

verify-prompt-forces-verbatim-quote.text: `VERIFY_PROMPT` explicitly instructs the model to copy the quote verbatim and to mark `INCONCLUSIVE` when source is missing, but the code does not verify the quote against the source.

verify-prompt-fragment-includes-source-o.text: `format_belief_for_verify` includes the node header, claim, source path/URL, and source content in the prompt fragment, and uses `(source not available)` when no source content exists.

verify-py-does-not-prevent-cycle-recursi.text: `reasons/verify.py` contains no antecedent traversal, visited set, or recursion guard; cycle prevention must occur in a caller such as `reasons/api.py:verify_belief`.

verify-py-is-source-verification-not-rms.text: `reasons/verify.py` implements LLM source verification with verdicts like CONFIRMED/STALE/PARTIAL/INCONCLUSIVE, not the RMS IN/OUT evaluator.
`reasons/verify.py` implements LLM source checks with `CONFIRMED`/`STALE`/`PARTIAL`/`INCONCLUSIVE` and has no gathered `justification`, `antecedent`, or `IN`/`OUT` matches.

verify-quote-not-validated-against-sourc.text: The verification prompt requests a verbatim quote, but no post-hoc substring check validates the returned quote against the source text.

verify-read-source-resolves-relative-to-.text: `read_source()` derives the resolution directory from the database file's parent path (`Path(db_path).parent`) and passes it as `db_dir` to `resolve_source_path`, so source paths are resolved relative to the database's location, not the current working directory.
`read_source` delegates to `check_stale.resolve_source_path` with the directory containing the database as the base for relative source paths.

verify-read-source-returns-none-for-miss.text: `read_source` returns `None` for an empty source string or a missing file instead of raising.

verify-read-source-truncates-large-files.text: `read_source` truncates large source files and includes the marker `[... truncated ...]`, keeping returned content under roughly 35k characters in the tested case.

verify-retract-sets-out.text: `retract=True` combined with a `STALE` verdict sets the node's `truth_value` to `"OUT"`.

verify-retract-sets-truth-value-out.text: In `tests/test_verify.py`, `test_retract_stale` asserts that `api.verify_belief(..., retract=True)` sets a `STALE` node’s `truth_value` to `"OUT"`.

verify-retract-stale-sets-out.text: With `retract=True`, a `STALE` verification verdict changes the node's `truth_value` to `OUT`.

verify-stamps-verified-at.text: Any successful `verify_belief` verification updates the node's `verified_at` timestamp.

verify-success-stamps-verified-at.text: Any successful `api.verify_belief` call populates the node's `verified_at` field.

verify-trace-checks-premises-not-derived.text: With `trace=True`, a derived node's `beliefs_checked` contains its premises (e.g. `p-a, p-b`), not the derived node itself.

verify-trace-redirects-derived-beliefs-t.text: When `trace=True` and the target node is derived (has an `sl` field), `api.verify_belief` verifies the premise nodes listed in `sl` rather than the derived node itself, and sets `is_derived=True` in the result

verify-verdicts-uppercased-not-validated.text: `parse_verify_response` uppercases verdict strings but does not validate them against `CONFIRMED`/`STALE`/`PARTIAL`/`INCONCLUSIVE`; an unknown verdict like `"MAYBE"` is passed through.

version-0-1-0-shipped-complete-tms.text: Version 0.1.0 shipped with SL justifications, retraction cascades, nogood detection, dialectical argumentation, SQLite persistence, and a multi-command CLI.

version-0-11-0-is-missing-from-changelog.text: The CHANGELOG.md sequence jumps from 0.10.0 to 0.12.0 with no 0.11.0 entry.

version-0-18-0-introduces-access-tags.text: Version 0.18.0, dated 2026-04-25, introduced RBAC-style access tags for provenance-based filtering.

version-is-manual.text: The version is statically declared in `pyproject.toml` with no dynamic version plugin, `__version__` import, or SCM-based versioning — it must be bumped manually.

version-is-static.text: Package version `0.58.0` is a static string with no `dynamic` source, so it must be bumped manually in this file for every release.

version-is-static-in-pyproject.text: The project version is statically declared in `[project]` with no dynamic version or `attr` lookup, so release bumps edit `pyproject.toml`.

version-lookup-requires-ftl-reasons-dist.text: `importlib.metadata.version("ftl-reasons")` succeeds only when a distribution named `ftl-reasons` is installed.

version-source-is-pyproject-not-dunder-v.text: No `__version__` assignment was found, so the observed version declaration is `[project].version` in `pyproject.toml`.

versions-0-15-0-through-0-17-0-share-dat.text: Versions 0.15.0, 0.16.0, and 0.17.0 all have the release date 2026-04-18.

versions-0-8-0-and-0-9-0-are-folded-into.text: Their features appear as bullets annotated `(0.8.0)` and `(0.9.0)` inside the `[0.10.0]` `Added` section rather than as standalone headings.

vertex-location-defaults-to-us-east5.text: `_invoke_api` uses `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION` for Vertex location and falls back to `"us-east5"` when it is unset.

vertex-prefix-requires-google-cloud-proj.text: `vertex:` models raise `RuntimeError` when `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is unset or empty.

visibility-check-has-no-side-effects.text: `_is_visible` only reads `node.metadata` and returns a bool; it performs no mutation, I/O, or logging.

visibility-is-subset-check.text: `_is_visible` requires ALL of a node's `access_tags` to be present in the caller's `visible_to` list (subset check, not intersection); nodes with no tags are always visible.

visibility-skipped-when-no-access-tags.text: `_is_visible` returns `True` for nodes without `access_tags` regardless of `visible_to`, so `visible_to=[]` blocks only tagged nodes.

visible-to-is-optional-filter.text: `_parse_visible_to` returns `None` when `--visible-to` is absent, which the API interprets as "no access restriction"; it never defaults to an empty list.

visible-to-is-per-subcommand-option.text: `--visible-to` is registered on individual CLI subcommands rather than as a single global CLI option.

visible-to-is-subset-check.text: A node with `access_tags` is visible only when every tag is present in `visible_to`; untagged nodes are always visible.

visible-to-none-disables-access-filterin.text: When `visible_to` is omitted or `None`, no access filter is applied and all nodes are returned; there is no deny-all default.

visible-to-none-disables-filtering.text: Every `_is_visible` call site is guarded so `visible_to=None` bypasses the check entirely; `None` means "no ACL" rather than "empty tag list."

visible-to-none-disables-rbac-filtering.text: Passing `visible_to=None` is the default and disables access-tag filtering for read APIs.

visible-to-none-not-supported-with-tags.text: `_is_visible` raises `TypeError` if `visible_to=None` and the node has non-empty tags; callers must guard `visible_to is not None`.

visible-to-requires-subset-tags.text: A node is clustered only if all of its `access_tags` are in `visible_to`, matching `_is_visible`'s subset rule

visible-to-subset-semantics.text: A tagged node is visible only when all of its tags are contained in `visible_to`; untagged nodes are always visible and omitting `visible_to` disables filtering.

visible-to-superset-semantics.text: A node with `access_tags: ["finance", "hr"]` is only visible to callers whose `visible_to` list contains both tags (superset/subset check, not intersection).

warn-multi-premise-called-only-after-suc.text: Its only call sites are `cmd_add` and `cmd_add_justification`, both after a successful API add call and after the success message is printed.

warn-multi-premise-none-premise-count-ra.text: Passing `None` as `premise_count` raises a `TypeError` from `premise_count >= 3` that the surrounding `ValueError`/`KeyError` handlers do not catch.

warn-multi-premise-prints-two-stdout-lin.text: The helper writes exactly two indented tip lines to stdout via `print`, never to stderr.

warn-multi-premise-tip-requires-three-pr.text: `_warn_multi_premise` prints its tip only when `premise_count >= 3` and `any_mode` is falsy.

warning-log-contract-action-target-value.text: Dangling-dependent warnings in `net.log` have `action="warn"`, a `target` field with the ghost node ID, and a `value` string containing both `"dangling"` and the parent node ID.

warning-log-schema-stable.text: Dangling-dependent warnings use the dict schema `{action: "warn", target: <ghost_id>, value: <str containing "dangling" and parent_id>, timestamp: <str>}` and tests enforce all four fields.

warning-value-identifies-parent-and-dang.text: Warning text contains both `"dangling"` and the parent node ID whose `dependents` set held the bad reference.

what-if-api-functions-use-deepcopy.text: `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, and `what_if_supersede` each deep-copy `net` before simulation at `reasons/api.py:542`, `:609`, and `:677`.

what-if-functions-never-persist.text: The `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` API functions are read-only simulations that load the network, apply the operation in memory, and pass `write=False` to `_with_network`, so no changes are persisted to the database.

what-if-is-read-only-never-persists.text: The `what_if()` MCP tool computes the full retraction/assertion cascade in memory but never writes to the database — subsequent `show_node` calls reflect the original unmodified state.

what-if-methods-do-not-mutate.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` return predictions but leave `get_status()`/`show_node()` unchanged, which the suite verifies explicitly in `test_what_if_retract_no_mutation` and `test_what_if_assert_no_mutation`.

what-if-operations-mutate-cache-copy.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` operate on a copy of the cached `Network` object, so their hypothetical mutations never corrupt the shared cache; the cached original retains its pre-hypothetical truth values.

what-if-operations-mutate-copies.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` operate on a copy of the network and never mutate `_network_cache[db][1]`.

what-if-operations-never-save.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` load the network, perform the operation in memory, diff truth values, and never save to SQLite.

what-if-retract-already-out-short-circui.text: If the target node is already `OUT`, `what_if_retract` returns a dict with `already_out=True`, empty `retracted` and `restored` lists, and `total_affected=0` without running cascade simulation.

what-if-retract-distinguishes-restored-f.text: A node in `changed` is classified as `restored` when it went `OUT → IN` (outlist-gate removal), which is distinct from the more common `IN → OUT` cascade.

what-if-retract-does-not-update-retracti.text: The simulated retraction only flips `truth_value` to `OUT`; it does not update metadata, timestamps, or `retracted_at`.

what-if-retract-excludes-source-from-tot.text: `what_if_retract` computes `total_affected` as `len(retracted) + len(restored)`, excluding the node being retracted itself.

what-if-retract-excludes-source-node.text: The retracted node itself is not in the `retracted` list; `changed` comes from `_propagate`, which seeds `node_id` into `visited` and only reports dependents.

what-if-retract-excludes-target-from-cas.text: The target `node_id` is never included in the returned `retracted` or `restored` lists, and `total_affected` excludes it.

what-if-retract-excludes-target-node.text: The node being retracted is filtered out of both `retracted` and `restored` (`if nid == node_id: continue`), so `total_affected` counts only cascaded changes, never the target itself.

what-if-retract-is-a-thin-wrapper-around.text: Nearly all TMS semantics (cascade, outlist gating, restoration) live in `Network.retract`; `what_if_retract` only adds preconditions, copy-isolation, categorization, depth annotation, and sorting.

what-if-retract-is-non-mutating.text: `what_if_retract` returns cascade effects without modifying the database (docstring at `reasons/api.py:517`).

what-if-retract-is-read-only.text: `what_if_retract` loads a read-only network, applies `net.retract` in memory, and never mutates the database.

what-if-retract-never-commits.text: The function always calls `self.conn.rollback()` in a `finally`, so no state from a `what_if_retract` call persists, even on success.

what-if-retract-pg-result-passthrough.text: When `pg_conninfo` is set, `what_if_retract` dispatches to `PgApi.what_if_retract` and returns its result verbatim without normalizing or validating the dict shape.

what-if-retract-preserves-cache-integrit.text: `what_if_retract` deep-copies the loaded `Network` before calling `retract`, which is necessary because `_with_network.__exit__` writes `self.network` (the original object) back into `_network_cache` regardless of mutations.

what-if-retract-raises-keyerror.text: Unknown `node_id` raises `KeyError` rather than returning an error dict, unlike some other API methods.

what-if-retract-raises-keyerror-for-miss.text: If `node_id` is not found in the domain, `what_if_retract` raises `KeyError` rather than returning an error dict.

what-if-retract-requires-autocommit-fals.text: If a caller supplies a psycopg connection with `autocommit=True`, the final `rollback()` is ineffective and the simulation's `UPDATE`s persist.

what-if-retract-returns-already-out-shor.text: If the target node is already `OUT`, `what_if_retract` returns `already_out=True` with empty `retracted`/`restored` lists and `total_affected=0`.

what-if-retract-rollback-discards-pendin.text: The `finally` rollback also discards any caller work that was uncommitted on the same connection prior to this call.

what-if-retract-short-circuits-on-out-no.text: Retracting an already-OUT node returns immediately with `already_out: True` and empty lists, and does not invoke `net.retract` at all.

what-if-retract-sorts-by-depth-then-id.text: `retracted` and `restored` are sorted with `key=(depth, id)` before returning.

what-if-retract-sorts-results-by-depth-t.text: `what_if_retract` sorts both `retracted` and `restored` results by `(depth, id)`.

what-if-retract-unknown-node-raises-keye.text: `what_if_retract` raises `KeyError` when `node_id` is absent from the network, including for an empty string.

what-if-rollbacks-are-unconditional.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` both call `self.conn.rollback()` in a `finally`, so they can never persist a state change.

what-if-simulations-are-read-only-and-re.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` run the requested operation in memory without `write=True` and use `_cascade_depth()` BFS to report each affected node's distance from the trigger without persisting changes.

what-if-simulations-deep-copy-network.text: `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, and `what_if_supersede` each call `copy.deepcopy(net)` before mutating, preserving the cached `Network` object for subsequent readers.

what-if-simulations-never-persist.text: `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, and `what_if_supersede` open `_with_network(..., write=False)` and operate on a `copy.deepcopy` of the network, so the cached `Network` and the database are both left unmodified regardless of outcome.

what-if-simulations-use-deepcopy.text: The SQLite-path `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, and `what_if_supersede` functions operate on a `copy.deepcopy(net)` and never write to disk, returning predicted truth-value effects without mutating the cached or persisted network.

what-if-x-implements-simulation-via-sepa.text: `api.what_if_retract`, `api.what_if_assert`, and `api.what_if_supersede` (in `reasons/api.py`) implement non-mutating preview via `_with_network(db_path, write=False)` and `copy.deepcopy`, not via a `dry_run` kwarg.

wiki-authentication-is-independent-of-bu.text: The authentication question for eem-wiki is independent of the build process because the output is static HTML.

wiki-llm-failure-silent-fallback-to-dete.text: If LLM page generation fails in `build_wiki` (timeout, model error, bad response), the affected topic group silently falls back to the deterministic per-node markdown rendering; no exception propagates to the caller and the page is still produced.

wildcard-reexport-drops-all-attribute.text: `reasons_lib.mcp_server` has no `__all__` attribute even if `reasons.mcp_server` declares one.

wildcard-reexport-omits-underscore-names.text: Names beginning with `_` in `reasons/mcp_server.py` are not accessible via `reasons_lib.mcp_server`.

wildcard-shims-are-unfiltered.text: The repo has 33 wildcard imports and zero `__all__` declarations, so each `reasons_lib/*.py` wildcard shim re-exports all non-underscore names from its target module.

with-default-none-params-are-not-require.text: Any parameter with a `None` default (e.g., `belief_ids`, `node_ids` on APIs, `visible_to` throughout `reasons/api.py`) is optional in the MCP schema; parameters without a default (e.g., `nogood(node_ids: list[str])`) are required.

with-network-cache-keyed-by-db-path-and-.text: Read-only calls reuse `_network_cache[db_path]` only when `os.path.getmtime(db_path)` matches the cached mtime; `write=True` ignores the cache.

with-network-cache-stale-race.text: On read-only exit, if another process changes the DB mtime between `__init__` and `__exit__`, the stale in-memory `Network` is cached under the new mtime, causing future stale cache hits.

with-network-ctx-init-runs-eagerly.text: `_with_network` returns a `_Ctx` instance, so DB open/load runs eagerly at factory-call time before the `with` block, and load errors propagate from the factory call.

with-network-exit-is-missing.text: The `_with_network` implementation needed to prove `after` snapshot and publish ordering is absent from the observations.

with-network-external-writes-require-cac.text: Out-of-band raw SQLite writes such as `add_tags`, `add_source`, and `import_json` must call `clear_network_cache(db_path)` or bump mtime, because `_with_network`'s mtime cache will otherwise serve stale `Network` objects.

with-network-is-only-publish-site.text: The sole call sites of `pubsub.publish`/`pubsub.compute_changes` are inside `_with_network.__exit__` (reasons/api.py), which is entered only when `pg_conninfo` is falsy.

with-network-is-sole-db-lifecycle-manage.text: Every API function accesses the SQLite database exclusively through `_with_network(db_path, write=False)` — a context manager that loads a Network from Storage, yields it, and saves only on clean exit when `write=True`. No API function manages Storage directly.

with-network-pubsub-subscribers-sampled-.text: Pubsub delta publishing occurs only for `write=True` when `pubsub.has_subscribers(db_path)` was true at `__enter__`; subscribers added after `__enter__` do not trigger an event.

with-network-save-failure-leaks-connecti.text: In `__exit__`, `store.close()` is not in a `try/finally`, so an exception from `store.save()` or `pubsub.publish()` can leak the SQLite connection.

with-network-skips-save-on-exception.text: _with_network saves the network only when write=True and no exception occurred in the context body.

with-network-write-atomicity-and-pubsub.text: The `_with_network` context manager in `api.py` saves the network, publishes pubsub events, and updates the in-memory cache only on a successful write-path exit; if an exception occurs, none of these side effects execute and the prior cache entry is preserved.

with-network-write-mode-always-loads-fre.text: `write=True` always opens `Storage` and loads a fresh `Network`, then saves on successful exit; it never operates on the cached `Network`.

workflow-not-locked-to-resolved-dependen.text: The test command omits `--frozen`/`--locked`, so dependencies are re-resolved at run time rather than pinned by a committed lockfile.

workflow-provides-no-service-containers.text: The job defines no `services:` or `env:` blocks, so tests requiring Postgres, Pub/Sub, HF, or network access must self-skip to keep CI green.

workflow-requires-test-extra-for-pytest.text: pytest is installed solely through `uv run --extra test`, so removing pytest from the `test` extra in `pyproject.toml` breaks CI before any test executes.

workflow-triggers-only-on-main.text: The workflow runs on `push` and `pull_request` events filtered to the `main` branch, and has no `workflow_dispatch` or tag triggers.

workflows-directory-has-no-siblings.text: The `workflows/` directory contains no sibling files or subdirectories in the provided tree.

would-resolve-is-heuristic.text: A premise appearing in `would_resolve` for a nogood node only means the premise is transitively in that node's assumption set; it does not guarantee retraction will flip the node to `OUT`.

write-context-bypasses-cache.text: `_with_network(db, write=True)` always yields a freshly loaded `Network` distinct from any cached one, proven by `net1 is not net2`.

write-context-suppressed-on-exception.text: `_with_network.__exit__` saves and publishes only when `write=True` and `exc_type is None`; on write exceptions it neither saves the network nor refreshes `_network_cache`, preserving on-disk/cache agreement.

write-contradiction-plan-defaults-all-en.text: Every contradiction is emitted with an `[APPLY]` marker; exclusion requires human editing to `[SKIP]` or deleting the block.

write-contradiction-plan-does-not-create.text: It opens the file directly with `open(path, mode)` and never calls `mkdir`, so a missing parent directory raises `FileNotFoundError`.

write-contradiction-plan-lazy-imported.text: `write_contradiction_plan` is imported inside `_flush_results` rather than at module top to break the circular dependency with `reasons/api.py`.

write-contradiction-plan-produces-parsea.text: The markdown it emits is designed so that `parse_contradiction_plan(Path(output_path).read_text())` reproduces the original `id`/`claims` pairs for every block left as `[APPLY]`.

write-contradiction-plan-requires-non-wh.text: Because the consumer regex in `parse_contradiction_plan` matches `(\S+)` after `NOGOOD`, any `id` containing whitespace silently breaks the round-trip.

write-contradiction-plan-skips-header-wh.text: In `append=True` mode the `# Contradiction Plan` title and the `reasons contradictions --accept` instruction are not written; only blocks are appended.

write-false-prevents-persistence.text: Functions using `_with_network(write=False)` can mutate the in-memory network (as `what_if_retract` does) but changes are never saved to SQLite; write-or-not is declared upfront and never conditional.

write-persistence-requires-clean-context.text: All mutations are only persisted (and pub/sub events published) if the `_with_network(write=True)` block exits without raising.

write-proposals-file-roundtrips-through-.text: `parse_proposals(write_proposals_file(proposals))` reconstructs the same proposal shape, keeping writer and parser in sync.

yaml-quoting-is-partial.text: Only `project_name` and `base_network` are double-quoted; `license`, `domain` items, and `source_repos` items are emitted unquoted and unescaped, allowing malformed YAML from untrusted input.

zero-accepted-beliefs-is-valid-success-o.text: In the `diary-update` pipeline, `accepted == 0` is a valid successful outcome, not an error; the run still reports `status: "completed"`.

zero-accepted-beliefs-run-is-error.text: This is contradicted by the entry: a run accepting 0 beliefs still records `status: "completed"` and a `completed_at` timestamp.

zero-accepted-beliefs-still-completes.text: A run that accepts 0 beliefs still records `status: "completed"` and a `completed_at` timestamp; a zero-accept result is not treated as a failure.

zero-accepted-is-completed-status.text: A run where `accepted == 0` is reported as `status: "completed"`, not as an error.

zero-cost-indicates-unpriced-endpoint.text: `cost_dollars: 0.0` alongside nonzero token counts means the endpoint has no configured rate, not that the run failed.

zero-cost-models-still-log-token-counts.text: Proxied or zero-price models can log full `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` counts while reporting `cost_dollars: 0.0`.

zero-cost-models-still-log-tokens.text: Proxied/zero-price models (e.g., `rits/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`) still log full input/output token counts with `cost_dollars: 0.0`.

zero-cost-with-nonzero-tokens-means-unpr.text: A `cost_dollars: 0.0` value alongside nonzero token counts indicates the model endpoint has no configured price, not that the run failed.

zero-result-sentinel-preserved-after-out.text: When the only belief matching a search or lookup query has OUT status, the API returns a sentinel string ("No results found" / "No beliefs found") rather than an empty string or list, preserving a distinguishable empty-result contract for callers.

zero-runtime-dependencies.text: `ftl-reasons` declares `dependencies = []` in pyproject.toml; the entire `reasons_lib` package runs on Python's standard library alone (sqlite3, json, argparse); PostgreSQL support is opt-in via the `pg` extra

zero-runtime-deps.text: `ftl-reasons` has zero runtime dependencies; the entire library runs on Python's stdlib alone (SQLite via `sqlite3`, dataclasses, etc.).
